When we raise our hands before Him and think about putting our needs before Him, we should begin from a place of gratitude, from a place of acknowledgement of His favours, His greatness, His perfection. Our du’as should not be limited to demands and asks; they should include words of praise and glorification.

And the benefits of remembering Allah are at times far greater than the benefits of simply asking Him for this or that. You can get so much more out of glorifying and praising Allah than you can get from putting your needs before Him — because our asks are limited to what we can think of, what we can imagine, what we can wish for, and our knowledge and awareness is very limited. Allah’s treasures are vast, and He is able to give us more than we can even imagine we are in need of.

As Ibn Mas’ud (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) said: when one of you intends to ask, he should begin with the praise and glorification of Allah, then send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and then ask for what he wishes.

Reported from ‘Ali (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu)

Every du’a is veiled until salat is sent upon Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. One of the scholars, al-Munawi, explained that every du’a is prevented from being granted until the supplicant sends salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam.

So sending salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is a wasilah. It is a means of closeness to Allah, and a means of having du’as accepted. Some of the ulama said: begin your du’a with salawat, then in the middle of your du’a send salawat again, and at the end of your du’a send salawat once more — meaning, continue to send salawat on him for as long as you are making du’a.

Ubayy ibn Ka’b and His Question

Ubayy ibn Ka’b (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) was a companion very well versed in the knowledge of the Qur’an. One day the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam asked him what the greatest ayah of the Qur’an was, and he answered at once: Ayatul Kursi. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam struck him on his chest and said, “Congratulations on your knowledge” — expressing great joy. He was someone who paid great attention to the Book of Allah and did a great deal of tadabbur, which is why he could answer so quickly.

Hadith

Ubayy ibn Ka’b said to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam: I send a great deal of salat upon you — how much of my du’a should be sending salat upon you? He said: “Whatever you wish.” Ubayy asked, “One quarter?” He said, “Whatever you wish, and if you do more that will be better for you.” He said, “One half?” He said, “Whatever you wish, and if you do more that will be better for you.” He said, “Two thirds?” He said, “Whatever you wish, and if you do more that will be better for you.” He said, “I will make all of my du’a for you, then.” He said: “Then your concerns will be taken care of, and your sins will be forgiven.”

This hadith does not mean a person should never make du’a for themselves and should only send blessings upon the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam — that would be contrary to his own practice, because he made so many different du’as and taught people so many du’as as well. What “I will make all of my du’a for you” means is: I will spend the time I used to spend making a certain du’a in sending blessings upon you instead. Some of the scholars explained that Ubayy perhaps had a specific du’a he would make for himself regularly, and he was asking about replacing that du’a with salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam.

People do have du’as they make regularly: ya Allah, grant me good health; grant my parents well-being; protect me from such and such illness; protect me from extreme old age, from becoming dependent on my children and my family. These are the concerns we carry, the fears and apprehensions we have. But when you send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam once, Allah sends upon you ten blessings, forgives your sins, and raises your ranks.

So if you were to ask for different things, how many things can you ask for, and what exactly are you asking for? It is possible you are asking Allah to protect you from extreme old age or dependency on others — and who knows, Allah may already have decreed good health for you until the end of your life. So you are spending time asking for something that may not even apply to you, and you do not know it. But if you ask Allah to send blessings upon the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, Allah will bless you ten times more, forgive you, and raise your ranks. The du’a you make for him is far more beneficial for you than the du’a you can make for yourself.

Imam al-Shawkani explains that if Allah takes care of a person’s concerns, such a person will be free from trials and troubles in this world — because every trial inevitably causes some concern, even if it is little. And if Allah forgives a person’s sins, then he will be safe from the trials of the Hereafter.

But With Moderation

There should, of course, be moderation. Some people, on the basis of this hadith, mandate on themselves or on their children that they must send salawat at such and such occasion, this many times a day — and then they don’t teach them the other du’as the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught. We must benefit from the du’as Allah has taught us in the Qur’an and the du’as the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught us otherwise, and we must also send salat on him. We should do both.

Chapter Forty-Five

What Salat and Salam Actually Mean

The Qur’an

“Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels ask Him to do so. O you who have believed, ask Allah to confer blessing upon him and ask Allah to grant him peace.”

In this ayah Allah shows us the status of His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. Not only is Allah honouring him through this ayah, in his life and also after his death, but Allah is telling us what his status is before Him: that Allah sends salat on His Messenger, and His angels send salat on him. This is what happens in the highest assembly. This is what the inhabitants of the heavens do — so all inhabitants of the earth should do the same.

Because when you send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, you are conforming with an action that Allah ‘Azza wa Jall does, and with an action His angels are doing. You are conforming with a heavenly deed, something done in the heavens by the inhabitants of the heavens. So while you are on the earth, you should also do something heavenly — because it will raise you in your ranks. And this shows us that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is praised and mentioned in the higher world and also on the earth.

The Meaning of Salat

Salawat is plural; salat is singular. Linguistically, the word salat means du’a and prayer; rahmah, mercy; istighfar, seeking forgiveness; and husnuth-thana, good praise. It also means baraka, a blessing that Allah bestows, and it means praise, good mention, to commend someone. All of these meanings are included in it.

When Allah sends salat on the Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, it means that Allah bestows His mercy upon him, that Allah praises him before His angels, and that Allah bestows His ridwan, His approval, upon him. When the angels send salat on him, it means that they pray for his forgiveness, they praise him, and they ask Allah to bestow His mercy and His blessing upon him.

Some ulama say the word salah is connected to the word sillah — a reward or gift. Because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is already forgiven; Allah tells us Himself that his past and future sins were all forgiven. So if salat includes praying for forgiveness, and he is already forgiven, what does it mean? It means: O Allah, bestow Your sillah, Your gift, upon him. And what is that gift? It is the gift of praise, of good mention, that He will commend him in the highest gathering, in the mala’ul a’la.

Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) made du’a: O Allah, bestow on me a good mention among the later people — meaning, let the people who come after me remember me in a good way. And everyone has this wish: that after I am gone, when I am no longer with people, they should remember me well and talk about me positively. This does not mean we are seeking the praise of people. It means we are hopeful that while we are with people we do such good, such beneficial things, that when we leave them they have nothing negative to say — only something positive. In other words you are asking: ya Allah, give me the ability to do good while I am among people, to benefit them, to protect them from harm. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was granted that anyway: he is mentioned and praised not only in this world, but also in the highest gathering.

The Meaning of Salam

Salam is one of the names of Allah, and it means soundness, perfection, safety. So when we ask Allah to bestow salam on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, we are asking Allah to bestow soundness on him, so that he is preserved and safe during his lifetime — and this was relevant to the companions. But after he departed from this world, how is it applicable? It means we are asking Allah to bestow soundness on his deen, and to bestow him with soundness on the Day of Judgment.

Because the Day of Judgment is a day of terror, a day when even the prophets of Allah will say Allahumma sallim — O Allah, grant safety. So when we ask Allah to send salam on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, it means: O Allah, grant him safety on that day, grant him safety and well-being and calm in his heart on that day. And part of this is that we are asking Allah to bestow safety and protection in the form of protecting his shari’ah, his deen, his sunnah, his teachings — that they may be preserved, and that people are not able to tamper with them or change them or harm the deen of Allah in any way. Because this is what he dedicated himself to conveying to us. So: ya Allah, preserve his efforts, preserve his work.

How Appreciative Allah Is

If you think about this, it shows us how very appreciative Allah is. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam spent twenty-three short years as a prophet in this world, conveying the message of Allah. Those twenty-three years are quantifiable — you can count them. But look at the reward Allah is bestowing upon him: it is endless. We are to send salat on him in every salah, after every adhan, when we enter the masjid, on so many occasions. Allah Himself sends salawat on him, and His angels send salawat on him. This shows us how pleased Allah is with His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and how He appreciates his efforts.

And think about this: when you do something for the sake of Allah, yes, it is a measurable deed — small, quantifiable — but the reward Allah gives is without measure. You cannot count it. So whatever we do in obedience to Allah, let us do it for Him alone, with utmost sincerity, seeking His approval — because when our deeds are sincere for His sake, they will be accepted. And let us do them in the best way we can. Don’t compare yourself to others; compare yourself to the guidelines Allah has given, and ask whether your action matches what He has instructed.

For example, in the night prayer: some people in your family may be going to the masjid every night, praying eight or twenty rak’ahs, standing in qiyam for so long, coming home after two hours. And what did you manage to do in those two hours? Maybe put a crying baby to sleep five or ten times. Maybe you barely managed to clean the kitchen. Maybe you managed to pray your fard and two rak’ahs, or four — very little compared to what other people are doing. But the way you perform those two rak’ahs: do them with ihsan, with sincerity. Pay attention, recite Surat al-Fatihah with khushu’, and ask Allah to accept your little efforts. Because yes, your deeds are little, but when they are done with ihsan, with ikhlas, with the best of your ability, and in a manner Allah is pleased with, then the reward Allah bestows is very, very generous. And the example of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is proof of that: he worked for twenty-three years, and look at the limitless reward Allah is bestowing upon him.

Chapter Forty-Six

His Favours Upon Us

Why should we send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam? A lot of people have difficulty understanding this — he was a messenger of Allah, he conveyed the Qur’an, he taught us what to do, and all right — but why do I have to send salat on him, and why has Allah promised so many benefits for it?

There is a reason. The first is that it is the right of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam that we pray for him, that we praise him, that we ask Allah to bestow His mercy and blessings and protection and safety upon him, that we ask Allah to mention him and praise him. Because he deserves this from us. It is a sign of love for him, and a sign of true faith. In a hadith we learn that he said none of you will have faith until he loves me more than his father, his children, and all of mankind. When a person sends salutations upon him, it is a sign that they honour him, that they respect him, that they do not hold him in light estimation — that they have great love for him.

And why? Look at his favours upon us.

The Qur’an

Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you; and to the believers he is kind and merciful.

This is how he felt for his ummah: it was very hard on him to see his ummah suffer, he was eager for their benefit and reward, and he was kind and merciful to them. Allah says in the Qur’an that the Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves — closer to the believers than they are to themselves.

Hadith

He said: there is no believer but that I, of all people, am the closest to him both in this world and in the Hereafter. Then he recited the ayah above, and said that if a believer dies leaving some property, his relatives will inherit it; but if that believer dies leaving a debt or leaves poor children, then let those creditors and children come to me, and I will take care of them — I will pay off the debt on his behalf and take care of his children on his behalf.

This shows us that he was closest not just to the believers of his time, the companions, but to all who believe in him — those of his time and those who came later. Now think about this: is there any leader who would say something like this, that whatever you leave of property is for your family, but if you leave any debt, I will take care of it? Is there any leader, any friend even, who would say this?

He Wept for Us

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam recited the statement of Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam): “My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me, then he is of me.” And he recited the statement of ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam): “If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Then he raised his hands and said, “Allahumma ummati, ummati” — O Allah, my ummah, my ummah — and he wept.

So Allah said to Jibreel: go to Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and though your Lord is Most Knowing, ask him what is making him cry. So Jibreel came and asked him, and he said: my ummah, my ummah. Jibreel went back, and Allah said: O Jibreel, go to Muhammad and say that indeed We will please you in regard to your ummah, and We will not let you be displeased.

He was concerned for us because he saw what happened to the ummah of Ibrahim, where people went back to idolatry, and what happened to the followers of ‘Isa, who ended up committing shirk — so what would happen to his ummah? This is how eager he was for our salvation and our protection: that we, his ummah, should not suffer punishment in the Hereafter. He was more concerned for us and more compassionate to us than even our own parents are. Because most of the time our parents are concerned for our dunya — our health, our wealth, our worldly future — but he was worried for our dunya and our salvation.

Hadith

‘A’ishah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) once saw that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was in a good mood, so she asked him to make du’a for her. He said: O Allah, forgive ‘A’ishah all of her sins, whatever she did first and whatever she did afterwards, and whatever she did secretly and whatever she did openly. She was so happy that she began to laugh, and as she laughed she dropped her head in his lap. He asked her, “Does my du’a make you happy?” She said, “Why would it not make me happy?” He replied: “By Allah, this is my du’a for my ummah in every salah.”

In every salah he made this du’a for us: O Allah, forgive my ummah their sins — whatever they did first, whatever they did later, whatever they did secretly, whatever they did openly.

He Saved His Request for Us

On one occasion he was told to ask Allah for something special, because every prophet was granted a unique request. Sulayman (‘alayhis salam), for example, asked for a kingdom that would be exclusively his, the like of which would not be given to anyone after him, and that du’a was accepted. So the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was also told to make du’a, because every prophet has a request that is granted. And what did he do? He said: I have saved mine for the Day of Judgment — and it is for you. Meaning, my du’a is going to be for you, on the Day of Judgment, for those who bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah.

He did not ask for anything for himself in this world. He saved that du’a for his ummah on the Day of Judgment. Try to understand the love and the concern he had for his ummah — for you and me, who never saw him. What did he get from us?

We learn that on the Day of Judgment he will be granted shafa’ah, the chance to intercede for his ummah. And in another hadith we learn that on one occasion he was praying in the night, and throughout his night prayer he kept reciting the ayah, “If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” In the morning he was asked why he had recited only this ayah throughout the night prayer, and he said: I asked my Lord for the ability to intercede for my ummah on the Day of Judgment, and I was granted that.

And in another hadith we learn that Allah has forgiven his nation — because of him, because of his du’a, because of his request — for their errors, for their forgetfulness, and for what they are forced to do. So they will not be held responsible or punished for these matters: if they make an error and do not even realise it, or they forget something, or they are compelled to do something wrong, they will not be held sinful, because he made that request.

He Did Not Wish to Burden Us

He was eager to convey good to us and to encourage us to do good, but at the same time he did not wish to burden us. He said that if it was not hard on his ummah, he would have commanded them to make wudu for every salah — but he did not give that instruction, because making wudu before every salah is difficult. And with the night prayer in Ramadan, when the companions prayed behind him they enjoyed it so much, but he did not do that every night of Ramadan — because he was afraid it might become mandatory on the ummah, and then how would every person be able to pray qiyam al-layl every single night?

Hadith

“My example and the example of the people is that of a man who made a fire, and when it lit up what was around it, moths and other insects began falling into the fire. The man tried his best to prevent them from falling in, but they overpowered him and rushed into it. Similarly, I take hold of the knots at your waists, trying to prevent you from falling into the fire — but you insist on falling into it.”

Hadith

He said: I wish I could have met my brothers. The companions said, “Are we not your brothers?” He said: “You are my companions. My brothers are those who believe in me and have not even seen me.”

He had so much love for his ummah, even those he had not met, those who would come much later. So why should we not have that love for him, and why should we not send salawat on him?

Chapter Forty-Seven

What You Gain, and When to Say It

When we send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, we are the ones who benefit.

  • If anyone sends salat on him once, Allah sends salat on that person ten times — Allah blesses him ten times.
  • In another hadith: ten sins are forgiven, ten ranks are raised, ten good deeds are recorded. You get instant benefit.
  • You also receive baraka. In a hadith we learn that when you send salat on him, that is zakat for you — a means of purification and growth, meaning an increase in reward.
  • Ibn al-Qayyim said that sending salat on him is a means of acquiring blessing: in one’s actions, in one’s life, in one’s goals. Why? Because it is a du’a that is mustajab, certainly accepted. You are asking Allah to bless him, so Allah will bless you; you are asking Allah to raise his ranks, so Allah will raise your ranks; you are asking Allah to protect him, so Allah will protect you.
  • Ibn Hajar said that one of the most effective things to repel ta’un — a plague, a disease that spreads quickly among people — and to repel other tribulations, is to increase in sending salawat on him. One thing is that a person suffers at a personal level; another is that an entire community or nation is suffering. When we ask Allah as a community to send His blessings on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, Allah will bless the entire community with more blessings and grant more forgiveness. This is how you repel tribulation, not just at a personal level but at a community level also.
  • Ibn al-Jawzi said that when Allah intends good for a slave, He makes it easy for him to send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam.
  • When you send salawat on him, it is actually conveyed to him, no matter where in the world you are — angels convey it to him.
  • Those who send salat on him a lot will be worthy of his intercession on the Day of Judgment, and they will also be close to him.

Some ulama said it is the people of hadith who will be closest to him on the Day of Judgment — because those who study hadith, who write it, research it, listen to it, read it and teach it, send a great deal of salat on him, since they come across his name so much and every time they mention or read or write it they say salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. So make the intention to join some halaqah, some class where hadith is studied, so that you can be among those who receive these blessings.

The One Who Does Not Send Salat

The person who does not send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is truly stingy and miserly — he is al-bakhil. That the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is mentioned and he does not send salat on him: this is stinginess.

Hadith

Once the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was ascending the mimbar and said, “Ameen, ameen, ameen.” The people asked him why, and he said Jibreel came to him and said: may his nose be soiled with dust, the one who finds one or both of his parents in old age and does not enter Paradise because of it — and he said, “Ameen.” Then Jibreel said: may his nose be soiled with dust, the one in whose presence you are mentioned and he does not supplicate for you — and he said, “Ameen.” Then Jibreel said: may his nose be soiled with dust, the one who finds the month of Ramadan but does not receive Allah’s forgiveness — and he said, “Ameen.”

When to Send Salawat

Every time we hear the name of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, we should send salawat on him. And do not get bored, do not get tired, because every time you send salawat you are the one who benefits.

  • Even when you are writing his name, make sure to write salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam.
  • After the adhan — make the du’a to be said after the adhan, and also send salawat on him.
  • When you enter the masjid, along with asking Allah to forgive your sins and open the doors of His mercy.
  • In salah, in the tashahhud.
  • In ‘Umrah, while doing sa’i.
  • Especially on the day of Friday — he told us to send a great deal of salawat on him on that day.
  • In the funeral prayer, after the second takbir.
  • When praying qunut.
  • When making du’a — and this is one of the reasons we are studying this topic in so much detail.
  • When we are in a gathering.
Hadith

When people gather together and do not remember Allah in that gathering, and do not send salawat on their Prophet, then that gathering will be a means of loss for them, and it is up to Allah to punish them or forgive them. In another narration: such a gathering will be a means of regret for them on the Day of Judgment.

So make it a habit to say it frequently. When you say it frequently, then even in your gatherings — when you sit together with family and friends for iftar and you are talking about different things — you will make sure to send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam as well.

And remember that where we send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, we should also send salawat on all of the prophets of Allah. When their names are mentioned we should say ‘alayhis salam. Two things are there: salat and salam. So we should do that for the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and also for the other prophets of Allah.

Chapter Forty-Eight

The Words He Taught Us

How can we send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam? What are the words we can use? The best words are the words we have been taught by him himself. Some people have invented their own ways of sending salat on him, and even if the meaning of those wordings is correct, the best words are the words he himself taught us. All four wordings below are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad

O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad. Zayd ibn Kharijah reported that he asked the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam how to send salat on him, and he said: “Send salah upon me and strive hard in supplication,” and then, “say: Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad.”

To strive hard in supplication means that when you are making du’a you should not be weak in your determination, or lazy, or lacking eagerness and vigour. Strive hard. And sometimes striving hard in making du’a means striving hard in being attentive, in showing humility, in bringing tears to your eyes.

Notice here that we are not just asking Allah to send salat on Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, but also on his al. And al includes two things: family, and followers — and this is how the word has been used in the Qur’an, for the family of someone and also their followers. So the al of Muhammad includes his wives, his children and his relatives, but it also includes his followers.

2. Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin in-nabiyyil ummiyyi wa ‘ala ali Muhammad

O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon the family of Muhammad.

3. The Salat Ibrahimi

Hadith

‘Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla met Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah, who asked him: shall I give you a gift? And he expressed his willingness. So Ka’b said: once the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam came to us and we said, “O Messenger of Allah, we know how to greet you, but how should we send salat on you?” So he taught us the words of the salat Ibrahimi.

He taught these words, and they are a gift for us. How? Because when we say this we are not only praying for the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and his followers — we are essentially praying for ourselves, because we are saying: O Allah, bless the al of Muhammad, his family and his followers, and we are his followers. So we are asking Allah to mention us, to forgive us, to bestow His approval, His mercy and His blessings on us.

And specifically in this we say: as You have bestowed blessing on Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) and his family. The favours Allah bestowed on Ibrahim are well known — he is the father of the prophets, he is the Khalil, the close friend of Allah; Allah tested him and he passed all of those tests and showed perfect obedience, fulfilling every command he was given, so Allah was pleased with him. So we are asking Allah to send the same or even more — because the word kama does not just mean “just as,” it also means “because”: because You have sent blessings on Ibrahim and his al, You are able to send even more blessings on Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and his al.

4. Upon Him, His Wives and His Progeny

O Allah, bestow favour upon Muhammad and upon his wives and his progeny, as You have bestowed favour upon the family of Ibrahim; and bless Muhammad and his wives and his progeny, as You have blessed the family of Ibrahim. You are praiseworthy, most glorious.

Why are we asking Allah to send His blessings upon his wives and his children specifically? Because they played a huge role in his mission. You see the wife of Nuh (‘alayhis salam) and the wife of Lut (‘alayhis salam) — these women betrayed their husbands. The son of Nuh did not believe in him. But look at how Khadijah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) supported him from day one; how his daughters took care of him from the beginning; and how later the other wives believed in him, supported him, took care of him, and then played such a huge role in teaching his sunnah. ‘A’ishah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) and Umm Salamah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) played a huge role in teaching the ummah. So: O Allah, bless them also.

And when any person does some work, their family supports them. Without the support of the family, without the sacrifice of the family, and sometimes without the suffering of the family, a person cannot do much work. Look at the poverty the family of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam endured. Fatimah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) was exhausted with housework; she had little children, she would work so hard, and her husband ‘Ali (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) did not have much to provide her with. So she went to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam asking for a servant who could help her with the work — and he did not give her one, because other people were in greater need. He made his own daughter sacrifice for the benefit of the ummah. Instead, he taught her some words of dhikr to say at night, for ease.

‘A’ishah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) said that for many days the fire would not be lit in their home, because there was nothing to cook, and the family would survive on the two black things: water and dates. So the family of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam also deserve that we love them, that we remember and honour their sacrifice and their efforts, and that we pray to Allah for them also — just as the family of Ibrahim was blessed. We are asking Allah to reward them abundantly and to raise their ranks.

So when we make du’a, we should send salat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. Sending salat on him is a means of great blessing and great benefit for us in dunya and akhirah, and it is a means of relief from worry and grief and anxiety and troubles. Increase in it. And it is good that we vary the wordings we use — so of the different versions above, try to memorise the one you do not know, and use that also. Because if the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught us these words, then every single one of them is worthy of being recited, and each one brings a different benefit.

Allahumma salli ‘ala Muhammadin wa ‘ala ali Muhammad.
Ameen.
Chapter Forty-Nine

Those Who Know and Those Who Don’t

Allah our Lord loves praise, and He listens to our praise. When we praise and glorify Him, when we remember Him, He remembers us; when we call upon Him, He answers us. So we should continue to call upon Him, and we should not forget to glorify and remember Him in our du’as, especially at the beginning.

About the dhikr of praise we learned in a hadith that it is better than remembering Allah night and day — that if you were to remember Allah continuously all night long and the entire day, these words would still be better than that. This shows us that while we busy ourselves in worshipping Allah, it is important that we also learn the best ways of remembering Him and worshipping Him, because there is a difference between people who know and people who do not know.

Earlier we learned about how Juwayriyah was sitting in her prayer place worshipping Allah for so long, and the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that he had said four phrases three times, and the reward of those phrases was greater than the reward for all that she had done for the duration she was sitting there. So there is a difference between those who know and those who don’t. Those who know are able to worship Allah better and more, and in a way that is pleasing to Him and that brings them more reward. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is the one who brought this sacred, beneficial knowledge to us.

Those who know are different from those who don’t know. Those who know are able to excel, able to get ahead, able to bring benefit to themselves and to others, and able to earn the pleasure of Allah.

What ‘Ilm Actually Is

The opposite of ignorance is ‘ilm, and ‘ilm is to know something the way it actually is, in a solid and proper way. For example, if a person really has knowledge of salah, of how to pray, then if they were asked in which cases one is supposed to perform sajdah sahw, they would be able to answer right away. But if they say, “I don’t remember, I’m not sure,” then that means they do not have ‘ilm. ‘Ilm is to know something as it is, and to know it firmly, so that a person is able to retrieve that information and apply it whenever they have to.

Three Kinds of Knowledge

  1. Beneficial knowledge. Knowledge that brings a person benefit in their worldly matters and also in their religious matters, so that they benefit from it in the world and in the Hereafter. This is real knowledge; this is the best kind.
  2. Harmful knowledge. Knowledge that harms a person in their dunya and in their deen, bringing them suffering and loss in this world and religiously, so that they continue to suffer because of it in the Hereafter. For example, if a person learns ways of hacking software and computers and then commits crimes through it — yes, they are an expert in that field, but this knowledge is harmful. Or if a person learns the knowledge of magic and then performs magic, this brings them harm in regard to their deen: loss upon loss, harm upon harm, in this world and the next.
  3. Useless knowledge. Knowledge that neither brings benefit nor harm — a complete waste. For example, a person has very good information on the different players of a certain team and how their performance has been over the years; or a person knows a great deal about famous people, where they live, what they eat, who they are dating, what their morning routine is and their nighttime routine. This kind of knowledge is certainly useless, but too much of it can in fact become harmful, because then a person spends their time on these matters and is distracted from what is beneficial, from worshipping Allah. And if a person has knowledge of people who are sinful in their life choices, what happens is that they begin to follow them, and so they become closer to sin than to good deeds.

So we should seek knowledge that is beneficial — information that will actually benefit us, in the worldly sense and in the religious sense.

Chapter Fifty

The Knowledge We Must Seek

Knowledge of the Deen

Beneficial knowledge is of two kinds. The first is knowledge of the deen — whether it is related to worship, or to the life and teachings of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, or even knowledge of the Arabic language so that a person can understand the Qur’an better and read the explanations of hadith. This type of knowledge strengthens a person in their ‘aqidah, in their worship, in their dealings with people, and in their relationship with Allah. It increases a person in guidance — and when we ask Allah to guide us to the straight path, part of that guidance is that a person learns the right way of worshipping Allah, because only when they have that knowledge can they act upon it, and only then are they rightly guided.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that seeking knowledge is an obligation on every Muslim, and this is knowledge of the deen. Because if a person does not know Surat al-Fatihah, how can they pray? If a person does not know when to begin their fast and when to end it and how to observe it and what they are supposed to abstain from, how can they keep a fast? If a person does not know that if they are unable to fast they should give the fidyah, how can they give it? Why would they give it when they don’t even know? So this type of knowledge is an obligation on every person.

And it is the best form of knowledge, because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said the best of you are those who learn the Qur’an and teach it. The purpose of learning the Qur’an is to learn the deen — and why learn the deen? So that you can follow it and do the things which are pleasing to Allah.

Knowledge of Worldly Matters

The second type of beneficial knowledge is worldly knowledge: knowledge of those matters which are of benefit to people and essential as well. Knowledge of medicine, for example — if we don’t have doctors, if we don’t have people who understand medicine, people would suffer so much. Knowledge of trade, of agriculture, of engineering: all of these help people in their lives and in earning their livelihood. This type of knowledge is an obligation on the community. Every person does not have to become a doctor or a farmer, but there must be some people who have this knowledge — because if no one has it, the entire community will suffer, and Muslims will get left behind while other people excel.

And this is a prophetic way. About Dawud (‘alayhis salam), Allah tells us that He softened iron for him, so he was able to make coats of mail and chain mail, and Allah mentions that in the Qur’an. You would think that a prophet of Allah would only have knowledge of the deen — but we see that of course he had knowledge of the deen, he was an excellent worshipper and he was a king, yet he also knew how to work with iron. So learning such skills, which help us take care of ourselves, fulfil our needs, earn an income and provide for our families, is beneficial, and we are encouraged to learn them.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: be keen on what benefits you. These days, learning how to use a computer, or how to use your phone in a way that helps you be more organised and productive — this is not useless knowledge, this is beneficial knowledge. If you learn how to operate a machine, if you learn how to use spreadsheets, then you are able to do so much work, you become better at your work, and you bring benefit to yourself and others. And he said: seek help from Allah and do not give up. Because sometimes learning this type of knowledge is boring, especially when a person finds more joy in learning the Qur’an and the Sunnah — so when you have to take a workshop or study something related to the dunya, you feel it is a waste of time. It is not a waste of time. Seek Allah’s help, and even this will become an act of worship.

The Order of Priority

The knowledge most essential for every human being is the knowledge that Allah is One, because Allah says: know that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah. This is essential for every person, because only then can a person be saved in this dunya and in the Hereafter.

After the knowledge of tawhid comes the knowledge of worship: how to obtain purification, how to praise Allah, how to perform the various acts of worship. So set goals for yourself — I am going to take a course, I am going to study a book on how to perform salah properly. Alhamdulillah, there are so many courses available in so many languages so that our salah improves, so that we know how to calculate and give zakat, how to remember Allah. The purpose of seeking this knowledge is so that we don’t spend our lives in confusion and ignorance, because knowledge removes doubt and confusion. When we don’t have knowledge of how to worship Allah, we remain in doubt, unsure whether we are doing things properly, and we do not find the joy of worshipping Him.

And after learning the different ways of worshipping Allah, we must also learn what is halal and what is haram — when it comes to food, to earning money, even to the relationship between husband and wife.

Two Obstacles

We should not have shyness or arrogance in the path of learning. Shyness prevents a person from seeking clarity. And arrogance is the assumption that I already know, that I do not need to ask, I do not need to learn any more — because if I do, then I am admitting that I don’t know, and if I don’t know, then that is beneath me. Both shyness and arrogance are huge obstacles in the path of learning.

Chapter Fifty-One

The Pen, and Those Who Sought Knowledge

Knowledge is extremely important in our deen. First of all, our Lord Himself has knowledge; it is one of His attributes. We learn in the Qur’an: do you not know that Allah knows what is in the sky and the earth? And Allah has knowledge of everything, and He has encompassed everything in knowledge. There is nothing except that Allah knows about it.

Hadith

The first thing Allah created was the pen, and then He commanded it to write everything that will happen. In another narration we learn that Allah created four things with His hand: the Throne, the pen, Adam, and the Garden of Eden.

Look at the importance Allah has given to the pen — so much so that Allah takes an oath by it: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.” So we should develop the habit of not just listening to beneficial things passively, but actively — and use the pen. Write. Because when you write something you are preserving that knowledge with yourself; you will be able to access it when you have forgotten, and you will be able to remind yourself of it.

And don’t be ashamed of writing. Sometimes when we look at how poor or how slow our writing is, or when we compare it to other people’s, we say, “My writing is not that nice, I can’t take good notes, so I am not going to write.” No — try your best. The more you write the better you will become, and the more you write the more you will remember and understand what you are learning.

The first revelation given to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was: read, read in the name of your Lord who created, who created man from a clinging substance; recite, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man that which he knew not. So the use of the pen is essential for learning. This shows us that while we listen to different lectures, that is nice — but we should also study, take courses. After Ramadan, set goals for yourself: I am going to take this course, then that one. See what your ability is. Can you take a course once a week, twice a week, full-time, part-time, weekday, evening, weekend? Because when you enrol in a class, you will definitely use the pen, you will take notes.

Allah is very merciful to His people. We learn in the Qur’an: the Extremely Merciful — He taught the Qur’an, He created man, He taught him eloquence. Notice that even before mentioning the ability to express ourselves, Allah mentions the blessing of the knowledge of the Qur’an. And the knowledge of the Qur’an is not limited to reciting it: we should learn to recite it properly, memorise its verses, but also learn its meaning, its language, and the different sciences related to it — how the Qur’an was preserved, the different recitations, the tafsir. All of this is beneficial, and this is the mercy of Allah.

And one of the first blessings Allah bestowed on Adam (‘alayhis salam) was that He taught him knowledge — knowledge He had not given to the angels. And based on that knowledge Allah commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, to show him honour. So the dignity people have been given is because of the knowledge Allah has given us. We should not turn away from it; we should be eager to acquire it and increase in it.

The Prophets Were People of Knowledge

Allah describes Yusuf (‘alayhis salam) as a possessor of knowledge, because We had given him knowledge. Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) said to his father: certain knowledge has come to me — I have knowledge that has been given to me from Allah, and this knowledge is such that you do not know about it.

Musa (‘alayhis salam) was so eager to increase in his knowledge that he travelled a difficult journey on foot to find Khidr, and when he found him he asked to be taught of the truth which he had been taught. Khidr said: is it not sufficient for you that the Tawrah is in your hands? Allah has already given you the Tawrah — what more do you want to know? So Musa knew the knowledge of the Tawrah, yet he was eager to learn more. And in their journey they saw a bird take some water from the sea with its beak, and Khidr said: by Allah, my knowledge and your knowledge is like what this bird has taken with its beak from the sea. When a bird dips its beak in the sea, how much water comes onto it? Very, very little. So the knowledge of people is like that drop compared to the knowledge of Allah.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was given blessed knowledge; in fact he was sent as a teacher. As Allah says: He teaches you the Book and the wisdom, and teaches you what you did not use to know. Jibreel would come in order to teach the Sahabah different things — he would come and ask the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam questions before the companions, and afterwards the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told them that was Jibreel, who had come to teach you your religion.

Learning, and Passing It On

It is an obligation on the Muslim ummah that we learn sacred knowledge and also impart it. Allah says it is not for the believers to go forth to battle all at once; rather, there should separate from every division of them a group to obtain understanding in the religion and to warn their people when they return to them, so that they might be cautious. Just as every nation has an army dedicated to defending it, there must be some people dedicated to learning the deen and teaching people — because if no one dedicates themselves to it, how will people learn? Over time they will forget. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam warned us that this is how knowledge will depart: the people of knowledge will finish, and those left behind never bothered to learn, so they never became people of knowledge; and as each scholar leaves the world there are fewer people of knowledge left.

And he encouraged us: convey from me even if it is one ayah. You don’t have to be an expert scholar before you convey something. If you know very little, and you know it well and understand it properly, then pass it on. Teach Surat al-Fatihah to your child, to your toddler — your toddler does not know it yet, you know it, so teach it. And he made du’a for those of his ummah who learn something he taught and then pass it on: may Allah cause his face to shine on the Day of Judgment. And the benefit of passing on knowledge is that you remember it yourself, because when you teach you are forced to review what you have learned, to understand it well and remember it well — and then you are also able to apply it.

He would send companions to different places to teach the locals. He sent Mu’adh to Yemen and told him that the first thing he should teach people is the oneness of Allah; when they learn that, tell them that Allah has enjoined on them five prayers; and when they pray, teach them about zakat. So teach gradually, starting with what is most important.

And Allah teaches us that when you don’t know something, ask those who know. It is wrong for a person to speak about something without knowledge — if you don’t know something, don’t talk about it. Silence is better.

Chapter Fifty-Two

What Knowledge Does

Allah asks us: are those people who know equal to those who do not know? The answer is obvious. They are not equal — because it is those who have knowledge among the servants of Allah who fear Allah. They know Allah, so they fear Him. And those who don’t have knowledge don’t know Allah, so they don’t have fear of Him; they end up saying things which are inappropriate, wasting their lives, wasting their time, wasting excellent opportunities, and making many mistakes.

Hadith

Whoever Allah intends good for, He gives that person understanding of the deen.

Because when a person understands the deen, the doors of goodness open for them. For example, if you understand the meaning of SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, then you say it in the morning, you say it in the evening, you say it in your free moments, you say it when your hands are busy but your mind is free — for example when you are doing the dishes. And what is happening? You are earning so much reward at the same time. So Allah has given you so much good by giving you knowledge of those words.

This is why we should be begging Allah: ya Allah, grant me knowledge, increase me in knowledge. Because knowledge brings a person out of ignorance, out of misguidance, out of darkness; it takes a person towards light, it brings clarity and confidence, and it takes a person onto the straight path. If a person does not know, they are wandering and making errors.

In Surat al-Fatihah we ask Allah to guide us to the straight path, the path of those on whom He has bestowed favour, not of those with whom He was angry, nor of those who are astray. Who are the people with whom Allah is angry? Those who have knowledge but do not act upon it. And who are those who are astray? Those who don’t even know what is right and what is wrong, what is guidance and what is misguidance, who Allah is, whether He is One, or how to worship Him — they have no knowledge of these matters, and when they don’t have knowledge they are lost, and they don’t even know that they don’t know. So we are taught to pray for the path of people with whom Allah is pleased: people who have knowledge and who act upon it.

Knowing the Difference Between Truth and Falsehood

These days everyone has their own truth: this is my truth, I have found my truth, I live my truth. There are so many versions of truth, and so much confusion, because truth has been mixed with falsehood and everyone is told, “You are right, just follow your heart, just live your truth.” We sometimes forget what is actually right and what is actually wrong.

We cannot be of those people who say everything is right, because everything is not right. We cannot be of those who say each person must live their own truth — because truth is not determined by desire. If a person who is twenty years of age says, “I identify as a sixty-year-old,” or “I identify as a five-year-old child,” that is pure foolishness; that is not truth. Sometimes when we get exposed to such concepts, where everybody claims that what they are doing is right, we forget that there is actually haqq and there is actually batil — there is truth and there is falsehood. And in order to know the difference, we must learn the knowledge of the deen. Without it we will become of those who say everything is right.

Knowledge Brings the Heart to Life

Allah tells us: O you who believe, respond to Allah and the Messenger when the Messenger calls you to that which brings you life. And what does the Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam call people to? To Allah, to the deen of Allah. So learning the deen is life for the heart. Ibrahim ibn ‘Uyaynah said that Allah has made knowledge for the hearts just as rain is for the earth: when rain falls, the earth comes to life, there is growth, there are plants. Just like that, when a person has knowledge the heart comes to life, and a person is able to do something good and beneficial, and to do things in the right way.

And when a person learns knowledge they are able to avoid sins, because they recognise what is wrong. ‘Ilm doesn’t just bring you information; it also brings you fear of Allah and humility — and when a person has fear of Allah they are able to stay away from what displeases Him.

In order to protect ourselves from Shaytan too, we have to learn the deen. Right after mentioning the straight path, Allah tells us not to let Shaytan stop us — because Shaytan makes knowledge of the deen seem boring, telling a person this is hard, this is difficult, putting obstacles on that path.

Blessing, and Provision

When people acquire knowledge of the deen, there is blessing in their homes and in their lives. It was said that when the Qur’an is recited in a house — and the Qur’an cannot be recited without knowledge of recitation — then that house becomes vast for its inhabitants, the angels are present in it, the shayateen leave it, and its goodness increases. But when the Qur’an is not recited in a house, it becomes constricted for its inhabitants: it may be three thousand square feet, but people feel tight in it, they want to get out, they want to run away. The angels leave that house, the devils are present in it, and its goodness decreases.

When a person acquires knowledge they receive the mercy of Allah, and sakinah, tranquillity, descends upon those who recite the Qur’an and discuss the Book of Allah and learn it together.

Hadith

There were two brothers at the time of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. One of them would go to him every day in order to learn, and the other would go out to work in order to make money. One day the one who worked came and complained about his brother — that he just comes to you every day, he doesn’t come to work with me, he doesn’t help me, he is wasting his time. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: perhaps you are provided because of him.

Meaning it is possible that when you go to work and are able to make money, you are able to do that because Allah is giving you sustenance — and why is He giving it to you? Because you are making money for your family, and part of your family is your brother, who is studying the deen. Because of studying the deen, people are provided with rizq, given success, given success even in the world.

Preparing for the Meeting

Allah tells us that we should know we are going to meet Him. So it is necessary to learn about that meeting so we can prepare for it, because if we don’t prepare we will be in great difficulty on that day. Think about it: if you have to take an entry test, even if you just want the privilege of driving a car, do you not need to read the book at least once, to learn what the different road signs mean? If you don’t, you are going to go overconfident into that test and actually fail.

We learn that on the Day of Judgment the feet of a person cannot move until he is asked about five things: about his life and what he did with it, his knowledge and what he did with it, his wealth — how he earned it and where he spent it — and his body and what he did with it.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that whoever follows a path in pursuit of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him the path to Paradise. And the person who dies while knowing that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah will enter Paradise.

Imam Ahmad used to say that the need people have for knowledge is greater than the need they have for food. Because food and drink you need once or twice a day; when you are fasting it is sufficient to eat twice a day, and some people cannot even eat properly at iftar time — you can survive with one or two meals. But when it comes to knowledge, you need it for every breath that you take, every moment of your life, because you need knowledge in order to decide what to do and what not to do, and if you are doing something, how to do it, and if you are leaving something, how to leave it. So our need for knowledge is greater than our need for food and drink.

Chapter Fifty-Three

Sincerity in Seeking It

Why should we learn the knowledge of the deen? For the sake of Allah alone. Because if a person learns it in order to show off, in order to be called a scholar or a very good speaker or an excellent author, to acquire such titles — if the goal is to be called something in the world — then this will be a source of punishment on the Day of Judgment.

Hadith

On the Day of Judgment a reciter of the Qur’an will be brought, and Allah will remind him of His blessings upon him and ask him what he did. That person will say: I learned the knowledge of Your Book and I recited it. And Allah will say: you have told a lie. You did not seek it for My pleasure; you learned that knowledge so that you would be called a scholar, so that you would be called a reciter — and you were called that. You got that reward in the world, so now there is nothing for you. And that person will be dragged to the Fire.

Sincerity is very important. It was said: seek knowledge in order to invite people to Allah through it. Your goal should not be to sit with that knowledge or merely to be given a certain title; your goal should be that you benefit yourself and then benefit others. And when you call people to Allah, do so with knowledge — it is not sufficient that you just hype people up; you also have to give them solid ‘ilm, because it is through ‘ilm that you know who Allah is and that you are able to worship Him properly and with ihsan.

And we should never be arrogant about the knowledge Allah has given us. Rather we should be humble. We should not use our knowledge to argue with people, to belittle those who don’t know, to use fancy words and big terms in front of them to make them feel like they are nothing and that we are so knowledgeable and better than them. Nor should we seek knowledge to attract people’s attention. All of these are wrong objectives, and they will be a source of regret and loss and punishment on the Day of Judgment.

Ignorance Is Condemned

Knowledge should be a goal of our lives, something we are constantly seeking, because ignorance is condemned in our deen. Allah says most of the people do not know — and this is not praiseworthy; this is bad. Allah tells us that people have invented equals to Allah, and all of this they do without any knowledge, because when a person does not have knowledge of Allah they begin to associate partners with Him and to say things in ignorance that can lead them to the Fire.

How often people assume things about the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam or about the deen of Allah and then say, “This is in the Qur’an, this is what the Prophet said.” And he warned us that whoever ascribes to me what I have not said, let him occupy his seat in the Fire. And it is of hypocrisy that a person does not understand the deen — about the hypocrites Allah says they do not realise.

When a person is ignorant, they go astray and they mislead others also. Allah says that many people mislead others with their desires without any knowledge — because when you don’t know, the blind will lead the blind. Think about it: if a mother does not have knowledge of the Qur’an and the Sunnah, how is she going to teach her children? She doesn’t know, so her children will not know; she will make mistakes, and her children will make mistakes in her footsteps. Sometimes people say women don’t really need to learn the deen. No — it is essential for women to learn.

And when a person does not have knowledge of the Qur’an and turns away from it, Allah says such a person will have a very difficult, constricted life, and will come on the Day of Judgment blind, and will be under the influence of Shaytan, because Shaytan will be a close companion to him.

Ibrahim ibn ‘Uyaynah said that the first trick of Iblis is that he prevents people from learning knowledge. Why? Because knowledge is light, and when Shaytan puts out the lamps, when people are in darkness, he leads them however he wants and makes them fall and slip however he wants. Think about it: even in your own bedroom, if it is pitch dark you can fall, you can trip over something, because you cannot see. Life without knowledge is like this. And it was said that of the tricks of Shaytan is that he turns people away from reflecting upon the Qur’an, because he knows guidance is obtained by reflecting on it.

Hadith

In the grave, when people are asked who is your Lord, what is your deen, who is your messenger, the believer will give the answers properly, with confidence. But the other will say: “Ah, ah, I do not know — I used to say whatever the people would say.” And he will be told: you neither learned nor did you read.

Chapter Fifty-Four

The Du’as for Knowledge

All of the du’as in this chapter are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. My Lord, increase me in knowledge

Allah teaches this du’a to His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam in the Qur’an. Isn’t this amazing? He was not taught to say “My Lord, increase me in status,” or “increase me in wealth” — but increase me in knowledge. Because the more knowledge you have, the better your life becomes, the more joy you find, the more productive you are, the more you are able to do things with confidence and benefit yourself and others. And what is meant specifically here is the knowledge of the Qur’an, the knowledge of the deen.

It was said: how worrisome and shocking it is, and what a great loss, that a person spends his entire life learning but departs from the world without having understood the truths of the Qur’an. Meaning a person can be a person of knowledge and still be in ignorance — when they only have knowledge of other things and not of the Qur’an. So if we have learned many different things and have degrees in different fields but we don’t know the Qur’an, then this is ignorance. Knowledge of the Qur’an is what removes darkness, what guides a person in this world, and what will benefit a person in the Hereafter.

One of the salaf, when he would recite this ayah, would say: O Allah, increase me in knowledge, and in iman, and in conviction. And one of the scholars said there is no joy of the world that resembles the joy of the Hereafter except the joy of faith and knowledge. Any blessing of this world, when you experience it, brings joy — eating fruit, for example; and in Jannah there will be fruits too, but the fruits of Jannah are very different from the fruit of this world. However, the joy you have with iman — the joy of knowing that Allah hears me, that Allah answers, that Allah helps, that Allah heals — and the joy you get when you learn something, when you learn about one of the attributes of Allah or about something in Paradise: this joy the people of Paradise will also experience.

2. My Lord, expand for me my chest

This is the du’a Musa (‘alayhis salam) made when he was being sent to Fir’awn, and it is related to the previous du’a — because while we ask Allah for increase in knowledge, we should also ask Him for ease in learning, since it is not always easy to learn, and not always easy to find places or opportunities to learn.

“Expand for me my chest” means: expand my chest so that I am able to grasp knowledge, able to grasp the light of knowledge and the light of iman and wisdom, able to contain that in my chest, to understand it and remember it. And when the chest is filled with iman and knowledge, when it has nur in it, then a person is able to bear verbal and physical hardships. Only when the chest is open can a person bear hardship, and only when they can bear hardship are they able to do something. Musa was going to face a very difficult challenge — to go and speak to Fir’awn, that arrogant tyrant. He knew the task was extremely difficult. And you can only have determination when you are confident, and you can only have resilience when you have determination in your heart. How do you get that confidence? When you have iman settled in your heart, and with that iman you have light, wisdom, and acceptance of and surrender to Allah’s commands and decrees.

Remember that it is knowledge that expands the chest, and ignorance that constricts it. When a person does not have knowledge they become impatient, they quit, they give up very quickly; they don’t have much tolerance, they don’t have grit.

“Make my task easy for me” — meaning make the acquiring of knowledge easy for me, and make the task I have been given easy for me. “Untie the knot from my tongue so that they may understand my speech” — because Musa was to go and speak to Fir’awn, and in order to speak to someone you have to speak confidently, in a flow. And this shows us that as we ask Allah for the ability to learn, we should also ask Him for the ability to convey. And conveying doesn’t just mean standing on a huge stage and addressing people; sometimes teaching something means teaching your own child, who is not willing to listen to you or sit with you or is not interested in what you want to teach. So ask Allah to help you in that.

3. O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge

“And I seek refuge with You from knowledge that does not benefit.” Because there are different types of knowledge, and knowledge that does not benefit eventually leads to wrong things and becomes a source of loss and regret. And remember that an idle mind is the devil’s workshop — so if you busy yourself learning something that brings no benefit, Shaytan will use that as an opportunity to misguide you.

4. Beneficial knowledge, good provision, accepted deeds

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this du’a after performing the Fajr prayer, and in it you ask Allah for three things: beneficial knowledge, pure provision, and accepted deeds. If you think about it, we are in need of these three things every single day, and these are three goals we should have every day. He began his day with these three goals, and we should too: today I want to learn something beneficial; whatever I eat, I want to make sure it is pure and halal and good for me; whatever I earn, whatever I bring into my house, I want it to be halal; and whatever deed I do, I want it to be accepted by Allah — because only if it is accepted will it be rewarded and be of benefit to me.

But it is not enough to just have these goals at the beginning of the day. We need to ask Allah for assistance, because both things go hand in hand: prayer and effort. If a person makes this du’a after Fajr and then sleeps all day, and in the evening wakes up and starts watching a three-hour-long movie, then goes out to eat and spends three hours chilling with friends — what did they do? Du’a alone is not enough; with du’a there must also be the use of the means Allah has given us. So every day learn something new, something that will benefit you. There is no break from learning. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam continued to increase in his knowledge until he left this world, and he was instructed to pray for increase in knowledge — which means that no matter how much we have learned, it is not enough.

5. Benefit me with what You have taught me

“And teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge.” If you think about it, we are asking for the same thing in three different ways, and the reason for this is istizadah — you are asking Allah for even more beneficial knowledge.

Another way to understand it: first we say, O Allah, benefit me with what You have taught me — meaning, whatever knowledge You have taught me so far, give me the ability to benefit from it. Because not everyone benefits from what they have learned. The real benefit of knowledge is that a person is able to act upon it, to live by it, to use it. You may have learned the entire Qur’an, but if you are not applying it, you are not benefiting from that knowledge. And then: teach me what will benefit me — meaning, give me more beneficial knowledge in the future also, not knowledge that will harm me or be an argument against me or lead me to sin and disobedience.

Sometimes when you are taking a course and reaching its completion, you wonder: what next? I want to learn more. You should be making this du’a.

6. Refuge from four things

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, from a heart that is not humble, from a soul that is not satisfied, and from a supplication that is not answered.”

Knowledge that does not benefit: knowledge that is useless, or knowledge a person does not bother to apply, or knowledge of random or wrong things that fills the mind and concerns of a person so that they waste their mental energy and their life. Such knowledge can be dangerous; it can lead a person to sin and to waste of life.

A soul that is not satisfied: that no matter what a person gets, they are not happy, they are always greedy for something else. And a supplication that is not answered — why would it not be answered? Because a person is busy committing sins. As in the hadith where a person is in a dishevelled state and calls upon Allah, but why would their du’a be granted when their body is nourished on haram food, their income was haram, their clothing is haram — when they have acquired everything in their life by disobeying Allah? So: O Allah, protect me from becoming such a person, who disobeys You and opposes Your commands, and then their du’a is not granted.

So we should be eager to acquire beneficial knowledge, and we should never be satisfied with the knowledge we already have. Rather we should ask Allah to benefit us with that knowledge and to continue to increase us in knowledge until we die. Ibn ‘Abdul-Barr said that the person who dies while seeking knowledge, this is a sign of a good end — because he is dying in a state of obedience to Allah. So every day of our lives we should be eager to learn something new and beneficial.

Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta.
Chapter Fifty-Five

The Key to Success

Allah tells us in the Qur’an: so seek forgiveness from Him, then repent to Him — indeed my Lord is near and responsive. He is near, so He hears. He is responsive, because He cares and He is able to give us what we are in need of. So we begin our du’as with praise and glorification, and we send salawat on the one Allah was most pleased with, Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and then we make du’a.

We believe that Allah is One, that He has no partner, no equal, no one similar to Him. And belief in tawhid is the key to success in this world and in the Hereafter. If a person does not believe in tawhid and leaves this world, then they can never be successful. And if a person believes in the oneness of Allah, then this faith is a source of relief and comfort for them, a source of ease in this world and in the next life for eternity. This belief in the oneness of Allah is what is going to save a person.

The Prophets Asked for It

Among the du’as of the prophets of Allah is that they would ask Allah to give them the ability to worship Him alone. Ibrahim and Isma’il (‘alayhimas salam), when they built the Ka’bah, prayed: our Lord, make us Muslims in submission to You. Meaning, make us such that we surrender to You, we fully submit to You — and that can only happen when a person knows and believes and realises that Allah is the only one worthy of worship, and so surrenders their entire being, their entire existence, their entire life to Him. Surrender means that they worship only Allah, seek help from only Allah, fear Allah the most, love Allah the most, and place their hope in Him. And they prayed: and from our descendants also, make a nation in submission to You.

Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) also made du’a: O Allah, keep me and my children away from the worship of idols. Isn’t this amazing? He is the one who broke the idols. He is the one who left his people and his family when they threatened to kill him because he was not upon their ways; in fact he called them to the worship of Allah alone, and left them for the sake of Allah. Yet what is he asking for? Protection from the worship of idols, for himself and for his children.

Because a person cannot rely upon themselves and think, “I’m a Muslim, I already believe in Allah, so I’ll be fine, I don’t need to worry about my faith.” No. A person can only have iman when Allah grants them iman, and can only be firm upon faith when Allah grants them that firmness. So we should never take Islam for granted. We should never take our belief in Allah for granted. We should value this treasure and ask Allah to preserve and strengthen it for us.

The Qur’an

Those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.”

If you think about it, Iblis used to be a worshipper of Allah; he used to be among the angels. And what happened to him? His heart changed. He turned away from the worship of Allah, from being a servant to Allah, to becoming an enemy to Allah. So we should never think that because I believe in Allah right now I will be fine forever, or that because I am a Muslim right now I don’t need to worry about the future of my faith. We should always call upon Allah: ya Allah, do not let my heart deviate.

The believers in ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam) said: our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and we have followed the messenger, so register us among the witnesses to truth — and when can that happen? When we die upon the truth. The worshippers of Allah say: our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire — and how can a person be protected from that punishment? When they die upon iman. The people of intellect say: our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying believe in your Lord, and we have believed.

And the magicians of Fir’awn, who believed, understood how precious this light is, so they prayed: our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims in submission to You. Meaning: allow us to die in a state in which we are in submission to You, believing in Your oneness and Your perfection, in obedience to You, with faith in You, trust in You, hope in You, love for You and fear of You. This is surrender.

Chapter Fifty-Six

What Tawhid Really Is

Tawhid is a word we have been hearing since childhood — that we are Muslims, we believe in tawhid. But what exactly is it?

Tawhid literally means to make something one, to unify. And tawhid of Allah means that a person believes in the oneness of God, not in plurality. It is to believe in the unification of all divine attributes in one supreme being.

Different people in the world have different beliefs, and even though many believe in one creator, what mistake do they make? They think that there is someone else who is a child to God, or someone else who has the power to heal, the power to save a person — and people of different religions give such concepts different names. And in some religions there is literally belief in many gods: for each thing in the universe, for each power, for each force, there is a god dedicated to it. There is a god that controls the weather, a god that grants children, a god of beauty, a god of misery. All such beliefs contradict the belief that we have; all of them are false.

Allah is One. There is only one deity worthy of worship, because there is only one perfect being who is the creator of everything, who controls everything, and who possesses all perfect divine attributes — and that being is Allah alone. Allah tells us: and I did not create the jinn and men except that they worship Me. This is tawhid: that we worship only Allah. And the statement of tawhid is la ilaha illallah — there is no god worthy of worship but Allah. This is the central and most important concept in Islam.

There are many religions that claim to be monotheistic but in reality are not — because while they believe that God is the creator, they also believe that someone else has the power to influence the world in the same way God does, or they dedicate their worship to someone other than the creator. This is not pure monotheism.

Ibn al-Qayyim’s Explanation

Ibn al-Qayyim (rahimahullah) says that tawhid is not simply that a person declares there is only one creator, or only one Lord, one king of the entire existence. Rather, tawhid is that a person believes in one God and at the same time dedicates his ultimate love to that one God, and surrenders before Him, and shows humility and weakness before Him. And when there is such love and surrender and humility, this means a person will obey Allah happily, and will be sincere in his worship, and will intend to seek the face and approval of Allah through everything he does — whether he is saying something or doing something, his ultimate goal becomes Allah.

So a person begins to live for the sake of Allah. When they give something, they give it for the sake of Allah. When they withhold something, that is also for the sake of Allah. When they love something, when they dislike something, when they leave something — all for the sake of Allah. Their entire life, their sacrifice, their living and their dying, all of it is dedicated to Allah. A person thinks about Allah, believes in Allah, loves Allah, fears Allah, remembers Allah, eats in the way that is pleasing to Allah, drinks in a way pleasing to Allah, deals with their family in a way pleasing to Allah. It is to live one’s life for the sake of Allah. This is tawhid: that your ultimate concern, your ultimate love, your ultimate fear is of Allah — you fear Him the most, you love Him the most, you are concerned about pleasing Him the most, and everything else becomes secondary.

And when a person has such tawhid in their heart, this tawhid becomes a barrier between them and disobedience to Allah. Every time there is an invitation to disobey Allah, tawhid will stop them: no, you cannot go towards that sin, because Allah knows you are doing it, and Allah — the one whom you love — is not pleased with this. So a person stays away from sins because of Allah.

The Three Categories

  1. Tawhid al-uluhiyyah — that a person believes only Allah is worthy of worship. So their prayer, their charity, their du’a, their ‘umrah, their hajj, any ritual worship, sajdah, sacrifice, all of it is dedicated to Allah alone and no one else.
  2. Tawhid ar-rububiyyah — to believe that Allah alone is in absolute control of the creation, because He is the one who created it and owns it and carries out His decrees in it. There is no creator other than Allah, and no Malik of this universe other than Allah. He is the only creator, the only owner, the only Mudabbir, and it is His command that prevails.
  3. Tawhid al-asma wa’s-sifat — believing that Allah is one and unique in all of His perfect names and attributes. There is no one like Him in His knowledge, in His hearing, in His seeing, in any of His attributes.
Chapter Fifty-Seven

The Message of Every Prophet

Tawhid is so important that every prophet of Allah invited people to the worship of Allah alone. This was their primary, basic message; this is what every prophet began with.
