Nuh (‘alayhis salam) said to his people: O my people, worship Allah, you have no god besides Him. Hud said the same thing to his people. Salih said the same. Shu’ayb said the same. All of these prophets said: worship Allah, you have no god other than Him.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam began with the same thing. At Hajj he was calling people, saying: O people, say la ilaha illallah and you will succeed. We all know there are five pillars of Islam, and the first pillar is to bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah and that Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is His messenger.

Ibn Hajar says that the verses revealed first in the Qur’an were verses that spoke about tawhid, about the oneness of Allah — not just stating that Allah is One, but making it clear that Allah is the only one with absolute power, because you return to Him and on the Day of Judgment you have to answer to Him. All of the verses that talk about the Day of Judgment, about the previous prophets, about the different things Allah has created — what are they establishing? The oneness of Allah. And he says that after that, verses related to the various commands were revealed.

This shows us that the first and most important thing we need to strengthen in ourselves, and to teach our children and our families and our loved ones, is belief in the oneness of Allah.

Our First and Last Obligation

It is our first obligation because when a child is born and begins to understand things, one of the first things you must teach them is la ilaha illallah. Allah says: know that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah. Every child deserves to be taught this, and we must emphasise it.

And it is our last obligation because we learn in a hadith that the person whose last statement is la ilaha illallah will enter Jannah. So if we want to enter Jannah, this is something we should declare at the end of our lives also. Tawhid is relevant from the beginning of our lives to the end.

Knowing Who Allah Is

When a person believes in the oneness of Allah, it means first of all that we should know Allah. It is not enough to just say Allah is One, or that we are Muslims and we believe God is one. Yes, Allah is One — but who is Allah? And you cannot know the oneness of Allah without knowing His perfect names and attributes.

The reason many people turn away from belief in God is that they have a very twisted understanding of who God is. First of all they make the mistake of comparing God to the creation. When they see that people of power become greedy, they think God is the same way. When they see that people of power are not perfect in their decisions and make mistakes, they think God is the same way. And that is not correct. Allah is not like His creation: the creation makes mistakes, Allah does not; the creation fails in their promises, Allah does not — indeed Allah does not break His promise; the creation does not know everything, and Allah knows everything.

Hadith

There is no person who dies while bearing witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah and that Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is the messenger of Allah — and he dies upon that with a heart filled with conviction — except that Allah will forgive him.

So we must have yaqin, conviction in this. We don’t just say “I believe in the oneness of Allah” because this is what we have heard people say and so we repeat the same statement. We should understand the statement, say it from our heart, and accept it as the truth.

Chapter Fifty-Eight

What Believing in Tawhid Means

  • It means we become obedient to Allah. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was asked what Islam is, and he said that you surrender your face to Allah, and that you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is His worshipper and His messenger, and you establish the salah and give the zakat. Allah says: obey Allah and His messenger if you are truly believers.
  • It means we are sincere to Allah. Whatever we do, we do it for the sake of Allah, so that He is pleased with us, knowing that He is watching us, seeking His approval — and therefore we do it correctly and properly. Allah says: worship Allah while making your religion sincere to Him.
  • It means we love Allah the most. Those who believe are most intense in their love for Allah. And we learn in a hadith that none of you can truly believe until Allah and His messenger are more beloved to him than everything else.
  • It means we fear Allah more than we fear people, that we obey all of His commands and refrain from all He has prohibited, and that whenever there are differences we refer to what Allah has revealed.
  • It means we turn to Allah in difficulty — we ask Him for help, we pray to Him, and we rely upon Him, putting our faith and trust in Him, that He is enough. Upon Allah the believers should put their trust.

Being Pleased With Him

When something bad or difficult happens, we recognise that it happened by the will of Allah, and that it cannot go away without the will of Allah. There is good in this; if Allah decreed it, there is goodness in it. So when a person believes in the tawhid of Allah, this means they are also happy with Allah — pleased with Allah, with whatever He has revealed, with all of the commands of Islam, and with whatever He has decreed.

Some people are not happy with the decree of Allah. Why are there men and women? There should only have been one gender. And then they are always drawing differences between men and women, always trying to prove that one is better than the other — or, because one is better than the other, that we need to abolish the different genders and treat everyone the same. As if they are upset with the decree of Allah, as if they think they know better.

Believing in the oneness of Allah means we believe He is perfect in His knowledge, in His wisdom, in His decrees, in what He has created, in what He has legislated.

Hadith

Whoever is pleased with Allah as Rabb, and with Islam as his deen, and with Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam as his Prophet — Paradise is guaranteed for him.

So ask yourself: do I just believe that God is One, or am I pleased with Allah? Because when you recognise someone’s greatness and perfection, then you trust their decisions; and when you trust their decisions, then even if initially you don’t understand, you go along — and eventually you understand. And even if you don’t understand and you see some kind of hardship, you still trust their decision, because you know they did not make a mistake. If this is the case with people whom we love, who are full of mistakes, why can we not have such good thoughts about Allah?

Sadly, so many Muslims say inappropriate things about Allah. Why did Allah create me like this? Why did my family have to be like this? Why did I have to be born in this country, at this time? Why was I created anyway? These statements are all contrary to pure tawhid.

Belief in tawhid means that we are grateful for the favours Allah has bestowed on us: be grateful for the blessings of Allah, if it is only Him that you worship. And it is to believe that nothing happens without the will of Allah — nothing can reach us except what Allah has already decreed for us. So whatever happens in my life, in your life, in the life of your pet, in the life of your loved one, inside your house, outside your house, in your country, in the neighbouring country, in the continent you live in or another, in this world or on Mars or on Jupiter or on the sun, in the Milky Way or elsewhere — nothing happens without the will of Allah. Not a leaf falls except that He knows about it. This is tawhid.

Chapter Fifty-Nine

Shirk, Kufr, and What Tawhid Brings

The opposite of tawhid is shirk. Shirk is to make an equal to Allah, to say that someone else shares in the powers of Allah or in His attributes — to believe that Allah is worthy of worship and that someone else also deserves our worship. Shirk can be in du’a, that a person makes du’a to someone other than Allah. It can be in sajdah, that a person prostrates to someone in a grave. Where tawhid is the ultimate truth, shirk is the ultimate lie, because Allah has no partner.

Allah says: do not set up equals to Allah; indeed your God is one God. Say, all praise is for Allah — because He is the only one worthy of all praise, the only one who is perfectly perfect. He has no child, no equal, no partner. He doesn’t need a helper; He doesn’t experience any weakness because of which He would need a helper.

The Qur’an — the words of Yusuf (‘alayhis salam)

“Are multiple, separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?”

And think about it logically: if there were multiple beings controlling the different things we are in need of, our life would be so hard. One decides that there should be rain, the other decides no, it should be sunny. You see this in a family where parents are not on the same page — the children are constantly suffering; one says do this, the other says do that. In a workplace where two people have equal authority, all the workers suffer for the same reason.

And imagine if we had to go to multiple beings to seek their help. Sometimes you go to one person, you tell them your whole story, your whole situation, and then you make your request — and they say, “Oh, I’m so sorry, I can’t help you, go to that person.” You go to that person, and again you repeat the whole story, the whole situation, the request — and they say, “Go to someone else.” Every time it is so hard, because you have to make them aware of your entire situation. So logically also it does not make sense that there should be multiple gods. Allah is Al-Wahid, the One, and Al-Qahhar — the Irresistible, in the sense that when He decrees, when He decides, no one can resist; He prevails. No one can run away from Allah.

Kufr

The opposite of iman is kufr. Kufr is to deny, and kufr is also to be extremely ungrateful. So where there are people who associate equals with Allah or ascribe a child to Allah, there are others who completely deny the existence of God.

And there is this new trend now: to just “trust the universe.” What is this universe? The universe itself does not function on its own. There is a realisation, when people say trust the universe or ask the universe to grant you good and to work in your favour, that there is someone behind all of this existence, someone who is in control. Why don’t you accept that that someone is Allah? Take His name. Mention His name. Think about it: if someone were to refer to you without ever taking your name, without ever acknowledging your being and your person, are they really being fair to you? Among Muslims also this has become very trendy, to not say the name of Allah and replace it with “the universe” or things like that. And this is wrong.

Kufr is also the opposite of taqwa, because taqwa is to live a life of consciousness — that you are alert and aware that Allah is there, that Allah is watching me, that I have to avoid what displeases Him and do what pleases Him. And kufr is the opposite of gratitude: gratitude is that you acknowledge that Allah gave you all of these things, and kufr is to deny that He is the one who gave you what you have. There is major kufr, which expels a person from Islam, and there is minor kufr also, where a person is arrogant towards the commands of Allah, or refuses to obey, or is ungrateful. We need to refrain from all types of kufr.

What Tawhid Brings

  • Allah guides such a person to the straight path, and brings them out of darkness into light.
  • Allah grants them hayatan tayyibah, a good life in this world. And a good life does not mean a life free of problems and challenges — there will be challenges, trials and difficulties. But their belief in Allah will be like an anchor, something to keep them grounded, so that they don’t despair, don’t get lost, don’t quit. They have a reason to have hope, a reason to be strong. And they have a purpose every day of their lives, regardless of their circumstances. Even if a believer is extremely ill and housebound, unable to go anywhere, having lost their mobility, unable even to get out of bed — every day they wake up they have some goal, something to look forward to. Now I am going to pray salah: they may not be able to make wudu, but they make tayammum, and on their bed they pray. Then they make some dhikr, then they recite some Qur’an. And even if they don’t have the energy for that, maybe they will listen to some Qur’an, or think about the rewards Allah has for those who are patient. They have something to look forward to. This is a good life.
  • Allah preserves and increases their reward in the Hereafter for everything they do, for every little thing.
  • A person is granted firmness and stability in this life, and security in this life and the next.
  • Their iman increases. Ibn al-Qayyim said that the strength of iman in the heart of the believer is in proportion to the strength of tawhid in his heart. And he said that Surat al-Ikhlas is a surah of few letters — only a couple of lines — yet it is equal to a third of the Qur’an, because it contains only tawhid.
  • Their good deeds increase and are accepted, and they receive the help of Allah.
  • Ibn al-Qayyim also said that what purifies the heart and the soul is tawhid. How does it purify a person? It makes them more honest, more sincere, more original — they are not fake, not pretentious; their inside and outside are the same, because they know Allah is watching them here and there, and knows them inside and out.
  • They will have the privilege of receiving the intercession of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and their sins will be forgiven even if they come on the Day of Judgment with the fill of the earth in sins. And ultimately such a person will enter Paradise.

In contrast, when a person associates partners with Allah, this is the greatest injustice, the biggest sin, the sin most hated to Allah, a sin Allah does not forgive, a sin because of which a person’s deeds will be wasted in the Hereafter and carry no worth. Their charity will not be rewarded, their truthfulness will not benefit them, and even if they ask forgiveness a thousand times they will not be forgiven. So we should ask Allah to grant us strength in iman, strength of belief in His oneness — that You alone have absolute power and absolute control; when You give something, no one can stop it, and when You withhold something, no one can bring it.

Chapter Sixty

The Du’as for Strength in Faith

All of these du’as are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. The du’a of Yunus (‘alayhis salam)

“There is no deity except You; exalted are You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.” When he said la ilaha illa anta, that is tawhid al-uluhiyyah, declaring that only Allah is worthy of worship. Subhanaka — O Allah, You are perfect, free of any fault — that is tawhid al-asma wa’s-sifat, declaring your faith in the oneness of Allah in His names and attributes, because in them He is perfect and no one is like Him. And inni kuntu minaz-zalimin — indeed I am of those who have done wrong, and I am in need of Your forgiveness. So here there is ‘ubudiyyah: you are showing servitude to Allah, making Him your ultimate goal, knowing that it is only Allah who can pardon you and only Allah who can bring you out of difficulty.

2. Declaring His oneness a hundred times

“None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, who has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is able to do all things.”

Remember that in some du’as we ask Allah for something, and in others we praise and glorify Him and declare His oneness — and this is also a kind of du’a. Because when we affirm our faith in Allah, that becomes a means of receiving from Him what we are in need of: when we say that Allah has no partner and He owns everything, then He owns what I am in need of; He deserves all praise, meaning I am happy with His decree because He does not make mistakes; and He is able to do all things, meaning He is able to change my circumstances and bring me the healing I am in desperate need of. So sometimes you ask Allah very clearly with your words, and other times you ask indirectly, by declaring His oneness and praising and glorifying Him.

Hadith

The person who says these words a hundred times a day will have the reward equivalent to freeing ten slaves; a hundred good deeds will be recorded for him, a hundred sins will be forgiven, and he will be protected against Shaytan on that day until the evening.

Sometimes a person feels they are under the effect of magic, or that some shaytan is bothering them, or they have constant negative thoughts. So how do you protect yourself? Say these words a hundred times a day.

And this statement is so easy on the tongue. No matter what condition you are in, you can say la ilaha illallah very easily, because all you need to do is move the tip of your tongue. You don’t need to join your lips. You don’t need to use your throat. You don’t have to make your tongue touch the teeth. You are just moving your tongue up and down. So even if you are very unwell and don’t have the energy to move, you can move the tip of your tongue. This is why, when a person is near death and it is obvious they will die very soon, you should encourage them to say la ilaha illallah. If it were not possible for a person to say this, we would not have been encouraged to say it.

We also learn that if a person says this when they go to bed, together with the words of la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah and tasbih and tahmid and takbir, their sins will be forgiven. And when we wake up in the night — sometimes you get startled or you simply wake — we should say these words again; and if after that you make du’a, that du’a is accepted. We should say these words in the morning and evening, and especially after Maghrib we should say the version that includes yuhyi wa yumit — He gives life and causes death — ten times, and Allah will send angels equipped to guard a person against Shaytan; as if you have guards around you to protect you. And when you enter the market, say the version that adds wa huwa hayyun la yamut, and a million good deeds are recorded for you. This is also the best du’a to say on the day of ‘Arafah.

3. Refuge from disbelief and poverty

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. There is no god worthy of worship but You.” This is among the du’as we say in the morning and the evening, three times each.

We are asking Allah to protect us from disbelief — from ever disbelieving in Him, rejecting Him, being ungrateful to Him, not being conscious of Him — and from poverty. Because poverty can also be very dangerous. Sometimes because of poverty a person ends up earning haram, or ends up committing theft. There have been reports of people stealing donation boxes from different masjids, because they know that these days the boxes are full, people go to the masjid a lot and give a lot of charity — so they go from masjid to masjid stealing donation boxes. What kind of hardheartedness is this, that a person in the month of Ramadan, in the days of fasting and the nights of prayer, goes to the masjid to steal? Perhaps it is greed for money; perhaps that greed comes from a place of extreme poverty. Who knows. We should ask Allah to protect us from poverty, because poverty can put a person in fitnah and lead them to haram and to many sins.

4. In worry and sadness

“Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate any partner with Him.” This is a du’a we should make when we are worried, when we are sad. Because it is the declaration that I am not alone — that Allah, the one who is perfect, is my Lord; He knows what I am going through; what I am going through happened with His permission. He is able to bring the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living; He is able to bring the day out of the night and the night out of the day. This is His power. So He is able to change my situation also.

5. From the shirk we don’t notice

Hadith

Abu Bakr (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) was in the company of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and he said: O Abu Bakr, shirk among you is more hidden than the creeping of an ant. Abu Bakr asked: is there a kind of shirk besides associating anything with Allah? He said: by Him in whose hand is my life, shirk is more concealed than the movement of ants. Shall I not teach you something which, if you say it, will eliminate minor and major shirk? Say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know.”

Do you hear ants crawling? You don’t. Just like that, so quietly, in such a subtle way, shirk enters the heart of a person. Because a kind of shirk is to show off — to do something good in order to impress people, to garner their attention and praise, that they should like me, praise me, be happy with me. This is also a form of shirk, because you should be doing things only for the sake of Allah; you want to look good in the eyes of Allah, that He is pleased with you and will praise you before His angels and reward you. That should be our goal. So sometimes we don’t even realise, and such feelings creep into the heart. And we ask Allah for forgiveness: O Allah, forgive me for what I never intended, but which enters my heart and then corrupts my intention and my action.

6. Surrender, trust, and return

“O Allah, it is unto You that I surrender myself, and in You I affirm my faith, and upon You I put my trust, and to You I turn in repentance, and with Your help I contend with my adversaries. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your might — there is no god but You — that You send me astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while the jinn and mankind will die.”

In this du’a we are asking Allah to protect us from being sent astray. Because how often it happens that we hear of a person who was a born Muslim, who went to Islamic school, who memorised Qur’an, who used to attend all the lectures and do so much da’wah — and then what happened? They now say, “I don’t believe.” Never take iman for granted. Ask Allah to protect you from going astray. Ask Allah for increase in guidance. Ask Allah to keep you firm on tawhid, because the person who dies on tawhid will enter Jannah.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam warned us: do not associate any partner with Allah, even if you are cut to pieces or burned. Meaning, even if people physically harm you, forcing you to associate something with Allah, do not do that, no matter what you have to suffer.

We ask Allah to protect us from the tribulations of this world and the next, and to grant us the joy of knowing and understanding His oneness, and the joy of believing in tawhid. And may Allah grant us all sincerity, and protect us from all forms of shirk.

Ameen.
Chapter Sixty-One

Nothing Reaches Us Except What He Wrote

After salah the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say: there is none worthy of worship except Allah alone, who has no partner; His is the dominion, to Him be all praise, and He is able to do all things. There is no power and no strength except with Allah. There is none worthy of worship except Allah, and we worship none but Him. He is the source of blessing and kindness and the one deserving of all good praise. There is none worthy of worship except Allah, and we are sincere in faith and devotion to Him, even though the disbelievers detest that.

In these words we declare that all praise is for Allah, because every blessing, every kindness, every favour comes from Him. He is the only one worthy of worship; He owns everything and is able to do everything; and there is no power and no strength that anyone has except that Allah has granted it to them. He is worthy of praise no matter what He does, no matter what He allows, no matter what He commands and no matter what He decrees. He is always worthy of praise.

Our lives are ever-changing. We go from one stage of life to the next, constantly struggling to adapt to new circumstances. At times it is easy to adapt, and at other times it is incredibly hard. We are not ready for change, yet change happens. We don’t want things to change, but they change. We don’t want our bodies to change, but they change. We would like to avoid certain things from occurring in our lives, but they are beyond our control. Other times we desperately desire some things, we want them to happen, and they never happen.

The Qur’an

Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us. He is our protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.

We believe that nothing reaches us of good or bad except that Allah has already written it for us. So everything happens by the decree of Allah, and in our ups and downs we are not alone, because He is our master, our protector, our helper, the one who ensures our worldly and religious well-being. So whatever Allah has decreed for us is good for us, because He is our mawla, and He will help us.

We put our trust in Allah — trust that whatever He decreed in our lives is for a wisdom, that it is a command issuing from between His justice and His mercy. So we trust the decree of Allah, that there is good in it, and we trust that He will bring good out of what has happened — because whatever He has decreed, He has decreed it for us, not against us. And the person who puts their trust in Allah, Allah is enough for them; Allah will not fail that person. But this is only for those who believe: those who believe in Allah and in His divine decree.

At times it is easy to think like this — yes, whatever has happened has happened by the decree of Allah, there is good in it, Allah will bring something good out of it, this is coming from His justice and His mercy. At those times we are able to process our feelings. But other times we struggle. We have difficulty accepting what has happened. We have trouble understanding what good could possibly come out of it.

Chapter Sixty-Two

The Four Stages of Qadar

The terms qada and qadar are used to refer to divine decree. Qada means to decide or to decree something. Qadar is to determine the measure of something — so qadar is the measure Allah has determined for each creature: the measure of its lifespan, how long it is supposed to live, where it is going to be born, what size it is going to be, how it is going to find its food, how much sustenance it will receive. All of this is measured; the measure of each is determined by Allah. And al-qada is the decree of Allah that He has brought into existence.

To believe in qadar is to believe in Allah’s perfect knowledge, in His absolute will, and in His qudrah, His absolute power which prevails over the entire creation. We believe that Allah has full and perfect knowledge of what He is commanding, creating and legislating, and of all His creatures; that nothing happens without His will; and that He is able to do all things. Nothing escapes His power, His knowledge and His will.

And to believe in qadar is part of our iman; it is one of the pillars of faith. Sometimes we hear statements like “your fate is in your hands” or “you create your own destiny.” If such statements are meant to emphasise that you have free will and must use it, that is understandable. But to say them in order to declare that you have complete power over what happens in your life — that is not true. Because as Muslims we believe that nothing happens without the will of Allah. At times we want something to happen and we are trying to make it happen, but it doesn’t happen, because Allah has not willed it. At other times we are trying our best to avoid something, and we are not able to avoid it, because Allah has willed that it should happen.

The Qur’an

“Indeed, all things We created with predestination.” “And ever is the command of Allah a destiny decreed.” “Allah has created everything and determined it with precise determination.”

Before Anything Comes Into Existence

  1. ‘Ilm — His knowledge. We believe in the absolute and perfect knowledge of Allah, that He encompasses everything in knowledge, and that there is nothing even equivalent to the size of an atom in the skies or the earth that can escape His knowledge. So before something comes into existence, Allah knew about it. What is happening today, what you ate for suhoor, whether you are fasting or not, what you did and what you are going to do — it is happening today, but Allah had knowledge of it before this day came into existence. He knows what was, what is, and what will be. He knows what exists and also what does not exist; and if something were to happen, what would happen; all the possibilities, all the probabilities. Sometimes we say things like, “This shouldn’t have happened,” or we ask, “What if such and such had happened?” Allah knows what is, and He also knows all the what-ifs. So trust His knowledge. Sometimes certain things happen that are very difficult for us, and we think it was a mistake, a glitch, something that should not have happened. No — Allah knew about it, and it was going to happen.
  2. Kitabah — the writing. We believe that Allah has recorded the decrees of the entire creation in al-Lawh al-Mahfuz. Before something happens, it is already written. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught us that the first thing Allah created was the pen, and He instructed it to write everything that is going to happen. So whatever is happening today in your life — Allah did not just know about it; He also had it written. It was pre-planned, decided, recorded.
  3. Mashi’ah — His will. Everything that happens, happens by the will of Allah. Whatever He wills occurs, and whatever He does not will shall never occur, and there is nothing outside of His will. Whether a leaf falls, or someone is born, or there is a fire, or someone wins a huge prize, or someone gets into an accident or survives — anything that happens, whether painful or a source of joy, easy or difficult, happened by the will of Allah, meaning Allah allowed it to occur. If He had not willed it, it would never have occurred. Even your intention to do something happens when Allah allows you to have that intention. Our will is under the will of Allah; it is not independent of it. Because if it were independent, then we would be saying His power is limited, that someone could challenge His power — and how could someone be equal to Him?
  4. Khalq — His creation. Allah is the creator of everything; there is nothing that exists except that it is His creation, and He has absolute power over it all. And this includes the actions of people also: Allah created you and also your actions, because you would not be able to do anything unless Allah allowed you and made those actions possible for you.
Chapter Sixty-Three

Believing In It

Believing in al-qadar is very important. Many among the Muslims, when they are not clear on the matter, begin to say strange things, and they begin to argue about qadar and to reject it. We should not argue about qadar, and we should not reject it either. If we don’t understand it, if we don’t have knowledge about it, at least we should say: I believe in it, even though I don’t fully grasp the concept. Because Allah said in the Qur’an that He has created everything according to a decree — and when Allah has mentioned this, who are we to reject it?

Hadith

A slave of Allah shall not believe until he believes in four things: the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is the messenger of Allah; that Allah sent the Messenger with the truth; that he believes in death and in resurrection after death; and that he believes in al-qadar.

Hadith

There is a reality to everything, and a servant cannot attain the reality of iman until he knows that whatever has reached him could not have missed him, and whatever has missed him could not have reached him.

Meaning: until a person grasps this concept, they haven’t really experienced what real faith is. What has reached me could not have avoided me, and what has avoided me could never have reached me.

We learn that the person who denies al-qadar — Allah does not accept any deed from him, neither obligatory nor voluntary. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar would swear an oath by Allah and say that were you to spend in support of Allah’s cause an amount of gold equivalent to Mount Uhud, Allah would not accept it from you until you believe in divine decree. So it is a prerequisite for the acceptance of good deeds.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam expressed his fear: what I fear the most for my ummah of later times is three things — that they will believe in the stars, meaning that the stars affect their lives and their destiny and their future (and no matter how much societies have modernised and people have become materialistic, somehow people still have faith in stars determining their fate); that they will deny divine decree; and the oppression of their rulers. And we see all three of these things today.

Fifty Thousand Years Before

We learn in a hadith that Allah inscribed the decree of the entire creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Imagine: fifty thousand years before the sky and the earth were created. And remember that Adam (‘alayhis salam) was not sent to the earth the day the earth was created; the earth was there from before, because Allah said He was going to place a khalifah on it, and a khalifah is someone who succeeds someone, who comes after someone. So there was creation that inhabited the earth even before the first human being was sent. Imagine then: way before that, fifty thousand years before even the earth and the sky were created, Allah had the decrees of the creation recorded in al-Lawh al-Mahfuz.

We also learn that Allah has decreed for every creature five things: his lifespan, his provision, his actions, and whether he will be of those who are successful or those who are losers — meaning those who will go to Paradise or those who will go to Hell. And being written from before does not mean that people have no will; people have will, but it is under the will of Allah.

Hasan al-Basri would say that Allah created the creation and created them according to a certain measure; He decreed their terms according to a certain measure, and decreed their sustenance and their trials and their well-being and their safety. Everything that happens in the life of a creature is already decreed. So you drink a sip of coffee and enjoy it — this was written from before. You drink a sip of coffee and burn your tongue — that was also written from before. Every little and big thing about you was written from before.

We learn that a person can only attain of the world what is already written for him. There is no created soul except that Allah is its creator — so if a person has children, that was already written; if a person does not have children, that was also written. Even illness that a person experiences was written from before. Even the weakness a person experiences, or the intelligence they have been granted, or a person’s colour of skin — all of this is qadar.

And if it was decreed, that means there is no avoiding it. So why get upset with it? Why be angry about it? Because if we are angry and upset, that is not going to change anything; it is just going to cause us to be more stressed out. Think of it this way: if a certain process has to run on a machine — for example you initiated an update on your computer — then once the update begins it has to go through a certain process, and the entire process is written from before, the code and everything. You cannot interrupt it; you can only make changes after it is done.

Ubayy ibn Ka’b and the man who was confused

A man came to Ubayy ibn Ka’b and said: I am confused about qadar, so tell me something by means of which Allah may remove the confusion from my mind. Ubayy replied: were Allah to punish everyone in the heavens and in the earth, He would do so without being unjust to them; and were He to show mercy to them, then His mercy would be much better than their actions. Were you to spend in support of Allah’s cause an amount of gold equivalent to Mount Uhud, Allah would not accept it from you until you believed in divine decree and you knew that what has come to you could not have missed you and what has missed you could not have come to you. And were you to die believing anything else, you would enter Hell.

The man then went to ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said the same thing; and to Hudhayfah, who said the same thing; and to Zayd ibn Thabit, who said the same thing. Look at how strong the faith of the companions was in al-qadar.

So first of all: believe in Allah’s perfect knowledge and His right to execute His will, whatever it may be. Trust Allah’s judgment, because He is the creator, the only one worthy of worship; He has no equal; He knows everything; He does not make mistakes; He is ever wise, ever just, and extremely merciful. Sometimes we have difficulty accepting or understanding — this is so terrible, how could Allah let this happen, why did Allah do that? We should stop questioning Allah and begin questioning ourselves. Why did I say something so evil? Why did I think something so evil? Why did I not do this good thing? Question yourself, because you are going to be held accountable. No one is going to hold Allah accountable, because He is the supreme power, He is Al-Malik who owns everything. He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.

So never question Allah, never raise objections to His will or His decree. This is the foundation of belief in al-qadar: that Allah knows what He is doing, and He is not unfair.

Chapter Sixty-Four

Every Decree Has Wisdom

Everything happens by the will of Allah, it is decreed — and Allah did not make a mistake in allowing it to happen. If a person is born with a certain deformity, that was not an accident on the part of Allah; it was decreed. If a person is born at a time or in a place where there are many dangers, again that is not a mistake on the part of Allah.

And something that may appear to be evil or harmful — we do not know the hidden mercy that is in it. Because first of all, Allah does not make a mistake. Secondly, Allah does not do anything that is useless: did you think We created you in play, without a reason? We did not create the sky and the earth and what is between them in play. Thirdly, Allah is not unjust to anyone — not to one person, not to one creature, not at one instance; He is free from injustice.

There Is Always Good In It

Every decree Allah has decreed has something good in it. Allah does not allow something that is pure evil.

  • There are matters that are all good, and everything associated with them is good.
  • There are matters which have good in them but also a little evil associated with them. For example, a mother who is very kind to her children, very good to them — but there are also those times when she is angry with them. Not all the time, but those moments. So the children receive the love of the mother, the care, the affection, everything — and at the same time they also receive a little bit of hurt.
  • There are matters in which there is more evil and less good. For example the existence of Shaytan: yes, there is a lot of evil associated with that, but there is also some good. How? When Shaytan causes a person to slip, yes, something bad happened, a person disobeyed Allah and incurred a sin — but then they turn back to Allah and repent, and when they turn back they draw closer to Him, they recognise their weakness, and next time they are more alert.
  • And pure evil does not exist. Allah does not create or legislate or allow something that is pure evil or harmful for His slaves, because He is Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim.

This means that when something harmful or painful happens, we trust that there is good in it. Sometimes we see the good and it is obvious; other times we don’t see it yet, but it is there and it is going to come about.

We learn about the young boy who was killed in the story of Musa and Khidr: if he had lived on, he would have involved his righteous parents in defiance and unbelief. Because some children push their parents to commit kufr, they lead their family into disbelief, they are so strong in their kufr that they lead their parents into it also. So Allah gave them another child in his place, one who was more pure than the first and who was good to his parents — and the ulama say that child was actually a daughter.

And the mother of Maryam wanted a son; when a daughter was born she began to apologise — but Allah knew better of what she gave birth to. There was a wisdom in giving a daughter and not a son, because that daughter, Maryam, was going to become the mother of ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam); she had to give birth to a child without a father, a miraculous birth, and a boy could not do that.

Hadith

There are two things which the son of Adam dislikes. He dislikes death — but death is better for the believer than tribulation. And he dislikes the shortage of wealth — but the shortage of wealth is easier in terms of the reckoning.

Meaning: if the believer continues to live and continues to suffer test after test, what is easier? And on the Day of Judgment, when a person has to answer for all the blessings they enjoyed — imagine if they enjoyed many, many blessings; the reckoning is going to be longer and tougher. But if they had little wealth in the world, their reckoning is going to be easier.

So whenever something painful and hard happens, remind yourself: don’t think it is bad for you, it is good for you. Say: there is good in this, insha’Allah Allah will bring something good out of this; it appears to be terrible, but there is good in it.

Sufyan al-Thawri said that what a person dislikes is actually better for him than what he likes for himself, because what he does not like makes him turn towards Allah and supplicate, and what he likes makes him kindle a fire for himself. For instance, you like to go to the mall and you are able to go — so you go and look at things, maybe things which are not decent; maybe you waste a lot of time; maybe you waste some money; maybe you listen to things which are not appropriate; maybe you get impressed by someone committing a sin. You are going to a place where Shaytan is very active. So you like it, but it is actually spiritually bad for you. Now imagine you are trying to go and you are not able to, because your husband calls and you have to pick up the children and take them to their after-school programmes because he has to go somewhere — and there goes your evening. You don’t like that, but what you don’t like turns out to be good for you, because when you are put in a situation you don’t like, you turn towards Allah, you recognise your weakness, you realise you are in need of help.

An incident the teacher related

I used to live in an apartment building, and we had to go somewhere early in the morning on a weekend. I remember that morning thinking, why do I have to go on a weekend morning? But I went anyway. And a couple of hours later I checked my phone and I had about thirty missed calls, because my neighbour was calling me: there was a fire on the floor beneath ours, in an apartment very close to mine. So Allah protected me and my family.

Sometimes we become hasty and get annoyed — why do I have to do this, why do I have to go there, why did this have to be the case? But when Allah has decreed something for you, accept it, because you never know what Allah is protecting you from, something more dangerous. Allah’s wisdom is vast; He knows what is good for the slaves better than they know themselves. And tomorrow on the Day of Judgment they will be grateful to Allah for all the trials He sent their way, because they will see all the reward they received through those trials — just as a child, after growing up and developing intelligence, is grateful to his parents and his teachers for teaching him discipline. When you grow up you think about how your parents taught you, how your teachers were tough on you, and you are so grateful that they disciplined you, because if they had not, who knows what would have happened to you. So through trials Allah disciplines us. Trials are a mercy.

Chapter Sixty-Five

Being Pleased With It

We should be pleased with Allah’s decree, and never upset with Allah. No matter how painful a decree is, don’t ever be upset with Him. He cares about you; He is affectionate and kind to you before something painful happens and also afterwards; He is merciful to you.

Hadith

A man asked the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam which deed is best. He said: to believe in Allah and affirm Him, and to strive in His way. The man said: I want to know something easier than that. He said: pardon and patience. The man said: I want something even easier. He said: do not blame Allah in regard to anything He has decreed for you.

This means: don’t say why, Allah, why did You allow this to happen; ya Allah, why did You give me this; ya Allah, why did You not give me this. Don’t blame Allah, don’t question Him, don’t be upset with Him.

We learn in a hadith: be pleased with what Allah has decreed for you and you will be the richest of all people — because you will have contentment. And whoever is pleased with what Allah has decreed for him, Allah will bless him in it and expand that blessing for him; and whoever is not pleased with Allah, that person will not be blessed in what he is given.

Sometimes people are very unhappy about the child they have — why do I have another daughter, another girl, another boy. Don’t be upset; this is Allah’s decree, that you should have two daughters or three or five or six, or all boys, or all girls, or no children. Be pleased with what Allah has decreed for you.

This doesn’t mean you are not allowed to feel sad. If Allah has decreed that you should not have children, it doesn’t mean you are not allowed to feel sad. And if Allah has decreed that you should have children, that means in a sense you cannot have your own life — a mother, once she has her children, it is as if she has signed up for life to do the dishes, to be the designated house chef, the designated maid, the designated chauffeur. And you wonder: these are not things I signed up for; I just wanted a cute baby and I thought that was enough, but I have these responsibilities now for life. So yes, sometimes when you compare yourself to others you feel a little sad, you feel left out, you wonder about goals you had and whether you will ever be able to accomplish them. You are allowed to feel sad — like the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam felt sad when his son Ibrahim died. He was crying, he was sad, but he said: we will only say what pleases our Lord.

The Peak of Faith

It was said that the peak of faith is in four things: that you are patient with Allah’s decree; that you are pleased with Allah’s decree and remain pleased with it — because sometimes we are patient initially, and we say the right things initially, but then after a month, after five years, we get impatient and unhappy; that you are sincere in putting your trust in Allah, because sometimes people say they have tawakkul but they don’t really show real tawakkul; and that you surrender to Allah in obedience, no matter what happens.

Hadith Qudsi

Allah says: I am as My servant thinks I am.

So he can think about Allah whatever he wants, and it is up to you: if you want to think good, you will find Allah good with you; if you want to think negative and evil, then that is what you will find.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam visited a man who was sick, and it was his habit when visiting someone sick to say: la ba’s, tahurun insha’Allah — no harm, this is a purification if Allah wills. And when he said that, the man said: you say it is a purification? No, this is a fever boiling in the body of an old man, and it will lead him to the grave. The man thought it was terrible, it was evil. Sometimes it happens that when we are experiencing some illness we like to blow it out of proportion and present it as something terrible and way worse than it actually is. So the man said these words, and the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: then may it be as you say. If that is what you expect, that is what will happen.

So how are you thinking about Allah? When something bad happens, think good. Think that insha’Allah this will be a purification — because no fatigue or disease or sorrow or sadness or hurt or distress befalls a Muslim, even the prick of a thorn, but that Allah expiates some of his sins because of it.

Four Things to Avoid

  • Don’t blame others. When things don’t go as we wanted, we want someone to blame so that we can come to terms with what happened: it is his fault, it is her fault, it is because of these children, because of such a husband, because of such a mother-in-law. We want targets to blame, and this is not right. This doesn’t mean that when someone has messed up you don’t let them recognise their fault — you do. But ultimately realise that the harm that reached you through people was also decreed by Allah. And don’t always look for people to blame, because then you will be upset with people all the time, and you will burn bridges and say and do things you will regret later, and your relationships will be affected.
  • Don’t say “if only.” The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told us that if something hits you, do not say “if only I had done such and such, then such and such would have happened,” because “if only” opens the door for the work of Shaytan. When you say if only she had not come, if only he had not advised me to do this, if only you had listened to me — do you think the other person will stay happy with you? They are going to get upset, they are going to get hurt, there is going to be an argument, and the argument is going to escalate, and you are going to put yourself in greater difficulty. Rather say: this was Allah’s decree, and whatever Allah wanted happened.
  • Don’t use qadar as an excuse. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam once visited ‘Ali and Fatimah and told them to pray in the night. ‘Ali said that our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He wants, we will get up and pray. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam did not like that response. Yes, only if Allah wills, you will be able to do something — but that doesn’t mean you always make qadar an excuse and don’t do anything yourself. When Allah allowed you to wake up in the night, and when Allah allowed you to receive the reminder, then it is your turn to act.
  • Don’t argue about qadar. Some people without knowledge like to discuss the topic. We learn in a hadith how the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam became angry with the companions at one point when they were arguing about qadar; in another narration he said: when divine decree is mentioned, refrain from speaking about it. And don’t think you know the future of someone, or their destiny, saying things like “Allah will never forgive them” or “Allah will definitely reward them.” You don’t know the future; it is only Allah who knows. Recognise your limits and stop there.

When a person believes in qadar and surrenders to the decree of Allah, their tawhid becomes pure, they have more conviction in the oneness of Allah, they have stronger determination, they have more tawakkul, they have contentment in their heart — and such a person is led to Paradise.

Chapter Sixty-Six

The Du’as for Contentment

All of these du’as are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. There is no might and no power except with Allah

These are words we should repeat very often, because they are a treasure of Paradise. When a person says them they are surrendering themselves to Allah: only then can I do something, only then can I avoid something, because everything is by the decree of Allah. This is one of the doors of Paradise. And this is more than just a statement we say; we should believe in this fact. When a person says it, a tree is planted for them in Paradise, and the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam advised saying it frequently.

2. Sufficient for me is Allah

“Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no god except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.” Sometimes you wonder about your future; sometimes you fear for your children; sometimes you are anxious about circumstances not in your control; you get worried about what people say, what people might say, what people might do, how things might change. All these fears are real. So remind yourself: Allah is there, Allah is enough for me, and whatever Allah has decreed for me is good for me.

3. Indeed we belong to Allah

“Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.” When something upsetting happens, when there is a loss, keep repeating these words. We belong to Allah; His will prevails over us. He decided that I should experience such a loss; He decreed that I should lose this person or this thing in my life; He decreed that I belong to Him, and He is allowed to make that decree, because He is the owner. And I am going to return to Allah — I am not going to just live on my own; I have to die, I have to return to Him, and He will show me the consequences of my actions, my choices, my words. So in hope of good reward I am going to be patient right now; I am going to be pleased with Allah’s decree.

4. I am pleased with Allah as my Lord

“I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam as my Prophet.” These words are very powerful. Painful things are part of life; Allah has already told us that we will surely be tested with something of fear, hunger, loss of wealth and loss of lives. Life is ever-changing. So with every change, with every test, express your happiness with Allah: what You have legislated is within Your power, this happened by Your permission, You don’t make mistakes, You are not unjust. Say these words out loud sometimes, and sometimes say them to yourself, so that you have contentment with what Allah has decreed. And when a person says them, they are granted happiness with the decree of Allah.

5. Contentment after the decree

“I ask You for contentment after the decree has been passed.” Meaning: after You bring about a decree, I ask You to grant me happiness with it also, so that I am not upset, not angry. Because sometimes it is difficult to accept certain things, difficult to accept certain losses, so that you are not able to move past it; you are stuck in your grief. You are allowed to grieve, but being stuck in it does not allow you to move on — and moving on does not mean you have to forget what happened or the pain you experienced; it means there are still things to do in life.

6. The last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah

We have been taught to recite them every night, and the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said the one who recites them, they will be enough for him. “Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred” — because sometimes something bad happens and you forget that you should not say negative things, and you realise only after a few moments; so you ask Allah: forgive me, because I forgot, forgive me, because I made a mistake. “Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us” — because sometimes you hear about very difficult trials people have experienced, so you ask Allah to protect you from such burdens. “Our Lord, burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear” — only decree for me what I am able to bear. “And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us; You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.”

7. Refuge from severe calamity and an evil fate

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the difficulties of severe calamity, from being overtaken by wretchedness, from an evil fate, and from the malicious joy of enemies.” There is a calamity, and then there is the difficulty that comes with a severe calamity. For example, if a person is sick, they are sick in their body — but then there is the difficulty that comes along with it: sometimes it means you are no longer able to work; sometimes your relationship with your spouse is affected, your relationship with your children is affected, your mind is affected, your work is affected, and you are struggling so much emotionally and mentally. So ask Allah to protect you from that, and from an evil fate — a fate that turns out badly for you — and don’t let people who dislike you have the chance to be happy because of your suffering.

8. Bless me in what You have decreed

“And bless me in what You have bestowed, and save me from the evil of what You have decreed; indeed You decree and none can decree over You.” This is part of the du’a of qunut in witr. So anything bad that has been decreed — ya Allah, protect me from it, make it good for me, make it easy for me, turn it away from me.

9. From the decline of His blessing

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the decline of Your blessing, the changing of Your protection, the suddenness of Your punishment, and from all things that cause Your anger.” You have granted me protection and safety, and all of a sudden that changes — ya Allah, protect me from all that.

10. None can withhold what You give

“O Allah, no one can withhold what You expand, and no one can expand what You contract; no one can bring near what You put far, and no one can put far what You bring near; no one can give what You withhold, and no one can withhold what You give. O Allah, expand for us of Your blessings and Your mercy and Your favour and Your sustenance.” And at the end you seek refuge in Allah from the evil of what He has given and also from the evil of what He has withheld — protect me from all evil, protect me from all harm.

So we should ask Allah to grant us contentment with His decree, to help us surrender to it, to accept it, to be pleased with it. And when we are pleased with it, only then can we take the next steps: use the means Allah has provided, put our trust in Him, be patient with His decree, remember Him, and not exhibit any displeasure with what He has decreed.

Ameen.
Chapter Sixty-Seven

After the Right of Allah

Of the things we should be asking Allah for is that He bestow mercy on our parents. Our du’as should include du’as for our parents.

The Qur’an — Surat al-Isra

“And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age while with you, say not to them a word of disrespect and do not repel them, but speak to them a noble word. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say: my Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.”

After the right of Allah and the right of His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, the people who deserve the most from us are our parents. In this ayah Allah gives us a final decree, a ruling — meaning this is not something we have a choice about. Your Lord has decreed, first, that you should not worship anyone except Him; and second, good treatment to parents.

And this shows us the sanctity of being good to one’s parents — how sacred an act this is, that it is a religious deed, because Allah has obligated it. This is not an ordinary good deed; it is an obligation, just as it is an obligation on us to worship Allah. Both are mentioned in the same ayah, and when both commands are given in the same sentence, it means both are important.

What Ihsan to Parents Includes

Ihsan with one’s parents is to treat them in an excellent way — not only with your good, kind words, but also with your beautiful actions, your acts of service. Every such word or deed that brings your parents something of benefit or some joy or happiness is a form of ihsan. And ihsan includes both things: that on the one hand you treat them well, and on the other hand you protect them from your harm — that you do your best not to accidentally or deliberately hurt them, or do something to annoy or upset them.

Ibn al-Jawzi explains that ihsan with parents is:

  • To obey them in what they command, as long as it is not something forbidden or wrong.
  • To give preference to their command over voluntary deeds — so if your parents have asked you to do something and you wish instead to do something good but voluntary, you give preference to the command and the wish of your parents over your own.
  • To stop from what the parents forbid you from.
  • To spend on them from your own lawfully earned money.
  • To fulfil their wishes, and to strive hard to serve them with your hands and your feet — to run their errands, do their dishes, prepare food for them, physically work in order to make their life easy.
  • To be respectful towards them and show proper adab: not to be rude or harsh, not to treat them the way you treat a friend, or someone younger than you, or someone who doesn’t understand much.
  • To have heba in one’s heart for them — such utmost respect that you do not raise your voice at them, and do not look at them with your eyes fully open. Meaning: do not give them the look, the way you might to a child, when they say or do something upsetting. That is contrary to ihsan.
  • Not to address them by their name, but by a fitting expression or title used in your culture — mother, father, dad.
  • Ibrahim ibn Adham says that part of it is that you walk behind them, not in front of them as if you are leading and they have to catch up with you.
  • And to be patient over anything they do which you dislike. Because parents are human, and sometimes their preferences are different, their upbringing was different, the part of the world they grew up in and the culture they are accustomed to is different, and according to that they may say or do something you find strange or even dislike. At that time be patient, because parents are not deliberately trying to annoy or harm or hurt you; it is just what they are used to. And sometimes when they are tired or upset or stressed about something, because they feel very safe and comfortable around you, they are able to express themselves completely — and sometimes that comes across to us as rude. Bear that with patience.
Chapter Sixty-Eight

Not Even a Word of Disrespect

Allah says: if they reach old age with you. Before, you used to be with your parents and you were in need of them; now they are with you, because of old age and weakness, and they are in need of you. They took care of you, and now they are in need of being taken care of.

And in that situation, do not even say uff to them. Uff is any expression of speech that is harsh or disliked; originally the word refers to something detestable or dirty — the dirt under the nails. It is used to show disgust, dislike or contempt, and at times annoyance and frustration.

So Allah tells us: do not even say uff. Meaning yes, there will be times when you feel annoyed or frustrated — that you have been working so hard to do things the way they like and yet they find a reason to criticise; or that their needs never end; or that you cannot have time to yourself; or that you always have to attend to them, one thing after another; or that you have to not answer back. You feel frustrated. But Allah tells us: do not show that frustration, do not show that annoyance, do not even say it with the two-letter word uff.

And think about it: if uff is not allowed, then what is more than that is not allowed at all. How can it be acceptable that a person begins to yell at their parents, raise their voice, and talk to them as if they were talking to a criminal or someone completely ignorant?

And Allah says: do not repel them, do not rebuke them. This shows us the status of parents — that children are not allowed to tell off their parents, not allowed to speak to them harshly, not allowed to rebuke them, ever. Even if parents are doing something the children dislike or get annoyed with, as children we are not allowed to raise our voice or rebuke them.

So we are being taught here: neither show little frustration nor a lot. Do not say small words out of being passive aggressive, nor be openly aggressive or lose it with your parents.

A Noble Word

Qawlan karima is speech that is soft, gentle, respectful and modest — speech that shows a person has adab, that they are speaking very carefully, selecting their words with care and attention, not speaking freely and carelessly. Mujahid explains that it means not to address your parents by their name or kunyah, but to say something like ya abati — O my dear father.

And some said this means that just as your parents did not feel or show any disgust in cleaning you when you were little, but treated you very lovingly, you should treat them the same way, without showing any disgust and only lovingly. Think about it: when a mother or father is changing their baby’s diaper in the middle of the night, they are not going to yell at the baby — did you really have to dirty your diaper at this time? Do you not understand what time of night it is? Do you not realise how tired I am? Why do you have to dirty so many diapers? Do you understand how expensive they are? Parents don’t say such things to their babies. Yet when children have to take care of their elderly parents, they begin to get annoyed over every little thing, and they remind their parents of the favours they are doing, and constantly show frustration and disgust. We are taught here that whatever you do for them, do it lovingly, and use speech that is very respectful. Do not let them feel that they are a burden on you, that you have done so much for them, that you are so tired looking after them, that it is becoming very expensive taking care of them.

Lowering the Wing of Humility

This has been interpreted in two ways. Some say it means you should guard and protect your parents and look after them, just as birds look after their young. When birds are looking after their chicks, they don’t just spread out their wings and lift them; they lower their wings onto their young in order to cover them fully. There are videos showing an eagle sitting in its nest completely covered in snow, and then it gets up and shakes off the snow, and you can see the eggs and the chicks it was protecting. This is what parents do for their children: they bear cold and physical hardship and pain and even danger in order to provide comfort and ease and safety to their children. So we should treat our parents the same way: protect them, guard them, defend them, look out for their well-being and safety. How often it happens that friends make fun of their friends’ parents, and a lot of people don’t have the courage to defend their parents — in fact they get carried along and make fun of their parents with their friends. We are being taught the exact opposite.

The other interpretation is: be humble before your parents. Because when a bird flies and rises high it spreads its wings, and when it needs to descend it lowers them. So lowering one’s wings before one’s parents means showing humility before them. And some say that in this is an indication that the more humble you are before your parents, the more Allah will raise you in the heavens. Use your wings of humility, lower yourself before your parents, and Allah will take you high, will give you success and good mention and status — but it begins with how you treat your parents.

Chapter Sixty-Nine

Why They Deserve It

We are taught to make du’a for our parents, and this shows us that we can never return the favour our parents have done for us. We can never reciprocate, and no matter how hard we try we will still fall short, because we cannot do for them what they did for us. Even when we are in a situation where we have to help our parents and provide them personal care, our feelings are not the feelings our parents had when they were looking after us. So we can only make du’a, and ask Allah to give our parents what they deserve, and to take care of them and be merciful towards them.

And what we are asking Allah for is that He bestow His mercy on our parents — and rahmah includes all good things with respect to deen and dunya. When you ask Allah to show mercy to your parents, you are asking Him to bless them in their deen, to forgive them, to accept their good deeds, to give them good rewards; you are asking Him to grant them good health and well-being and ease in life; and rahmah includes the benefits of the Hereafter: ya Allah, forgive them, admit them into Paradise, raise their ranks. Praying for mercy for your parents is the best thing you can do, because it is very comprehensive.

And we are especially taught to say: have mercy on them just as they raised me when I was little. Meaning: just as they showed me mercy by raising me, You show mercy to them in the same way. And kama rabbayani saghira also means because — because they raised me, because they looked after me, and I am not able to reciprocate, so ya Allah, You show mercy to them, You reward them, You make up for what I fall short in. Here we are reminded of our infancy, our childhood, our weakness, our complete dependency on our parents — when we were in need of protection, care and love, and our parents provided that to us.

And parenting is something very hard. Sometimes in your life you see your parents struggle with your younger siblings — so don’t just watch them struggle, don’t just feel pity; make du’a for them: ya Rabb, have mercy on them, make it easy for them. Sometimes you see your parents struggling with some illness or with their work — don’t just feel pity, don’t just feel that regret in your heart that you were not able to do such and such for them; channel that energy into making du’a. Because when Allah envelops them with His mercy, then all of their affairs will become easy. This doesn’t mean you don’t do anything yourself; in this ayah we are taught both things — do good to your parents, and also make du’a for them. Both are necessary.

Abu Hurayrah (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) and his mother

He went to his land in al-‘Aqiq, and when he entered it he raised his voice, because his mother was far, and said: peace be upon you, mother, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. She replied: and peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. And then, before he even reached her, as he was walking towards her, he said: may Allah have mercy on you as you raised me when I was a child. And she replied: and may Allah repay you well and be pleased with you, as you were dutiful towards me when I was old.

Look at how he is talking to his mother. A lot of times men think they don’t have to speak nicely with their mother; in fact when they go to see her they expect to be served as if they are still a five-year-old child who needs to be fed. Grow up already. You are going to see your mother, you are spending time with her — you should be serving her, not expecting that she should be serving you. And if she brings some food you are not a fan of, you grumble and fuss. What kind of behaviour is this? Of course mothers will want to feed their children even if their child is forty or fifty years old, and that is fine — but you should not go to your mother expecting that she has to do everything for you. You should go with the intention that you are going to serve her and be good to her. And begin with your good words.

Sometimes when people go to see their parents they just say salaam and sit down on the couch, turn the TV on, or start using their phone — and the mother is sitting there watching their face, wondering: will he ever talk to me, will he give me some attention? You can check your phone at other times; you can watch TV at another time. Now that you are seeing your mother, give her your full attention. Be fully present. Talk to her. Say good words to her. Say kind words. Make her happy. Comfort her. Listen to her.

The Way of the Righteous

‘Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr’s son said that when his father died, he made the same du’a for an entire year: O Allah, forgive my father. We think making du’a for our parents once or twice is enough — and he is making du’a for an entire year after his father’s death.

It was said that the one who prays five times a day is among those who are grateful to Allah, and the one who prays for his parents after every salah is also grateful to his parents. This is why traditionally children are taught that part of the du’as they can make in salah is the du’a asking Allah to forgive us and our parents. So whether parents are alive or deceased, you can make this du’a.

But what does Shaytan do? Shaytan makes us believe that our parents are toxic, that they are unfair, that they are ignorant, that they are backward, that they are abusive, that they do not understand — and we forget to see how toxic we are, how abusive we are, how ungrateful we are. If ever you have encountered a parent and child yelling at one another, you can see how the child is often being more rude, more disrespectful, in the way they are rolling their eyes and raising their voice. This is what Shaytan makes us believe: that we are victims and our parents have always been abusive towards us.

Some of the companions would say that not praying for one’s parents makes a person’s life difficult and constricted. Imagine, then, what happens when a person mistreats their parents. Sometimes you see in your own life that you are struggling with your work or your education, or in your marriage; or you see your friends struggling, your spouse struggling in their work, sometimes in their mental health, constantly anxious. So remind them to be good to their parents, to pray for them, to give sadaqah on their behalf.

The Weight of Their Right

  • Allah mentions the right of parents after His own right, in many places in the Qur’an: worship Allah, associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good.
  • The previous nations were also obligated to this: Allah took a covenant from Bani Isra’il that they worship none but Allah, and to parents do good.
  • Allah tells us to be grateful to Him and also to our parents: We have enjoined upon man care for his parents; his mother carried him, increasing her in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years — be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination. Even the healthiest and strongest of women bear difficulty in pregnancy, and that difficulty does not end at full term; it only increases with birth and labour. And then it continues, because before she was able to sleep through the night, and now she is up every hour or two, nursing, changing, burping, because the baby is entirely dependent on her.
  • And out of both parents, the right of the mother is even greater: his mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning period is thirty months. Becoming a parent is life-altering. There are not just the physical struggles a mother experiences; there are also emotional and social struggles. Women have to give up their studies, give up their work, give up their social life; sometimes they are not able to talk to their friends or spend any time with them; they experience isolation, physical hardship, emotional stress in raising little ones. And it is not just mental health; women also experience spiritual loss — they can’t fast in Ramadan, they cannot go for taraweeh, they can’t pray in the night. There is so much a mother is not able to do because of her little child. But she does not think, as she is raising her child, “it is because of him, it is because of her”; she does not treat that child as a burden; she lovingly embraces the child and looks after the child. Allah is reminding us of what our mothers have done for us. So have some gratitude for your parents.
  • The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: Allah enjoins you to be dutiful to your mothers — he said it repeatedly — and He enjoins you to be dutiful to your fathers. And we learn that the right of the mother is three times that of the father.

Two Kinds of Children

Allah mentions people who grow until, when they reach maturity and reach the age of forty years, they say: my Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to work righteousness of which You will approve, and make righteous for me my offspring; indeed I have repented to You, and indeed I am of the Muslims. And Allah says regarding them: those are the ones from whom We will accept the best of what they did, and We will overlook their misdeeds, and they will be among the companions of Paradise — the promise of truth which they had been promised.

On the other hand, Allah mentions the one who says to his parents, “Uff to you — do you promise me that I will be brought forth from the earth, when generations before me have already passed on?” while they call to Allah for help and say to their son, “Woe to you, believe!” and he says, “This is not but legends of the former people.” Such individuals — who are rude and harsh to their parents and have no gratitude for them — eventually that leads them to disbelief, and they will be losers in the Hereafter.

So we see these two opposite characters: children who are good to their parents, who believe, who are humble, who serve them; and those who are very ungrateful, who can only recall and blow out of proportion the mistakes of their parents — and parents are not angels, they are humans — and because they are so focused on those mistakes, they are rude to them, argumentative with them, they answer back, they reject and belittle every advice their parents give, and eventually they even leave the fold of Islam.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: the one who is not grateful to people is not grateful to Allah. Yes, your parents made mistakes, but they also treated you well. Your mother gave birth to you and raised you. And yes, she might not have treated you nicely always, because she is human; maybe she had her own personal struggles, maybe she was struggling mentally, maybe financially. We have seen how so many women struggle to raise little children because they don’t get help from their husbands. There are studies showing that children grow up in poverty because of absent fathers. So when a mother has to work and do so many things and look after her children also, it is possible she doesn’t treat them in the best way — but the fact that she gave birth to you and raised you is enough of a reason to be grateful to her and good to her.

Ingratitude is a kind of kufr — less than major kufr, so it does not take a person out of the fold of Islam, but it is a form of it, and it causes a person to lose their dunya and akhirah. And look at what parents do: when children misbehave with their parents, parents make du’a for their rude children. But when parents come across as harsh to the children, what do children do in response? They begin to avoid their parents, detest them, not want to talk about them, move away from them, cut off from them.
