And these days this has become very trendy — if someone is toxic, if someone doesn’t support you, cut them off. This is not the way of the Muslims. Cutting off the ties of kinship is forbidden. And labelling parents as toxic is very disrespectful.

Even Then, Be Good to Them

  • The prophets of Allah were especially good towards their parents. Allah describes Yahya (‘alayhis salam) as kind and gentle and god-fearing, and especially dutiful to his parents, not a disobedient tyrant — meaning he would not disobey his parents, and was not harsh or forceful with them. And ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam) said that Allah made him dutiful to his mother and did not make him a wretched tyrant. The parents of Yahya were very old when he was born, and it is especially hard to be good to parents who are elderly, because they are limited in their ability and sometimes scold or criticise more. Yet Allah mentions his dutifulness in the Qur’an.
  • Being good to one’s mother is a deed even more important than jihad. A man came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and said: O Messenger of Allah, I want to go for jihad with you, seeking the face of Allah and the reward of the Hereafter. He asked: is your mother still alive? The man said yes. He said: go back and honour her. The man approached from the other side and tried again, and again he said: is your mother alive? Go back and honour her. The man tried a third time, and he said: go back and serve her, for there is Paradise.
  • When he was asked which deeds are best, he said: prayer at its early time, and being good to one’s parents, and then jihad.
  • Serving one’s parents is given preference over voluntary good deeds. We learn the story of Jurayj the worshipper, who was busy in voluntary worship, and his mother would come and call him and he would not answer her or go to her — and he suffered a great trial because of how he treated her.
  • Even if parents are disobedient to Allah or doing things clearly contrary to the teachings of Islam, you should still be good to them. We learn about the son of ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, who was very disrespectful to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. His son was a sincere believer and became very angry with his father, and went to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and said: O Messenger of Allah, if you want, I can bring you the head of my father. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam forbade him, and said: no — go and be good to your father.
  • In the Qur’an we learn that if your parents try to force you to associate partners with Allah, do not obey them — but still accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness. Sometimes when children become more religious than their parents they begin to avoid them, don’t meet them, don’t do anything for them. What kind of religiosity is this? Asma’ (raḍiyallāhu ‘anha) had a mother who was a mushrikah, and she came to her expecting some financial help, and Asma’ asked the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam whether she should help her, and he said yes. If this is the case with mushrik parents, the right of Muslim parents is even greater.
  • A child cannot repay what he owes to his father unless he finds him in slavery and buys him and sets him free. Sometimes children think, “I did this for my parents, so I have repaid them” — no, you cannot.
  • When a person is good to their parents, they receive increase in life and in wealth: whoever loves that his term of life be extended and his sustenance increased should be good to his parents and join the ties of kinship. And we learn of a companion known to be very good to his mother, whom the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was made to hear reciting Qur’an in Paradise; when he asked who it was, he was told it was that man — and he said: this is real piety.

And the Opposite

If a person is disrespectful to their parents, rude and harsh, and neglects them, this is something very serious. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said Allah has forbidden you to be undutiful to your mothers. When he was asked about the major sins, he mentioned being undutiful to one’s parents. In another narration, may Allah curse the one who insults his parents or cuts off from them. And people who are like this — their obligatory and voluntary good deeds are not accepted.

We learn that the pleasure of the Lord is in the pleasure of the father, and the displeasure of the Lord is in the displeasure of the father. So be eager to make your parents happy with you. And it was said that when a person disobeys his parents his life term is reduced, and that the person disobedient to his parents will find his children disobedient to him. There is punishment in the grave for such behaviour, and such a person, constantly disobedient, will not enter Paradise.

Of the rights of parents is that you serve them and obey them, as long as they tell you to do something permissible. And part of it is that you serve them in such a way that they become happy and make du’a for you — because of the du’as that are accepted is the du’a of the parent for his child. So make them happy, serve them, do things for them so that they make du’a for you, because as long as they are alive you have this privilege; once they leave the world you lose something very precious.

Part of treating parents well is that you do not make them cry. A man came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and said: I am making hijrah, and I left my parents crying. He said: go back to them and make them laugh as you made them weep. You think you have done something huge by making hijrah at the cost of making your parents cry — return and make them happy first.

And if parents ever make a mistake, do not embarrass them, do not be harsh to them; overlook and forgive. And spend on your parents. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said while standing on the mimbar that the hand which gives is the upper hand, and that you should start with those for whom you are responsible — and he said: begin with your mother, your father, your sister, your brother, then the next closest and the next closest.

Muhammad ibn Sirin would buy the softest clothes for his mother — not just any clothes, the softest — and on ‘Eid he would colour her clothes himself, and he would never raise his voice at her louder than hers, and never speak to her at a volume louder than hers. And when Ibn ‘Umar would remove something harmful from the road, he would say: O Allah, reward my mother and father for this also. Look at his eagerness — ya Allah, reward them also, because they raised me and taught me to do all these good things, so when I am doing anything, reward them also.

And when parents have departed from the world, we should especially make du’a for them, because it benefits them. We should seek forgiveness for them, give sadaqah on their behalf — especially the sadaqah of giving water to people — and do voluntary good deeds on their behalf, such as Hajj, and fulfil their vows, and be good to their friends and their relatives. You will be rewarded for that, and they will also be rewarded.

Chapter Seventy

The Du’as for Parents

These du’as are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. My Lord, have mercy upon them

“My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.” I was small, I was incapable, I was in need of protection and mercy and love and affection and constant round-the-clock care — and they gave that to me. I can never do the same for my parents, so ya Allah, You give them what I am not able to give them.

Sometimes you are in a situation where you are not able to help your parents — maybe your physical health is such, or you live in a different country, too far away, and you are not able to do anything for them. So especially make du’a, give sadaqah on their behalf, send them financial gifts so that their life is easy — but especially make du’a for them, and make this du’a regularly, as one of the scholars mentioned: after every salah.

2. Forgive me, my parents, and the believers

“Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day the account is established.” And this is the proper order of making du’a: first for yourself, then for your parents, then for other people.

Parents deserve that you make du’a for them, especially for their forgiveness, whether they are alive or deceased, whether Muslim or non-Muslim. If they are non-Muslim, of course you pray for them while they are alive — once they have passed away you cannot make du’a for them, but while they are alive especially make du’a for them after every salah: ya Allah, guide them; ya Allah, forgive them. And forgiveness will only come after their guidance, so the du’a for their forgiveness includes the du’a for their guidance.

3. Enable me to be grateful

“My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve, and admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants.” Sulayman (‘alayhis salam) made this du’a.

He asked: awzi’ni — enable me, restrain me. The word is used in the Qur’an for restraining forces and armies. Because the nafs is such that when it enjoys certain blessings and privileges, it can get out of control: you begin to think, I am self-made, I have accomplished all of this with my own hard work. And you forget that you are the product of your parents’ hard work; your parents have invested so much in you. If you are able to speak well, if you have any privileges, Allah granted them to you through your parents. And sometimes it is because of the mistakes of your parents that you learn there is a better way of living, that we should be more obedient to Allah.

So you are asking Allah: restrain me, give me the ability, enable me to be grateful to You for the favours You have bestowed upon me, and also for the favours You have bestowed upon my parents — because whatever your parents enjoy, you also enjoy, directly or indirectly. And then he made du’a for his actions: allow me to do actions You will be pleased with. And he prayed for Allah’s mercy and for the company of the righteous in Paradise.

4. Make my mother among the beautiful of Paradise

One of the companions was asked to make du’a, as people do when they gather together, and he made du’a; and they said, make more du’a; and he said: O Allah, make me among those who are brought near to You, and make my mother among the beautiful women of Paradise.

We think that the hur are some different creatures that will be in Paradise — but first and foremost are the believing women. And for many children, they see the beauty of their mother decline: you see how the hair is falling, turning grey and white; you see the wrinkles on the face; you see the body becoming weak; those hands that were so soft are now maybe experiencing some skin condition. You witness your parents as they age and their physical beauty declines. So he especially prayed for his mother’s beauty — that she be of the beautiful women of Paradise.

Rabbi irhamhuma kama rabbayani saghira.
Chapter Seventy-One

Coolness of the Eyes

The Qur’an — Surat al-Furqan

“And those who say: our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the righteous.”

This is the du’a of ‘ibadur-Rahman, the worshippers of the Most Merciful — those whose walking, whose interacting with people, whose speech Allah praises. And here their du’as are mentioned: they call upon Allah for their spouses and their children.

The scholars say this du’a includes people who are married and people who are not married, people who have children and people who do not. Because “from among our spouses” is for those who are married; “and our offspring” is for those who have children; and “make us an example for the righteous” includes every believer, whether or not they are married and whether or not they have children. We should all be asking Allah to make us an example, a leader, for those who are righteous.

And Allah says regarding these people: those will be awarded the chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and words of peace, abiding eternally — what an excellent place of residence and a permanent abode.

What Qurrata A’yun Means

Dhurriyyah includes male and female children, young and older. It doesn’t matter how old or young your child is, you can still make this du’a for them — and even if they are not born yet, you can still make it.

Qurrata a’yun literally is the coolness of the eye, and the ulama say it means three things.

  1. When the tears cool off. When you are crying out of grief, out of worry, sometimes out of frustration and helplessness, your eyes are hot; and when you stop crying they cool off. And when is it that you stop crying? When you have some reason to be happy, or something comforts you. So you are asking Allah to grant you happiness and joy through your children — happiness by having children, happiness by having children who are righteous, and happiness by seeing your children doing good things. Because for a mother or father to see their child suffering, even religiously or spiritually, is extremely painful.
  2. Through sleep. When a person is not able to sleep for a very long time, the eyes are hot; and when finally you are able to close your eyes and sleep, your eyes cool off. And why is a person not able to sleep for a long time? Because of worry, because of concern. And so often mothers and fathers are awake all night long, for hours, worrying about their child, about their daughter, about their son. Or sometimes people are awake at night in their sadness, wondering: will I ever have a child? So: ya Allah, grant me that rest, that comfort, that feeling that I have a child, I have a good child, I have a righteous child.
  3. Happiness — they say this is rida, inner contentment.

Ibn ‘Abbas explained that you are asking Allah for children who are obedient to Allah, and in this way they will be a means of joy and coolness for you in this world and in the Hereafter. Because when someone sees their child committing sin, disobeying Allah, committing crimes, that is incredibly painful.

Here coolness of the eye does not mean “make them good-looking.” This is a concern many people have: I want a child who is very cute, very good-looking, who has green eyes and fair skin or such hair — because we have to take cute photos and share them on the internet. We are so obsessed with physical appearance, and that is not what is meant here. The scholars say clearly that this is not referring to outward beauty; rather it refers to obedience to Allah. Because even if your daughter is tall, beautiful, with lovely hair and beautiful skin, excellent in her appearance and her choice of clothes — if she refuses to pray salah, how painful is that? The physical beauty will not bring you comfort. What will bring you comfort is that she is praying salah.

Ibn Jurayj said you are asking Allah for spouses and children who are good worshippers and who do not commit sins and crimes — because when a child commits sins, that affects the family also. For instance, if your child wants to listen to loud music and makes a big fuss about it, or they are older and in their room playing very loud music, is that not going to affect you? Of course it will. The sins of one person affect those around them. And at the end of the day a father and a mother are answerable for their children. So you are asking Allah to protect your children from committing sins, so that you don’t fall into the same sins and are not affected by them, and don’t become complacent towards disobedience to Allah.

Make Us an Example for the Righteous

You are asking Allah to make those under you fearful of Allah. Because every person has some kind of authority, some kind of leadership. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: each one of you is a shepherd, and each one of you will be asked about his flock. A father is the shepherd of his household; a mother is also a shepherdess of her household. So you as parents are answerable for your children. Likewise in a workplace, in a school, in any organisation there is some hierarchy — so the people who work under you, whom you are responsible to guide and lead and instruct and teach, you are praying for them: ya Allah, make them righteous.

What this really means is that you are asking Allah to make you righteous — because only a righteous person can lead those who are righteous. A righteous person is an example for the righteous. A person cannot expect that they are disobeying Allah and their children become happy with the Qur’an. Your children will emulate you; they will follow you. And so often it happens that people have different standards for themselves and different standards for their children, and then they complain that my children don’t listen, they don’t do this, they don’t do that. The first question is: are you doing it yourself? Sometimes people complain about those they work with, that they don’t do their work, don’t come on time. The first question is: are you doing your work yourself?

And Allah tells us: We made them leaders, guiding by Our command, and We inspired to them the doing of good deeds and establishing prayer and giving zakah, and they were worshippers of Us. So only when a person has such qualities — doing good, praying salah, giving zakat, worshipping Allah — can they be a good leader of the righteous.

And Allah tells us they were made leaders when they were patient, and they used to believe in Our verses with certainty. So sabr and yaqin — these two qualities are essential. If a person is always losing their cool with their children, how can they lead them in piety? Their children will not want to listen to them; they will become extremely rebellious. And yaqin, conviction — in Allah, in the Hereafter, in the words of Allah, the deen of Allah, the promises of Allah — because then you have hope, and then you are consistent, and when you are consistent, the people under you will also be consistent. So as a parent, hold on to these two qualities. The more convinced you are of the religion of Allah, the more convinced your children will be. Begin with yourself.

And the people who make such du’as, Allah will grant them the ghurfah — the highest room in a building; think of a penthouse — beautiful homes in Paradise, which the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam described as such that you can see the inside from the outside and the outside from the inside. When he was asked who they are for, he said: for those who feed others, who spread the salaam, who pray in the night while people are sleeping — and in another narration, who fast. So in Ramadan all of these good deeds are combined for the believer. And they will get it because they were patient.

And this is a quality essential in parents: sabr. Sabr first of all in doing good things yourself — because it becomes very hard to pray, to recite the Qur’an, to make dhikr, to spend in sadaqah when your children are always around you or always have needs you must attend to. So sabr means that while you are taking care of your children you don’t neglect yourself; you must make time for your salah, for your ‘ibadah. Secondly, sabr in staying away from sins — because sometimes it is so tempting, even for the sake of your own children, to allow or do something displeasing to Allah. And thirdly, sabr in dealing with hardships. Who said that being a parent is easy? It is incredibly hard, and the difficulty only increases with time. A mother thinks pregnancy is the hardest stage. It is not. The real difficulty begins once the child is born. And you would think infancy is the hardest, or the toddler years — no, that is actually easy; yes, it is physically hard, but the real test begins when the child is able to speak and answer back and say they do things differently, when they want to do something else, when they don’t agree with you, when they argue with you.

Chapter Seventy-Two

Righteousness Is Not in Our Hands

The prophets of Allah made du’a for their children — they made du’a to have children, and they also made du’a for the righteousness of their children.

  • Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) made du’a: my Lord, grant me a child from among the righteous.
  • The righteous say: my Lord, reform for me my offspring — meaning make my children righteous.
  • Zakariyya (‘alayhis salam) made du’a: my Lord, grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit from me and from the family of Ya’qub, and make him, my Lord, pleasing to You.
  • Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) also made du’a: my Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from among my descendants; our Lord, and accept my supplication.

So it is the way of the prophets, and the way of those who believe, that they pray: ya Allah, grant us children; grant us righteous children; and the children that we have, ya Allah, make them righteous, make them such that they establish salah, make them such that they do good.

When a person makes du’a for having children, or for the health and well-being of their children, they should also ask Allah to make their children righteous. Because it is not correct to think that we can teach piety to our children and make them righteous ourselves. Righteousness is not in our hands; it is not in our control. We can do our best to teach them the Qur’an and good manners — but at the end of the day they will only do what they choose to do, and what Allah gives them the tawfiq to do.

Consider Nuh (‘alayhis salam). He worked for 950 years calling people to the worship of Allah. And we can only imagine that if he worked so hard to call his nation, he would have worked even harder to teach his children — because a person begins with those closest to them, and this has been the way of the prophets; the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was also taught to warn his closest family, so he began by inviting them. Yet what happened? Nuh’s own son did not believe; he was of those who disbelieved, and he drowned in the flood.

So we should never think: my children love me, they are very good to me, I have taught them this, I have sent them to Islamic school, both my husband’s family and mine are good and on the deen, so I don’t have to worry. No. You must always be concerned about the deen of your children, and ask Allah to guide them. In fact this is something you should be concerned about for yourself also.

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would often say: Ya Muqallibal-qulub, thabbit qalbi ‘ala dinik — O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. Anas (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) said: I asked him, O Messenger of Allah, we believe in you and in what you have come with — do you still fear for us? And he said: yes, indeed the hearts are between two of the fingers of Allah, and He turns them as He wills.

The state of the heart does not remain the same; it can change over time. So be concerned for your own deen and for the deen of your children. And don’t just rely on your efforts; along with efforts there must also be du’a.

And sometimes people tend to make du’a only when they face some hardship from their children — when the children are being rebellious, showing bad manners, not doing their work, not taking life seriously. Then parents begin to make du’a. We should be making du’a for our children even before we have children.

Someone once asked their teacher: why should I make the du’a “my Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from among my descendants” when I am not even married and do not have children? The teacher said: you should still make this du’a, because when you do have children, insha’Allah, you will want them to establish salah. And du’a itself is worship. So don’t wait for some hardship; don’t wait to get married; don’t wait to have children in order to make du’a for them. Make du’a anyway.

Why Righteous Children Matter

Having children is a blessing of Allah. Some people say raising children is hard, so I don’t want to ever have children. Yes, it is hard; there is no doubt about this. It is painful. It is expensive. There are a lot of tears, a lot of sweat, a lot of hard work, a lot of worry. But Allah rewards very generously those who strive hard in His way.

When you look at this from a worldly perspective — considering all the money, all the physical work, all the emotional labour, all the sacrifices — is it worth having children? From a purely worldly perspective, it is not; you would rather not have children, live a comfortable life, spend your money on travel, on experiencing good things, maybe go for ‘Umrah every year. However, the reward a person gets by raising good children is continuous. Because in a hadith we learn that when a person dies, his actions come to an end, his good deeds stop, except for three things — and one of them is a righteous child who prays for him.

And the way a righteous child prays for their parents is very different, because that child will recognise the favour of their parents and be grateful to them; they will continue to make du’a for them, give sadaqah on their behalf, do Hajj and ‘Umrah on their behalf. We also learn that Allah raises the rank of a righteous slave in Paradise, and that person asks: ya Rabb, how come my rank is being raised? And he is told: this is because of your child seeking forgiveness for you. You could have many good friends and many good relatives, and yes, they love you and care about you — but the way a child cares about their parents is very different.

So we should make du’a: ya Allah, grant me righteous children. And the prophets, when they made du’a to have children, didn’t just say “ya Allah, grant me children”; they said: grant me from among the righteous.

Chapter Seventy-Three

What Children Have a Right To

It is not enough to just desire children and have children. Children also have rights. Where parents have rights, children also have rights on their parents. In Imam al-Bukhari’s al-Adab al-Mufrad there is an entire chapter on taking care of children — this is a very important matter that many people neglect. A lot of times people think it is only the parents who have rights over their children; it is the other way around as well.

And the rights children have over their parents are not limited to providing food and drink and shelter and clothing and sending them to school. That is not enough. Al-Munawi said: just as your parents have rights over you, so too your child has rights over you — rather many rights, such as teaching them the individual obligations. It is your responsibility as parents to teach your children how to pray. It is your duty to ensure they are fasting. It is your duty to ensure they are learning the ways of remembering Allah. Teaching them Islamic manners — it is your obligation to teach them not to steal, not to be rude, how to speak nicely, how to eat properly. Giving them gifts equally: you must treat all of your children the same, so that if you buy something for one child you buy the same or something similar for the other. And he said that if preference is shown with no reason, that is regarded as invalid by some scholars and as makruh by others.

He said Allah has called them al-abrar, the dutiful, because they are dutiful to their parents and to their children. Birr is that you are good to your parents and you are also good to your children. Just as you have a duty you owe your parents, so you have a duty you owe your child.

Hadith

Each of you is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. The man is the shepherd of his household and is responsible for them. The woman is the shepherd of her husband’s house and child and is responsible for them.

And in a hadith: indeed your child has a right over you. So often men think their only responsibility as a father is to go to work, make money and pay the bills. No — your child has a right over you: that you sit with your child, you look at him, you feed him, you talk to him. Just as you teach your child how to use a computer or ride a bike, you also teach them good things.

But so often children are neglected. There are studies showing that so many children in the West are growing up in poverty because of absent fathers. First of all they are not there when the child is born. Other times, because of divorce, children are completely abandoned by their fathers. And sometimes the marriage is intact but the father is still absent — he is spending his money on his own enjoyment while the children are suffering in poverty.

This is in the hadith where the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught that your Lord has a right over you, your body has a right over you, your spouse has a right over you, your guest has a right over you — and your child also has a right over you.

So are you spending quality time with your children? Are you giving them what they deserve from you? Because sometimes we say, my children don’t listen to me, and we just want some du’a that will work like a miracle — just tell me something I can say and within five minutes my child will become an angel. It doesn’t happen like that. Along with du’a there must be effort, and there must be accountability: how am I raising my child? What am I giving to my child? How can I complain when I have neglected my child?

Hadith

There is no person whom Allah puts in charge of others, and when he dies he is insincere to his subjects, except that Allah will forbid Paradise to him.

What a serious hadith this is. If Allah has put you in charge of your children, then you must be sincere to them, deal with them fairly, and give them their rights. In another hadith: it is sufficient sin for a man that he neglects those on whom he is obligated to spend. Because some men are very stingy with their children; they want to save money so they can build a fancy house back home, while their children cannot even go to Qur’an class because the father is not willing to pay any fees, and cannot go to Islamic school. And think about it: giving your children a proper, good upbringing is your responsibility. If you are putting them in a situation where they are constantly exposed to shirk and to sins and to things hateful to Allah, and then they become okay with it and begin to practise it themselves — who will you blame then? Is that fancy house back home worth it, when it came at the cost of your children’s upbringing?

The Qur’an

“O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are appointed angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and who do whatever they are commanded.”

So Allah is telling us: save yourselves and your families. And who is your family? Your children. So save them. Don’t just be okay with “they’re adults now, this is their choice, it’s up to them, what can I do?” You still have to do something. And begin with du’a, because the du’a of a parent for their child is accepted; Allah does not ignore that. And then along with du’a, think about what you need to do — how you need to provide for your children, not just financially but emotionally, being present, being there.

Because some people, while they are around their children, are constantly disconnected from them; they are in some other world. And these days the phone is such a big fitnah, that even when the child is telling something to the parent so excitedly, sharing a joke or something that happened, what are the parents looking at? Their phones. At dinner, at breakfast, in the living room, when they are sitting together, when they are going somewhere — all the time we are busy with our phones, and the children are hungry for love and attention. They are desperate for it. And when we don’t give it to them, they seek it from somewhere else.

Their Rights, One by One

  • That a man choose a good wife, and a woman a good husband. When thinking about marriage, don’t just think about whether your potential spouse is wealthy, whether they can take care of you financially, whether they will be a good fit for your family, whether you get along, whether they are good-looking. All of that is important — but you must also ask: would they be a good parent to my child? Do I want to raise children with this person? Are they someone who prays salah, who speaks the truth, who earns a lawful income, who is good to their family, who cares about family? Don’t just think about yourself when looking for someone to marry; look at whether they are a good potential parent as well. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said a woman is married for several reasons — her wealth, her beauty, her status, her religion — and he said: choose the one who has deen. And he said that when someone whose deen and whose akhlaq pleases you proposes, then give your daughter or sister in marriage to him. Because when a person has these values, they will pass them on to their children.
  • That they be given a good name, and that their basic needs of food, drink, clothing and accommodation are fulfilled according to what a person can afford, without being stingy or extravagant.
  • That you ask Allah to protect them from Shaytan — even before they are born. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught that when one of you comes to his spouse, he should ask Allah to keep Shaytan away from them and from what He provides them; and he said that if a child is born as a result, Shaytan will not be able to harm that child. And the mother of Maryam, when her daughter was born, said: I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Shaytan, the expelled. So ask Allah to protect your children from the influence of Shaytan — and not just at one point; continue to ask. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would make du’a for both his grandsons, Hasan and Husayn, placing them in Allah’s protection against the evil of every shaytan and every venomous creature and every evil eye.
  • That parents teach them good manners and good behaviour and the deen in whatever way they can. If you can teach them yourself, excellent; and if you cannot, you must provide them such opportunities. Begin by teaching them the rights of Allah. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: teach the child to pray when he is seven years old. So if you don’t teach your child at that tender age, what is going to happen when they turn seventeen and you shame them for not praying or for not knowing how to pray? Who is to blame? Begin early; don’t delay. In the Qur’an, Luqman said to his son: O my son, do not associate others with Allah; indeed shirk is a great wrong. So begin by teaching them about the rights of Allah. And develop in them the fear of Allah: Luqman said, O my son, if there should be the weight of a mustard seed, and it should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. So build that awareness in your children, that Allah knows everything.
  • That you be firm without being harsh. Sometimes it means you have to be a little firm, and there is nothing wrong in being firm. But being firm does not mean that you beat them in such a way that they are hurt emotionally, that they feel they are not loved, that you are always harsh to them. Some people have a habit of slapping their children over every little thing, throwing shoes at them. This is so common in some cultures — people will beat their children with slippers, or pull their ears, or pinch them. This is not right. Why do you have to use punishment all the time in order to discipline your children? The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam did not do that. Look at how he would honour his daughter; look at how he would play with his grandchildren. Show them love — and love does not spoil. What spoils children is your inconsistency. So be consistent yourself, and be firm; and being firm does not mean being harsh or violent.
  • That you include them in your work. It is the way of the prophets: when Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) was building the Ka’bah, he built it with Isma’il — father and son together. And especially for boys it is important that fathers spend time with them, take them to work, take them to the different places they go, so they learn from a young age that this is part of life.
  • That you are fair with them and show them love. A Bedouin once came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and asked: do you kiss your children? Because we do not kiss them. And he said: can I put mercy in your heart after Allah has removed it from it? Kissing children is not limited to babies — the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would kiss Fatimah on her forehead when she came to him, and she was married and a mother. ‘Umar wanted to appoint a man as governor, and in conversation the man said: I have such and such a number of children and I have never kissed any of them. And ‘Umar said: Allah will only show mercy to the kindest of His slaves. He did not like this — if this man is so harsh that he has never kissed any of his children, how will he treat his people?
  • That you care about their feelings. Abu Bakr (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) was so careful about how he spoke in front of ‘A’ishah. He once said: by Allah, there is no man on the face of the earth that I love more than ‘Umar. And after some time he came back and asked ‘A’ishah what he had said, and she told him. And he said: yes, ‘Umar is dearer to me — although one’s child is closer to one’s heart. He wanted to make sure she did not feel that her father loved ‘Umar more than he loved her. And she was an adult at that point; yet he cared about her emotions and her feelings. Sometimes we think we don’t have to care about the feelings of our children, because of “tough love.” The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said about his grandchildren: they are my sweet basil in this world. And he was once seen carrying Hasan on his shoulders, saying: O Allah, I love him, so love him.
  • That you show them mercy. A woman came to ‘A’ishah begging for food, and she had with her two of her daughters. ‘A’ishah gave her three dates. So the woman gave one date to each daughter, and was about to eat the third herself when both girls began looking at her — so she broke her date into two halves and gave each half to each daughter, and ate nothing herself. ‘A’ishah was amazed and mentioned it to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and he said: are you surprised at that? Allah will show mercy to her because she was merciful towards her child. So when a mother or father is merciful to their child, this is a means of earning the mercy of Allah for themselves.
  • That when they reach adulthood, you help them get married, find them a good spouse, help them get settled and become independent, help them stand on their feet. And if a child is well past the age of puberty and wants to get married, and the parents do not facilitate that marriage, and that child falls into sin — Qatadah said the parents are sinful. And these days there are so many opportunities to fall into indecency; a person does not even have to go out, all they need is a computer. So protect your children. And if your child is in their twenties, find a suitable spouse, and make du’a for them — for their marriage, their health, their well-being — because a parent’s du’a for their children is not rejected.
Chapter Seventy-Four

The Du’as for Children

These du’as are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. Grant me a child from among the righteous

“My Lord, grant me from among the righteous.” Make this du’a even before you have children, and make it even if you have children — that any child you have, ya Allah, make them righteous. This is the du’a Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) made, and Allah says: so We gave him good news of a forbearing boy. And this is Isma’il (‘alayhis salam) — so forbearing that when his father said he was commanded to slaughter him, he said: O my father, do what you have been commanded. He did not object. So forbearing that he was building the Ka’bah with his father.

2. Do not leave me alone

“My Lord, do not leave me alone, while You are the best of inheritors.” This was the du’a of Zakariyya (‘alayhis salam), made when he had no children. And what happened? Allah says: so We answered him, and We gave him Yahya, and We reformed for him his wife.

3. Grant me from Yourself a good offspring

“My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.” This is also the du’a of Zakariyya, and it shows us that he did not make du’a just once for a righteous child; he made du’a many times, over and over again. And who is a good offspring? A child who is good not just in their health and their physical body, and not just in their emotional and mental health, but also spiritually. And look at his hope: indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.

4. Seeking refuge for them from Shaytan

Like the mother of Maryam said: I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Shaytan, the expelled. When you see your children misbehaving — and sometimes you can see clearly that they are under the influence of Shaytan, and there is no reason to misbehave, no reason to be angry, no reason to be so irritable, but they are, answering back — make du’a: ya Allah, protect my child from Shaytan. And this can be whether your child is a few minutes old or many years old, whether they live with you or not.

5. Make me and my descendants establishers of prayer

“My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from among my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.” This is a du’a you can make in your salah and at the end of salah also. So often parents complain: my daughter doesn’t pray, my son does not pray, they don’t want to pray, they used to pray and now all of a sudden they have stopped, or they don’t pray properly; they say they have prayed but I have a feeling they have not; they say they have wudu but I have a feeling they don’t. So make this du’a: ya Allah, make me someone who prays properly, and make my children also those who pray properly — because when they give the right of Allah, they will be conscious of Allah in other aspects of their life also.

6. Comfort to our eyes

“Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the righteous.”

7. Make righteous for me my offspring

“My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to work righteousness of which You will approve, and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.”

“Make righteous for me my offspring” doesn’t just mean make them righteous towards me; it means make them righteous such that I can see them doing righteous things. Because so often it happens that parents don’t see the piety of their children — it is after they leave this world, when their children realise how short life is, that they repent to Allah and become righteous. So: make righteous for me my offspring, meaning I am able to see their piety. And also for me — make it in my favour, because when your children are righteous, this is something that will benefit you too. Righteous children will pray for you; they will do good deeds that you will also be rewarded for; and when you teach them how to worship Allah, then every time they worship Him, you will also be rewarded.

8. Forgive his sin, purify his heart, guard his chastity

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam made this du’a for the young man who came to him asking permission to commit zina. He spoke to him and made him understand how zina is something evil — and then he also made du’a for him: O Allah, forgive his sin, purify his heart, and guard his chastity.

Sometimes you worry for your growing children as they go out in the world, and maybe they are falling into fitnah. You don’t know what sins they are committing, what they are hiding from you. You talk to them, you discuss with them, and they understand — and yet they slip. For example you talk to your daughter or your son about not having such a relationship with someone of the opposite gender. Or sometimes you see your own child having same-sex feelings, and you don’t know what to do; you find yourself in so much confusion. Logically maybe your child understands, but they don’t have that emotional and spiritual strength to stay away from sin. So make du’a for them: O Allah, forgive his sin; purify his heart — whatever desire there is in his heart, remove it; and guard his chastity. And for your daughter, say it in the feminine. This is a du’a we should be making anyway, because there is so much fitnah in the world.

9. Guide his heart

“O Allah, guide his heart” — or for your daughter, “O Allah, guide her heart.” This is the du’a the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam made for ‘Ali (raḍiyallāhu ‘anhu) when he sent him as a judge to Yemen, and ‘Ali said to him: I am a young man, I don’t know how to judge. And sometimes your child is struggling with grown-up decisions — struggling at work, struggling at school. So make du’a for them.

10. Cure his heart

“O Allah, cure his heart.” Sometimes you see that your child is suffering from a spiritual illness, or sometimes even a mental illness. Sometimes your child is so bitter about something that happened, or so jealous, or so angry, or has so many unrealistic desires for this world, or so many doubts that worry you. So make du’a: O Allah, cure his heart, cure her heart.

11. Protection from a child who becomes a master over you

In the du’a that asks Allah for protection from an evil neighbour and from a spouse who causes you to age before old age, we also ask: and protect me from a child who becomes a master over me — a child who begins to treat me as a slave, as a servant; a child who becomes a rabb over the household, so that the entire family, the entire home, is disrupted because of the behaviour of one child.

So we should be making du’a for our children, on the one hand being attentive to our duties towards them, and also making du’a for them. And don’t wait for something difficult or painful to happen to raise your hands before Allah for your children. Make du’a for your children anyway — whether you have them yet or not, whether they are young or old, whether they are obedient or not, whether they are righteous or not. It is your children’s right that you pray for them.

Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilaik.
Chapter Seventy-Five

Marriage Is a Sign

Marriage is a huge blessing — in fact it is an ayah, a sign from the signs of Allah.

The Qur’an

“And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates, that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.”

So the purpose of marriage is that people find tranquillity in one another. And affection and mercy are the two key ingredients for a happy marriage.

Marriage is encouraged in our religion. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam instructed young people to marry: O young people, whoever of you can support a wife should marry — because marriage helps you control your eyes and preserves one from immorality, and it protects a person from doing wrong things. And whoever cannot marry should fast, because it is a means of reducing desire; so fast in order to develop discipline and self-control.

Allah says: marry the unmarried among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves — not just the free but also those who are slaves — because this is a human need. And Allah promises: if they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-encompassing and knowing.

Marriage is a sunnah of the prophets of Allah, not only of Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam: and We have already sent messengers before you, and assigned to them wives and children.

Hadith

Some people came to the wives of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and inquired about his habits, and they seemed to have belittled the amount of worship he did. So one of the men said: I will not marry. Another said: I will not sleep in the night. And the third said: I will always fast. When the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam found out, he did not approve, and he addressed the people and said: I am the most god-fearing among you and the most knowing of Allah among you — and I pray in the night and I sleep; I fast some days and do not fast other days; and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me.

So it is not religiosity or piety that a person forbids himself from marriage, or from sleeping in the night, or from ever taking a break from fasting. The height of religiosity and devotion and servitude is in the practice of the prophets of Allah; and his worship, his actions, his lifestyle is what is most loved by Allah — which is why we have been told: if you love Allah, then follow me.

Asceticism in that sense is not part of our religion, where people abandon worldly or human desires completely. There is moderation. We are allowed to eat, but we are taught not to commit excess. Where we eat on some days freely, we also fast on some days. Where we sleep in the night, we are also encouraged to pray in the night.

And when it comes to marriage, the lawful relationship between a husband and wife is not something indecent, not something gross, not something unbefitting a believer. It is completely befitting. In fact the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said there is reward when a person has intimate relations with their spouse. The companions were surprised, and he explained: if a person were to fulfil that desire in an unlawful way, would they not incur sin? They said yes. So he explained that when a person fulfils their desire in a lawful way, there is reward in that.

So marriage is not only permissible; it is encouraged, it is rewarded, it is a sunnah, and it is a gift and a blessing in this world. Allah, who created us, knows us, and He has created us with different types of needs and has given us a religion that accommodates all of these needs in a healthy way. We are not forbidden from fulfilling our needs; we are guided to fulfil them in a healthy, responsible way.

Chapter Seventy-Six

Coolness of the Eyes in a Spouse

In the du’a of ‘ibadur-Rahman, they ask Allah for the gift of coolness of the eyes through their spouses and their children. Azwaj is the plural of zawj, and the word applies to both husband and wife. So when men make this du’a it refers to wives, and when women make it, it refers to husbands. Both can and should make it.

For Those Who Are Not Yet Married

Those who are not married, when they make this du’a, are asking for the blessing of a happy marriage. Being single is something that is hard, and finding a good spouse brings a person not only good companionship but friendship, the fulfilment of physical desire, and the completion of half their faith. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that when a worshipper of Allah gets married, he has completed half of his religion, so let him fear Allah in regard to what remains.

Because when a person gets married they are protected from a lot of wrong and indecency and unfulfilled desire; and there is a level of sukun in knowing “I am married,” so that a person is able to focus on other things in their life. This is very common: people who are not married and who want to get married — the only thing on their mind is marriage; if they meet someone, if they talk to someone, it is constantly on their mind, and they are not able to focus on their studies or their work. And in marriage there is a lot of opportunity to do good, because now a person has a supporter in the worship of Allah, someone who can remind them, who will assist them, who will worship Allah along with them, so worship becomes easier.

This does not mean marriage is a solution to all social problems. If a person has a bad habit of watching pornography, they shouldn’t think their wife will solve their addiction. If someone has bad companionship or is addicted to drugs or has any kind of issue, the family thinks: get them married, marriage is the solution to all their problems. No — it is not the solution; it is a solution, one thing that will aid them. A person must strive on their own part to leave sins. It is not correct that a person marries someone and puts them in a difficult situation, thinking that by bringing someone into their life all their problems will go away and they don’t have to do anything. They have to go through therapy, through rehab, whatever it is they need to solve their problem — and marriage is something that aids a person; it is certainly helpful.

And marriage is a human need, so there is nothing strange or shameful about wishing to marry. In Paradise the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said there are no singles; everyone will have a spouse. So if a man wishes to get married he is not being weird; if a woman wishes to get married she is not being weird. This is a completely normal, healthy human desire.

For Those Who Are Married

Those who are married, when they make this du’a, are asking for happiness in their marriage — because at times marriage can be a source of pain, a source of anguish and worry. So often it happens that a woman is crying because of her husband, out of hurt, out of feeling abandoned, out of worry; and when she is crying constantly, her eyes are burning. So qurratu a’yun is that you are asking Allah to take your worries away, to take your hurt away, to take your sadness away — and that will happen when your spouse is a means of joy for you, not a source of pain and hurt.

And when there is marital peace — both husband and wife on the same page, getting along with one another, fulfilling each other’s rights, affectionate and kind to each other, respectful, caring about each other — then a person can sleep peacefully, and the eyes can experience coolness.

And qurrah is inner happiness. It is not that you look at someone and find them beautiful and their beauty pleases you — that certainly brings joy, but qurratu a’yun is the happiness you feel in your heart. And for the believer, what makes them really happy in their marriage is when they see their spouse doing good things, when they see their spouse being a good worshipper to Allah. Their physical appearance delights them, of course, but what brings inner happiness is the piety of their spouse — because a pious spouse fears Allah in regard to their marriage. If a husband is obedient to Allah and worships Allah, he will be careful about how he is treating his wife; when a wife is fearful of Allah, she will be careful about how she is treating her husband. So this is a means of strengthening the marriage, the family, the household.

And notice that in this du’a, before asking for children, we ask for a spouse who is a coolness of the eyes. This shows us that you can only focus on your children once your marriage is settled, and you can only expect your children to be a means of joy for you when your spouse is a means of joy for you.

Allah Is Able to Change Hearts

Sometimes a person feels they are being neglected in a certain aspect of their married life, and they understand they must communicate with their spouse — but they have a lot of difficulty communicating; or they have tried and their spouse just does not understand; or they understand but don’t care; or they understand and care but don’t know how to help, don’t know how to accommodate. It is not always in their control to change the situation.

So Allah is able to open ways for His slaves. Allah is able to guide people, to give them the understanding of what they should do and how they should do things differently. And Allah is able to change the hearts of people — as the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam explained, the hearts of people are between the fingers of Allah, and He is able to turn the heart however and whenever He wants.

This is why, no matter what problem we are having in our marriage — whether it is a communication problem, or too many family members meddling in personal affairs, or not feeling connected with your spouse, or feeling neglected — ask Allah. Make this du’a.

So often it happens that people will speak to their friends for hours complaining about their spouse, or talk to their family complaining about their spouse, and the purpose of complaining is just to lighten the heaviness they feel in their heart. If we put this effort into making du’a instead — ya Allah, You improve my marriage, You make things work out — making du’a will be far more effective. And if you want to seek advice on how to improve your marriage, then go to someone who can actually help you: read a book, attend a workshop, listen to a lecture, go to a marriage counsellor. Do something to actually help your marriage. Complaining about your husband right, left and centre is not going to fix him — in fact it is going to make things worse. Complaining about your wife is not going to fix her. What is needed is that you actively seek out real help; and the first step is that you make du’a to Allah, and then you seek the advice of people who are knowledgeable, who are sincere to you, who care about you, and who will speak the truth to you even if you dislike it — because when we complain to our friends about our spouses, our friends are going to take our side; they are not necessarily going to tell us that you are wrong here, you should not be talking like that to your spouse, you should not be treating your spouse this way.

A Happy Marriage Is a Blessing of Paradise

People in Jannah will be admitted with their righteous spouses: enter Paradise, you and your spouses, delighted. Allah says those who believe and do righteous deeds will be admitted into Paradise, and there they will have purified spouses. And: gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants — meaning families will be united in Paradise; even if one person, because of their deeds, is in a lower level, their rank will be raised so they can join their righteous spouse and family. And the angels make du’a for the believers: our Lord, admit them into gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them, and whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring.

Chapter Seventy-Seven

Choosing Well, and Living Well

Finding a Righteous Spouse

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: choose the best for your offspring; and marry those who are compatible, and give in marriage to those who are compatible — in terms of deen and in other matters as well. So it is very important that a person is deliberate and careful in choosing a spouse.

Some people are so eager to get married that the first person they find willing to accept them, they say yes. Don’t have such low self-esteem or low self-worth that you think you are not good enough, so anyone who asks for your hand you have to agree. You have to see: are they compatible? Is their character such that it pleases you? Is their deen at such a level that it will be a source of strength for you?

He advised: when someone whose religion and character you are pleased with proposes, then marry your daughter or sister to him. And he said a woman is married for four things — her wealth, her family status, her beauty, and her religion — and he said: you should marry the religious woman, otherwise you will be a loser.

Why is finding a righteous spouse so important? Because a righteous spouse will fulfil their duty.

  • The best thing in a man is that when married he looks after his family and provides for his wife. Allah tells us that men are in charge of women by right of what Allah has given one over the other and because they spend from their wealth. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: what you feed yourself is sadaqah for you, what you feed your child is sadaqah for you, what you feed your wife is sadaqah for you. So when a man spends on his wife he is not wasting his money; he is being rewarded for it.
  • The best thing in a woman is that she is righteous: righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband’s absence what Allah would have them guard.
  • And both husband and wife should be loyal in marriage; they should not be taking secret lovers. With regard to men, Allah says they should be desiring chastity, not unlawful intercourse; and with regard to women, that they should be chaste, neither of those who commit unlawful intercourse nor those who take secret lovers. The standard is the same for both.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: the world is only a quick passing enjoyment, and the best enjoyment of the world is a pious and virtuous woman. So piety is what we should be seeking.

What Makes a Marriage Work

  • Live with your spouse in a good way. Allah addresses the men: live with them in kindness. You are living with someone, so live with them in a kind way — and that means you are kind to them when you look at them, when you speak with them, when you spend time with them. Kindness means you help them, you don’t abandon them, you listen to them, you show love and affection in different ways, you care about each other’s goals and work and priorities, you support each other.
  • Even if you dislike something, appreciate what is good. There is no perfect human being in this world; if you are seeking someone perfect in every way, you will not find that here — you can only find it in Jannah. So accept people as they are; you cannot expect them to be perfect, because you yourself are not perfect, and people put up with you. Allah says: and if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good. It is possible that there is something about your wife you do not like — maybe the way she laughs, or the way she irons your clothes, or that she drives around too much and uses too much gas, or that she spends without realising how much she has spent. People have different weaknesses. So whatever it is you do not like, focus on their good qualities. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said no believing husband should dislike his believing wife — if there is something about her he dislikes, he will certainly be pleased with something else about her.
  • Be gentle, not harsh. He said: act kindly toward women. Do not be harsh, do not be forceful, do not talk to a woman the way you talk to a man, do not yell at your wife the way you yell at an employee or someone on the street. Do not be violent, do not be aggressive. And this is in all matters. When you talk to her, when you are with her, be gentle, be caring. Allah describes in the Qur’an a place of cultivation for you — and when a person is dealing with plants, they cannot be harsh and aggressive; you have to be gentle and careful. Likewise men must be gentle and considerate with their wives. Even if there is something you have to tell her about, show it in a nice way, talk to her in a nice way — because if you are forceful and harsh you will cause her to break from the inside, you will hurt her feelings. And in a hadith he mentioned that a woman is like a rib, and a rib is a bone you cannot straighten — meaning accept her as she is; do not try to change her by force. Do not use force and violence and aggression in order to “straighten her out,” because you will never straighten her out; you will only break her and injure her and harm her. And when you harm her, you harm your children.
  • Play with one another. A person should be loving towards his spouse, and when he is, he is not engaging in uselessness. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam mentioned some things that are not useless amusement, and one of them is that a man and his wife play with one another. We see that he raced with ‘A’ishah; and he stood at the door while she put her chin on his shoulder so she could watch the people showing their displays in the masjid. Any kind of play husband and wife do with each other, as long as it is lawful, is permissible — in fact it is encouraged, because it helps both of them bond, build happy memories, and build fondness and love.
  • Fulfil each other’s rights. It is the right of the woman that a man provide for her and not abandon her; if he is angry with her and needs to stay away for some time, he can go — he should not kick her out. And then respect for each other, love for each other, fulfilling each other’s physical needs; all of this is essential.
  • Good akhlaq. He said: the most perfect of the believers in faith is the one whose behaviour is most excellent, and the best of you are those who are best to their wives. This is the standard. And it is important that we are not verbally abusive to one another.
  • Gratitude and patience — grateful for the blessing of marriage, and patient over the things that bother us.
  • Loyalty, not deceit. Some people are one person in front of their spouse and do very different things behind their back. There must not be secrecy and deceit in marriage. Of course people are allowed privacy — but not secrecy, because that means there is deceit, or things going on that could be harmful for the other person and would ruin the marriage.

Seven Levels of a Sound Relationship

There is a book published by the Gottman Institute in which they discuss the “sound relationship house” — that a good relationship between a husband and wife is built on seven levels.

  1. Build love maps. Know your spouse, and continue to learn about them, and continue to communicate with them and listen to them in order to stay connected. Sometimes initially when a couple marries they are very into each other, always talking, spending time together; but then over the years, as one is busy outside the house and the other inside, they barely get to talk, and they are not even familiar with what their spouse likes or doesn’t like.
  2. Share fondness and admiration. Nurture love and admiration in your marriage. At the beginning a husband and wife love one another, but over time that love tends to fade, especially as there are children and strains and stresses and conflict. So both must work on that fondness and build it. We see that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was very loving towards ‘A’ishah and showed it in many ways. She said: I would drink, and I would hand the vessel to him, and he would put his mouth where mine had been and drink from the same place; and I would eat from a bone and hand it to him, and he would put his mouth where mine had been. And the fact that they ate together also builds love and trust and fondness.
  3. Turn toward each other, not away. It is understandable that you have work and children and things to do — but throughout the day, can you appreciate the small moments of positive connection? Say salaam in the morning, smile at each other, don’t be grumpy first thing in the morning, have breakfast together, share your plan for the day, send messages, stay in touch. Turning away is when one is trying to hug and the other turns away, when one is trying to make conversation and the other closes that opportunity. Turning against is snapping back and withdrawal.
  4. Positive perspective. There is always something about your spouse you can dislike, but there is also something you can appreciate — so focus on the positive. Allah tells us: do not forget graciousness between yourselves.
  5. Manage conflict. It is not possible to eliminate conflict; you can only manage it. Conflict is very natural: if the husband thinks independently and the wife thinks independently — which is a very good sign — then they will not always agree. So just because a husband and wife disagree over something, it doesn’t mean they don’t love each other or aren’t meant to be. Having conflict does not mean the marriage is ruined. What is important is that we learn to manage it: communicate respectfully, agree to disagree, accommodate even when we do not agree.
  6. Make life dreams come true. Support your spouse in fulfilling their goals — and that means sometimes you have to make sacrifices: look after the children in the evening so your wife can study, or manage housework on your own without your husband’s help so he can study. Yes, there will be difficult periods, but in the end you will grow in your love and appreciation for one another.
  7. Create shared meaning. Together produce something good, something that will benefit others; and as a family, along with your children, create shared meaning — family rituals you make over the years, traditions you stick to, because there is something keeping all of you together and bringing joy into your life.
Chapter Seventy-Eight

The Du’as for Marriage

These du’as are collected, with their Arabic, in the memorisation tracker at the end of this book.

1. For finding a good spouse

“My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.” This is the du’a of Musa (‘alayhis salam), and it was answered right away.

When he fled from Egypt and came to Madyan, he was fearful, because the people of Fir’awn were looking for him to kill him. He didn’t know where he was going to go, where he was going to live, what he was going to do with his life. He was lost, and tired from the long journey, and he had no wealth with him. In that condition, when he saw two women struggling with their flock, unable to water them, he found that strange and went and asked what the matter was; and they explained that they wait for the shepherds to leave, and they have to do this themselves because their father is an old man. So Musa understood that these women were struggling, and that if they were to stand there they would be standing all day, and by the time the men left and they took their flock to the water, the water might be finished. So he watered their flocks for them and returned the animals to them.

He did ihsan to people without expecting any return, and with honesty: he did not take advantage of the women, he did not demand payment, he did not make conversation with them. He just did the favour he wanted to do, and then went to the shade and sat and made du’a. And when he made du’a he expressed his complete weakness before Allah: I am faqir for any good You send my way — I am desperate, I will take anything. And then when the father of the women called him, he went and was truthful and straightforward about his situation; he did not hide anything; he welcomed a good connection. And what happened? Allah granted him not only a job but a home, a wife, and security.

So make du’a to Allah. Sometimes when people are very eager to get married and can’t find someone, they think they should perhaps fall into an unlawful relationship. Musa did not do anything unlawful; he was not even perhaps seeking marriage at that time — he was asking Allah for anything good. And Allah gave him a home, a family, and a job, so that he would have stability in his life.

2. Refuge from four things

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil neighbour, and from a spouse who causes me to grow old before old age, and from a child who becomes a master over me, and from wealth that becomes a punishment for me, and from a cunning friend whose eye watches me and whose heart plots against me, such that if he sees something good he buries it and if he sees something bad he spreads it.”

  • An evil neighbour — because if someone who lives next to you bothers you, hurts you, constantly harasses you, then your life becomes very difficult; you don’t find safety and comfort in your own home. And if you don’t find safety and comfort in your own home, where else will you find it?
  • A spouse who causes you to age before old age — who causes you to grow grey hair before you are supposed to. And why would a person age quickly because of their spouse? Because that spouse is a source of stress and worry, not a source of sukun: they are constantly doing things damaging to the family, their speech is very vulgar, their habits are indecent, or they have endless demands, or they are always negative and always unhappy, or you feel constantly abandoned by them and unsupported. And this doesn’t mean you are asking Allah to get rid of such a spouse; rather you are asking Allah to fix them for you. And people can change.
  • A child who becomes a master over you — extremely disobedient, very bossy, very demanding, very arrogant.
  • Wealth that becomes a punishment — where a person is constantly looking after their wealth and property, and the constant care it needs is a source of great hardship.
  • A friend who plots against you — who is constantly watching you and appears to be a friend, but is actually looking for a mistake you made; and if he sees something good in you he hides it and pretends you never did it, and if he sees something bad he spreads it.

3. Join our hearts and mend our relationship

“O Allah, join our hearts, and mend our relationship, and guide us to the ways of peace, and bring us out of darkness into light, and save us from indecencies, those that are apparent and those that are hidden. And bless us in our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses and our children, and accept our repentance — indeed You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. And make us grateful for Your blessings, those who praise You for them, those who accept them; and perfect these blessings for us.”

Sometimes a husband and wife are coexisting: there is no love, no feelings of care and concern for each other; the hearts are not united. So make this du’a. And sometimes there have been so many problems, so many fights, so many negative things that have happened and negative patterns established. So ask Allah: ya Allah, mend our relationship. And guide us to the ways of peace — those things that will be peaceful in our relationship, not damaging, not disruptive. And bring us out of darkness into light — because sometimes both the husband and wife fall into a sin they are committing together, or into a bad pattern, where for instance both of them begin to miss Fajr every day out of habit, or both develop the habit of using foul language or committing certain sins. And bless us in our hearing, our eyes and our hearts — give us the ability to use these faculties in obedience, to listen to something good, to see something good, to think and believe in something good; because barakah is increase and growth. And bless for us our spouses and children by giving them the ability to do good, because when they do good, I will also do good. And make us of those who are grateful for the blessings, because sometimes people, even though they have a marriage and children, are very ungrateful for their marriage, for their spouse, for their house, for their children.

4. Guide me to the best of conduct

“And guide me to the best of manners, for none can guide to the best of them except You; and turn away from me bad manners, for none can turn them away from me except You.”

A lot of times relationships are ruined and destroyed because of bad akhlaq — because of anger, rudeness, foul language, hurtful speech. So ask Allah for good akhlaq. Outside the house you can pretend; you can be pretentious; even though you are angry you can smile. But inside the house, with your spouse, you are who you actually are — so if your akhlaq is not actually good, you cannot fake it with your spouse. Your akhlaq needs to become good so that your marriage will work and will not suffer.

Sometimes when husband and wife are angry with each other, they say such rude things as they would not say to anyone else; they roll their eyes at each other, they snatch, they stomp, they act in such a bad way — and when you reflect on yourself afterwards you think: what is wrong with me? How could I behave like that? How could I respond like that? Why am I behaving so arrogantly? So ask Allah: guide me to the best of conduct, because none can guide to that except You.

So continue to make du’a to Allah to grant you a righteous spouse, to grant you happiness in your marriage, and to make you a good spouse for your spouse.

Ameen.
Chapter Seventy-Nine

Why Salah Comes First

The main reason we pray salah is to remember Allah. He said to Musa (‘alayhis salam): establish salah for My remembrance. So in one’s life, throughout the day, a person turns towards Allah in order to remember Him. Yes, we remember Allah throughout the day, but five times a day in a formal way, through ritual worship, we remember Him: His greatness, His perfection, the fact that He alone is the creator, the owner, the sustainer, and that He alone is worthy of worship. And salah has been obligated so that we are able to maintain these feelings throughout the day.

Everything in the universe glorifies Allah. We learn about the angels that they glorify Him constantly, in the night and in the day, and they do not slacken. So we should also declare the perfection of Allah, and the best way to do that is in salah.

Knowledge, Faith and Action

Allah mentions the establishers of prayer alongside those firm in knowledge: but those firm in knowledge among them, and the believers, believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you — and the establishers of prayer especially, and the givers of zakah, and the believers in Allah and the Last Day: those We will give a great reward.

So salah is one of those deeds for which Allah has promised a great reward. It is no ordinary action; it is not something you do only when you are free or have nothing else to do.

Rasikhun means those who are firmly rooted — a tree that is firmly rooted does not get uprooted by winds or storms. People deeply rooted in knowledge are not perfect or complete in it, because there is no limit to it; rather they are firm in what they know. They believe in the truth, they have beneficial knowledge, and they do not blindly follow the trends of the people of the world; they follow evidence. And with this knowledge there is also action, because Allah mentions that they establish salah and give zakah. So firmness in knowledge is that a person has knowledge of the truth, believes in that truth, and then acts upon it. And when a person is firmly rooted in knowledge, they are protected from deviation; they do not get swayed by their surroundings.

There is a deep relationship between ‘ilm, iman and ‘amal salih. When a person has knowledge of the truth and understands it and believes in it, their knowledge leads to iman; and their iman leads to action; and action in return strengthens their faith. So it is not enough that a person says “I believe” and that is sufficient. With iman we must strengthen both sides: our knowledge and our actions, because both preserve and strengthen our iman. And iman is the most valuable blessing a person has — more precious than their car, their house, their bank account, everything they own.

Establishing, Not Just Performing

Salah is also called iman in the Qur’an: Allah will not waste your faith — and what is meant there is your salah. Salah is essential to one’s iman; if a person does not pray salah, their iman is questionable.

And it is not enough to just do salah. Allah says: the establishers of prayer.
