To establish salah is to perform it properly and correctly, fulfilling all of the conditions, observing all of the pillars and the obligatory actions, and perfecting it with the recommended deeds as well. Ibn ‘Abbas said that establishing salah is to properly perform the ruku’ and the sajdah — not rushing through them — and that you recite Qur’an, and that you observe your salah with khushu’, with humility and attentiveness. And Qatadah said that establishing salah is to guard the times of salah, making sure you perform it at the right time, and making the ruku’ and sujud properly, not speeding through them.

The Purpose of Our Lives

Salah linguistically means to pray; technically it is an act of worship performed by saying certain words and performing certain actions, which begins with takbir and ends with taslim — it begins when you say Allahu Akbar and ends when you say as-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah.

The ultimate goal of our lives is to worship Allah; that is the reason He created us. So out of all the things that are important in your life, what is at the top of the list? Salah. Salah is literally the purpose of our lives. So if in a day you are not able to finish an assignment, not able to get your chores done, not able to prepare any food for yourself, not able to accomplish anything on your to-do list — but you are able to perform the five daily prayers, then you have fulfilled the purpose of your life for that day. This doesn’t mean other things are not important; they are. But salah is more important than anything else you can busy yourself with.

When the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was asked which deed is most beloved to Allah, he said: performing salah at its proper time. When a person becomes a Muslim, the first thing they learn is to perform salah; it is the first and foremost act of worship. When children are taught to worship Allah, the first thing they are taught is to pray. Salah comes before fasting, before Hajj, before other acts of worship.

And all of the prophets performed salah. Musa was told: establish salah for My remembrance. Ibrahim prayed: my Lord, make me an establisher of prayer. He left Isma’il in the middle of the desert — and why? So that they would establish salah. ‘Isa, when he was a baby and spoke in defence of his mother, mentioned that Allah had commanded him to pray salah and give zakah for as long as he lived. Maryam was told: be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate. Luqman advised his son: O my son, establish salah. And Allah commands His slaves to establish prayer; it is a sign of sincere believers.

Salah is the second pillar of Islam. Allah has obligated five prayers during the day and the night, and the person who performs them properly and is not negligent about them will have a covenant with Allah on the Day of Judgment that Allah will admit him into Jannah; but the person who neglects his salah will not have such a covenant — it is up to Allah: if He wants He can punish that person, and if He wants He can forgive him.

Two times a day Allah asks His angels about our salah. Angels attend to us, observing our actions and recording our deeds, in two shifts; and as the shift changes they return to Allah, and He asks them: how did you find My slaves, and how did you leave My slaves? And if a person is of those who perform salah, the angels reply: when we left them they were praying, and when we reached them they were praying.

So there is no religiosity in a person if they do not pray salah. Sometimes we try to belittle its importance by saying, “I don’t pray, but I’m very respectful, and I am honest, and I am nice to my family, and my faith is in my heart.” Or, “I wear the hijab, I wear the niqab, I look after my parents, but when it comes to salah I’m not that consistent.” No. Real religiosity is that a person is loyal to Allah and fulfils the purpose of their existence by worshipping Him — and the worship Allah has obligated on us is salah. Salah is what differentiates between Islam and kufr.

And we are commanded not just to perform salah but to guard it: and guard the prayers. And to pray ourselves and also remind our family members: instruct your family to pray, and be steadfast therein — steadfast in performing it yourself, and steadfast in telling your family to pray. Children are to pray from the age of seven, so don’t be lazy in teaching them and reminding them.

Salah is so important that people are required to pray even in the thick of battle; and at the time of the Dajjal also salah will still be obligated, and the believers will pray. And the last words of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam before he departed this world were about salah: as-salah, as-salah — and be conscious of Allah regarding those whom your right hands possess.

And the first question we will be asked on the Day of Judgment is regarding our salah; this is how the reckoning will begin. So if a person passes the test of salah, the rest of the reckoning will also be easy; but if they get stuck there, everything else will be difficult.

What Salah Brings

  • Success: successful indeed are the believers, those who are humble in their prayers.
  • Mercy: the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that when one of you stands in prayer, the mercy of Allah is before him. And Allah says: establish prayer and give zakah and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
  • Sustenance, and freedom from poverty and dependency on people.
  • The du’as of the angels; and Allah brings a person out of their worry and their fear, and helps and guards and protects them.
  • Healing. Ibn al-Qayyim said that remembering Allah and turning towards Him and eagerly praying salah is something because of which many who were ill have been cured and granted safety and well-being. And illness is not just physical; it includes spiritual illness — the doubts we may have, the desires that constantly distract and burden us.
  • Erasing of sins, and protection from indecent and immoral actions. Because think about it: if a person has to pray five times a day with attentiveness and awareness of what they are saying, how can they indulge in indecent actions between two prayers? Salah breaks bad habits. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was asked about a man who prays but then goes and commits theft, and he said: if he is as you have said, then his salah will stop him eventually.
  • Real joy and comfort. He said: the coolness of my eye has been placed in salah. And he said that the person whose eyes are cooled through salah in this world will, in the Hereafter, have them cooled by closeness to Allah. Because salah allows you to experience closeness to Allah: in salah you are not allowed to talk to anyone, and in fact you should not even be thinking about anything; the entire focus should be on Allah.
  • On the Day of Judgment the limbs of those who pray will glow; this will be their distinctive mark. And salah will be a light and a proof and a salvation on that day, and a protection against the Fire.

And Neglecting It

If a person neglects salah, this is extremely dangerous, because it leads a person to kufr and to shirk, and deprives a person of their faith. Ibn Mas’ud would say: the one who leaves prayer has no religion.

Ibn al-Qayyim said there are six things in salah that are signs of hypocrisy: showing laziness in going towards salah; praying in order to be seen by people, so that people are happy that yes, she is someone who prays; delaying in performing salah, procrastinating, doing everything else before going towards it; praying very quickly, rushing through it; remembering Allah very little in salah — a person is praying but doesn’t remember Allah at all, constantly thinking about what they are going to do, what they are going to cook, what they are going to eat next; and not praying in congregation.

We also learn that the person who deliberately leaves salah loses the protection of Allah; and the one who loses one salah, it is as if he has lost his property and his family. If you have ever heard of people losing their homes to a fire, and the damage not only to property but the news that children died in the fire, that an entire family died — imagine what a huge loss that is. Losing one salah is greater than that loss.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the one who leaves the ‘Asr prayer, his actions are wasted. The ulama say this is about the one who delays ‘Asr without a genuine reason — out of procrastination and laziness, delaying and delaying until they end up missing it.

In the Qur’an we learn that the death of those who do not pray is very painful: and the leg is wound about the leg; to your Lord that day will be the procession. And he neither believed nor prayed, but instead he denied and turned away. And we learn that the person who does not pray will be with Qarun and Fir’awn and Haman and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

So we should pray: ya Allah, make me someone who establishes salah; make my children those who establish salah. And we should think about what we are saying in salah — because when we know what we are saying we are able to focus better, and then we are able to enjoy our salah, and then we can be consistent with it.

Chapter Eighty

Takbir, and the Opening Du’as

Salah begins with takbiratul-ihram, saying Allahu Akbar. It is called takbiratul-ihram because everything that was permissible before saying it becomes impermissible after saying it. A person is allowed to eat and drink and talk to people, look here and there, go in and out, walk around — these are all permissible acts. But once you say Allahu Akbar and begin salah, you cannot eat, you cannot drink, you cannot talk to people, you cannot even look here and there, you cannot go out of the room and come back.

And saying Allahu Akbar is a pillar of salah, without which there is no salah; without it salah does not begin.

You say Allahu Akbar many times in salah, and takbir is connected to salah in every way. Before salah there is the adhan, and in the adhan there is takbir. Then there is the iqamah, and in it there is takbir. When you begin salah you begin with Allahu Akbar. And every time you move from one step of salah to the next, you say Allahu Akbar in every transition, except when rising from ruku’. So takbir is the sha’ar, the symbol, of salah — just as the talbiyah is the sha’ar of Hajj. When people go for Hajj, what do they say constantly? Labbayk Allahumma labbayk. And in salah, what do we say constantly? Allahu Akbar.

So the secret of salah is ta’zim of Allah — to glorify and magnify Him and express His greatness. Ibn Hajar said that takbir is a dhikr said at a time of shock, surprise and fear. In the sirah we see that on many occasions when frightening news was given to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, he said Allahu Akbar. And you say Allahu Akbar at a time of happiness too, like on the day of ‘Eid, in order to show gratitude. And you say it at a time of fear, because you remind yourself that Allah is greater — greater than this problem that has come my way, and capable of helping me.

Allahu Akbar means Allah is the greatest. So the person praying says it in salah to declare that Allah is greater than anything else I could be doing right now. Allah is greater than the essay I was just typing — that is why I left it and came and started praying. Allah is greater than the food I was cooking. And in salah, when anything distracts you — the food, the essay, what people are saying — you say Allahu Akbar: Allah is greater than anything that could distract me or hinder me from salah.

And saying Allahu Akbar again and again saves a person from two major disasters. First, takabbur, pride and arrogance — because we think I am great, I am able to do this, I can do that; and Allahu Akbar reminds you that Allah is greater than you. Second, it protects you from turning towards someone other than Allah — because when you keep declaring Allah is greater, then Allah is greater than anything I love, greater than anyone I love, greater than anyone I fear, greater than anything I am concerned about; He is more worthy of my attention, more worthy that I talk to Him and glorify Him and converse with Him.

Al-‘Izz ibn ‘Abd as-Salam says about the wisdom of takbir in salah that the purpose of salah is to remember Allah, and in order to do that it is necessary to know the greatness of the one you are remembering. Sadly, when people are praying, sometimes they are looking here and there, not moving their lips, not saying anything — or they have the audacity to stand in prayer without wudu. And that is because they don’t recognise the greatness of the one they are remembering. Salah begins with takbir, which proclaims the greatness of Allah, so that a person knows who it is they are standing before, and sitting before in tashahhud, and making ruku’ and sajdah for. So when you remember the majesty of Allah by saying Allahu Akbar, you are able to show obedience and proper humility, observe proper adab, and ensure you have purification both external and internal — and only then can you focus on your conversation with Allah.

And when you say Allahu Akbar you also raise your hands — and when you raise your hands you are throwing behind yourself everything else and everyone else, focusing entirely on Allah. And the person who stands properly before Allah in salah will be able to stand properly on the Day of Judgment also.

After saying Allahu Akbar we place our hands on the chest, and our eyes should be looking at the place of sajdah — not to the right, not to the left, not at our hands or our toes or our clothes.

The Opening Du’as

Ibn al-Qayyim says that the secret of salah and its essence is that a person is attentive towards his Lord, making his heart present before Allah, not allowing it to get distracted. This is the entire struggle in salah. And he says that in salah the slave is similar to a person who goes towards the door of a king in order to meet him: before this meeting he needs forgiveness for his sins, and he needs to ask for the generosity of the king and for provision in order to have the strength to meet him; and when he reaches the door of the king, there remains nothing other than conversation with the king. This is why, before we recite Surat al-Fatihah — which is a conversation with Allah — we ask Allah for forgiveness, and praise and glorify Him, and ask Him to shower His blessings on us. We say the du’as of istiftah.

1. Allah is the greatest, the most great

“Allah is the greatest, the most great; praise be to Allah in abundance; and glory be to Allah at the break of day and in the evening.” Ibn ‘Umar reported that while they were praying with the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam a man said these words, and afterwards he asked who had said them. A man said: it is I. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that it amazed him, because the doors of the sky were opened for these words. So Ibn ‘Umar said: I have not left these words since I heard him say that.

And in this we are declaring the greatness of Allah along with His praise, while showing gratitude — and this brings contentment to the heart. When we declare Allah’s greatness we find ease; our problems are solved, our worries removed, our sorrow dispelled; our iman is strengthened; and the doors of goodness are opened for us. And we say “in the morning and in the evening” — because this is when the angels give the report of our deeds to Allah.

2. Set me apart from my sins

“O Allah, set me apart from my sins as far as the east is set apart from the west. O Allah, cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. O Allah, wash away my sins with water, snow and hail.”

First you are asking Allah to create a distance between you and your sins — a distance like that between the east and the west, a distance that can never be eliminated, because the east and the west can never be joined together. So you are asking for a permanent distance: take me far away from my sins and take my sins far away from me. You are asking for forgiveness for your past sins and for protection from committing sins in the future.

Secondly: cleanse me of my sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt. After thorough washing, the stains are removed and the garment is completely clean. So you are asking Allah to remove your sins and also to remove the effect of sins from you — because sins do have an impact.

And thirdly: wash away my sins with water, snow and hail. Three things — because if you are cleaning a garment and you put it through one wash cycle, and then leave it to soak, and then wash it again, through multiple rounds of cleaning, it is because you want to make sure it is completely clean. And why ask for something cool and cold like snow and hail? Because sins have a heat, a fire; and water and hail and snow are cool, and the water of hail and snow and rain is completely pure, untouched by the hands of people; it is pure and purifying. And when it comes to removing stains, cold water is often more effective than hot.

And you are asking Allah for ease in the removal of sins. Because one way a person is purified of their sins is in the fire of Hell — and we seek Allah’s refuge from that. Many who believe will, because of their sins, end up in the Fire and be purified by experiencing the punishment of those sins, and then be removed and admitted into Paradise. So we are asking: ya Allah, don’t purify me through fire; purify me through water, snow and hail, because You are able to forgive all sins. And sometimes leaving a bad habit or a sin is painful and hard, and a person struggles — so you are asking Allah for ease in that process.

3. Glory and praise be to You

“Glory is to You, O Allah, and praise; blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and none has the right to be worshipped but You.” The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would begin his salah with these words, so we should also begin with them — because in them we are glorifying Allah, praising Him, and declaring His perfection and greatness.

4. The opening of the night prayer

“I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth, unswerving in the worship of Allah alone, and I am not of those who associate partners with Allah. Verily my salah, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, the Lord of all that exists; He has no partner, and of this I have been commanded, and I am one of the Muslims.

O Allah, You are the Sovereign; there is none worthy of worship but You. You are my Lord and I am Your slave. I have wronged myself and I have confessed my sins, so forgive me all of my sins — none can forgive sins except You. And guide me to the best manners; none can guide to the best of manners except You. And turn away from me evil conduct; none can turn it away from me except You. O Allah, I am here at Your service; all goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You. I rely on You and I turn to You. Blessed are You, exalted are You; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.”

After the du’a of istiftah we seek refuge with Allah against Shaytan, and we can also say that we seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan — from his evil suggestions, from his puffing up (meaning making a person feel arrogant), and from his spitting, meaning from his influence. Then we recite Surat al-Fatihah, and after it some portion of the Qur’an.

Chapter Eighty-One

In Ruku’, and Rising From It

Then we say Allahu Akbar and go into ruku’. Ruku’ is described as a third of salah, and it should be performed properly, such that our back is completely straight. And in ruku’ we should observe stillness — we should come to a complete stop.

Some people, when they are driving and reach a stop sign, don’t make a complete stop; they make a rolling stop and then drive off. Some don’t even bother to stop. And if a police officer sees you doing that, there are consequences, because that is not a complete stop. In salah, in every position, we have to come to a complete stop — including ruku’. Become completely still before getting up from it. And as you are still, say the adhkar of ruku’.

Three Kinds of Humility

When we say words of glorification in ruku’ we are showing three types of humility. First, through our limbs: we are not standing up straight; we are bending our bodies, physically showing humility before Allah — not just lowering our eyes or our heads, but literally lowering our back. Secondly, through our tongue, by saying words of glorification. And thirdly, with ta’zim in our hearts — with respect and reverence and humility.

What to Say in Ruku’

  • “Glory be to my Lord, the Ever Great.”
  • “Perfect and Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.” Some ulama say that ar-Ruh here refers to Jibreel, and some say it refers to creatures hidden even from the angels. Angels can see us; we cannot see them — but they cannot see ar-Ruh.
  • “Glory and praise be to You; there is none worthy of worship but You.”
  • “Glory and praise be to You, O Allah, our Lord. O Allah, forgive me.”
  • “Glory and praise be to You; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.”
  • “Glory be to the Master of power, dominion, majesty and greatness.”
  • “O Allah, to You I have bowed, and in You I believe, and to You I surrender. My hearing, my sight, my brain, my bones and my nerves are humbled before You.”

In ruku’ you are completely erasing your own greatness — by bending your body, and by saying words of glorification. And you are supposed to glorify Allah for long; at times the ruku’ of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would be as long as his qiyam. So say “Glory be to my Lord, the Ever Great” three times, and then say the others.

One of the reasons we do not find joy in salah is that we repeat the same words over and over again, and we say them with our mouths and not with our hearts, while our hearts are somewhere else. So it is necessary that we learn different adhkar and bring variety into our salah, because that will help us with our khushu’.

Rising From Ruku’

After ruku’ is the qawmah — you get up again, and this standing position is shorter than the first one, but in it we should be completely straight, standing completely upright. And as we stand upright, again we glorify and praise Allah.

First, as we rise, we say: “Allah has heard the one who praised Him.” And then: “Our Lord, for You is all praise” — and there are different ways of saying this, and it is good to bring that variety into salah.

  • “Our Lord, for You is praise — abundant, pure and blessed praise.”
  • “O Allah, our Lord, for You is praise that would fill the heavens and fill the earth and fill whatever else You will.”
  • And to that we can add: “You are worthy of all praise and glory; the truest thing a slave has said, and all of us are Your slaves. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy cannot avail him against You.”
  • And in another du’a of the qawmah: “O Allah, purify me with snow, hail and cold water; O Allah, cleanse me of sins and errors just as a white garment is cleansed of dirt.”

Isn’t this amazing? He worshipped Allah in the most beautiful way, and this is why his example is the best example for us. We cannot come up with such beautiful, complete words; we can only learn them from him. And in these words we are taught to seek forgiveness from Allah — we just did that at the beginning, and now again after ruku’, when we glorify and praise Allah, we again ask Him for forgiveness and purification.

Chapter Eighty-Two

In Sajdah, and in the Tashahhud

In sajdah a person is in the closest position possible to Allah on this earth. Allah tells us: prostrate and draw near. Because in sajdah you cannot even see anyone; you are literally putting your head on the ground, and what you see is just the ground. In this position, lowering yourself completely, placing yourself on seven bones — your two hands, your knees, your feet, and your forehead and nose — you are close to Allah. And this is why we should make a lot of du’a in sajdah.

For every sajdah you are rewarded, your sins are erased, your ranks are raised. And the parts of the body involved in making sajdah — those seven bones — are forbidden to the Fire; even if a person ends up in the Fire because of some other sins, the fire will not consume those parts of the body.

And in sajdah, because we are closest to Allah, we should begin with His praise and glorification, and then ask Him.

  • “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
  • “O Allah, forgive me what I have concealed and what I have done openly” — you are conversing with Allah; this is a private conversation. My sins that only You know of, ya Allah, forgive all of them.
  • “Perfect and Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.”
  • “Glory be to You, O Allah, and all praise be to You; there is no deity except You.”
  • “Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and all praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me.”
  • “Glory be to the One who has all power, sovereignty, magnificence and might.”
  • “O Allah, forgive me all my sins — the small and the great, the first and the last, the open and the secret.”
  • “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and in Your forgiveness from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot account for Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.” So: ya Allah, even when You are angry with me for something I am guilty of, still You protect me from Your punishment. And I cannot praise You enough; You deserve even more.
  • “O Allah, before You I prostrate, and in You I believe, and to You I have submitted. My face is prostrated before the One who created it and fashioned it and brought forth its hearing and its sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.”
  • And the du’a of light — asking Allah for light in the heart, in the hearing, in the vision, on the right, on the left, in front, behind, above and below. Asking Allah to fill us with light.

The Sitting Between the Two Sajdahs

When we get up from sajdah and go back into sajdah again, we have to sit; and in this sitting position again we must become completely still. Some people do not observe stillness here; they get up from sajdah and go right back into it. No — when you get up from sajdah, sit still. And when you are still, say: “My Lord, forgive me. My Lord, forgive me.” And you can say this over and over again, not just twice; the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say it repeatedly.

The Tashahhud

In the tashahhud you glorify and praise Allah, send salat and salam upon the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and upon the righteous slaves of Allah, and then make du’a.

You begin: “All greetings are for Allah, and prayers and good words.” Tahiyyat means good words or words of greeting; the Arabs would greet one another with words meaning “may you live a long life.” So “all greetings are for Allah” means you are greeting and complimenting Allah. Salawat refers to the five daily prayers — and not just them, but every form of worship and every du’a — and you are dedicating that to Allah alone. And tayyibat means good words, words of dhikr, pure words, words of praise and glorification — and not just words; tayyibat also means good actions. So when you say this you are dedicating your words of worship, your actions of worship, and all other forms of worship including your charity and your spending, to Allah alone.

Then you say: “Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous slaves of Allah.” Isn’t this beautiful? You make du’a for the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and then for yourself and all of the righteous slaves of Allah. When you say this in salah you are making du’a for every righteous slave of Allah — whether they lived before, are alive now, or will come to the earth after you have left the world. So often people ask you to make du’a for them; when you say this, you are including all of the righteous slaves of Allah.

Then you say the words of the shahadah: “I testify that there is no deity but Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is His slave and His messenger.” And after that you send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. And remember that this is the best way of making du’a: you begin with words of glorification and praise for Allah, you send salutations upon the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and then you make du’a.

The Du’as After the Tashahhud

  • “O Allah, I have greatly wronged myself, and none forgives sins except You; so grant me forgiveness from Yourself and have mercy on me — indeed You are the Ever Forgiving, the Ever Merciful.” Here we are confessing our sins and acknowledging that no one can forgive sins except Allah, and asking for great forgiveness from Himself and for His mercy, because He is able to forgive all sins and is very merciful to His slaves.
  • “O Allah, forgive me my former and latter sins, what I have done secretly and what I have done openly, and where I have exceeded the limits, and those faults of mine of which You have better knowledge than I. You are the One who brings forward and the One who delays; there is no deity except You.”
  • “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, and from the punishment of the grave, and from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the trial of the Dajjal.” Here you are asking Allah to protect you from the greatest dangers. And the trial of death is that a person makes such a mistake at the time of death that their good deeds are nullified — because Shaytan does not leave a person even at that time. In another version we also seek refuge from sin and from debt: ya Allah, protect me from sin I do not even realise, and from the financial burden that makes life very difficult.
  • “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from stinginess, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit old age, and I seek refuge in You from the trials of this world and from the punishment of the grave.”
  • “O Allah, I ask You, because to You belongs all praise; there is no god but You, the Bestower of favours, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Sustainer — indeed I ask You.” And in a hadith we learn that when you make du’a to Allah with these words, your du’as are accepted and you are given what you ask for.

And remember that at the end of salah, before saying the salam, is an excellent time to ask Allah for whatever you want. So after these words you can ask Allah for anything.

And then we say as-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, to those on our right and those on our left. And remember that when you send salam to others, the same is for you — because when you make du’a for someone else, the same du’a is made for you.

Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdik, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilaik.
Chapter Eighty-Three

Glorify Him Before the Sun Rises

The remembrance of Allah is a very significant act of worship. It is something that Allah loves, and it is something that draws us closer to Him. And Allah tells us to remember Him, to make dhikr, in many, many places in the Qur’an. In fact, we are taught not only to remember Allah, but to remember Allah kathira — in abundance, and very frequently. And there are many, many benefits associated with the dhikr of Allah.

The Qur’an

“So be patient over what they say, and exalt Allah with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting. And in part of the night exalt Him, and after prostration.”

Here the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is specifically addressed, and he is instructed to be patient over what the people say — meaning be patient over the hurtful things the idolaters said to him: their words of rejection, denial, mockery, and their threats. So he is told: be patient. And then he is told wa sabbih bi hamdi rabbik — occupy yourself with the tasbih of your Lord, with the praise of your Lord.

Negation and Affirmation Together

Notice that he has not just been instructed to do tasbih, or just to make hamd. There is a combination here: sabbih bi hamdi rabbik — do tasbih along with the hamd of your Lord. And we see that in many of the adhkar: for example SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, or Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, where we are declaring tasbih along with hamd.

Tasbih is to declare Allah’s perfection and His freedom from anything that is unbefitting — whether it is the lies that people say about Him, or the criticism they dare to say about Allah, or the fault they find in His actions, His words, or His attributes, or that they associate an equal or partner or child with Allah. So when you say SubhanAllah, you are declaring Allah’s perfection and His freedom from anything unbefitting.

And in hamd, you are affirming His perfect qualities that befit Him. So when you do tasbih along with tahmid, you are combining the negation and the affirmation. Negation of what? Of anything that is unbefitting. And affirmation of what? Of the perfect qualities that befit Him. With the negation and the affirmation together, this is complete and perfect praise.

So the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is instructed here that on the one hand be patient over what the people say, and then occupy yourself with the glorification and praise of Allah. Combine the glorification and the praise.

❖  ❖  ❖

Which Times Are Meant

The ulama say that here tasbih means salah, because he is told wa sabbih bi hamdi rabbik at specific times. Which times? Before the rising of the sun, before the setting, and in the night. So they say tasbih here means salah: before the rising of the sun is the Fajr prayer; before the setting of the sun is Zuhr and ‘Asr; and in the night is Maghrib and ‘Isha. So here the five daily prayers are mentioned.

Other ulama say that tasbih here also refers to the dhikr of Allah: that especially do tasbih at these times — before the rising of the sun, before the setting of the sun, and also in the night. And if you think about it, these three times are excellent for making dhikr.

First thing in the morning when you wake up and you are getting ready for your day, your mind is occupied with the things you want to do. And as you think about all the work you have to do, or the hurtful things people have been saying, or the difficult people you have to deal with, you almost don’t want to start your day. So you begin with the tasbih of Allah, reminding yourself of Allah’s perfection, of His perfect ability. And this allows you to realise that you are not alone. On the other hand, it allows you to realise that if you are facing difficulty from people, this is because you are human — you are not perfect. It is only Allah who is perfect.

Then before the setting of the sun, meaning before Maghrib in the evening — and then in the night also. Why in the night? Because in the night, what is it that wakes you up? It is your worries. It is the things that cause you stress. Sometimes because of illness a person is not able to sleep, or because of one’s children a person’s sleep is constantly disrupted throughout the night. So don’t get frustrated at that time. Busy your tongue in the glorification and praise of Allah, and dealing with difficulties and challenges will become easier — because then you will know that you are not wasting your time. You know that you are engaged in one of the best acts of worship, which is the dhikr of Allah.

“And After Prostration”

At the end of the ayah, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is also told: glorify Allah with His praise wa adbar as-sujud — after the prostration. And adbar as-sujud, the ulama said, is that you should glorify Allah after you complete your sujud, meaning after you complete your salah. So this is referring to the dhikr after salah.

Ibn ‘Abbas (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that Allah instructed His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam to make tasbih after salah — and he used this ayah to prove that. And Mujahid explains that this is tasbih after the fard prayer especially. Meaning throughout the day you perform the fard prayer, and you also perform sunnah prayer, maybe some voluntary prayer, nafl prayer. The dhikr that we have been instructed to do here is the dhikr after the fard prayer, the obligatory prayers.

It has also been said that wa adbar as-sujud includes praying voluntary prayer after the obligatory prayer. So for example, when a person performs the four rak‘ah of ‘Asr, then makes dhikr, and after that adbar as-sujud again — meaning now get up and perform some voluntary prayer, perform two rak‘ah. And specifically, the ulama say this is referring to the two rak‘ah after Maghrib, because that also has special significance.

Chapter Eighty-Four

For Indeed You Are in Our Eyes

The Qur’an

“And be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our eyes. And exalt Allah with praise of your Lord when you arise. And in a part of the night exalt Him, and after the setting of the stars.”

In this ayah also the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is instructed to be patient. Be patient over what? Li hukmi rabbik. This has been interpreted as ‘ala hukmi rabbik — be patient over the command of your Lord. The things that Allah has commanded you to do, be patient with them. Do them properly. Do them with consistency. Do not give up and do not get bored.

And sometimes we feel like that: that we begin an act of worship with a lot of excitement, and at the beginning we are very attentive. For example, since Ramadan began, every day a person is very eager to perform certain acts of worship. But then what happens after the first ten days? There is a dip. There is a low. So here, wasbir li hukmi rabbik — over whatever your Lord has commanded you to do, be patient with that, be consistent, and do not give up, do not quit, do not slacken, do not get bored.

And then he is told: fa innaka bi a’yunina — for indeed you are in Our eyes. Meaning: We know what you are doing. We know you. We are watching you. And We are guarding you against your enemies. So carry on doing what you are supposed to do, and don’t fear your enemy.

How Do You Calm Your Heart?

It is one thing to know cognitively that I should not get bored, and I should not get worried, and I should not be afraid, and I should be patient. But to do it practically — your heart is not in your control. Your feelings are not always in your control. So how do you console yourself? How do you manage your emotions? How do you calm your heart, calm your nerves?

Wa sabbih bi hamdi rabbik. The solution is given here: glorify Allah, exalt Allah with His praise. And especially when? Hina taqum — at the time when you get up.

❖  ❖  ❖

When You Rise From a Gathering

Hina taqum means first of all that when you rise — when you get up from any gathering, from any place where you were with people and now you are getting up — then at that time say Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.

Why glorify and praise Allah then? Because that will be a means of expiation for anything that was inappropriate in the gathering. And it happens sometimes that you are sitting with people and you would think that gathering or that meeting would bring you joy or some kind of relief, but then as you get up you feel so guilty, you feel so horrible — because there was backbiting, or there was gossip, or there were negative things said, and you feel as though that gathering was such a burden. Or people have been extremely critical of you and have discouraged you from worshipping Allah, from doing certain good things. So say this.

And this is something we should say when we get up from any gathering — whether it is a gathering of knowledge, or a gathering where we just sat together and talked, or we were sitting and just relaxing with our friends, eating, and so on. When you get up from a gathering, glorify Allah with His praise.

When You Rise From Sleep

Secondly, “when you get up” also means when you get up from sleep. Whether you get up in the night — for example at Fajr time — or during the day when you get up from your nap: when you wake up, at that time make dhikr of Allah. The first thing you should say on waking up is the tasbih of your Lord along with His praise.

Mention Him — because in hadith we learn that when a person begins his day with the dhikr of Allah, then the angel is in his company, and so the influence of goodness will be stronger on you. And if you do not remember Allah at that time, then the influence of shaytan will be stronger.

When You Rise in Salah

And the imams said that this is especially when you get up in salah. Because in salah, what are you doing? You go down into ruku‘ and you get up. You go down into sajdah and you get up. You are going down and getting up. So in salah, make dhikr, make tasbih. This is why in sajdah we say Subhana Rabbiyal A’la, and in ruku‘ we say Subhana Rabbiyal ‘Azim. And we say other tasbihat in which there is also hamd. In salah we also glorify and praise Allah at the beginning: the du’a al-istiftah is what? You are glorifying Allah with His praise — Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, wa tabarakasmuka, wa ta’ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk.

And in the Night, Again

And then it is said: wa min al-layli fa sabbihhu — and in the night, again glorify Him. And isn’t this amazing? All day long — in the morning, in salah, any time you get up from a gathering, after salah — what are you doing? You are glorifying Allah with His praise. But then even in the night, glorify Allah again. SubhanAllah. And there is no end to the tasbih of Allah. There is always more tasbih that you can do, because Allah is always, always praiseworthy. And we are always in a situation where we should be glorifying and praising Allah, because we are constantly receiving His favours.

And glorification and praise of Allah is something that even the people of paradise will do — they will glorify and praise Allah as easily as we breathe. So we have to get used to that here: that on our tongue is the tasbih and the tahmid of Allah.

In the night especially, what does this mean? Since tasbih also means salah, this means that in the night perform qiyam al-layl. And in the month of Ramadan, qiyam al-layl is very important, very beneficial, because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that whoever performs qiyam in Ramadan with iman, with faith, and with ihtisab, with expectation of reward from Allah, then all of their sins will be forgiven. And if a person continues to perform qiyam al-layl throughout the month of Ramadan, and especially in the last nights, then insha’Allah they will also catch Laylat al-Qadr — and in Laylat al-Qadr also they will be performing qiyam al-layl, and that is also a means of forgiveness and great reward.

And fa sabbihhu in the night also includes making tasbih in the night. In general, in the night when you get up and you have to turn on your side, or you get up and have to adjust your blanket, or you get up and check the time, or you get up and have to use the bathroom — or these days you get up and get ready to perform some night worship, or make some food for your family — in the night, busy your tongue with the tasbih of Allah.

And when you do tasbih of Allah in the night, then you will not feel lonely. You will not feel scared. You will not feel like you are losing. Because in the night when a person gets up, especially if they are getting up again and again, there is that fear and worry: I’m not sleeping enough. And the problem with worry is that the more you worry, your worry only increases — it doesn’t go away. So channel that energy, that mental energy, into something productive. And when you do tasbih you are earning so much reward; and with the dhikr of Allah you will receive the mercy of Allah, sakinah, tranquillity — and with that you will be able to sleep so much better also.

After the Setting of the Stars

And then at the end of the ayah it says wa idbar an-nujum — and after the setting of the stars. Meaning when the stars set, when the stars go away, then at that time also glorify and praise Allah. And this is basically at the end of the night; and at the end of the night it is time for Fajr. So the ulama say that tasbih at this time refers specifically to the two sunnah before Fajr.

A lot of people are lazy with that. The two sunnah prayers before Fajr: these two rak‘ah are very light and technically very easy, but somehow very heavy. So a lot of people, even though they have the time and they have the energy, don’t bother to perform these two rak‘ah. Do not be lazy in this. Be eager to perform them. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam mentioned that these two rak‘ah are better than the world and everything in it — and he would not leave these two rak‘ah even when he was travelling.

So we see that in the Qur’an, in many places, we are taught to glorify and praise Allah in salah and outside of salah, in the night, in the morning, in the evening — at different times throughout the day and the night. And specifically, we should glorify and praise Allah after salah.

Chapter Eighty-Five

Sitting Until the Sun Rises

The dhikr of Allah is something we should do after we complete any act of worship.

In Surat an-Nisa, Allah mentions regarding salah: when you complete the salah, then remember Allah while standing, while sitting, and while lying down. Meaning after you complete your salah and you get up from your prayer place and you are going about your day — maybe you are standing in the kitchen, standing at work, sitting at your desk, or lying down because you are tired and need some rest — no matter what you are doing, keep your tongue busy with the dhikr of Allah.

And this is mentioned especially after salah. After Jumu‘ah salah also, when you leave the masjid, again remember Allah abundantly. After Hajj, Allah says that when you have completed all of your rituals, then remember Allah. After the fasting of Ramadan, Allah says: and complete the number of fasts, and magnify your Lord, mention His greatness — say Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. And this is also a form of dhikr.

So after completing any act of worship, there is dhikr. And after salah also, there is certainly dhikr. Making dhikr after salah is something we have been commanded to do; it is something greatly recommended, so we should not neglect it, and we should not be lazy about it either.

❖  ❖  ❖

He Would Sit Until the Sun Rose

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would continue to sit at the place where he performed the Fajr prayer until the sun rose.

And he would perform the Fajr prayer when it was still dark outside — so, early. And then after the Fajr prayer he would continue to sit in his prayer place until the sun rose; and when the sun had risen, then he would stand. So what would he do while sitting there? He would make dhikr.

We learn in another hadith that Jabir said that when the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam observed the Fajr prayer, he would sit at the place of his worship until the sun had risen, and then he would go about, talk to people, and go about his day.

He Did Not Lead a Congregational Du’a

Ibn Taymiyyah said that after leading the people in prayer, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would not lead people in du’a — meaning he would not make a congregational du’a, where he would say something and people would say “ameen” after him. He would not do that after salah, nor did his companions do that. He did not do it after Fajr, nor after ‘Asr, nor after any other salah.

Rather, after salah he would turn his face towards the companions — because he would be in front of them — so he would turn around and face the people, and then he would remember Allah. He would make dhikr, so that the companions would learn how they should remember Allah, and what dhikr they were supposed to say after saying the salam, after completing salah.

Like Making a Mirror Shine

‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) said that dhikr after salah is like making a mirror shine after cleaning it. She said: salah is light, which cleans the heart just as the mirror is cleaned of stains. And then making dhikr after salah is making the heart shine and sparkle, just as you make a mirror shine and sparkle after cleaning it.

And if you are cleaning a mirror, first of all you remove the stains; but then after that you want to make sure that it is also shining, sparkling. How do you do that? By cleaning it even more. Just like that, salah — yes, it is a means of purification, it is light. But then after that you also want some sparkle, some glow, some shine. And how do you get that shine and sparkle? Not through a fake filter, but with the dhikr of Allah.

And SubhanAllah, how much time we spend just looking at ourselves through different filters on our phones, trying to make different parts of our face shine and glow and sparkle. All of that is fake and useless. What is really going to cause a person to be purified and to glow near their Lord is the dhikr that they make, especially after salah.

As Long As You Remain Seated

Hadith

The angels keep on asking Allah’s forgiveness for one of you as long as he is at his musalla. They say: Allahumma ighfir lahu, Allahumma arhamhu — O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, be merciful to him.

So after salah, when you continue to sit in your prayer place, the angels continue to seek forgiveness for you. If you sit for five minutes, for those five minutes the angels are making du’a for you. If you are sitting for ten minutes, the angels will make du’a for you. So if we sit only for three seconds after salah, then how much du’a will we receive from the angels?

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam mentioned that this is as long as one of you sits in his prayer place without breaking his wudu. So as long as you remain in your prayer place without breaking wudu, sitting there, the angels are making du’a for you.

More Beloved Than Freeing Slaves

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam loved to make dhikr after salah. He said that if he were to sit and continue to remember Allah until the sun rises — to continue to sit in his prayer place and remember Allah, glorify Him, mention His greatness, say Allahu Akbar, and Alhamdulillah, and SubhanAllah, and La ilaha illallah, until the sun rises, the entire time, just saying these words of dhikr — then this would be more beloved to him than freeing two slaves from the children of Isma’il.

And the children of Isma’il are who? They are the family of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam — he was one of them; it is his nation, his people. So freeing two slaves from among them is a great act of worship, and something the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam loved to do — but even more beloved to him was to remember Allah in the morning. And the same after ‘Asr until the sun sets: making dhikr at that time is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves from the children of Isma’il.

Hadith

Whoever prays Fajr in congregation and then sits remembering Allah until the sun has risen, and then prays two rak‘ah, then for him is the reward like that of a Hajj and an ‘Umrah. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: “Complete, complete.”

Meaning the complete reward of a Hajj and the complete reward of an ‘Umrah — for praying Fajr in jama‘ah and then making dhikr until the sun rises. So especially encourage your family, the men in your family — your husband, your father, your brother, your son — that they should go to the masjid. If during the weekdays it is difficult for them because of work or school, then at least on the weekend. Encourage them: go to the masjid, pray over there; this is how much reward you will get, the complete reward of a Hajj and an ‘Umrah.

Those Who Have Gone Ahead

We also learn that Allah says: I am with My slave when he remembers Me and his lips move with My mention. Meaning as long as you are busy in the dhikr of Allah, Allah is with you. You are not alone. As long as you are remembering Allah, Allah is mentioning you.

Hadith

“Sabaqa al-mufarridun — the mufarridun have gone ahead.” The companions asked: O Messenger of Allah, who are the mufarridun? He said: “They are those who are busy in the remembrance of Allah.” In another narration: “They are those men and women who remember Allah a lot, in abundance.”

So if we make a habit of making dhikr after every salah, then that is a lot of dhikr if you think about it — five times a day, sitting for at least five or ten minutes each time. May Allah give us the tawfiq to do this with consistency, and may Allah count us among the mufarridun, those who remember Allah a lot.

Chapter Eighty-Six

The Adhkar After Salah

What we say once the salam is said
1. Allahu Akbar
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ

The first thing we say after saying as-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah is Allahu Akbar. Ibn ‘Abbas (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said: I used to recognise the completion of the prayer of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam by hearing the takbir. When he would say the takbir, then I would know he had completed the salah. So this means the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this Allahu Akbar slightly out loud, so that the people around him and behind him could also hear him.

And this is beautiful. You begin salah with Allahu Akbar, and you end salah with as-salamu ‘alaykum wa rahmatullah; and then the first thing you say after completing your prayer is again Allahu Akbar. Allah is the greatest.

Why are you saying Allahu Akbar again, when you just said it so many times in salah? Because after salah a person could feel in their heart: oh, I am so good; I just did four fard after this much sunnah prayer, and I recited so much Qur’an, and I spent fifteen minutes performing these four rak‘at, and I made so much dhikr in ruku‘ and in sajdah. There could be some kind of ‘ujb, where a person is very impressed and amazed with themselves. So Allahu Akbar teaches you humility: Allah is the greatest; I was able to do this by the tawfiq of Allah. Allah enabled me. Allah taught me.

Allah tells us wa la dhikrullahi akbar — and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And it is for the remembrance of Allah, and to glorify Allah, that we have been commanded to perform various forms of worship. So for example in salah there is so much takbir; after salah there is takbir; after the fasting of Ramadan, what is there? Takbir. In Dhul-Hijjah and on ‘Eid, again, what is there? Takbir. So we glorify Allah and mention His greatness, because the different acts of worship have been stipulated so that we glorify and remember Allah.

Some people, instantly after saying the salam, raise their hands and start making du’a. You can make du’a at any time — but when it comes to worship, remember that we should worship Allah the way we have been taught to worship Him by the one who taught us how to worship Allah. And he did not make it a habit that immediately after saying the salam he would raise his hands. No — after saying the salam he would say the takbir. And we should also do the same, in his footsteps.

2. Seeking forgiveness, three times
أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ · أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ · أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ

I seek forgiveness from Allah. Thawban reported that when the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times. And one of the narrators asked the one narrating the hadith to him: how would he seek forgiveness? He said: the way you say astaghfirullah, astaghfirullah, astaghfirullah. And these words are sufficient — that you just say three times: I seek forgiveness from Allah.

And this shows us how much humility the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam expressed before his Lord. In salah, what is it that you are doing? You are humbling yourself before Allah. You are constantly glorifying and praising Him. You are lowering yourself in ruku‘ and in sujud. You are not looking here and there; your eyes are looking down. You are showing humility. But then after salah, again humility, and especially seeking forgiveness.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was someone whose sins had already been forgiven, and he was informed of this: that Allah has forgiven all of your past and future sins. And he was ma‘sum — it is not that he committed sins as we do. Rather, when it comes to the prophets of Allah, the ulama explain that this is not acts of disobedience to Allah; rather these are acts that are not as excellent as they should be. The prophets of Allah, and those who are righteous, those who are close to Allah, the muqarrabun — if they do something that is good enough, at the level of excellence for an ordinary person, that is an average deed for them. Hasanat al-abrar sayyi’at al-muqarrabin. What is expected of the prophets is much greater. So the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam recognised that, he acknowledged that, and he would seek forgiveness from Allah after salah three times.

And this is amazing. After salah we are taught to seek forgiveness from Allah — for what? Because we know that we have not prayed perfectly. We know that there were moments in which we were completely distracted, we didn’t even know what we were saying, or we were thinking very inappropriate thoughts, we were not paying attention to what we were saying at all.

Remember that when a person recites Surat al-Fatihah — you say alhamdulillahi rabbil ‘alamin and Allah answers. But do we ever recite Surat al-Fatihah like that? Maybe we have done that a few times in our lives, where we are pausing after every ayah and reciting nice and slow, with so much attention, with so much love and dedication. If we are honest with ourselves, we don’t always pray like that. We don’t always recite like that. Sometimes we rush through salah. We know we should come to a complete stop, but we still rush. May Allah forgive us.

And if we were to honestly analyse our prayers, we would find more faults in them than things we have done at the level of excellence. So astaghfirullah — ya Allah, forgive me. In hadith we learn that a person prays for sixty years and perhaps their prayers are not accepted. Why? Because they didn’t do their ruku‘ properly; they didn’t do their sujud properly. In another hadith we learn that a person performs salah and they only get a small portion of its reward — a sixth of it, a fifth of it, a tenth of it. Why? Because that is all that they paid attention to in salah; that is the only duration in which they were attentive, and the only portion of the salah that they actually performed correctly, with attentiveness and khushu‘. So astaghfirullah — don’t be lazy in this. Ask Allah for forgiveness: ya Allah, forgive me for not praying in the best way that I can and that I should be praying in.

3. O Allah, You are peace
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ، تَبَارَكْتَ يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ

O Allah, You are peace, and from You comes all peace. Blessed are You, O Owner of majesty and honour.

So after istighfar we are praising Allah by declaring: ya Allah, You are as-Salam. As-Salam is one of the names of Allah, and it means the One who is free from every defect, the One who is perfectly sound, and the One who is the source of safety. And wa minka as-salam — from You is salam; You are the source of salam. No one can be safe and sound unless You grant them that soundness and safety.

And then you say tabarakta ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram — blessed are You, O Possessor of glory and honour. And Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram is a description of Allah with which we should make du’a, as the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: hold on to ya Dhal-Jalali wal-Ikram — use that when you are making du’a; say that again and again when you are making du’a. And we say tabarakta — You are blessed, O our Lord. Tabarakta is from barakah: You are abundantly good, endlessly good, and all goodness comes from You. And jalal is greatness, and ikram has been interpreted as ihsan — generosity and kindness. So Allah is the One who gives honour to His slaves, and He is the One who is generous and kind to His slaves also.

4. Declaring His oneness — said three times
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

There is no true deity except Allah alone, having no partners. His alone is the sovereignty and His alone is the praise, and He is over all things fully competent. In a hadith we learn that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this after every salah, and he would say it thalatha marrat — three times.

5. The same, with what cannot be prevented
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، اللَّهُمَّ لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعْتَ وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الْجَدِّ مِنْكَ الْجَدُّ

O Allah, no one can prevent what You have willed to bestow, and no one can bestow what You have willed to prevent; and the might of the mighty one cannot help him against You.

Ya Allah, if You intend to give something, no one can prevent that; no one can stop it from coming my way. And if You decide that something should not reach me, then no one can bring it. No one can. And no matter how much might and power and wealth someone has, it cannot help them against You. All power is Yours.

And we say this statement after declaring the oneness of Allah. At the beginning of this dhikr is la ilaha illallah — there is no god worthy of worship but Allah; wahdahu — alone, further emphasising illallah; la sharika lah — further emphasising that He has no partner at all whatsoever. And then we mention His tawhid in another way: lahul mulk — to Him alone belongs all sovereignty; everything belongs only to Allah; He has no partner in ownership. Wa lahul hamd — and He is worthy of all praise, because of His perfection in His attributes, in His actions, in His generosity. Wa huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadir — He is able to do all things.

And this is so important: that we say this, and we believe in this, and we remind ourselves of this. That Allah is One. He has no partner. There is absolutely no one like Him, no one equal to Him. Everyone is under Him. He is above everyone. And He owns everything.

And if you find out that so-and-so is the richest person in the world, and now they are the second richest, and now they are the richest — it fluctuates, and we get so impressed. And this is the creation, who only own things temporarily, and imperfectly. Allah is the real owner. He is the real Malik. He is Malikul Mulk.

And He is always worthy of perfect praise. When it comes to people, when it comes to the creation, they are not worthy of perfect praise. One moment someone you love does something that makes you so happy, and then the next moment, the next day, a couple of hours later, they do something that is so hurtful, and then you wonder: what is wrong with them? What happened to them? Well, it is only Allah who is always perfect, who is always worthy of perfect praise. And He can do whatever He wants. In the Qur’an, Allah tells us that if Allah opens a door of mercy for people, no one can withhold it; and if Allah withholds something from people, no one can bring it forward.

So we see that in this dhikr we are affirming tawhid ar-rububiyyah — the fact that Allah alone is Rabb — and tawhid al-uluhiyyah — the fact that Allah alone is worthy of worship.

6. The longer form, with sincerity to Him
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَا نَعْبُدُ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ، لَهُ النِّعْمَةُ وَلَهُ الْفَضْلُ وَلَهُ الثَّنَاءُ الْحَسَنُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ

There is no might or power except with Allah. There is no true deity except Allah, and we do not worship anyone but Him. His are all blessings, His is all bounty, and His is the excellent praise. There is no deity except Allah; we devote our worship purely to Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it.

Every bounty comes from Allah, and the favours also come from Him, and He is worthy of excellent praise. And mukhlisina lahud-din — we purify ourselves, we make our worship exclusively for Allah, meaning we worship only Allah; we sincerely devote ourselves to Allah. Wa law kariha al-kafirun — even if the disbelievers dislike that. Some people do not like that you worship Allah alone; they have a big problem with that. But we worship Allah alone, even if people don’t like it.

And we learn in hadith that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam used to say these words after every salah. In these words also: first of all we declare the oneness of Allah; then we praise and glorify Allah; then we declare that all power, all might is with Allah, and nobody has the power to change anything, or finish anything, or remove anything, except with the tawfiq of Allah; and then we declare that we worship only Allah; we acknowledge that all favours, all blessings are from Allah, and that He is worthy of the most excellent praise; and then we make ourselves sincere to Him.

7. The tasbihat — thirty-three each
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ · الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ · اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ

Glory be to Allah, thirty-three times; all praise is for Allah, thirty-three times; Allah is the greatest, thirty-three times — a total of ninety-nine adhkar. In one narration we learn: say Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, so that it becomes a hundred. In other narrations we learn that after saying each of these thirty-three times, we say la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul mulku wa lahul hamdu wa huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadir once — and that is a total of a hundred adhkar.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that these are mu‘aqqibat — statements of remembrance that you say following salah. And he said la yakhibu qa’iluhunna — the person who says them will never suffer loss; they will never be deprived of the reward.

And this is so reassuring, because when you say SubhanAllah thirty-three times, then maybe for the first ten you are attentive; and then maybe for the next ten you get a little distracted; and then you bring yourself back — no, no, pay attention, SubhanAllah, mean what you are saying — and then the remaining thirteen maybe you say with attentiveness. So whether you said them attentively or not, as long as you are saying them, la yakhibu qa’iluhunna.

Of course, when it comes to the dhikr of Allah and making du’a, we should be attentive; we should be showing humility. But as humans it is normal that sometimes in the middle your heart gets slightly distracted, or you don’t pay as much attention as you should to what you are saying. So la yakhibu qa’iluhunna — because shaytan sometimes tells us: well, you know what, you are making dhikr without even thinking, so don’t say it at all, because it’s useless. No, it is not useless. It is not a waste. It is rewarded. So say it, and don’t let shaytan distract you. Don’t let shaytan make you feel that your dhikr is not good enough, so you should leave it.

The Companions Who Felt Left Behind

Hadith

Some companions came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam — they were poor, they were not wealthy — and they said that the wealthy people among us will get higher levels of reward and will enjoy so much more reward. They pray like us, they fast as we do; the only difference is that they have more money, and with their money they are able to go for Hajj, able to go for ‘Umrah, able to participate in jihad, able to give in charity. We are not able to do that, because we don’t have that money. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: “Shall I not tell you a thing upon which, if you acted, you would catch up with those who have surpassed you? And nobody could overtake you, except someone who does the same as you do?” And he told them: say SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each after every salah.

So the companions would say that. And in another narration we learn that the wealthy companions also found out about it, so they started saying it — and then the first group came and complained to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and he said: this is the favour of Allah, which He grants to whomsoever He wants.

In another narration we learn that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told them to say these adhkar ten times each. So in some narrations we learn thirty-three times each; in other narrations we learn we can say them ten times each. And both are correct; both are good. And sometimes it happens that you complete your salah, you have just started making your dhikr, and your baby needs a diaper change, or somebody is calling, or you know that somebody is waiting for you. So don’t leave dhikr completely — you can say SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar ten times each. If you cannot do it thirty-three times each, say it ten times each, but don’t leave it.

Counting on the Fingers

When it comes to these adhkar thirty-three times each, the sunnah is to count the adhkar on your fingers. Ibn Qudamah said: with the fingers on the right hand — use those to count the dhikr. You can use a misbahah also, a tasbih, or a tasbih counter; although there are some ulama who strongly advise against using that, and some say there is no harm. As long as you are using the misbahah as a means of helping you stay focused, or helping you complete the number, it is fine. But if you think that the misbahah itself is very holy, that becomes problematic.

And you should be eager to develop the habit of using your fingers to make dhikr, because this is not only the sunnah of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, but remember that your body is going to testify on the Day of Judgement about the things that you used to do. We learn that on the Day of Judgement the hands will speak. So if you use your hands to make dhikr, then your hands will testify in your favour.

Hadith

Yusayrah informed that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam commanded them — and by them she meant the Muhajirat, the women who had migrated to Madinah — that they should be regular in saying Allahu Akbar, and tahlil, la ilaha illallah, and different forms of dhikr on their fingers. And he said fa innahunna mas’ulatun mustantaqat — the fingers will be questioned on the Day of Judgement, and they will be made to speak.

So you want to make sure that you do dhikr on your fingers, so that when they speak on the Day of Judgement, whatever they say is in your favour, insha’Allah.

8. Ayat al-Kursi
اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ، لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ

Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. We learn in hadith that the person who recites Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, the only thing preventing him from entry into paradise is death — meaning when he dies, he will go into paradise.

This ayah is the greatest ayah of the Qur’an. And it is the greatest because it glorifies and tells us about the greatest One, Allah. The entire ayah is telling us about the greatness of Allah: that first of all He is Allah, that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah. He is so great, so perfect, that He is ever-living, the sustainer of all. He is so great that drowsiness and sleep do not overtake Him. He is so great that He owns everything in the heavens and in the earth. He is so great that no one can intercede before Him without His permission. He is so great that He knows what is before people and what is behind them — their present, their future, their past. He is so great that they cannot encompass anything of His knowledge; they cannot know anything about Him except what He wills. He is so great that His Kursi encompasses the skies and the earth — the skies and the earth are like a ring in a desert compared to His Kursi. This is how tiny we are. And He is so great that He does not get tired taking care of the heavens and the earth. And He is al-‘Ali al-‘Azim, the Most High, the Most Great. So we should make a habit of saying Ayat al-Kursi after every salah.

9. The Mu’awwidhat
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ · قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ · قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ

Surat al-Ikhlas, Surat al-Falaq, and Surat an-Nas. ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir said that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam commanded me to recite the Mu’awwidhat after every salah.

And in these surahs, what are we doing? In Surat al-Ikhlas we are declaring the oneness of Allah, His perfection. And in Surat al-Falaq and Surat an-Nas we are asking Allah to protect us from all forms of evil: evil that we know and that we don’t know, evil of the creation, evil of the night, evil of the magicians, the jealousy of people, the evil of shaytan — all types of evil. We are asking Allah to protect us from that.

And as humans we are weak, and we have sometimes genuine fears and sometimes imaginary fears. Sometimes we are afraid that so-and-so has affected us with the evil eye, or that maybe there is magic, or maybe there is jinn, or there is this or there is that. Sometimes these fears are real; other times they are imaginary. Sometimes something evil has happened, and other times we are afraid that it might befall us. So give yourself into Allah’s protection: ya Allah, You are the Lord of people, You are the owner of people, You are the God of people. You are the Lord of al-falaq — the daybreak; and falaq also means the entire creation. So give yourself into Allah’s protection.

10. Help me to remember You
رَبِّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ

O my Lord, help me to remember You, to be grateful to You, and to worship You in the best way.

This is a du’a we can say after salah, and we can also say it before saying the salam. Because the scholars say that the best time to make dhikr, when it comes to salah, is after salah — when you say the taslim, then you make dhikr; and the best time to make du’a is before the taslim. Why? Because in the tashahhud, when you say the tashahhud and you send salat to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, that is the best time to make du’a. So ask Allah at that time, make du’a. But then after salah also, when you have been making dhikr, you can again make du’a.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught this du’a to Mu‘adh ibn Jabal (radiyallahu ‘anhu). He said to him one day: ya Mu‘adh, by Allah, I love you. And Mu‘adh was a young man. And a lot of times what is it that young people feel? That the people who are older don’t care about them, that they don’t love them. Sometimes younger people get this feeling because it is just thoughts, it is imaginary, it is from shaytan. But sometimes there is genuine reason to feel like this: you don’t feel acknowledged by people who are older than you; they are always telling you off, or always telling you do this, do that, don’t do this, don’t do that; they always find fault in what you are doing; you are never good enough.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is telling Mu‘adh: ya Mu‘adh, by Allah, I love you. Can you imagine, for a young person, to be told that by the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam? How comforting and how encouraging. What joy. And he said: ya Rasul Allah, I also love you. And then the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told him: I advise you, O Mu‘adh, do not leave these words after every salah.

In another version: Allahumma a’inni ‘ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni ‘ibadatik. Because we can only remember Allah if Allah enables us, if Allah allows us. We can only be grateful if Allah gives us the tawfiq to feel grateful, to recognise those blessings.

And remember that dhikr is that we remember Allah with our tongues and our hearts. Sometimes we are just verbally remembering Allah and the heart is distracted. Sometimes the tongue does not want to move in dhikr — as if there is a knot preventing the tongue from moving in the remembrance of Allah; we can make dhikr, we know we should be doing dhikr, our heart is telling us make dhikr, but then the tongue is just stuck. So Rabbi a’inni ‘ala dhikrika wa shukrik.

Ya Allah, help me to be grateful to You. And gratitude is with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs — with the limbs, that you do those things which are pleasing to Allah. So we cannot recognise the blessings of Allah, we cannot feel happy about them in our hearts, we cannot do different acts of servitude out of gratitude to Allah, without the help of Allah. So ask Allah to help you be grateful. And the taqwa of Allah is the greatest form of shukr.

And shukr is something amazing: on the one hand you are asking Allah to give you the ability to be grateful — grateful for what? For the blessings that you have. And when you are grateful, you should be grateful for the fact that you are grateful, because you are only able to be grateful with the tawfiq of Allah. And then when you are grateful you receive more blessings — so, another reason to be grateful. So gratitude is something that is just never-ending.

And then wa husni ‘ibadatik. So often we perform different acts of worship — we pray, we recite Qur’an, we make dhikr, sometimes we even give sadaqah, we fast. But what is the quality of our worship? Is it excellent? Is it good? Is it very good? Is it average? Is it okay? We know that our ‘ibadah can be better. So ask Allah: ya Allah, help me to worship You in an excellent way.

11. Protect me from Your punishment
رَبِّ قِنِي عَذَابَكَ يَوْمَ تَبْعَثُ عِبَادَكَ

O my Lord, protect me from Your punishment on the Day when You resurrect Your slaves.

Al-Bara’ (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that when we prayed behind the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, we would like to stand on his right side, behind him. Why? So that he would turn his face towards us, and we would hear him say this du’a.

12. Forgive me for what has gone before and what is to come
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ وَمَا أَسْرَرْتُ وَمَا أَعْلَنْتُ وَمَا أَسْرَفْتُ وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي، أَنْتَ الْمُقَدِّمُ وَأَنْتَ الْمُؤَخِّرُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

O Allah, forgive me what I have sent before me and what I have left behind me, what I have concealed and what I have done openly, what I have done in excess, and what You are better aware of than I am. You are the One who sends forth and You are the One who delays. There is no true deity except You.

Meaning: the sins I have already committed, and the sins You know I will commit later. Or the sins I actually committed, and the sins I did not commit but was tempted to. Forgive me. And some of the salaf said that this refers to my negligence — what I have neglected, what I have left behind, what I have not done properly, what I left when I was actually supposed to do it.

And what I have hidden: sometimes there are evil thoughts, negative thoughts, that we just hide and bury in our hearts; and sometimes we say them out loud, we do it openly — and these days people like to advertise everything about themselves. And any excesses that I have committed, any limits that I have crossed: ya Allah, forgive me for that. Sometimes we are disciplining our child, even, and we cross the limits.
