We are trying to explain to someone that what they did is wrong or was not appropriate, and we cross the limits, and then we become the aggressor. So astaghfirullah.

And: what You are better aware of than I am. Sometimes we don’t even know the sins we are committing. We don’t even know that we may be saying things that are very displeasing to Allah. Maybe it is our facial expressions. Maybe it is some expressions that we use very habitually in our conversations, and we don’t realise they are very displeasing to Allah. So ya Allah, forgive me for what You are better aware of than I am.

13. Glory be to You, O Allah
سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ

Glory be to You, O Allah, and all praise is Yours; I seek forgiveness from You, and I repent to You. We learn in a hadith that when a person says this after a sitting, a seal is placed on his good deed — it is sealed and preserved for him until the Day of Judgement, and he will certainly receive its reward on the Day of Judgement. So before talking to people, we should say this dhikr.

14. Forgive me and accept my repentance
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الْغَفُورُ

O my Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; indeed You are the greatest acceptor of repentance, the Ever-Forgiving. We learn in a hadith that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this after every salah.

❖  ❖  ❖

After Particular Prayers

15. After Witr — said three times
سُبْحَانَ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ

Glory be to the King, the Most Pure. After the Witr prayer, when you say the salam, we should say this three times. And you see, the Witr prayer is the last prayer of the night — so after that, again, glory be to Allah.

16. After the sunnah of Fajr — the du’a of light
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ فِي قَلْبِي نُورًا وَفِي بَصَرِي نُورًا وَفِي سَمْعِي نُورًا، وَعَنْ يَمِينِي نُورًا وَعَنْ يَسَارِي نُورًا، وَفَوْقِي نُورًا وَتَحْتِي نُورًا، وَأَمَامِي نُورًا وَخَلْفِي نُورًا

O Allah, place light in my heart, and light in my sight, and light in my hearing; and light on my right and light on my left; and light above me and light below me; and light in front of me and light behind me. Ask Allah for light.

17. After Fajr — beneficial knowledge, pure provision, accepted deeds
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا

O Allah, I ask You for knowledge which is beneficial, sustenance which is pure, and actions which are accepted. After Salat al-Fajr, and after you have performed the two rak‘ah of Fajr, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would also say this.

18. Ten times after Fajr, and ten times after Maghrib
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

We learn in hadith that we should say this ten times after Fajr; and after Salat al-Maghrib, among the adhkar we should make should also be this, ten times.

In hadith we learn that if a person says this while sitting in the position of the tashahhud — you say the salam and you remain sitting in that position, you don’t stretch your legs, you don’t get up, you don’t move your position, you sit as you are — and you say this ten times, then ten good deeds are recorded for the person, ten sins are erased, ten ranks are raised, and the person is protected from shaytan and everything evil. There is also protection against many sins and shirk.

There is another hadith that tells us that if a person says this ten times after Maghrib, then they will be guarded against shaytan until the morning, and Allah will send angels to guard him. And the angels are described as muslahatan — angels that are well equipped. Think of guards equipped with their weapons to guard someone important: that is how much protection you get from Allah. So especially this dhikr after Maghrib.

Sabaqa al-mufarridun.
May Allah count us among them.
Chapter Eighty-Seven

I Am in Need of Any Good

The prophets of Allah are a perfect example for us, and when they found themselves in any difficulty they called upon Allah.

When Musa (‘alayhis salam) left Egypt and ended up in Madyan in a state of extreme poverty and weakness, he did not know where he was going to go or what he was going to do. He had no idea what was going to happen next. And he made use of the strength that Allah had given him and he helped those in need; he welcomed a new connection in his life; and he asked Allah for something good.

The Qur’an

“My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You would send down to me.”

He declared himself as a faqir — someone who is extremely poor, someone who has nothing at all. He was expressing his desperate need of anything good that Allah would send his way. And he combined du’a with effort: he made du’a, and he also did something to benefit those people who were around him. He didn’t just sit there waiting for good things to fall on him from the sky. He made du’a, and he used whatever means Allah had given him.

And what happened then? Allah responded to his du’a, and Allah gave him different types of good: not only a family, but also a job, job security, a home, security, safety in general, a good family. He received so much.

So in Musa (‘alayhis salam) we see that we should ask Allah for what is good for us. And a lot of the time we ourselves don’t know what is good for us. We may want something, we may really passionately desire something, but in reality it is quite possible that it is not good for us. And on the other hand, we might be trying our best to avoid something, but in fact it could be good for us. So we don’t know what is good for us all the time. It is Allah who knows. So we should be regularly asking Allah to grant us what is good.

❖  ❖  ❖

What Istikharah Means

Istikharah literally means two things. First of all, istikharah means to seek, to ask for — and what? Choice. Meaning you ask someone to choose for you, to pick for you, because you understand that you are not in the right state to make a decision for yourself. And why are you not in the right state to make a decision for yourself? Because you recognise that you don’t know the future, you don’t know everything, your knowledge is limited. So you ask the One who knows everything to decide for you, to pick for you, to select for you what is best.

And a lot of the time a person is feeling very indecisive; they are not used to making decisions, or the decision is very big, the risks are very high, the investment is very great, and so they are afraid — they are genuinely afraid. So they are asking Allah to make the decision for them, to pick what is best for them.

Secondly, istikharah means to seek what is good. So you are asking Allah to grant you what is good. Because sometimes you have made a decision and you are very clear about it; you have consulted everyone, you have done your research, and now you have made your decision. So before you go ahead with it, you ask Allah to make it good for you. This is also istikharah.

And this shows us that istikharah is something we can make when we are indecisive, when we don’t know what to do, when we are not sure about which option to choose for ourselves — both look good, or all three look good, and we are completely indecisive. We can make istikharah at that time. And secondly, we should also make istikharah when we have made a decision to go ahead with something, because then you are praying istikharah to ask Allah for what is good, to make what you have decided good for you.

And in istikharah you are showing complete surrender to Allah; you are showing your trust in Allah. So istikharah is a form of ta‘abbud — a form of complete servitude to Allah: ya Allah, I am Your slave, I am in need of You, You are the Master, You know everything, I don’t know. This is what I want, so You make it good for me; and if it is bad for me, You turn it away from me. And you are showing your complete reliance, your trust, in Allah.

What Is Khayr?

When you are praying istikharah you are asking Allah for what is good, or asking Allah to choose what is good for you, because He knows what is good for you. So what exactly is khayr?

Khayr is described as a thing that all desire; it is something that everyone wants — for example intelligence, or equity, justice, goodness and excellence, some virtue; and something that is useful, something that is of benefit. This is khayr, and it is the opposite of sharr, something that is evil.

And khayr is of two kinds. The first type is that which is absolute: something that is good and desired in all circumstances and by every person. So for example Jannah. Jannah is good, and it is good for everyone, for every person, no matter what circumstances they are in. They could be very pious or not, they could be in difficulty or not — whatever their condition, Jannah is good for every slave.

The other type is that which is relative: it is good for someone but not for someone else. So for example wealth, property, money — this is something that can be good for one person, and at the same time it can be very evil for another. A phone can be very good for someone who is using it to keep in touch with their family, to do their work, to listen to good things, to listen to Qur’an, to memorise Qur’an, to send good messages to their friends and family — they are using that phone for a lot of good, so the phone is good for this person. But the same kind of phone can actually be evil for another person, because they are using it to keep a haram relationship, or to watch something sinful, to listen to something sinful, to lie, to waste their time. So that wealth itself can be good for someone and evil for someone else. This khayr is relative; it is not absolute.

All Good Is in His Hand

Of course people love what is good. Allah says: and indeed the human being is very intense in his love for good. And khayr can also be understood as wealth, because a lot of the time in the Qur’an the word khayr is used to refer to wealth, since people think that wealth is good for them — and wealth certainly has a lot of potential for goodness, but it also has potential for evil.

Allah tells us in the Qur’an that a person does not get weary, does not get tired, of asking for goodness. People always want something that is good for them, and not just in the sense of deen but also in worldly terms: not just money but health, and good friends, good fun, good food, things like that. People are very eager for it, and they never get tired of it.

Hadith

“In Your hand is all good, and You are able to do all things.”

So Allah has created us such that we have an inclination to have what is good, and all good is in the hand of Allah. So what does this mean? This means that if we want anything good, who do we seek it from? We seek it from Allah. And if we want something to be good for us, then again, who do we seek help from? We seek help from Allah.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that indeed the only good is the good of the hereafter. And this shows us that something good in the world — of material things, of worldly things — these are good things, yes, but their goodness is limited and it is fleeting, and with the good there is also some kind of harm attached.

So for example a person thinks that a certain individual is perfect for them to marry, and they marry them, and alhamdulillah they receive a lot of good, they benefit a lot — but at the same time there are also things that are hurtful, or things that are annoying. You think that buying a certain phone would be excellent for you, but then you have it, and it is so fast and it has such a long battery life that you end up spending too much time on your phone. This is the reality of the good things of the world: their goodness is not absolute. The real goodness is the goodness of the hereafter. So where we are eager for good and we ask Allah for good, we should especially be seeking permanent goodness, the goodness of the hereafter. That is what we should be desiring.

Chapter Eighty-Eight

What Brings Good, and What Keeps It Away

Allah is the One in whose hand is all good. So how do we seek the good that is in His hand?

Iman and Taqwa

First of all, we seek it through faith and piety. Allah tells us in the Qur’an that if the people of the towns had believed and had adopted taqwa, surely He would have opened to them blessings from the sky and the earth — He would have opened the floodgates of blessings for them, and blessings would come upon them from the sky and also from beneath their feet. If only they had believed and adopted taqwa.

The Qur’an

“And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out; and He will provide for him from where he does not expect.”

An exit out of his difficulty — and then Allah provides him from where a person cannot even imagine. So the first step to achieving something good for ourselves is iman and taqwa.

Fulfilling Your Obligations

Secondly, fulfil your obligations: your obligations towards Allah, and towards those whom Allah has tied you with in some relationship. Whatever obligations you owe them, fulfil them — because Allah promises the people who fulfil their obligations that He will reward them for the best of what they used to do, and He will give them even more.

Obedience, and Moderation in Seeking

Another thing is that we should show obedience to Allah in general also. Yes, we are fulfilling our obligations, but at the same time we should also show obedience to Allah in other matters of our lives, and refrain from what He has forbidden.

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that anything that can draw you close to paradise, I have informed you about it, I have instructed you to do it; and if there is anything that can draw you close to hellfire, I have forbidden you from it. And he said that no soul can die without consuming the provision that was decreed for it — so fear Allah and adopt moderation in seeking provision. And the delay in sustenance should not urge you to seek it through disobedience to Allah, for what is with Allah can only be attained through obedience to Allah.

So don’t be so obsessive over earning money, or over acquiring things that you want, things that you like — because when you become very obsessive over it and you are putting all of your mind and energy into it, the result is only going to be what Allah has already decreed for you. So don’t go to extremes: don’t become lazy and do nothing, and at the same time don’t be chasing money all the time either.

And the delay in sustenance should not urge you to seek it through disobedience. For example, you are very eager to make some money so that you can buy something, and you believe that the thing you want to buy is good for you — so you should adopt lawful ways to acquire it. Because if you steal your parents’ money, or steal someone’s money, or cheat them, or lie to them in order to get money from them, and through that you acquire something that you love, this is very dangerous for you. So just because you can’t have something right now and you badly want it, don’t let that urge you to disobey Allah. If you want something that is really good for you, actually good for you, and you want it from Allah, then you have to obey Allah. You should not be using disobedience to Allah in order to earn it.

Gentleness, Good Deeds, Tawbah, and Dhikr

Another important thing we need to adopt is gentleness. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that whoever is granted gentleness has been granted a huge portion of goodness — because through gentleness you can acquire a lot of good.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the gates of goodness are fasting, charity, and other good deeds. So good deeds are gates of goodness. And tawbah and istighfar — repenting to Allah, seeking forgiveness from Him — these also bring goodness to a person.

And another thing is that we should be frequent in remembering Allah. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught words of dhikr to a man and said that this person has filled his hand with goodness. When you make the dhikr of Allah, you will receive a lot of good from Allah.

So in order to acquire something good in our lives: yes, we adopt the means — for example you go to the market in order to purchase something you want — but then at the same time you have to do such things as Allah likes, so that Allah facilitates that goodness for you and gives it to you in abundance. Remembrance of Allah, seeking forgiveness, doing good deeds, being gentle, refraining from haram, fulfilling your obligations, and most importantly faith and taqwa, the fear of Allah.

❖  ❖  ❖

What Prevents Good From Reaching Us

Remember that there are some things which prevent a person from attaining what is good. Sometimes it happens that a person is trying a lot, they are working very hard, but they are not able to find something good for themselves. For example, someone wants to get married, and now they talk to their family, they talk to their friends — if you find someone, please let me know — and year after year goes by and they are not able to find someone suitable. Or someone wants to make money: they work somewhere, they apply for a job in one place, then another, then another, they start a business, nothing is working, they are not able to make a decent income. Or a person wants to buy something for their family and is not able to purchase it; every time they want to buy it, something happens.

Sins and Acts of Disobedience

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam warned that when there is a nation in which sins such as zina and immoral, indecent actions become very common and people commit them very openly, then plague and different diseases spread among those people. When people cheat in buying and selling, meaning they are not honest in terms of weight and measure, then they are afflicted with famine and the oppression of rulers and other hardships. When people do not give zakat from their wealth, then Allah prevents rain from falling on them — and if it was not for the animals, no rain would fall on those people. And when people break the promise they have made with Allah, then Allah sends other nations over them.

So in this hadith the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam has given many warnings, and what do they show us? That when we disobey Allah openly, defiantly, then there are consequences, and a person is prevented from good.

Hasan al-Basri would say: O companions, by Allah, in the clouds is your sustenance — but you are prevented from it, you are deprived of it, because of your sins and your crimes and your deeds. Because Allah says that in the sky is your sustenance, meaning Allah sends the decree down from above. And what is it that prevents us from receiving that sustenance, from receiving that goodness? It is our own sins; it is our own faults.

So every person should think about themselves: if I desperately want something good, I am praying for it, I am trying to get it, and I am still not able to get it — then I need to check my actions. How is my akhlaq, my behaviour, with my closest family members, with my mother, with my father, with my sister, with my brother? Do I honour them? Do I disrespect them? Do I give them attention? Do I ignore them?

Sometimes people are constantly struggling in their work, constantly, with one stress after another. We need to do some introspection: why isn’t Allah making things easy for us? What lesson does He want me to learn? So check your actions. What is my behaviour like with the people who deserve my respect, who deserve my best treatment — especially my mother and my father? Because Allah tells us in the Qur’an that first is His right, do not associate any partner with Allah; and then with the parents, do ihsan.

So when I see my mother, what kind of a face do I make? When I sit with my mother, do I look at her, do I talk to her, or do I pretend like she is not even there, lost in my own world? This is extreme disrespect to one’s mother: that first of all a person doesn’t show their face for such a long time, and then when they come, they come in a moody way. So we need to check our actions, we need to check our behaviour. What is our salah like, and other matters? If we are disobeying Allah, if we are doing things that bring about His wrath and disapproval, then how do we expect ease in our lives?

Constant Argumentation

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam came out to the people in order to tell them when Laylat al-Qadr would be, and he found two men among the Muslims arguing. He said that he had come out in order to inform them — but because of their argumentation, that knowledge was taken away from him.

SubhanAllah. People were not informed of when exactly Laylat al-Qadr is — why? Because of two people arguing. Now think about it: if a husband and wife are constantly bickering in the house, if siblings are constantly bickering, if daughter-in-law and mother-in-law are always arguing, if father and son are always arguing, if in the house there is constant argumentation, no respect for people’s choices, no respect for other people such that you give them space — if there is constant argumentation, then how can we expect good?

Harshness and Ingratitude

Another thing is harshness. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that whoever is deprived of gentleness is actually deprived of a lot of goodness.

Another thing is ingratitude. We learn in the Qur’an that there was a people who were like this, and Allah made them wear the clothing of hunger and fear — He completely surrounded them, encompassed them, with constant hunger and constant fear, because of what they used to do, because of their ingratitude.

So you see, sometimes when we are not able to find the good or get the good that we desire, we tend to deflect the blame onto those around us. Sometimes people will blame society: oh, there are no good human beings, there is no good man left to marry, there is no good woman left to marry, these days the men are just horrible, these days the women are just horrible — and we will blame everyone but ourselves. Sometimes people will blame their families: I am still not married because of such and such reason, because of my father, because of my mother, because of my sister, because of my brother, because of this, because of that.

I am not saying that these things do not become a hurdle — they do. But ultimately, remember: good is not in their hand. Good is in the hand of Allah. Sometimes it is our own harshness, our own bad behaviour, our constant negativity and finding fault in other people, and being ungrateful with everything that is in our lives; and every time we find someone, we are bickering, we have a reason to argue and pick a fight. We are repelling good from ourselves; we are not inviting good into our lives.

So if we want good in our lives we have to invite it. How do we invite it? With a positive attitude, seeking it from Allah, and by doing the things that Allah likes, not those things which Allah dislikes.

Chapter Eighty-Nine

How Istikharah Is Prayed

Istikharah is something that is legislated.

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would teach the companions istikharah as he would teach them a surah of the Qur’an.

He would teach people the istikharah as if it was from the Qur’an. It is an essential for every Muslim: you must know how to pray istikharah, how to ask Allah for goodness in different matters. This is an essential in life. This is a very important habit that we all need to develop — that we ask Allah for goodness. Why? Because we are fuqara, we are poor, and Allah is the One who is rich, who is praiseworthy.

And we should do istikharah because we don’t always know what is good for us. Allah tells us that it is possible that you dislike something whereas in reality it is good for you, and it is possible that you love something and in reality it is bad for you; Allah knows and you do not know. So ask Allah to make the decision for you; ask Allah to grant you what is good.

And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told us that amazing is the case of the believer, because Allah does not decree anything for the believer except that it is good for him. So whatever Allah decides for you, what Allah picks for you, what Allah chooses for you — remember that is excellent for you. So ask Allah to choose for you; and if you have made a decision, then ask Allah to put good in it for you.

Zaynab Would Not Decide Without Her Lord

We see that before making any important decision, it was the habit of the sahabah that they would pray istikharah. We learn about Zaynab that when she was informed that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam intended to marry her — when it was mentioned before her, to see how she liked the idea — she said: I will not do anything until I consult my Lord.

Imagine, a proposal from the Prophet of Allah, and she said: I am not going to do anything until I ask Allah. Allahu Akbar. This is how much du’a they made to Allah; this is how much the companions would do istikharah.

And this shows us that even when something appears to be good for us, something that we like, something that we think is right for us, good for us — even then we should do istikharah. For example, if you want to travel back home to see your family after ten years, after fifteen years, yes this is something good, that you are going to visit your family — but still you should do istikharah. Why? Because then you are asking Allah to put good in your decision, to make it good for you, to make it abundantly good for you; and if there is anything harmful, dangerous, evil in it, to keep that away from you.

Some of the ulama say that without making istikharah a person should not go ahead with doing any major thing in his worldly matters. So worldly matters such as travel, or a big purchase, or marriage, or studying at a particular school, or studying a particular programme, buying a house, renting a house, getting a car, moving to a different city, taking a job — anything like that, any worldly matter: before you go ahead with it, pray istikharah.

And when a person prays istikharah, then they are protected from humiliation. Why? Because when you pray istikharah you are asking Allah to bless you in your decision, to put good in it, to protect you from harm. So after that, whatever happens, you are content with it, and you will not be worried, you will not feel embarrassed, you will not feel regret — because you will know that you consulted your Lord, and you know that you asked Allah to put good in it for you, so what has happened is good for you.

They say that the person who consults his Lord and prays istikharah, and consults the creation — meaning you also discuss with people who are knowledgeable of the matter, who know your situation; you consult them — and then makes a decision and is firm on it, because Allah says that when you have made a decision then put your trust in Allah, meaning now be firm, now stick to the decision: such a person will never be regretful.

Four Things, and No Deprivation

Other ulama say that if a person is granted four things, then they are not deprived.

First of all, the person who is given the ability to be grateful to Allah — then they will not be deprived of receiving more blessings, because when they are grateful Allah will give them more. Secondly, the person who is given the ability to repent to Allah — then he will not be deprived of the acceptance of repentance, because Allah is at-Tawwab, He accepts repentance; so he was given the ability to repent, and now when you do tawbah Allah accepts repentance. Thirdly, the person who is given the ability to make istikharah — then he will not be deprived of goodness, because you asked Allah for good, and Allah will give it to you, so whatever happens it will be good for you. And fourthly, the person who is given the ability to consult others — then he will not be deprived of what is right, what is correct for him, because you consulted others; and why? Because you want to know what is best for you, what is right, what is correct. So Allah will grant it to you.

So when you take a step, when you put in effort and you ask Allah, Allah will give you what you are seeking.

❖  ❖  ❖

In Which Matters?

Remember, istikharah is something that we should be making when we want to do something that is permissible and something that is recommended — something that is good: permissible, not sinful, not forbidden. So for example, if a person is praying istikharah — should I travel or not? — that is fine, because it is permissible to travel. But if a person wants to make istikharah — should I travel to such and such place and stay at that casino and take this much money with me and place such and such bet so that perhaps I win so much more money? — no, there is no istikharah for that, because travelling to such a place to commit sin is not permissible anyway.

And istikharah is supposed to be in those actions which are mustahab, those actions which are recommended — they are not obligatory. It is not like your five daily prayers; it is not like your obligation to be good to your parents. No, it is something recommended, like for example travelling to see your family — then yes, you should do istikharah in that.

Also, when it comes to marriage, to marrying someone, istikharah is also important there. Some people think istikharah is just for marriage, only for marriage; and what they will do is they will pray istikharah themselves, or they will not do it themselves — they will hire someone, they will ask someone, they will request someone: you do istikharah for me. First of all, remember istikharah is not just for marriage; it is for any worldly matter that is permissible, that is recommended. And it is something that you should do yourself.

Another important thing is that istikharah is not in those matters which are obligatory on you. So for example, a person should not be praying istikharah to decide whether they should give zakat or not — no, zakat you have to give. Likewise there is no istikharah for going for Hajj: should I do Hajj or not? Yes, you can do istikharah about whether you should go this year or the following year, because this year you have certain responsibilities about which you are not sure. But otherwise, if there is nothing preventing you and Allah has given you the opportunity to go for Hajj, then you don’t need to decide whether Hajj is good for you or not — it is good for you already, because Allah has obligated it on you. So if you are someone who is obligated to do Hajj, then you don’t need to do istikharah. You don’t need to do istikharah to decide whether or not you should be good to your mother, whether or not you should be good to your father, whether or not you should fast in Ramadan, whether or not you should give your zakat. These are all obligations on you.

The Manner of It

How do you perform istikharah? About this also many people are confused. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught us the way of doing istikharah, as he would teach us a surah of the Qur’an, so the sunnah is very clear about how istikharah is supposed to be performed.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that when one of you is preoccupied about a matter — meaning they are concerned, they are worried about a matter, they need to make an important decision — then what should they do? They should perform two rak‘ah; and secondly, these two rak‘ah should be other than the obligatory salah. So for example it should not be the two rak‘ah of Fajr; it should be two voluntary rak‘ah. And then after the two rak‘ah he should say the du’a that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught.

So we learn a number of things. First of all, the two rak‘ah have to be other than the faridah; however, they can be even your sunnah prayers. So for example you prayed the four of Zuhr, and after that you have to pray two rak‘ah of sunnah anyway, and the two sunnah are not obligatory; so you perform the two sunnah and then you pray the istikharah — you make the du’a of istikharah — and that is correct. However, some of the ulama say that no, these two rak‘ah are specific to istikharah, so after your sunnah you should perform two more rak‘ah and then make the du’a of istikharah. Remember that both ways are permissible.

And sometimes you have the time to pray the two rak‘ah and make the du’a; other times you don’t have that opportunity — for example you are in a rush, you have to step out of the house, or you don’t have very long to make the decision, or your child is crying, your baby is crying, you have to go back to a class, you have to go back to your work desk. So then, after your two sunnah prayers even, you can make the du’a of istikharah. But it would be good, when you do have the time and the ability, to pray the two rak‘ah of istikharah and then make the du’a. And then after the two rak‘ah we should raise our hands and make the du’a of istikharah.

If You Cannot Pray the Two Rak‘ah

There is a question: what if a person is not able to perform the two rak‘ah? So for example a woman is menstruating; she is not able to pray two rak‘ah, but she has to make an important decision that is urgent and cannot wait until her period ends. Or for example you are outside of your house, you are in a store, and you find a very good deal, and the person is saying that today is the last day, the store closes in thirty minutes, this is the last piece that is left, and you buy it now or you lose the deal. So now you don’t have the time to find a bathroom, make wudu, find a place to pray, do two rak‘ah and then make du’a. Or even if you have the time, you don’t always have the ability.

But it is an important decision — for example you are buying a mattress for your bed, something you have to use every single day, and if that mattress is not good, if it doesn’t turn out to be good for your back, it is going to be very difficult for you; so it is a major decision. Sometimes you have to buy travel tickets, plane tickets, and the deal is going to expire in ten minutes, five minutes. So then, before you make the decision to purchase, or before you make the purchase, you can just make the du’a of istikharah. Imam an-Nawawi said that if a person is unable to perform the two rak‘ah of istikharah, then he can just make the du’a of istikharah.

And this shows us that we should learn the du’a of istikharah, and we should also have it accessible — maybe save a screenshot on your phone, so that you have it accessible.

What to Recite, and When

When it comes to the two rak‘ah of istikharah, there is no surah that has been specified. You can recite any portion of the Qur’an in the first rak‘ah and in the second rak‘ah. You could recite a surah or verses that give you hope, that assure you of Allah’s promises, of the good that Allah gives His slaves — or any portion of the Qur’an; it is permissible.

Another question: when can you pray istikharah, meaning at which time of day or night? Remember, there is no fixed time. You can pray istikharah whenever you have the need to do so, because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: when one of you makes the firm intention to do something. So at the time when you have to make the decision, at the time when you have to go ahead with your decision, you can pray istikharah.

Now there is a question: there are certain times in the day when we are forbidden from prayer — the time when the sun is rising, the time when the sun is setting, and the time when it is at its peak, at the time of zawal. There is a clear hadith in which we learn that it is forbidden to pray at these times. But remember that this is for performing voluntary salah with no reason. If a person has a reason to pray, then it is allowed. So for example a person wakes up literally as the sun is rising, or just a few moments before that — what should they do? They should get up and pray Fajr if they have not prayed, because you are supposed to pray as soon as you wake up. Secondly, if there is a reason to pray: for example you have prayed ‘Asr and then you go to the masjid in order to pray Maghrib there and to eat iftar with your friends in the masjid, and you know the etiquette, that when you go to the masjid you should pray two rak‘ah — so when you enter the masjid, there is a reason to pray. If there is a reason to pray, you are allowed to pray.

Likewise, when it comes to istikharah: if you can delay the prayer of istikharah, go ahead and pray afterwards. But if it is an urgent matter, then there is a reason now to pray istikharah, and you can pray it. So for example you have to purchase plane tickets and the travel agent is waiting — tell me now, should I go ahead or not? So you ask them: just give me five minutes. And you pray two rak‘ah, you make the du’a, and you call the agent back and say: go ahead and purchase. But if the agent says, let me know by tomorrow, then you can wait until Maghrib, and you can pray Maghrib and then do the two rak‘ah. So if it is a time when voluntary salah is forbidden, then you should delay the istikharah until the time when you can pray; however, if the matter is urgent, remember there is a reason for you to pray, and if there is a reason for a person to pray at the forbidden times then it is permissible to pray at that time.

❖  ❖  ❖

There Is No Dream to Wait For

There is a question: when you pray istikharah, what should you do after that? Should you go to sleep and wait for a dream? No. Istikharah is not a way of knowing, of finding out, what is in the unseen. Istikharah is not a way to access unseen knowledge. Istikharah is a way of asking Allah for goodness, and asking Allah to decide what is good for you, to grant you what is good for you. It is not a window into the unseen.

So when you pray istikharah, what should you do? You should put your trust in Allah, and you should trust His decision. And how do you know the answer to your istikharah? There is no answer to istikharah. Nobody is going to come in your dream and tell you. And if you think about it, sometimes in one night you have three or four dreams — so which of those dreams is the answer to your istikharah?

So remember that dreams, yes, they are mubashshirat, something through which Allah gives you good news — but you don’t base your decisions, your deen, on dreams. You ask Allah; and in the du’a of istikharah you are asking Allah anyway that if this is good for me, make it happen; and if it is not good for me, turn it away from me, and grant me something good in its place, and make me happy with it. So istikharah is a way of asking Allah for goodness.

And sometimes what happens: you pray istikharah — for example about whether or not you should marry someone — and then you go ahead with that marriage, and then that marriage turns out to be very painful, very difficult. So then you say: but I did istikharah. Yes, you did — and you know what, this difficulty that you are experiencing right now was actually good for you, and that is why Allah decreed it for you. Because any trial, any test that a believer faces, that is good for the believer; it is not bad for the believer. Everything that happens, that Allah brings about, remember there is goodness in it, because Allah does not decree what is evil.

Two Scenarios

One scenario is that before you make an important decision, you consult people who can give you good advice, you do your research, you weigh the pros and cons; and then when your heart is determined on one matter, when you are determined that you are going to go ahead with this decision, before you make the decision you pray istikharah. So for example you want to travel: before you purchase the tickets for a certain date, you consult your family — is this good? — you consult your boss: is it good if I travel at this time? You consult someone who has travelled recently, and you figure out that yes, this is a good time to travel. Then before you make the purchase of the plane tickets, what do you do? You do istikharah. And when you do istikharah you are asking Allah to make it good for you.

Another scenario is that you have a couple of options before you and you don’t know which one to choose. So now you are completely indecisive. So first of all you consult people — you do istisharah, you consult people: not everybody, but those people who are people of knowledge and understanding, people who understand your situation, who can advise you what is good for you. And then you pray istikharah: ya Allah — asking Allah to make the choice, the decision, for you.

Now what happens after istikharah? You feel more inclined towards one option. So remember you can do istikharah again, and you can pray istikharah again and again, until you are confident about a particular decision. So remember you are allowed to make istikharah more than once, until you are firm, until you are confident, about a certain decision. This is permissible.

Can Someone Else Do It for You?

There is a question: can you ask someone else to do istikharah for you? You can only ask them to do istikharah for you if the decision also applies to them — along with doing istikharah yourself.

So for example, let us say you want to purchase a house. Now before you make that purchase, what do you do? You pray istikharah; and you also ask your spouse to pray istikharah, because they are going to be living in it; and you ask your parents also to do istikharah, because they are going to be living in it. So if the decision affects other people, then yes, they should also do istikharah. But otherwise, if they are not affected by that decision, if it has nothing to do with them, then no, you don’t ask other people to pray in your place.

And just like that, you don’t tell other people to pray istikharah for you — because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that when one of you wants to make a decision, then he should pray two rak‘ah. The person who is affected by the decision should pray the two rak‘ah. And when it comes to salah, you cannot ask someone else to pray on your behalf. So for example you go to the masjid with your friend and you say: oh, I’m so tired, I’m just going to sit down, can you pray the two rak‘ah of the masjid for me? No, you don’t tell your friend to pray for you; you have to pray yourself. If you are unwell you cannot ask your child to pray for you — no, you have to pray yourself. Just like that, when it comes to the prayer of istikharah, you have to do it yourself; and the people who are affected by that decision, they should also pray istikharah, because it affects them.

Never a Fortune Teller

Another important thing is that we should not go to a fortune teller for istikharah. SubhanAllah, some people will pay a fortune teller a huge sum of money and ask: should I marry this person or not? And then that fortune teller has a bird, and the bird will be let loose and the bird will pick something, and based on that they will say yes, go ahead with it, or no, don’t go ahead with it. Or they will put their hand on some glass globe and make some sounds, and they will say go ahead with it or don’t go ahead with it.

This is very dangerous. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that whoever goes to a fortune teller and then confirms him in what he says — meaning he believes the fortune teller — then he is disbelieving in what was revealed to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. And this will ruin a person’s faith. So be careful.

And SubhanAllah, this is so common: that people will ask someone, they will pay someone — pray istikharah for me regarding this matter — and then they will call them and they will say: yes, we did this istikharah for you, and you should not go ahead with this marriage, because this person is evil in this and this way, and if you do, then such and such will happen. They will start talking about matters of the future, matters of the unseen. This is wrong. When it comes to istikharah, this is salah, that you have to perform yourself. So you do it; you don’t hire someone, you don’t pay someone, you don’t ask someone else to do it for you.

If Hardship Comes Afterwards

Sometimes you do istikharah and then afterwards you experience some pain or hardship or difficulty. Then remember that that difficulty was good for you. And also remember that it may appear to be something evil for you, something bad for you, but hidden inside it is much more good.

So for example you make istikharah before travelling, and when you travel, what happens — may Allah protect you — sometimes people get sick, they get into an accident, their wallet gets stolen, and then they are not able to find a means of travelling back home on time, and then their work gets affected. And so they say: oh my God, I have suffered so much since I travelled, and I actually prayed istikharah. Well, maybe that sickness was a means of purification for you, and that loss was a means of increase in your ranks.

Hadith

Allah has a certain status for a slave — meaning Allah wants the slave to reach that position, that status, that higher level. And a person is not able to reach that level merely with his deeds. So then Allah puts that slave to the test; Allah puts him in trial in regard to his body, or his wealth, or his child. A person suffers illness, or they get fired from their job, or their child suffers — and then the person is patient, and because of that patience Allah makes that person reach that higher level.

Allahu Akbar. So yes, on the surface there was suffering, there was loss, there was pain — but hidden inside was much, much more good, that is permanent, that is everlasting.

So when you pray istikharah, then after that focus on the good; and no matter what happens, believe that it is good for you, because you asked Allah for goodness, and Allah will grant you that goodness. And even if something painful happens, remember that is good for you. Do not attribute evil to Allah. Do not say: O Allah, You did such and such evil to me — astaghfirullah. Don’t say such negative things, wrong things, about Allah.

And praying istikharah means that you are trusting Allah’s decision; you are asking Allah to make the choice for you, the decision for you. So this is a form of tawakkul. Sometimes you are so busy, so tired mentally, there are so many things going on, that you cannot decide what to cook. So what do you do? You just ask your family: what do you want to eat? And they say rice and lentils. So what do you do? You just go and make that. In your mind you might be thinking: I don’t know if they are going to enjoy it, I don’t know if they are going to like it, we just had this recently. But no — they said this is what they want, so you go ahead with it, because you don’t have the mental bandwidth to make that decision.

Just like that, you don’t always have the mental bandwidth to make decisions for yourself, to know what is really good for you. So you ask Allah to make that decision, to choose what is best for you. And then once Allah decrees something for you, now you trust Allah’s decision.

And when sometimes after istikharah you still suffer, remind yourself: the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the sweetness of this world is the bitterness of the hereafter, and the bitterness of this world is the sweetness of the hereafter. Allahu Akbar.

When you are fasting, is it always easy? No. You experience thirst, you experience so much fatigue, a headache maybe. If you have seen your children fasting this Ramadan, you may have noticed that they look a little weaker, their cheeks may appear to have gone in, they may not have the energy to do their homework or anything. Yes, you feel for them — but you know that fasting is good for them and they should fast, because Allah has obligated fasting on them. So yes, you see them struggling, but you know that it is worth it, because the reward in the hereafter is much greater.

Just like that, if you experience anything painful after praying istikharah, then remind yourself that the bitterness of the world is the sweetness of the hereafter. And actions are determined by how they end. So if the final outcome is good — that you are pleased with Allah, and you are obedient to Allah, and your deen is fine — then everything is good, insha’Allah.

Chapter Ninety

The Du’as for Asking What Is Good

The du’a of istikharah, and the du’as for khayr
1. The du’a of istikharah
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِي الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ

O Allah, I seek Your choice by Your knowledge, and I seek Your decree by Your power, and I ask You of Your great favour. For indeed You decree and I do not decree, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of all unseen matters. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in regard to my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me and make it easy for me and then bless me in it. And if You know that this matter is bad for me in regard to my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, and then make me pleased with it.

Astakhiruka bi ‘ilmik — I ask You for the good because of Your knowledge; I am praying istikharah to You, asking You for good, asking You to make the choice for me. Why? Because of Your knowledge, because You know everything and I don’t know everything; You have perfect knowledge of my situation and of what is good for me, and I do not.

Wa astaqdiruka bi qudratik — I seek from You because You have qudrah; You have the ability; all power is in Your hand, it is not in my hand; You are able to do everything, You make the final decree, and I don’t. Wa as’aluka min fadlika al-‘azim — and I ask You for Your great favour. And this shows us that whatever we have of good, it is from Allah.

And then we say that indeed You are the One who decrees and I am not the one who decrees; You have power and I do not have power; wa ta‘lamu wa la a‘lam — and You know and I do not know. You know the knowledge of the unseen; You know the internal and the external, the hidden and the visible; You know what is good and what is evil. So You encompass everything in knowledge and I do not know. And You are the Knower of all unseen matters; nothing is unseen from You. Sometimes you are making a decision, for example whether or not to marry someone: they appear to be good, but you don’t know — what if they are hiding some really terrible things from you? Or you think they are good for you in one way, but who knows, they could be terrible for you in many other ways. So: O Allah, You are the Knower of all unseen matters.

Then you say Allahumma in kunta ta‘lamu — O Allah, if You know. Now you may be wondering: doesn’t Allah know everything? Why do we say “O Allah, if You know”? Of course Allah knows everything. This is just a style of speech, and what you are saying is: O Allah, if in Your knowledge You know this matter to be good for me — because You know everything and I don’t know everything — then if this is good for me fi dini wa ma‘ashi wa ‘aqibati amri, in terms of my religion, in terms of my livelihood, and in terms of my final outcome, then decree it for me, make it happen for me.

And if You know that this matter is bad for me, evil for me, in regard to my religion, in regard to my livelihood, in regard to my final outcome, then fasrifhu ‘anni wasrifni ‘anhu — turn it away from me, and turn me away from it.

And this is so beautiful. Turn it away from me — because when something is in front of you, then you are tempted; and the more you see it, the more tempted you are. So if it is not good for you, you are asking Allah: turn it away from me, so I don’t even see it, because if I see it I am going to be tempted, I am going to wish for it. And turn me away from it — turn my heart away from it. Because sometimes our heart is still clinging to something that we cannot have, and because it is clinging to it, it is yearning for it, and we are sad and not able to think about anything else; we are not able to enjoy the other things that Allah has given us.

And then decree for me something good from wherever it may be — because You own everything, You are able to do all things, so You will give me something good in its place, and You know how to bring it about. And then make me happy with it — because so often a person has something but they are not happy with it, they are not pleased with it. So you are asking Allah: ya Allah, You are able to decree what is good for me, so You make it happen however You can, and then grant me happiness with it also; make me pleased with it.

And notice: O Allah, if You know this to be good for me or bad for me in terms of my religion, my livelihood, and my final outcome. Notice how, out of the three, what is mentioned first? My religion — because deen is the most important. And then ma‘ashi, my livelihood, my life, my income, my house, my food, my money. And then my final outcome, my final destination in the hereafter, or the final outcome of the matter I am deciding about. If it is really good for me, make it happen; if it is bad for me, then turn it away from me.

❖  ❖  ❖

Besides the du’a of istikharah, we can also make some other du’as to ask Allah for what is good for us.

2. The du’a of Musa (‘alayhis salam)
رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

O my Lord, indeed I am in desperate need of whatever good You send down to me. And this is a very comprehensive du’a which includes the goodness of this world and the goodness of the hereafter; it includes goodness in terms of money, in terms of family, in terms of security, in terms of your home — everything. So make this du’a for yourself.

3. Guide me to the most correct of my affair
اللَّهُمَّ اهْدِنِي لِأَرْشَدِ أَمْرِي وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ نَفْسِي

O Allah, guide me to the most correct of my affair, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would teach this du’a. So we should make this du’a also when we are confused about a matter, when we don’t know what to do, when we are indecisive: ya Allah, guide me to the most correct of my affair — what is the best option for me? Guide me to that.

4. All good, that which I know and that which I do not
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنَ الْخَيْرِ كُلِّهِ عَاجِلِهِ وَآجِلِهِ، مَا عَلِمْتُ مِنْهُ وَمَا لَمْ أَعْلَمْ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الشَّرِّ كُلِّهِ عَاجِلِهِ وَآجِلِهِ، مَا عَلِمْتُ مِنْهُ وَمَا لَمْ أَعْلَمْ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ عَبْدُكَ وَنَبِيُّكَ مُحَمَّدٌ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا عَاذَ بِهِ عَبْدُكَ وَنَبِيُّكَ مُحَمَّدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَا قَرَّبَ إِلَيْهَا مِنْ قَوْلٍ أَوْ عَمَلٍ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ كُلَّ قَضَاءٍ قَضَيْتَهُ لِي خَيْرًا

O Allah, I ask You for all that is good, that which comes quickly and that which comes later, that which I know of it and that which I do not know; and I seek refuge in You from all evil, that which comes quickly and that which comes later, that which I know of it and that which I do not know. O Allah, I ask You for the good that Your worshipper and Your Prophet Muhammad asked You for, and I seek refuge in You from the evil that Your worshipper and Your Prophet Muhammad sought refuge in You from. O Allah, I ask You for paradise and whatever can bring me close to it in word or in action; and I ask You to make every decree that You have decreed for me good.

‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) reported this du’a. All types of goodness — everything good for me, that which can come quickly and that which comes later, meaning the good of this world and the good of the hereafter; the good that I know and also the good that I don’t know. Because sometimes you believe something is good for you, so you ask Allah to grant it to you — but what if there is something so good for you, excellent for you, and you don’t even know that it is out there, you don’t even know that it is good for you? If you don’t know, you are not going to pray for it. So in this du’a you are asking Allah to grant you what is good for you, whether you know about it or you don’t know about it.

And: anything good that he prayed for, O Allah, I pray for the same good for myself; and O Allah, I ask You to protect me from everything evil that the Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam asked You to protect him from. And whatever can bring me close to paradise in terms of word or in terms of action — ya Allah, grant me that. And I ask You that You make every decree You have decreed for me good: anything You have decreed for me, ya Allah, make it good for me. This is such an excellent du’a. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught this to someone he loved, so we should also make this du’a for ourselves.

5. In the evening
أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَخَيْرِ مَا فِيهَا وَخَيْرِ مَا بَعْدَهَا، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهَا

We have entered the evening and the dominion has entered the evening belonging to Allah; and all praise is for Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what comes after it; and I seek Your protection against the evil of this night, and the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what comes after it.

6. In the morning
أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرِ مَا فِيهِ وَخَيْرِ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ

The same du’a, with slightly different wording: instead of amsayna we say asbahna, because you are entering the morning and not the evening; and you ask Allah for the good which is in this day. So this is what we should say regularly in the morning and in the evening — and we should say it with attention: ask Allah for what is good and for protection from anything that is evil.

7. When the wind blows
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا فِيهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا فِيهَا وَشَرِّ مَا أُرْسِلَتْ بِهِ

O Allah, I ask You for its goodness, the goodness that is in it, and the goodness that it was sent with; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil that is in it, and the evil that it was sent with. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would make this du’a when the wind blew.

Now you might say: how does the wind affect me, I am inside the house? Well, it may not directly affect you, but indirectly it certainly can. How often it happens that a wind turns into a storm, or because of the wind trees are uprooted, or there is a power outage, and because of that heat and water get affected, pipes in houses can burst — and not just that, food shortages can happen. So don’t think yourself too secure. Ask Allah for the good that is in the wind, and to protect you from the evil that is in it. Sometimes it happens that when it is too windy and you are in your car, as you get out and open the door the door closes on you — because of the wind — and that can cause a bone to fracture, it can cause you to get seriously injured. So ask Allah for good when the wind blows also.

8. When something new comes into your life
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا جُبِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا جُبِلَتْ عَلَيْهِ

O Allah, I ask You for its goodness and the good that it was created with, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil that it was made with. We learn in a hadith that when a person gets married, or gets a new animal — meaning a means of transportation — or a new servant, when something new comes into your life and this something new is very integral to you and is going to directly affect you, then you ask Allah for the good in it. Because anything new that comes into your house, into your life, there is good in it, and there can also be potential evil in it. So you are asking Allah to grant you the good and protect you from anything evil in it.

9. When wearing new clothes
اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ كَسَوْتَنِيهِ، أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِهِ وَخَيْرِ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهِ وَشَرِّ مَا صُنِعَ لَهُ

O Allah, Yours is all praise; You are the One who has clothed me. I ask You for its goodness and the goodness of that for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of that for which it was made. So often it happens that you wear something new and it looks nice on you, it looks good on you — but then it is not right for the weather and you get too cold or too hot, or that material is not suitable for your skin and you develop a rash. So these things can happen. So even when you are wearing something new, ask Allah to grant you the good that is in it.

10. After eating
اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَأَطْعِمْنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ

O Allah, bless us in it and feed us better than it. When you eat something, also ask Allah to give you what is good, to make what you ate good for you.

11. When someone is good to you
جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا

May Allah reward you with goodness.

12. When two people get married
بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِي خَيْرٍ

May Allah bless you and shower His blessings upon you, and join you together in goodness.

All of these du’as teach us that no matter what the situation is, no matter how confident or secure we feel, and no matter how afraid or apprehensive we feel — in every situation we should ask Allah for goodness: in our food, in our clothing, in our relationships, in anything new that enters our lives, in the coming day and the coming night. In everything, ask Allah to grant you goodness.

Wa aqdur li al-khayra haythu kan, thumma ardini bih.
Ameen.
Chapter Ninety-One

Among the People Are Those Who Say

Du’a is a means of receiving what you desire, what you wish for. Du’a reflects what your goals are, what your wishes are. It reflects your beliefs, and what kind of a person you really are. And we ask Allah for good things in this life and also for good things in the next life because Allah is able to give us both.

Those who aim high don’t just ask Allah for good things right now, or just in this life. They ask Allah for a lot, because they know that the treasures of Allah are great; none knows the forces of Allah except He, and Allah has the keys to the treasures — He is the One who owns everything, and He is the possessor of great favour. So when we ask Allah, we should have high hopes. We should aim high. We shouldn’t settle for asking for a few things, or little things. We should ask Allah for big things, for many things, for many favours, because Allah is able to give us all of them and even more than we can imagine, more than we can even think of.

The Qur’an — Surat al-Baqarah

“And when you have completed your rites, remember Allah like your remembrance of your fathers, or with greater remembrance. And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world’ — and he will have in the Hereafter no share. But among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account.”

The Fair at Mina

Before the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, in the time of jahiliyyah, the mushrikun would hold a fair at Mina upon the completion of the rituals of Hajj. And as they would spend their time eating and drinking, they would also boast about their greatness by talking about their ancestors.

So they are told here: leave such talk. Do not waste your time talking about the greatness of your ancestors; the time you used to spend in frivolous things, now you should spend in the remembrance of Allah, in mentioning Him. Because the remembrance of Allah is something that brings contentment to everyone’s heart, but the remembrance of forefathers can bring a lot of discomfort and a sense of low self-worth to some people.

For example, if you sit with your friends and you talk about how great a house your grandfather had, how much land he owned, how he was the authority in his village, how much food would come into the house and how much charity would go out of it — if you talk about the greatness and the wealth of your ancestors, you feel good about that. But those listening to you don’t necessarily enjoy it, because they will instantly compare you to themselves, and they will feel inferior — because they did not have a grandfather or an ancestor who was as wealthy, or as generous, or even someone who believed.

So Allah is teaching us here that we should talk about those things that everyone finds happiness in, not those matters that cause discomfort and hurt to others. And the dhikr of Allah is something that brings tranquillity to everyone’s heart.

Dhikr First, Then Du’a

Here people are taught: remember Allah much. And after that, Allah directs our attention towards du’a — because first dhikr is mentioned, and then du’a is mentioned. So this shows us that when a person makes du’a after a lot of dhikr, then it can be hoped that their du’a will be granted.

And remember that Hajj has many different rituals, many different places you have to go to: Mina, then ‘Arafah, then Muzdalifah, then back to Mina; and at Mina you have to do the stoning, the ramy al-jimar, and offer the sacrifice, and then the trimming or shaving of the head. So after completing all of the rituals of Hajj, then remember Allah.

It is very common in people that after they complete an act of worship they tend to forget to remember Allah. Why? Because on completing a certain act of worship, we feel: okay, we’ve done something, we’ve completed it, now I’m on a break, I’m free — and being free means comfort yourself, enjoy yourself, go eat, go rest.

But this is not limited to Hajj; this is applicable to all acts of worship. We are taught that after the month of fasting we should glorify Allah, we should say the takbir on the day of ‘Eid — the day of ‘Eid is a day of dhikr. After praying salah also we should make dhikr, and we have discussed that in great detail earlier. So after completing any act of worship, remember the dhikr of Allah.

And this is very important — why? Because remembering Allah after completing an act of worship is taking the effect of that worship along with you into whatever work you are doing now. You want to benefit from what you just did.

And here, remembering Allah means specifically in the days of Mina, by saying the takbirat, and it also includes making du’a, calling upon Allah. Remember Allah as you used to remember your forefathers — or rather, ashadd, remember Allah with even more attentiveness, more sincerity, more frequency, in greater abundance.

❖  ❖  ❖

The First Group

Then it is said: among the people are those who say, “Our Lord, give us in this world” — and they shall have no share in the Hereafter. Why? Because they are only praying for good things in this world. Rabbana atina fid-dunya — give us in the world. Give us what? Our share, anything of benefit, anything we desire; give us those good things here.

Ibn ‘Abbas (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that there were bedouins among the Arabs who would come to ‘Arafah, or to different places of Hajj, and one of them would stand up and make du’a saying: O God, make this year a year of rain and plenty and abundance and healthy children. That is all they would pray for. They would not pray for anything related to the Hereafter; they would not pray for Allah’s forgiveness, they would not pray for Paradise, they would not pray for any reward in the Hereafter, or for the acceptance of their deeds. They were only concerned about the things of the world.

And the reason for this is that they simply did not believe in the Hereafter. And when they did not believe in the Hereafter, then their Hajj was for the sake of the world, their prayers were for the sake of the world, their efforts — everything, whatever they spent in order to get there, whatever they did in order to get to Hajj — all of it was dedicated to just getting more dunya.

And this is very similar to how people are today: that people will exert a lot of effort seeking the good things of the world. They will exert not only physical effort, but they will invest financially, and they will even try to do different things spiritually — whether it is meditation, or saying certain affirmations on a regular basis — in order to get more of the world.

Al-Baghawi said that this ayah is referring to the mushrikun, the polytheists, who when they would come for Hajj would only pray for the things of this world. For example they would say: O Allah, give us goats and camels and cows and slaves. A man would get up and say: my lord, my father used to have a huge tent and he had a lot of wealth, so give me the same as You gave him.

Qatadah said that this is the person whose sole concern is the dunya. So he spends his money for the sake of the dunya, and he works for the sake of the dunya, and he gets tired and exhausted and bears hardship and difficulty — only for the sake of the dunya.

SubhanAllah, this is something so common today that even among Muslims their entire concern is the things of the world: whether it is a career they want to establish, a name they want to make, a title they want to achieve, a house they want to build, a certain amount of money they want to have, or shares they want to own. The ultimate concern is just the dunya, and so their education, their work, their mental energy, their prayers — even if they have some spirituality, even that is dedicated to just getting more dunya. Such a person will have no share in the Hereafter. Why? Because he never wanted it. He never prayed for it. He never asked for it. He only wanted the world, and that is all he asked for.

The Second Group

And among them are those who say, “Our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.” Meaning: all people are not like that. There are those who believe in the Hereafter, who aim for the Hereafter, who seek the Hereafter as well. They seek the world and they also seek the Hereafter. They want both.

And this is the person who aims very high, who asks Allah for a lot, because he knows that Allah is capable of giving a lot. So he is not just praying for dunya; he is also praying for eternity, for the Akhirah.

When a person makes du’a for dunya, they are asking for something that will benefit them for how long? Maybe five years, twenty years, thirty years — who knows; less than a hundred years. But when a person prays for something good in the Hereafter, this means that they want that benefit for eternity, forever and ever. So why do we aim so low? Why should we ask for very little, when Allah is capable of giving us so much more?

Chapter Ninety-Two

What Hasanah Means, Here and There

They ask Allah firstly for good things in the world — because they are living in the world, and in order to live this life in a good way, and in order to prepare for the Hereafter, a person must have access to good things.

Hasanah in This World

What is hasanah in the world? It includes ample and lawful sustenance. A person prays for ample, lawful sustenance, money, wealth — because this is good for the believer; he will use his good wealth to earn the pleasure of Allah. If a person has ample wealth that he has earned lawfully, this means he can go for ‘Umrah, he can go for Hajj regularly, he can travel for the sake of Allah, he can support those who are in need of help, he can build a masjid, he can sponsor students of knowledge, he can spend in the way of Allah. There is so much that he can do with his lawfully earned wealth.

Secondly, it includes a righteous spouse — and being married is a very normal wish that any person can have. If a person prays for a righteous spouse who will assist them not only in their worldly matters but also in preparing for the home of the Hereafter, this is excellent.

Then hasanah in the world includes righteous children: good children, healthy children, obedient children, children who have very good manners. And it includes comfort, and rest, and ease, and convenience in life, as well as beneficial knowledge and righteous actions. And all permissible things are included in hasanah in the world.

Hasanah in the Hereafter

But they don’t just ask for hasanah in the world; they also ask Allah for hasanah in the Hereafter. And hasanah in the Hereafter is of course Jannah, because Allah says that those people who have done good in the world shall have al-husna, the most excellent reward in the Hereafter, which is Jannah — and wa ziyadah, and even more than that.

So yes, it includes Paradise, but not just Jannah; it includes more than that. A person asks for hasanah in the Hereafter, and this includes: ya Allah, grant me safety and protection on the Day of Judgement; ya Allah, grant me beauty in Paradise; grant me an easy hisab; make my deeds heavy in the scale; give me my record of deeds in my right hand; protect me from punishment in the grave, and on the Day of Judgement in the great gathering; grant me Your approval, grant me Your closeness, give me the privilege to see You, bestow on me Your ridwan, Your approval. So the list of hasanah in the Hereafter is endless, because the Hereafter is endless.

And Save Us From the Fire

And one more thing they pray for: and save us from the punishment of the Fire. Meaning: ya Allah, protect me from those deeds that lead a person to Hellfire, and forgive me my sins so that I am not punished with the Fire. So guard me against those deeds which could lead me to Hellfire; and if there are any sins I have already committed, ya Allah, forgive me for those also.

❖  ❖  ❖

The Most Complete Du’a

This du’a is the most comprehensive and complete du’a — which means that if you don’t know any other du’a, and you know this du’a, then you know what to ask Allah for. You are asking for goodness in the world, goodness in the Hereafter, and protection against the Hellfire. These are the three main things that each person needs, that each person wishes for.

And sometimes there are situations in your life where you are not able to make a lot of du’a. You would like to, you want to, you make the intention that now I am going to sit and make du’a — but what happens, especially if you have little children, is that you are needed; or you have many obligations; or you are at work; or you have your exams. And even when you do make time, you are mentally so occupied, you are being called from different directions, that you are not able to make that time for yourself.

In such times, do not leave making du’a for yourself. You must make du’a for yourself no matter how busy you are — but learn the most effective way of asking Allah, the best du’as that you can make for yourself. And this is one of those: very comprehensive and very complete. This is why this du’a is given preference over other du’as as well.

Hadith

Qatadah asked Anas: which du’a did the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam make the most? He said: the du’a he would make most frequently is “Allahumma atina fid-dunya hasanatan, wa fil-akhirati hasanatan, wa qina ‘adhab an-nar.”

And whenever Anas would want to make du’a, he would always begin with this du’a: first he would make this du’a, and then he would make some other.

We learn in another narration that Anas was told that some people have come to see you from Basrah, and they want that you should make du’a for them. So he said: O Allah, forgive us and have mercy on us, and give us in the world good and in the Hereafter good, and save us from the punishment of the Fire. So those people said: make more du’a — we came all the way here and we want you to make du’a for us, so ask for something else. So he said the same du’a again, and then he said: if you are given this, you have been given the good of this world and the next — what more do you want?

Hadith

Anas reported that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam visited a man who was so weak that he had become like a baby bird. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam asked him: did you not used to ask your Lord for sound health, is there something that you used to pray for? The man said: I used to say, O Allah, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: SubhanAllah, you are not capable of that. Why did you not say, “Allahumma atina fid-dunya hasanatan, wa fil-akhirati hasanatan, wa qina ‘adhab an-nar”?

So this shows us that this is a du’a we should make when we want something — whether it is health or wealth or family, children, success, education, anything that we want of this world; or anything we want of the Hereafter: Paradise, forgiveness, ease on the Day of Judgement. We can make this du’a.

And we can also make this du’a when we are feeling extremely bad and guilty about our sins, ashamed of the wrong things that we have done. Sometimes we have a lot of hope in Allah’s mercy, and then there are other times when we have a lot of fear — when we are very afraid, when we think: I don’t know what is going to become of me, I don’t know if I am going to be forgiven because of such and such sin of mine, or such and such shortcoming. Don’t fall into despair at that time; rather make this du’a, which is so comprehensive.

This du’a is also meant to be made during tawaf, especially when a person is walking between the two corners. Ibn Rajab said that the salaf would especially make this du’a in the days of tashriq, in the days of Mina at Hajj. And ‘Ata said that any person who goes for Hajj and is returning to his family, to his home, should make this du’a.

And Imam an-Nawawi said that there is no specified time or place for this du’a, because this is something a person can make at any time, any moment, any place. A person can make this du’a in their salah, outside of salah, at the beginning of their du’a, in the middle, at the end. You can make it when visiting someone who is ill, as the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught. You can make it when performing the rituals of Hajj. So make sure that you know this du’a well, and that you teach it to your children and encourage them to make it; and encourage your family to make it too.

In the Qur’an the wording is Rabbana atina, and in the sunnah the du’a begins with the word Allahumma.

Those Will Have a Share of What They Have Earned

Allah says regarding these people that they will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account.
