Meaning each group will have their reward according to what they have done, according to what they have earned. Allah will recompense people based on their intentions and their efforts. And ula’ika here refers to both groups: those who pray only for dunya, and also those who pray for dunya and Akhirah. Those who pray only for dunya will only have dunya — however much dunya Allah had already written for them. And those who pray for dunya and Akhirah will get both, because that is what they are praying for, that is what they are asking for.

And it has been said that this verse shows that Allah hears everyone’s du’a — whether they are Muslim or not, whether they worship Allah the right way or not, whether they commit sins or not. Every person: Allah is the One who hears, He is the One who gives to people what they ask for.

And “Allah is swift in account” — on the Day of Judgement Allah will take the accounts of people very quickly. And do not think that the Hereafter is far; it is very near. You don’t know, perhaps the Hour is very near.

Because sometimes we focus our du’as only on the things of the world, because they are immediate — we see them, so we feel like they are more urgent, more real to us; and the Hereafter seems very far, and what is far seems to be unlikely, and so we forget what is going to come later and we just focus on the present. Don’t make that mistake. Focus on the present and also on the future.

Chapter Ninety-Three

Eight Lessons From This Du’a

1. Pray for both the dunya and the Akhirah

Whenever you make du’a for anything — whether it is health, or your children, or your safety, or your success in your exams, or for your parents — also pray for the Akhirah. Your du’a should not be focused only on the good things of the world. And if you don’t know what to ask for, then at least make this du’a, because it covers all of the good things of the Hereafter: those you know of and those you don’t, those you can think of and those you cannot think of.

2. Ask for more of the Hereafter than of the world

In this du’a which Allah is teaching us, for dunya we are asking for just one thing — our Lord, give us good in this world — but when it comes to the Hereafter, we are asking for two things: good in the Hereafter, and protection from the punishment of the Fire. So if you divide your du’a into three sections, one section should be for the dunya and two for the Hereafter. Or: for any good thing you ask Allah for in this world, ask double of that for the Hereafter.

3. Call upon Him by His names and attributes

The du’a begins with Rabbana in the Qur’an, and with Allahumma in the sunnah. Allah says: call upon Allah by His names. Address Him, talk to Him, take His name — of course very respectfully, with love, with fear, with adoration, with reverence and respect, with all of those good feelings; but take His name. Some people, when they are making du’a, don’t say things like Allahumma or Rabbana. So call upon Allah by His names and His attributes. And notice that in this du’a an action of Allah is also mentioned — wa qina, and save us — because it is Allah who saves, it is Allah who protects.

4. Aim high

Aim very, very high. If you are asking Allah for wealth, don’t just pray for a thousand dollars; don’t just pray for fifty thousand; pray for millions, because Allah is able to give you that. When you want to get a car and you are making du’a, don’t pray for just any car — ya Allah, I want any car as long as it moves, even if it’s rickety and old and rusted and it has a million problems, it’s okay, I just desperately want a car. Don’t pray like that. Make du’a for a car that is good, that will not give you trouble, that is very comfortable, very spacious, that you can use for a very long time.

Aim high. Because when is it that you ask for little favours? You ask for little favours from people — which people? The people who have very little to give. But when you know that someone is very generous and they have a lot to give, then you don’t ask for little favours; you ask for huge favours, you don’t hesitate asking. So with Allah, don’t hesitate asking.

5. There is nothing wrong in asking for the world

There is nothing wrong in asking Allah for good things in the world, as long as a person is also praying for good things in the Hereafter. If you find out that someone is making du’a in the month of Ramadan for a new car, you might say: oh, look at them, they’re praying for dunya, which is so lowly. There is nothing wrong in praying for dunya as long as a person is also praying for the Akhirah — because this is what we are being taught here. Ask Allah for good things here in the world and ask Allah for good things in the Hereafter. Ask for both.

6. Everyone is in need of this du’a

Every person, no matter who they are, is in need of good things in this world and good things in the Hereafter. You could be very wealthy, you could be healthy; maybe you have memorised the Qur’an, maybe you have done Hajj and many ‘Umrahs in your life; maybe you give a lot of sadaqah as well, maybe you teach people a lot of good things. You still need more good things in the world and good things in the Hereafter. Because it has not been said that this du’a is especially for those who are in difficulty, or those who are suffering, or those who are poor or struggling. No — this du’a is for everyone. Never feel that since Allah has blessed you with good health and good wealth you should not be asking Allah for good things in the world. You should still be asking, because for the believer every good thing in the world becomes a means of earning more good in the Hereafter.

7. Pray with hope and fear

On the one hand we have hope when we say: ya Allah, give us good in the world, give us good in the Hereafter — you are asking for something good, you have hope. And then you also have fear when you say: and save us from the punishment of the Fire. So combine both fear and hope. Ask Allah to give you the things that you desire, and also ask Allah to protect you from the things that you are afraid of.

8. Use the du’as of the Qur’an

The du’as which Allah mentions in His book are truly excellent, very comprehensive, meaningful. So in the du’as we make, we should include the du’as that Allah has taught in the Qur’an. These Rabbana du’as are very comprehensive and very complete in their meaning, so we should learn them and we should make them.

Chapter Ninety-Four

Whoever Seeks Only the World

In these verses, people who only seek the dunya have been condemned. And this is something we should bear in mind: that we should not just be seekers of this dunya, because the Hereafter is better and it is more lasting.

No matter how much of this dunya we can have, remember it is limited, it is temporary, and every good thing in this world is such that it also brings with it some kind of challenge. So for example, if you ask Allah to give you a big house, then of course you also have to pay taxes; you also have to pay for the bills, and maybe you have to pay for the maintenance, and maybe you have to work very hard yourself to maintain that house, to clean that house.

So we should not just be seeking the dunya, because the Hereafter is better and more lasting. If you want a good house in the world, ask Allah for it; ask Allah to make it good for you. But along with that, also pray Rabbi ibni li ‘indaka baytan fil jannah — O my Lord, build for me a house near You in Jannah. I want a house in Paradise. And anything that you wish for in the world because you feel like it is going to be very beneficial for you, remind yourself that the benefit of the world is little, and the Hereafter is way better for the one who has taqwa of Allah.

In a hadith we learn: know that your return is to Allah, and then there is either Jannah or the Fire. And the home of the Hereafter, whether Paradise or Hellfire, is such an abode from which there is no departure; and there is such eternity that there is no death; and there are such bodies that will not die. So focus on the Hereafter. Prepare for that, because the real life is the life of the Hereafter.

And whatever Allah gives you in this world, be grateful for it — but don’t be satisfied with it in the sense that you think that now you are successful. When you get something of the world, realise that there is much more in the Hereafter that you still need to seek. So aim for that, strive towards that, and pray for that.

❖  ❖  ❖

Doing Good Deeds Only for Worldly Gain

We also learn that the person who only seeks the world will have no share in the Hereafter. There are several verses in the Qur’an that teach this lesson: that if you seek the world, then you only get of this world what is written for you. So don’t just seek this dunya; also aim for, wish for, strive for the reward that Allah has in the Hereafter.

It has been said that if a person does good deeds only to get benefit in the world — for instance some people fast so that they can lose weight, or some people make sure that they are praying long qiyam so that they can burn more calories — if a person does good things for worldly gain, then Allah will give that person the dunya he is asking for, but in the Hereafter this person will have nothing.

So just because we are doing a good deed, that alone is not enough. We need to ask ourselves: what do I want through this good deed? What do I want Allah to give me — just benefit now, or benefit in the Hereafter as well? So aim for the Hereafter; make your intention sincere for the Akhirah, so that Allah will give you a reward over there.

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was asked about certain individuals who, before Islam, in the time of ignorance, were very generous, very hospitable, good to their relatives, who would set slaves free and give food to others: will such people be admitted into Paradise? Will their deeds help them? He said no — because these people never said, “My Lord, forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgement.”

They only aimed for dunya. They did all of these good things, whether it was out of seeking fame, or for benefit in return from people — whatever it was, they didn’t do it for the sake of Allah. And when they did not do it for the sake of Allah, that means they will not have any reward from Allah in the Hereafter.

So we should be very careful. Sometimes we exert so much effort in fasting and praying, in reciting Qur’an, in saving to go for ‘Umrah or Hajj — what is the intention? Are we only seeking worldly benefits? For example, some people are advised: go for ‘Umrah if you are having trouble finding a spouse, and insha’Allah you will find a good spouse. Or: you’re having trouble in your business, go for ‘Umrah; you’re having trouble having a child, go for ‘Umrah.

And it is okay — you do something good and make du’a, because this is a way of having your du’as accepted. But your ultimate concern and goal for ‘Umrah should not be so that you can get married. That is not the only outcome you are seeking. You are seeking Allah’s mercy, His vast, generous mercy, in the Hereafter and in this world — and a tiny portion of that vast mercy is that you are granted a child that you so badly want, or a spouse that you so badly want, or health or wealth, or whatever it is that you wish for. So don’t just seek dunya; ask Allah for His generosity, which includes dunya and Akhirah.

The Slave of the Dinar

And when a person only seeks the dunya, then their heart becomes deviated, and it makes a person a coward — they no longer have inner strength or courage.

Hadith

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: may the slave of the dinar be ruined, and the slave of the dirham, and the slave of the khamisah — a garment — the one who is greedy for clothes. Let him perish: if he is given, he is happy; and if he is not given, he becomes annoyed. And if he is pierced with a thorn, let him not find anyone to take it out for him.

This is how some people are even with Allah: that they make du’a for nice clothes, and if they don’t get the nice clothes they get angry — ya Allah, why didn’t You give me nice clothes? They are so eager and greedy for the things of the world that if they get them they are happy, and if they don’t get them they are not happy. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: let such a person perish. This is how much he disliked people who are so greedy for the world.

The Three Portions

It was said that Allah has divided the world into three portions: one portion is for the believer, another portion is for the hypocrite, and another portion is for the disbeliever. The believer takes his portion of the world in order to prepare for the Hereafter — whatever a believer enjoys and uses of this world, the goal is to seek the home of the Hereafter. The hypocrite uses the world in order to adorn and beautify himself over here; he just uses it to show off, to boast, to impress people, to look good in the eyes of people, because that is what a hypocrite is: a seeker of people’s approval. And the disbeliever takes his share to enjoy himself; he only enjoys in the world.

So who are you? What are you seeking? If you have anything of this world, what is the objective? Is it to thoroughly enjoy it? Is it just to adorn yourself with it? Or is it to use it in order to earn the home of the Hereafter?

Malik ibn Dinar’s Scale

Malik ibn Dinar said that your concern for the Hereafter will depart from your heart in proportion to your concern for the world. Meaning the more concerned you are for this dunya, the less concerned you will be for the Hereafter; and vice versa — your concern for the dunya will depart from your heart in proportion to your concern for the Hereafter.

And you will notice this: that when you are overly concerned about, for example, the cleanliness of your home, or your health, your physical appearance, your money, then you have less mental bandwidth to think about the Hereafter, to focus and pay attention to the deeds that will help you there. If you wake up in the morning thinking about how you have to clean the house and all the things you have to get done and how you have to go shopping and all the things you need to buy and the bills you have to pay — then from the morning until you fall into your bed at night, what is it that you are chasing? The dunya. And the time that you take out in order to pray: how is that time spent? Salah will be rushed; you will not be able to remember Allah in salah; you will not be able to remember Allah after salah. Maybe you are so busy cleaning, cooking, doing the chores, going out of the house, shopping, that you forget to make dhikr in the morning, you forget to make dhikr in the evening, you forget to give sadaqah, you forget to recite Qur’an.

And if you are concerned for the Hereafter, then your concern for the dunya will reduce. When you wake up in the morning and think: today I have to recite this much Qur’an, today I have to help so-and-so for the sake of Allah, I have to go and attend a gathering of knowledge, I have to do such and such good deed — when you have all those good things in your mind, then you are focused on them; and yes, cooking will also get done, groceries will also get done, but you will not be overly concerned with those matters.

And concern for the Hereafter brings a person calm in this life, in the sense that they are not panicking, they are not worrying all the time. When a person is concerned about the dunya all the time, they are always stressed out, always worried — because there is no end to the things of this world; there is no end to the work that you can do over here; there is always more to do.

Chapter Ninety-Five

The Du’as for Good in Both Homes

And what to hold in your heart as you say them
1. The most comprehensive du’a
رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ

Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

What to Have in Mind

When you say rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah, have in your mind: ya Allah, give me religious and worldly blessings. Ya Allah, strengthen my Islam, strengthen my iman, give me the ability to spend more time with the Qur’an. Bless my family and my wealth so that I can use them for Your pleasure — so that of my family, of my children, I can teach them about You, I can teach them Your book, they will do righteous deeds, they will be good Muslims.

Ask Allah to give you the ability to do good things, good deeds, good acts of generosity, of forgiveness, assisting people, assisting Allah’s creation. Ask Allah that you live your life in a way that is pleasing to Him, that you use the blessings Allah has given you in the right way, in a good way; that Allah grants you health and safety in your body; that Allah gives you a righteous spouse, a good neighbour; that Allah gives you a comfortable means of transportation and a comfortable home; that Allah gives you satisfaction; that Allah gives you patience and gratitude, and a heart and tongue that remember Allah a lot; and that Allah gives you the ability to spend generously in His way. As Qarun was told: seek the home of the Hereafter through what Allah has given you. So ask Allah: ya Allah, give me the ability to use all of this to earn the home of the Hereafter, to use the good things of this world in a way that is permissible.

And when you say wa fil-akhirati hasanah, have in your mind: ya Allah, make my death easy for me; make my death a time of receiving good news of Paradise; make my grave spacious for me; give me blessings and ease and protection and comfort in my grave. Ya Allah, grant me ease in the hashr, in the great gathering; ya Allah, forgive me in the great gathering. Ya Allah, give me the water of al-Kawthar, allow me to drink from there; allow me to be in the shade of Your Throne on the Day of Judgement; give me my record of deeds in my right hand; give me the ability to cross the Sirat very quickly, very swiftly; make me enter Paradise; save me from the punishment of Hell. Ya Allah, grant us the privilege of seeing You, and bestow Your approval on me.

❖  ❖  ❖
2. Forgiveness and well-being in every part of life
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي

O Allah, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, in my worldly affairs, in my family, and in my wealth.

3. Set right my religion, my world, and my Hereafter
اللَّهُمَّ أَصْلِحْ لِي دِينِي الَّذِي هُوَ عِصْمَةُ أَمْرِي، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي دُنْيَايَ الَّتِي فِيهَا مَعَاشِي، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي آخِرَتِي الَّتِي فِيهَا مَعَادِي، وَاجْعَلِ الْحَيَاةَ زِيَادَةً لِي فِي كُلِّ خَيْرٍ، وَاجْعَلِ الْمَوْتَ رَاحَةً لِي مِنْ كُلِّ شَرٍّ

O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affairs; and set right for me the affairs of my world, wherein is my living; and set right for me my Hereafter, on which depends my afterlife; and make my life a source of increase for me in every good, and make my death a source of comfort for me from every evil.

Because if your religion is good, then everything else is good. And set right for me the affairs of my world, because this is where I am right now. And make my life such that I only increase in good deeds, in goodness; and make my death a source of comfort for me so that I am protected from every kind of evil.

4. The best of what can be asked for
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَسْأَلَةِ، وَخَيْرَ الدُّعَاءِ، وَخَيْرَ النَّجَاحِ، وَخَيْرَ الْعَمَلِ، وَخَيْرَ الثَّوَابِ، وَخَيْرَ الْحَيَاةِ، وَخَيْرَ الْمَمَاتِ، وَثَبِّتْنِي، وَثَقِّلْ مَوَازِينِي، وَحَقِّقْ إِيمَانِي، وَارْفَعْ دَرَجَتِي، وَتَقَبَّلْ صَلَاتِي، وَاغْفِرْ خَطِيئَتِي، وَأَسْأَلُكَ الدَّرَجَاتِ الْعُلَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ

O Allah, I ask You for the best thing that can be asked for, the best du’a, the best success, the best deed, the best reward, the best life and the best death. Make me firm, and make my scales heavy, and make my faith true, and raise my rank, and accept my prayer, and forgive my sin; and I ask You for the highest ranks of Paradise.

Sometimes we don’t even know what to ask Allah for — so you say: I ask You for the best thing that I can ask for.

5. The keys of goodness, and good endings
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ فَوَاتِحَ الْخَيْرِ وَخَوَاتِمَهُ، وَجَوَامِعَهُ وَأَوَّلَهُ وَظَاهِرَهُ وَبَاطِنَهُ، وَالدَّرَجَاتِ الْعُلَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ

O Allah, I ask You for the openings of goodness and its endings, and all of it — its beginning, its outward and its inward — and the highest ranks of Paradise.

Meaning: whatever thing I begin, let that be good; and let the endings be good also. Anything I begin, let me begin it in a good way, and let me accomplish it. Give me the ability to do good things, to say good things, to do good works, internally and externally. And I ask You for the highest ranks of Paradise.

6. Raise my mention, lighten my burden
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تَرْفَعَ ذِكْرِي، وَتَضَعَ وِزْرِي، وَتُصْلِحَ أَمْرِي، وَتُطَهِّرَ قَلْبِي، وَتُحَصِّنَ فَرْجِي، وَتُنَوِّرَ قَلْبِي، وَتَغْفِرَ لِي ذَنْبِي، وَأَسْأَلُكَ الدَّرَجَاتِ الْعُلَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ

O Allah, I ask You that You raise my mention, and put down my burden, and set right my affair, and purify my heart, and guard my chastity, and put light in my heart, and forgive me my sin; and I ask You for the highest ranks of Paradise.

“Raise my mention” is that You mention me before Your angels — and that can only be when Allah is pleased with His slave, when Allah loves His slave.

7. Barakah in my whole being
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ أَنْ تُبَارِكَ لِي فِي نَفْسِي، وَفِي سَمْعِي، وَفِي بَصَرِي، وَفِي رُوحِي، وَفِي خَلْقِي، وَفِي خُلُقِي، وَفِي أَهْلِي، وَفِي مَحْيَايَ وَفِي مَمَاتِي، وَفِي عَمَلِي، فَتَقَبَّلْ حَسَنَاتِي، وَأَسْأَلُكَ الدَّرَجَاتِ الْعُلَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ

O Allah, I ask You that You bless me in my own self, and in my hearing, and in my sight, and in my soul, and in my form, and in my character, and in my family, and in my life and my death, and in my deeds; and accept my good deeds; and I ask You for the highest ranks of Paradise.

8. A house near Him in Paradise
رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ

My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise. Whatever you ask for of this world — a house, a home — ask for its equivalent, and better, in Jannah.

Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina ‘adhab an-nar.
Ameen.
Chapter Ninety-Six

Sulayman and the Ant

Shukr is a form of worship. Gratitude is a way through which a person finds closeness to Allah; it is a way of drawing closer to Him.

When we worship Allah — for example when we pray — we are essentially showing thanks, because in our salah we say alhamdulillahi rabbil ‘alamin, all praise is for Allah, the Lord of the worlds. So one of the reasons why the different acts of worship have been legislated is so that we show gratitude to Allah. That is the objective; that is the purpose.

And Allah is the most deserving that we praise Him, that we give thanks to Him, that we show gratitude to Him — because wa ma bikum min ni‘matin faminallah: whatever blessing you have, it is from Allah. Whether it is the blessing of existence, of sustenance, of health, wealth, children, family, education — anything that we have is from Allah. And every moment of our existence we are receiving blessings and favours from Allah. So whether we are in a situation where we are very happy, or in a situation where we are struggling, in ease or in hardship, in every situation, every period of our lives, Allah is deserving of praise and thanks from us.

Allah tells us in the Qur’an: and He has given you whatever you have asked of Him. And we ask Allah in two ways. One way of asking Allah is through our tongue — to actually ask directly: ya Allah, grant me this, ya Allah, grant me that — and Allah gives us that. And another way of asking Allah is through our state, through our condition: that when we have a need, whatever that need may be, Allah takes care of it, He fulfils it. And if you think about it, Allah gives us so much without us even realising that we are in need of those things.

And if you were to count the blessings of Allah, you would not be able to enumerate them. You cannot count them; you cannot quantify them. There are so many. Indeed the human being is very unjust and very ungrateful. Allah is not unjust; Allah is very generous. We are unjust when we forget the blessings of Allah and we dare to show ingratitude.

And we see that there are two types of people: those who are beloved to Allah, and those whom Allah does not like. The people whom Allah loves are those who are grateful to Him, and the people whom Allah does not like are those who are ungrateful. And even among people we see this: those who are appreciative, who are grateful — even among your children, among your friends — you tend to appreciate them even more; and those who ignore the favours that you do, or the little things that you do, or who take them for granted, over time you also get fed up of such people. So remember that gratitude is something that Allah loves in His slaves.

❖  ❖  ❖

A Grateful Servant in the Qur’an

Sulayman (‘alayhis salam) was a prophet of Allah, the son of a prophet of Allah; he was a king, and the son of a king. And Allah had given him so many favours: not just that he was a prophet and a king, but Allah had bestowed on him special knowledge, knowledge of different matters; Allah had given him kingship and authority over not just people but even the jinn and the birds; he knew the language of the birds, and he could even understand what the ants communicated with one another; and he could control the wind. And he was also very grateful.

The Qur’an — Surat an-Naml

“So he smiled, amused at her speech, and said: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve; and admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants.”

Sulayman (‘alayhis salam) was once travelling with his armies — and his armies were not just of people but also birds and jinn; you can imagine what a huge, massive army that was. And as they were proceeding they came upon a valley, and there was an ant, and Allah enabled Sulayman to hear, to grasp, to understand the speech of the ant — what the ant communicated with the rest of the ants. And she communicated: look, Sulayman and his armies are coming, so enter into your homes, because otherwise Sulayman and his armies might unknowingly trample over you and destroy you without even realising.

On being informed of the speech of the ant, Sulayman smiled. He smiled, amused at her speech. And why was he so happy at this? Because Allah made him feel the blessings that he had been given. Sulayman felt the blessings of Allah upon him, the unique, the special blessings of Allah upon him, and out of that he was so happy.

And what is it about the statement of the ant that delighted Sulayman? It could be the intelligence of the ant, and how concerned the ant was to protect her folk. And secondly, perhaps Sulayman found her speech something that made him happy because it made him realise that even the ants knew him, and even the ants thought well of him and his army.

So this smile was out of gratitude — because sometimes when you are feeling very grateful you start to smile. Notice that it has not just been said that he simply smiled, because a person can smile out of many different reasons: a person can smile out of anger, a person can smile out of mockery, a person can smile out of pride. Allah clarifies here: dahikan — he smiled out of amusement, laughingly; he was actually happy.

Rabbi Awzi‘ni

And then he made du’a. He said Rabbi awzi‘ni — O my Lord, enable me. And this word awzi‘ni literally means “restrain me,” because waza‘a is to restrain — for example an army, to keep them in place, not let them go here or there. So: restrain me, control me, do not let me loose, do not let me fall into pride and injustice; keep my reins tight. And how? An ashkura ni‘mataka — inspire me, enable me, that I am grateful to You for Your favour.

And here Sulayman is acknowledging that whatever blessings he had were blessings from Allah upon him: those blessings which You bestowed on me, and also those blessings which You bestowed on my parents. Why does he want to be grateful for the blessings which Allah gave his parents? Because a person benefits from the blessings that their parents have, directly or indirectly. And it is also a form of recognising the favours that a person has received from their parents — so this is in a way showing gratitude to Allah and also showing gratitude to one’s parents.

And then he says: and give me the ability to do those righteous actions that You are pleased with. A righteous action is an action that is done purely for the sake of Allah and in a way that is pleasing to Allah. Sulayman was a person of knowledge, he was a prophet, and he had been given different types of knowledge — and now he was concerned about ‘amal, action, work. Because when Allah gives you knowledge, Allah is offering guidance to you; now it is your responsibility to act on that knowledge, and if a person does not act on it, then that knowledge becomes an argument against the person.

So Sulayman is asking Allah: ya Allah, give me the ability to do righteous deeds — but what kind? Those righteous deeds tardahu, that You will be pleased with. He is specifying here: I want to be able to do those good deeds that You will be pleased with. Because it is not necessary that every deed which appears to be good is pleasing to Allah.

We know the hadith about the reciter of the Qur’an, and the martyr, and the one who used to spend very generously in the way of Allah. Externally these three deeds are all very good; they are excellent, they are righteous deeds. But these deeds will not be accepted on the Day of Judgement; Allah will not reward these people for their apparent good deeds; Allah will not be pleased with them. Why? Because the reciter of the Qur’an recited Qur’an in order to be called a reciter; the person who used to spend generously spent so that he would be called a generous man; and the martyr participated in battle and died so that he would be called a martyr. So those deeds, even though apparently they were very righteous, were not pleasing to Allah, because they were not done sincerely for His sake.

And so often it happens that a person begins something with the right intention, but then halfway through, a person becomes more concerned about: are people watching me, are they happy with what I am saying, with what I am doing; what are they saying about me, how are they talking about me? This shows that there is now a problem with the intention. So we should ask Allah: ya Allah, give me the ability to do those good deeds that You will be pleased with, that are acceptable, that You will reward generously for.

And then he says: and admit me, with Your mercy, among Your righteous slaves. He doesn’t say “by my deeds” — he says bi rahmatik, with Your mercy, out of Your mercy. And where are the righteous slaves of Allah? In Paradise. And this shows us that entry into Paradise is not possible without the mercy of Allah — which means that no matter how much good a person has done, it is not on the basis of their good deeds that a person can enter Paradise. Entry into Paradise is with Allah’s mercy.

❖  ❖  ❖

Lessons From This Du’a

First of all, we should understand the importance of this du’a, because Allah has mentioned it — especially the beginning of it — twice in the Qur’an: once in this context where Sulayman made it, and second in Surat al-Ahqaf, where a righteous slave of Allah makes a very similar du’a, beginning in the same way. So we should also make this du’a very frequently, because this is the du’a of a righteous slave of Allah who is grateful to Allah and also grateful to his parents. And it is the du’a of a prophet of Allah, which means that this should also be our du’a.

Secondly, we see here that we are asking Allah for the ability to be grateful — because really a person cannot feel grateful without the tawfiq of Allah. Sometimes a person is surrounded by blessings, they have so many good things in their life, but they are unable to see any of them, unable to appreciate any of them. They are not happy with what they have been given, because they are focused on what they do not have, on what Allah has kept away from them for a wisdom, for some reason that He is knowing of.

And gratitude is extremely important for our mental well-being, for our spiritual health, and for our relationships. If a person is not grateful, then the negative thoughts, the feeling that “oh, I have nothing,” or “I still don’t have this, I still don’t have that” — this negativity eats them up from the inside, and a person cannot function well.

Spiritually, gratitude is essential, because our relationship with Allah is about gratitude. We praise Allah, we do good deeds, we show obedience to Allah — why? Because we are grateful to Allah; Allah has created us, Allah has given us so much. And if a person does not feel grateful to Allah, then that person is not able to obey Allah; the joy of ‘ibadah departs.

And for our relationships: if a person is not appreciative of their children’s efforts, then they will always focus on what their child is not doing, or what their child is doing wrong; and when they constantly point out “you were bad at this, you were not doing this, you made this mistake again,” constantly focusing on the negatives, their own children will begin to dislike them. And it goes the other way as well, between husband and wife: the relationship improves so much when there is gratitude on the part of both parties, and when there is ingratitude the relationship is ruined.

So we should ask Allah: ya Allah, give me the ability to be grateful. You might think: I am very grateful, alhamdulillah, I’m not negative, I am very grateful to Allah, I’m very grateful to my family, to my spouse, to my children, to my parents. Good — you can be even more grateful. So ask Allah for the ability to be grateful.

Thirdly, we see in this du’a that whatever blessings we have, all of them are from Allah. Any good thing that you enjoy in your life — whether it is fast internet, or the ability to hear, or food that you can order from your phone, or food that you are enjoying at your table — a blessing that we recognise, a blessing that we do not recognise: everything we have is from Allah. And even when we receive a favour through someone — let’s say somebody gives you a gift of money — why did they give it to you? How did they think of giving it to you? Because Allah put that feeling in their heart to be generous to you. So ultimately every blessing that we receive, every good thing we enjoy, is coming from Allah.

Then we learn from this that we should be grateful to Allah and also to our parents, because we receive so many blessings through them. If you begin to calculate how much your parents have spent on you even before you were born — so often it happens that before a child is born parents begin to save money for their child; the child is not even going to school, it is still an infant, and parents are saving money for his or her university education. Sometimes parents have to spend so much to have children at all. And then how much parents spend on their children afterwards; and if these parents are also righteous Muslims who teach you how to pray, who teach you about Allah, who send you to a place where you can learn your deen — how many blessings we have received from our parents.

And then we learn that we should ask Allah to give us the ability to do those deeds that are pleasing to Him. Ask Allah: ya Allah, grant me wisdom, give me the ability to make the best decisions, to do the best deeds, to make the best use of my time. Because sometimes a person has so many opportunities before them to do something good but they don’t realise it; or sometimes they realise but they don’t have the willingness; or sometimes they even have the willingness, they want to, but they’re not able to, because there is something else that is more urgent or that prevents them.

Chapter Ninety-Seven

What Shukr Actually Is

Shukr is to recall a blessing, and then to manifest it.

First of all you recall a blessing. Sometimes a blessing can be before you and you see it and you recognise that yes, it is a blessing, you think of it as a blessing. And other times there are blessings that are not right in front of you, or not in a tangible form — so you recall it, you think of it in your mind. And even if something is in front of you, you recall that yes, this thing is a blessing of Allah: this table that I have, this computer that I have, the software that I have, the food that I had, the phone that I have, the ability to see with my eyes, the ability to speak, the ability to listen, the ability to read, the ability to see different colours, the ability to breathe the fresh air.

And secondly you manifest it, you show it — in the sense that you use it; not that you hide it away and pretend it does not exist. The opposite of shukr is ingratitude, and ingratitude is that a person forgets a blessing, does not think of it, does not recall it, does not remember it; and then a person hides it, in the sense that they don’t show it, they don’t use it, they don’t benefit from it, they pretend like it does not exist, they don’t mention it.

Shukr also means to be content with a little. An animal that is shakur — a horse that suffices on little food and still looks healthy — the blessing of the little food is visible on it, the favour of the little food is apparent.

And shukr is also to mention the bestower of the blessing a great deal. So someone who is grateful is someone who mentions the giver of the gift a lot. If we are grateful to Allah, this means we should mention Allah a lot.

❖  ❖  ❖

How the Blessing Is Shown

How do you show the effect of the blessing? It is to mention the blessing on the tongue — when you talk about the blessing you are showing the blessing. For example you got a new phone, and when you mention it to your sister — alhamdulillah, I got a new phone; alhamdulillah, I got such a good deal; alhamdulillah, this phone is amazing — you are mentioning the fact that Allah gave you something. This is manifesting the blessing on your tongue.

Secondly, it is to show it in the heart, in the sense that you feel love and appreciation in your heart for the One who has given the gift to you. So you don’t just verbally express it; you also allow yourself to feel the emotions of love and happiness and joy.

And thirdly, shukr includes that you show obedience with your limbs — that you become more obedient to Allah. So for example you receive very good news, so you fall into sajdah; you receive something that really delights you, so you go and give sadaqah; or you say alhamdulillah, or you increase in your good deeds.

And remember that every act of worship is essentially shukr. This is why the ulama say that salah is shukr, fasting is a form of shukr; every good deed that you do for the sake of Allah is a form of shukr. And to say alhamdulillah — that is also shukr.

The Five Parts of Shukr

Shukr has many components in it. First of all, shukr includes that you acknowledge the gift of the giver. Secondly, it includes that you praise the giver. Thirdly, it includes that you love the giver. Fourthly, it includes that you show humility before the giver. And fifth, it includes that you use the gift in what the giver loves, not in what the giver dislikes. If Allah has given you a blessing, you use it in a good way, not in a way that is displeasing to Allah.

Chapter Ninety-Eight

The Blessings We Cannot Count

Allah has bestowed on us many blessings, external and internal — outside of our bodies and also inside of us; blessings that are visible and also blessings that are hidden; blessings that are tangible and blessings that are intangible. There are so many blessings of Allah that we cannot enumerate them; we cannot even perceive all of them.

Three Kinds of Blessing

Ibn al-Qayyim says that you can divide the blessings of Allah into three categories.

First of all, those blessings which you have already received and you know them, you recognise them, you acknowledge that they are Allah’s blessings — for example the fact that Allah created you, the fact that Allah gave you the blessing of Islam, that Allah gave you a family.

Secondly, there are those blessings which you are awaiting, which you are expecting, which you are hopeful Allah will grant you in the future. For example you are hopeful that Allah will bless you with a healthy child; you are hopeful that Allah will give you a long healthy life; you are hopeful that Allah will give you the ability to go for ‘Umrah, to go for Hajj; you are hopeful that your child will become a hafiz. And just having those hopes and wishes is itself also a blessing — because when can you expect to have something good in the future? When you are already in a position where you have received some blessing. If a person is married, now they are hopeful that soon insha’Allah they will have a child. So the blessings of the future are also a blessing.

Thirdly, there are those blessings which a person has, and is even using, but does not even perceive, does not even realise are there.

❖  ❖  ❖

Islam First

Of the blessings Allah has given us, the first and most important is the blessing of Islam — Islam is called Allah’s blessing. The teachings of Qur’an and sunnah are a blessing of Allah: remember the favour of Allah upon you, and especially what He has revealed to you of the Book and wisdom. The Qur’an is a blessing; the teachings of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam are a huge blessing; the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam himself is a blessing for us — Allah has bestowed a huge favour on the believers when He sent among them a Messenger.

And the ease that Allah has given us in our religion is also a blessing; Allah mentions it and then says at the end of the ayah that He completes His blessing upon you — meaning by giving you so much ease and convenience in your religion, Allah is perfecting His favour upon you.

And Then Everything Else

Life is a blessing. The limbs we have in our body, that we can use in so many different ways, and the different faculties that Allah has given — the ability to hear, to see, to think — all of these are blessings. And if you think about it, when even a small thing goes wrong, when it malfunctions in the body — whether there is an increase of a certain hormone, or a deficiency, or certain connections are not forming properly — any kind of disruption can cause so much harm to a person. So the body Allah has given us: every part, everything about this body, is such a huge blessing. And when you study any aspect of the human body, whether it is psychology or any aspect of the physiology, you are amazed at how Allah has blessed us — and we don’t even realise.

Health is a blessing. The time we have is a blessing. Even the joy we feel — sometimes we are in a good mood, and that is also a blessing. When people’s hearts are united — so for example the people of a family are very friendly to one another, loving and supportive of one another, or people who work together — that is also a huge blessing. The sustenance we receive from above, that comes down from the sky, and that we receive from below our feet, that grows from the earth, is a blessing. Children are a blessing. Wealth is a blessing. Even mountains, subhanAllah, are listed among the blessings.

The blowing of the wind is a blessing — because without it, how would clouds move from one place to another, how would there be pollination, how would ships sail, how would we have trade? Rain is a blessing. The fact that ships sail is a blessing. Different modes of transportation that Allah has provided us are a blessing. The animals that Allah has created for our benefit are a blessing. The different types of foods, clothing that Allah has given, and the blessings of different colours, different shapes, different shades, different kinds — all of them are a blessing.

Think about colourful birds, or colourful insects. The other day I went for a walk and there was an emerald green insect that I saw — such a beautiful colour. I was amazed, because the forest was still dead; it is still relatively cold over here; and all of a sudden there was this tiny bug, emerald green, such a beautiful colour. And you wonder: these colourful creatures Allah has created, yes for different reasons, but also, as Allah tells us in the Qur’an, He has subjected all of these things for us, so we find joy in looking at the different colours. I don’t know what its name is, I don’t know what it eats, I don’t know what kind of a bug it is, whether it lives here or came from somewhere else — Allahu a’lam. However, I found joy in just looking at that bug, just the colour of its wings. So this is also a blessing that we fail to recognise.

And then the fact that Allah conceals our sins, and does not punish us right away, does not hold us to account right away for our sins — that is also a blessing.

And even when we are able to remember something, that is a blessing. It was said that sometimes a person does not realise what blessings he has; and a person closes his door, and Allah sends those people to him who knock at his door and ask him for something, and so he remembers that yes, I have such and such, so I can give it to him. For example you may have a sweater or a shawl or a jacket hidden away in your closet, or something packed away in your basement, and over the years you forget about it; and then somebody comes and asks you: do you know where I can get such and such from? And then you remember: oh, I actually have one, I can give it to you. Being able to remember that you have something is also a blessing, because now you can actually do something with it — you can give it, you can gift it, you can sell it, you can make use of it in one way or another. And if you did not remember that you had that blessing sitting there, and it just sat there and got wasted over time, then this is a loss of an excellent opportunity.

Chapter Ninety-Nine

Why Gratitude Matters

Allah Himself Is Ash-Shakur

Shukr is incredibly important for us because, first of all, Allah Himself is very appreciative. Allah Himself is Shakur, meaning that He acknowledges the good deeds of His slaves; He acknowledges their effort and He rewards them very generously; He raises their ranks; He appreciates their gratitude, so He multiplies good things for them. On the Day of Judgement He will not reward with one reward for one good deed; rather He will give the reward ten times more. And Allah is so appreciative that He praises His slaves before His angels in the highest gathering. So any little good deed that a person does for the sake of Allah, Allah appreciates it.

Hadith

Once a man was walking on a road and he found a thorny branch, and he removed it — and so Allah appreciated that, and Allah forgave him.

The Prophets Were Grateful

The prophets of Allah were grateful to Allah. We learn about Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) that he was grateful for His blessings. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would stand in prayer until his feet would swell, and when he was asked why he did so much, he said: should I not be a grateful slave? Even the angel Jibril showed gratitude to Allah when the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam chose to drink milk instead of wine when he was presented both on al-Isra.

Allah is deserving of praise in the skies and the earth, meaning by everything. And we are taught that yes, we should worship Allah, and along with worship washkuru lah — be grateful to Him. So we should pray, fast and so on, but then we should also increase in saying alhamdulillah, in showing gratitude to Allah: worship Allah and be of those who are grateful.

Ibn al-Qayyim said that the entire religion is based on two things, because Allah says: remember Me, I will remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful to Me. These are the two main pillars: remembrance of Allah, and gratitude to Allah.

And a person is always in one of two states: either a person is in a state where they are enjoying a blessing, and for that they should be grateful; or they are in a state where they have wronged themselves and are in need of seeking forgiveness from Allah — and for that also we should be grateful, that Allah gave us the ability to recognise and turn back to Him, and taught us a way of seeking forgiveness from Him.

And when Allah brings about changes in the world — the night comes to an end and the day begins, the day comes to an end and the night begins — why does Allah bring about all of these changes? So that we become grateful; so that we realise the blessings that we have. Because we only realise the blessings we have when they go away. When the night comes to an end, then we realise: oh, the night was a blessing, I could have prayed. And then you look forward to the next night so that you can pray in a better way.

And the best slaves of Allah on the Day of Judgement are al-hammadun, those who praise Allah a lot. And on the Day of Judgement we are going to be asked about our blessings: what did we do with them, where is the gratitude for all of that?

❖  ❖  ❖

From the First Breath to the Last

We should be grateful to Allah the moment we receive a blessing, the moment we feel a blessing. We learn that as the soul was breathed into Adam (‘alayhis salam) and his nose came to life, he sneezed, and when he sneezed he said alhamdulillah. These are the first words spoken by the human being: alhamdulillah. So it is essential that we continue with alhamdulillah.

And when the believer departs from the world, the believer says alhamdulillah — at the time of departure from the world also the believer is praising Allah. And the people who enter Paradise will say alhamdulillah; the people of Paradise will continue to glorify and praise Allah out of gratitude. So we have to get used to that; we have to make it a habit right now.

What Gratitude Does

When a person is grateful, the benefit is that gratitude benefits the person themselves first and foremost: it makes you happier, it secures your blessings, it brings you the approval of Allah, it increases your blessings.

Hasan al-Basri said that when a person is not grateful for the blessings that they have, then those blessings are turned into punishment. The same thing that used to bring you joy once upon a time will now become a means of torture for you. So if we want to preserve our blessings, we have to show gratitude to Allah. It was said that the people used to call gratitude al-hafiz — the one that preserves and guards and secures blessings. So if you want to preserve the blessings you have, then show gratitude to Allah.

Hadith

The person who eats and is grateful is like the person who fasts and is patient.

SubhanAllah — some people are not able to fast in the month of Ramadan, so when they eat they feel guilty, they feel horrible about themselves. Don’t lose that opportunity: as you eat, show gratitude to Allah, say alhamdulillah; and with shukr you can reach the same level as that of the fasting person who is patient.

Mutarrif (rahimahullah) said: I prefer that Allah should give me blessings on which I am grateful, than that Allah should test me and I am patient. He liked the path of gratitude more than the path of patience — why? Because patience is harder; it is definitely harder. And since you can reach the same level with gratitude, then why not ask Allah for the easy way?

And the person who is grateful is saved from the punishment of Allah. And Allah will reward those who are grateful very generously. When a person says alhamdulillah, we see that alhamdulillah is something that fills the scale; the reward is massive. And when a person says alhamdulillah, the reward is so much that the angel did not know how to record it, so Allah told him: write it exactly as My slave said it, and I will give the reward for it.

What Ingratitude Does

When people are ungrateful, this is a big loss. It means that a person is a target of shaytan — because shaytan said that O Allah, You will not find many of the people to be grateful. So if a person is being ungrateful, this means that shaytan has a very strong influence on them, and such a person is a companion to shaytan.

When people are ungrateful they invite upon themselves the punishment of Allah; and their blessings will be ruined; and because of ingratitude people are covered with trials and tribulations and problems, so that they wake up and leave their ingratitude.

Ingratitude is only something that makes things worse. A person typically feels ungrateful when things are hard — so if in that situation you begin to think negatively and show more ingratitude, then you are only making things worse for yourself. And if you stop yourself and say: no, I am not completely deprived; Allah has saved me from this and this and this; Allah has given me this and this and this — and you deliberately, consciously take yourself towards the path of gratitude, you will feel better, and you will invite more blessings of Allah.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam warned us that of the people of Hell, many of them are women; and the reason is not that they are women — the reason is that many women show ingratitude. This doesn’t mean that men are not ungrateful; even they can be. But this is very common in women, so we should be extremely conscious of this and show more gratitude to Allah and also to the people in our lives.

❖  ❖  ❖

How to Show It

We can show gratitude to Allah by showing more obedience to Him; by having love for Allah; by acknowledging the blessings of Allah; by praising Allah for those blessings; by using the blessings of Allah correctly; and by talking about the blessings, mentioning them.

Really, think about it: in your conversations, whether with your family, your friends, your children, your parents, your spouse — what do you talk about? Is it just things that are not working? Or do you also say alhamdulillah for the things that are working? Remember that the best slaves of Allah on the Day of Judgement are al-hammadun, so be of those who say alhamdulillah a lot.

So: verbally express gratitude. Secondly, feel gratitude in your heart — remember and recall the blessings that Allah has given you, and feel those positive thoughts and emotions. Thirdly, use the blessings in ways that Allah likes. For example, if Allah has given you the blessing of a good phone that is very fast, in which the colours are very bright — how are you using it? What are you listening to? Are you listening to good things, are you watching good things, or are you wasting your time on it? Think about it.

Chapter One Hundred

The Du’as of Gratitude

Alhamdulillah at every hour of the day
1. The du’a of Sulayman (‘alayhis salam)
رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَى وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ

My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You approve; and admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants.

On Waking Up

2. The first words of the day
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي عَافَانِي فِي جَسَدِي وَرَدَّ عَلَيَّ رُوحِي وَأَذِنَ لِي بِذِكْرِهِ

All praise is due to Allah who healed me in my body, and returned to me my soul, and permitted me to remember Him. ‘Afani fi jasadi also means that Allah protected my body and kept it safe and sound, so that I was able to wake up. What a huge blessing.

In Salah, and Around It

We begin salah with alhamdulillah. In rising from ruku‘ we say alhamdulillah. We say alhamdulillah thirty-three times after salah. In the morning and in the evening also we show gratitude to Allah — SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi.

While Eating, and After

3. With every morsel and every sip
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that Allah is pleased with His slave who says alhamdulillah while taking a morsel of food, and while drinking.

Yes, we can say the du’a for after eating once we have finished our meal — but we can also say alhamdulillah with every bite, or every few bites. As you enjoy the different flavours in your mouth, the different types of food, especially at iftar time: you take a sip of water — alhamdulillah; you eat that sweet, delicious date — alhamdulillah; then you have that savoury pakora — alhamdulillah; then you have the fruit salad — alhamdulillah. With every type of food that you have. And the perfectly flavoured coffee at the perfect temperature — every sip you enjoy, say alhamdulillah.

4. After eating
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي كَفَانَا وَأَرْوَانَا غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ وَلَا مَكْفُورٍ

Praise be to Allah who has satisfied our needs and quenched our thirst; Your favour cannot be compensated nor denied. We can never thank You enough, and we cannot do without this, ya Rabb.

5. For bread, oil and salt
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَشْبَعَنَا مِنَ الْخُبْزِ بَعْدَ أَنْ كَانَ طَعَامُنَا الْمَاءَ وَالتَّمْرَ

Praise be to Allah who has filled us with bread, after our food had previously been only water and dates. Once his mother gave him bread with some oil and salt to eat — that is all he had — and he said this. So often when we eat we are thinking: the food is not like this, it should have been like that, how come today there are no samosas, how come today there is no fruit salad. We tend to complain a lot. And look at how grateful he is for bread and oil and salt, because he is thinking about what he used to have before.

On Going to Sleep

6. The last words of the day
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي كَفَانِي وَآوَانِي، وَأَطْعَمَنِي وَسَقَانِي، وَالَّذِي مَنَّ عَلَيَّ فَأَفْضَلَ، وَالَّذِي أَعْطَانِي فَأَجْزَلَ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ، اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ وَإِلَهَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ النَّارِ

Praise be to Allah who has given me sufficiency and has protected me, given me food and drink, been most gracious to me and given to me most lavishly. Praise be to Allah in every circumstance. O Allah, Lord and King of everything, God of everything, I seek refuge in You from the Fire.

❖  ❖  ❖
7. After salah — for the ability to be grateful
اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ

O Allah, help me to remember You, to be grateful to You, and to worship You in the best manner.

8. When you see people collecting gold and silver
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الثَّبَاتَ فِي الْأَمْرِ، وَالْعَزِيمَةَ عَلَى الرُّشْدِ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مُوجِبَاتِ رَحْمَتِكَ وَعَزَائِمَ مَغْفِرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ شُكْرَ نِعْمَتِكَ وَحُسْنَ عِبَادَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ قَلْبًا سَلِيمًا وَلِسَانًا صَادِقًا، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا تَعْلَمُ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا تَعْلَمُ وَأَسْتَغْفِرُكَ لِمَا تَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ

O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in all my affairs, and determination upon right guidance; and I ask You for the things that bring about Your mercy and the things that necessitate Your forgiveness; and I ask You for gratitude for Your blessing and for excellence in worshipping You; and I ask You for a sound heart and a truthful tongue; and I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the worst of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know — indeed You are the Knower of all unseen matters.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught one of his companions that when you see people collecting gold and silver — when you see people eagerly collecting the things of the world and enjoying the riches of the world — then you should say these words. Thabat fil amr is steadfastness in all my affairs: give me the ability to be steadfast, so that if I get a little bit of wealth I don’t begin to forget You; and it also means steadfastness in the matter of Islam, so make me steadfast in Islam. And determination upon right guidance — because sometimes we lack that determination; we become shaky, we become weak.

9. Make us grateful for Your blessings
اللَّهُمَّ اجْمَعْ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِنَا، وَأَصْلِحْ ذَاتَ بَيْنِنَا، وَاهْدِنَا سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ، وَنَجِّنَا مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ، وَجَنِّبْنَا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ، وَبَارِكْ لَنَا فِي أَسْمَاعِنَا وَأَبْصَارِنَا وَقُلُوبِنَا وَأَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا، وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ، وَاجْعَلْنَا شَاكِرِينَ لِنِعْمَتِكَ مُثْنِينَ بِهَا قَابِلِيهَا وَأَتْمِمْهَا عَلَيْنَا

O Allah, join our hearts, and mend our relationship, and guide us to the ways of peace, and bring us out of darkness into light, and save us from indecencies, those apparent and those hidden. And bless us in our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses and our children, and accept our repentance — indeed You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. And make us grateful for Your blessing, praising You for it, accepting it; and complete it for us.

There are so many people who are not grateful for the blessings of Allah. Ya Allah, make us grateful for Your blessings — and those who praise You for it. Because some people recognise the blessings but they don’t praise Allah for them; some people are too shy to talk about the blessings that Allah has given them, too shy to say alhamdulillah, too shy to acknowledge that Allah is the giver of all blessings. So give us the ability to be grateful, to praise You, and to openly acknowledge Your blessings, to talk about them — and then perfect Your blessings upon us.

10. Help me, do not help against me
رَبِّ أَعِنِّي وَلَا تُعِنْ عَلَيَّ، وَانْصُرْنِي وَلَا تَنْصُرْ عَلَيَّ، وَامْكُرْ لِي وَلَا تَمْكُرْ عَلَيَّ، وَاهْدِنِي وَيَسِّرِ الْهُدَى لِي، وَانْصُرْنِي عَلَى مَنْ بَغَى عَلَيَّ، رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي لَكَ شَكَّارًا، لَكَ ذَكَّارًا، لَكَ رَهَّابًا، لَكَ مِطْوَاعًا، لَكَ مُخْبِتًا، إِلَيْكَ أَوَّاهًا مُنِيبًا، رَبِّ تَقَبَّلْ تَوْبَتِي، وَاغْسِلْ حَوْبَتِي، وَأَجِبْ دَعْوَتِي، وَثَبِّتْ حُجَّتِي، وَاهْدِ قَلْبِي، وَسَدِّدْ لِسَانِي، وَاسْلُلْ سَخِيمَةَ قَلْبِي

My Lord, help me and do not help against me; grant me victory and do not grant victory over me; plan on my behalf and do not plan against me; guide me and make guidance easy for me; and help me against those who act wrongfully towards me. My Lord, make me greatly grateful to You, greatly mindful of You, much in awe of You, obedient to You, humble before You, and ever turning and returning to You. My Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin, respond to my supplication, establish my evidence, guide my heart, make my tongue true, and remove the malice from my heart.

Alhamdulillahi ‘ala kulli hal.
Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.
Chapter One Hundred and One

Ar-Razzaq

Allah is the Provider. He did not create the creation and leave them to fend for themselves. He created us all, and He also provided us with the means of subsistence — in fact He has provided it in our very home, meaning on this earth. We don’t have to go elsewhere, outside the earth, in order to find sustenance.

The Qur’an

“Allah is the One who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Are there any of your so-called partners who does any of that?”

Allah is our creator, He is our Rabb — which means that He created us and He also provides for us, and He provides for all of His creatures. He is ar-Razzaq, the One who provides a great deal of sustenance, because there is no moving creature on the earth except that Allah is the one who provides for it.

Imagine: there is no creature on the surface of the earth or inside of it, in the water or on the water, on the trees or in the sky, by the coast or in the forest, anywhere in the desert — any creature on this earth — except that Allah is the one who provides for it. And every creature has its own unique needs. What the fish eats is different from what the bird eats, which is different from what the camel eats, or what the cow eats. And our needs fluctuate: there are certain times when we are in need of certain things, and then we are no longer in need of those things, we need some others. As our needs vary, Allah is ar-Razzaq.

And Allah has placed in the earth the sustenance that different creatures need. They don’t have to go outside of the earth in order to seek it.

He Expands It and He Restricts It

Remember that Allah owns sustenance as well. It is Allah who provides, and it is up to Him: He can expand sustenance for a creature at a given time, and He can restrict it. He can give a lot to some and little to others. This is all His decision. Allah provides sustenance to whomever He wants without measure. There are some creatures who are given in abundance, so much; and then there are some who are given little. Allah is the One who expands sustenance and He is the One who restricts it, and to Him all of you will be returned.

Seek It, and Ask Him for It

So when we need sustenance, any form of sustenance, what are we supposed to do? Allah tells us that we should seek it from Allah — and this means that we make du’a to Allah to provide us, and we also use the means that Allah has given us.

For example, the birds don’t just remain sitting in their nests. Allah has provided their sustenance across the fields, across the trees — so the birds come out of their nests seeking sustenance. Likewise we also have to go and find sustenance; we have to use the means that Allah has provided us. And we also have to ask Allah, we also have to make du’a: ya Allah, provide us with sustenance.

And rizq is something that we are always in need of. There is never a time in our lives when we can say: I do not need food, I do not need drink, I do not need shelter or clothing. We are always in need of sustenance for as long as we live, and Allah is the One who provides what we are in need of.

And in life we are tested with different things, and of those tests is poverty, or shortage of sustenance, or lack of means. When we experience such difficulty, or any form of shortage — or we desire more so that we can do more in life: you want more money so that you can save up and go for ‘Umrah, or for Hajj, so that you can take care of your family comfortably, take care of your parents, take care of your loved ones, spend generously in good causes — whether we want the fulfilment of our basic needs or we desire more, we need to ask Allah for sustenance.

There are times in our lives when we just have to look after ourselves, and then there are those times when we have to look after ourselves and also our dependents. There are times when we don’t just have to provide food and clothing and shelter for our children; we also have to pay for their education, for their needs. So no matter how many needs we have, no matter how great they may be, no matter how many different kinds of needs they may be — remember Allah is the Provider. Sustenance is entirely in His hand. So we should seek it through lawful means, and we should seek it from Allah. We have to combine effort and prayer, both.

Chapter One Hundred and Two

You Are the Best of Providers

The Qur’an — Surat al-Ma’idah

“‘Isa, the son of Maryam, said: O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven, to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers.’”

The hawariyyun, the disciples who believed in ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam), asked him whether it was possible that Allah could send down a table spread of food from the sky for them. And ‘Isa said to them: fear Allah, if you are truly believers — meaning, why are you making such a demand? And they said: we are only requesting this so that we can eat of heavenly food, and so that our hearts are content, and this would be a miracle and a means of strengthening our faith. So ‘Isa made this du’a.

Calling Him by His Names

Notice that we typically begin du’a with the word Allahumma, but here we see Allahumma Rabbana — which teaches us that when we make du’a we should mention different names and attributes of Allah, and call upon Him again and again.

Without Effort on Our Part

And he said: provide for us, You are the best of those who provide. We can also say these words when we want sustenance from Allah: ya Allah, provide us, You are the best of those who provide.

They wanted the table spread of food to come down from the sky; they didn’t want to have to prepare that table themselves, because there is a lot of work and effort that goes into preparing a banquet — you end up spending so much time, so much money, so much effort preparing so much food. So they said: You provide us, without any effort on our part.

And sometimes you are in a situation where you don’t see the means, you don’t know through what means you can gather sustenance for yourself. You may not have any money in your bank account and you need food; you may not have enough money to pay for your tuition, or to pay for your ticket, or to pay for whatever it is that you want — especially when it is something that will benefit you in a religious way. So sometimes you see the means available before you, and other times you don’t know how you are going to make ends meet, you don’t know how you are going to pay the bill, you don’t know how you are going to take care of your matters. Especially in such a situation, where you are trying and looking, also look towards Allah and ask Him: provide us, You are the best of those who provide.

Religious Benefit First

And notice that when ‘Isa made this du’a, he first said: provide us with this table spread of food so that it will be a festival and a sign — and then he mentioned that we will also eat of it. He mentioned religious benefit before worldly benefit.

And when we ask Allah for sustenance we should keep the same order. For example, you are praying to Allah to bless you with money — why are you asking for money? So that you can go and buy a nice fancy bag and show off, or go and enjoy food at a fancy restaurant, and then maybe whatever is left over perhaps you can give some charity from it? Reverse the order. Always reverse the order: ya Rabb, grant me this so that I can do good things with this money, so that I can spend in Your cause, I can spend on my family, on my parents, on my relatives, on my loved ones, I can give sadaqah in the masjid, I can give to those who are in need — and then I also want to enjoy it for such and such purpose. And there is nothing wrong with that, as we learned earlier with rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah: we ask Allah for good in this world and for good in the Hereafter.

What “Best of Providers” Means

You are the best of those who provide: You give sustenance in the right measure, at the right time, in the most perfect way. Sometimes it is so amazing — you have a certain need, and you think of different ways of fulfilling it, and Allah sends you sustenance from where you did not even expect, from where you did not even imagine; and what He sent was perfect for you, exactly what you were in need of. Allah is the best of those who provide, because He gives to His slaves what they need, when they need it, and what He provides is perfect for them, excellent for them, of great benefit to them. If it were any less or more it would not be ideal; but what Allah chooses to bestow on His slaves is ideal for them.

Think of it this way: the foods that grow in the land that you live in, and especially seasonal food — that is food that you are actually in need of. This is why they say eat local; because the part of the earth you are living in is growing the food that you are in need of in that particular season, and these are the nutrients that you need. Allah has placed in every part of the earth the sustenance that the creatures on it need.

And the way that Allah provides is excellent. Look at an orange: look at how perfect the peel is, how it preserves the fruit inside, covering it, protecting it, acting as a seal so that nothing can permeate and nothing comes out — the fruit is perfectly protected inside. And when you peel it and throw away the peels, they do not cause any waste; they go back into the earth and provide nutrients, they decompose and get back into the cycle. There is no waste. And when we package food, how much waste we create; and how many unhealthy things are put inside the food in order to preserve it, in order to increase its shelf life, so that eating it becomes more dangerous for people than not eating it.

He Gives to All

And “the best of those who provide” also means that You give to all those who believe in You and also those who do not, those who obey You and those who do not.

What happens with us? If you as a parent provide for your child, and your child hits eighteen or twenty and they are still not taking life seriously, they are not studying or working, then what do you do? You say: from now, you have to pay for your car insurance yourself, you have to pay for your phone bill yourself, you have to pay for your clothes yourself. Some people even go to the extent of demanding rent from their children. Why? Because they are saying: if you don’t cooperate, if you don’t listen to us, then you can’t have all of this; you can’t take our generosity for granted. And sometimes when parents get angry with their children because of certain choices children make, they cut off from their children completely — they give nothing to them, even when it comes to inheritance; they will give their estate elsewhere, because they don’t want their disobedient children to take any of it.

We disobey Allah day in and day out. Think about it: in just one twenty-four-hour cycle, how many times do we say things which are inappropriate, perhaps displeasing to Allah? How many times do we do actions which Allah does not like? And even the good things we do — when we pray, what is the quality of our prayer? When we fast, what is the quality of our fast? But Allah does not withhold sustenance from us. He continues to provide us.

We learn that Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) made du’a for his descendants: whoever among them believes in You and in the Last Day, give them sustenance. And Allah responded that the one who disbelieves, I will still give him something — yes, it will be little, but it will be something. So Allah is khayr ar-raziqin, because He does not discriminate; He gives to all His creatures.

So often there is discrimination in the workplace, where women feel that their work contribution is way more than their male counterparts but they are not paid equally; or some people feel that because of their race, because of their accent, because of their background, they are not paid fairly. Sometimes children feel that my parents don’t treat me the same way as they treat my siblings. But Allah provides all of His creatures, whether they are obedient or disobedient, righteous or not — it doesn’t matter.

And “best of those who provide” also means that You are very generous. There are those who will give, but they are not generous in what they give. An employer will give you certain benefits, but not all of them — you want more, but they are not going to give; they are penny-pinching, they are being very careful about how much they give. Allah is al-Ghani al-Hamid, He is rich and praiseworthy, and He is most generous. Look at how much He provides His creatures — every second, every portion of a second, how many creatures are receiving from Allah what they are in need of, and so many different kinds of needs.

Chapter One Hundred and Three

What Rizq Actually Is

Rizq is anything by which one profits — anything that is of benefit to us. Rizq is also a means of support and growth of the body, the body of any creature. A baby is in need of milk in order to live, in order to survive, in order to grow. People are in need of food and water; different animals and different creatures are in need of different forms of subsistence so that their body can survive, live, and grow.

And as human beings we don’t just need food; we need water, we need oxygen, we need vitamin D from the sun. Look at how Allah is providing sustenance in so many different ways: from the food that we put in our mouths, to the water that we drink; there is food that goes into our stomach and then benefits us, and there is rizq that our skin absorbs, and there is rizq that through oxygen we absorb into our body. Isn’t that amazing?

Two Kinds

And rizq is of two kinds. There is apparent or material rizq, which is for the body: food, drink, oxygen, sunlight; and part of that is also clothing, because we need clothing to keep our bodies warm. And the second type of rizq is that which is unapparent, intangible, intellectual: the rizq of the heart is love; the rizq of the mind is knowledge, iman, faith — this is also sustenance.

So when we ask Allah for rizq, we are not just asking for a whole lot of cash, we are not just asking for money; we are also asking for the rizq of iman, the rizq of love, the rizq of good friendships, the rizq of contentment, the rizq of happiness, the rizq of having a spouse, having children. All of this is included in rizq. Every blessing is rizq.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said about the love that he had for Khadijah: I was given the rizq of her love. This love is a gift from Allah. And really, as human beings we need to feel that emotional connection with people, that closeness to them, that comfort in knowing there is someone we can feel close to — intimacy, closeness, attachment. This is a human need. And when a person feels lonely and isolated in this life, this is more difficult on a person than experiencing hunger. If you don’t eat all day you will survive; but when you feel lonely, when you miss companionship, when you desperately desire companionship, that is heavier and more difficult on the body than hunger.

General and Special

And rizq is of two kinds in another sense. There is rizq that is general: Allah provides all creatures — humans, animals, birds — and this is the sustenance that is for the body, food and drink and so on, which Allah has decreed for His creatures even before they enter this world.

The other type is special provision, exclusive provision, which Allah gives to His prophets, His messengers, His righteous slaves, those who worship Him: and this is the provision of faith, and belief in the oneness of Allah, and iman, and gratitude — such blessings as the heart experiences. And that is sustenance that we should be seeking from Allah as well.

A lot of the time, when we ask, we are only thinking about tangible things: a new car, new clothes, a whole lot of money, financial ease in whatever form. But remember, Allah can give you worldly sustenance and He can also give you spiritual sustenance. Worldly sustenance will end over here; spiritual sustenance is everlasting — it is something that accompanies the slave in the grave, and something that will be a means of success in the Hereafter. Eternal happiness and success comes with spiritual sustenance. So that is what we should be asking Allah for.

And remember that the best form of sustenance is Jannah.
