Allah tells us in the Qur’an that whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, Allah will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally — Allah has given such a person an excellent sustenance. So Jannah is the most excellent form of rizq that we should be asking Allah for.

❖  ❖  ❖

Our Responsibility

First of all we must put our full and complete faith in Allah when it comes to rizq. We should have tawakkul in Allah: Allah is the Provider; Allah has provided me before, Allah is providing me now, He will provide for me in the future; He provided for my parents, He provides for me, He will provide for my children. Put your trust in Allah — not in your business, not in your stable job, not in your parents’ estate, not in your investments; not even in your spouse, not in their job, not in their generosity. Put your trust in Allah, because Allah is the Provider.

Hadith

If you were to put your trust in Allah the way that you should, Allah would provide you the way He provides the birds: they leave their nests in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full bellies.

Having faith in Allah, putting your trust in Allah, doesn’t mean that you just sit at home — because the birds don’t just sit in their nests; they go out, and Allah provides for them. Likewise we also have to use the opportunities Allah provides for us: an opportunity to work, an opportunity to gain an education so that we can have better employment, submitting your resume here and there, going to work, having a good work ethic. We must do things on our part. But put your trust in Allah; don’t put your trust in your education, in your degree, in your job, in your work experience, in your work ethic, in your resume.

Hadith Qudsi

O My slaves, all of you are lost except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My slaves, all of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My slaves, all of you are unclothed except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you.

So any kind of need we have — spiritual, food-related, clothing-related, housing-related, transportation-related — be certain that Allah is able to give it to you, able to take care of your needs. And to think that the creation provides for you is complete foolishness, because the creation is not even able to provide for itself, so how can they provide for you? And to think that the creation can withhold sustenance from you is also a huge mistake, a sign of weak faith. If you get something, you get it because Allah gave it to you; if something is prevented from you, that is because Allah prevented it.

Ask With Full Conviction

Hadith

Once a guest came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and he asked his family to serve this person if there was any food — but there was no food in any of the houses of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. So he prayed: O Allah, I ask You of Your favour and Your mercy, for none owns it except You. And very soon a gift of cooked meat was brought to him, and he said: this is Allah’s favour, and we await His mercy.

So believe that whatever need you have — education, or money for education, a spouse, a job, children, food, drink, medication — anything you are in need of is with Allah; He is its provider and He is able to give it to you. So ask with full conviction. And remind yourself that your sustenance was already decreed, already written, before you even entered this world.

Be Pleased With What He Decreed

And be pleased with what Allah has decreed for you, because sometimes we fall into the mistake of constantly comparing ourselves to others: oh, my cousin is a millionaire; so-and-so has so much money, they have a house here, an apartment there, an investment there; and me, I am struggling to make ends meet. When a person falls into this trap of comparing themselves with others, this leads to unhappiness, to discontent, and eventually to a person being unhappy even with Allah, because they are desiring what is with someone else.

Don’t make this mistake. Whatever Allah has given you, be content with that. But being content doesn’t mean you don’t ask Allah — you have to ask Allah. And remember that Allah will give you what He has decreed for you, and whatever He has decreed for you is best for you, because He knows what you need and He knows how much to give you. You see this in people, sometimes in your own children: if you give them a little too much, they tend to take things for granted; they forget that they are privileged, and they start treating you as if you are just their bank account — they ignore you, and whenever they want something they come to you, and they don’t even ask nicely, they just demand, or they don’t even ask, they just take without permission.

It’s possible that if Allah gave me more, that would cause me to become sinful, that would cause me to forget Him, that would cause me to become wasteful — and we learn in the Qur’an that those who are wasteful are the brothers of shaytan. For example, when you have a limited amount of money that you designate for groceries, then you buy groceries very carefully, and whatever you bring into your house you use it. But if you don’t have any such budget, you go and buy whatever looks good, whatever looks nice, you just pick it up; and then it sits in the refrigerator, and after a week or two or three, when you clean out your fridge, you throw away half of what you purchased. So if Allah puts you in a situation where you have to budget your groceries, in a way that is good for you, because it is protecting you from being wasteful.

Moderation in Seeking

So seek sustenance, but seek it in a way that is lawful, without becoming greedy for the world, without making the world your ultimate goal and concern. Adopt moderation in seeking sustenance.

Because some people, when they have a good, stable job through which they make a lot of money, want to go further and further, and they work all the time; in Ramadan, in the day, in the night, they will not go for tarawih prayer because there are things related to their work that they want to complete. Their worship is being compromised, their family is being neglected, so that they can make more money. Isn’t it amazing that a person takes their family on vacation but more than half the time they are unavailable because they are still working; and they come home and are still unavailable because they are still working. What is the point of all of that money if you are not able to enjoy spending time with your children? Because children don’t stay little forever; they grow very fast, very quickly. So if you don’t enjoy those early years and you miss that because you are just obsessed with working all the time, then you are missing something so beautiful from your life.

Dawud (‘alayhis salam) was a king, he was a prophet, he was an excellent worshipper, and he would also earn an income with the work of his own hands. He had a very good balance in his life, where he would dedicate a day to passing judgement among his people, another day just for worship, another day for his work. So see what is feasible for you — but remember that your body has a right over you, your family has a right over you, your Lord has a right over you. And yes, you also have to make money. So making money is a part of life; it is not the goal of life, not the purpose of life. In fact the purpose of life is to worship Allah, and Allah says that He does not want from the people and the jinn that they should provide for Him or feed Him — it is Allah who is ar-Razzaq.

When He Tests With Shortage

And at times Allah tests His slaves with poverty, or shortage of wealth, shortage of food. At such times do not despair and do not get upset. We learn in a hadith that the people who were tested most severely were the prophets of Allah, and then the people of knowledge, and then those who are pious; people are tested according to the level of their faith, according to their level near Allah.

In the home of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, for days the fire would not be lit, the oven would not be turned on. ‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) mentioned how if they had oil they would not light lamps with it — they would drink it; they didn’t even have that much oil. And for days the stove would not be turned on; and if ever they had two meals, only one meal was cooked, the other was raw food, which was dates and water. That is it.

So be content with what Allah has given you, and don’t despair, and don’t feel pity for yourself if Allah has decided to give you limited sustenance in a certain period of your life — because the prophets of Allah also experienced poverty. The best of all creatures would be hungry for days on end, and so often he would wake up in the night and toss and turn out of hunger and thirst. This is Rasulullah salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. So if Allah tested His beloved with hunger and poverty, and if He decides to put us in the same test, why should we despair, and why should we think that Allah does not like us?

Don’t ever make this mistake of thinking that if Allah gives me a lot of sustenance that means Allah is happy with me and loves me, and if Allah does not give me a lot of sustenance that means Allah does not like me. Having sustenance is not a proof of Allah’s love and His approval. Allah gives to all creatures — those whom He loves and those whom He does not, those He is pleased with and those He is not pleased with. So be pleased with whatever Allah gives you; and that is better for you than having a lot that could make you think Allah is happy with you and because of that you end up disobeying Him.

Chapter One Hundred and Four

What Increases It, and What Keeps It Away

What Increases Sustenance

Faith and piety. We learn in the Qur’an that whoever fears Allah, Allah creates an exit for him out of his troubles and provides him from where he does not even imagine, from where he does not even expect. And Allah tells us that if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, He would have opened for them blessings coming down on them from the sky and coming to them from the earth. So iman and taqwa are a means of receiving abundance in one’s sustenance.

And remember that abundance is not just more quantity; abundance is also related to contentment. You can have your refrigerator full of food, but if you are a super picky eater it is possible that you don’t eat anything of it, you don’t want any of it. And if Allah gives you contentment and you eat whatever is available to you — as long as the food is healthy, nutritious, safe and lawful — look at how much sustenance is available to you.

Fulfilling your obligations. We learn that the people who, in their trade and in their business, do not forget to fulfil their obligations such as prayer and zakat — Allah provides them. So when you fulfil your obligations, Allah will provide for you.

Obedience to Allah, and leaving sins. Ibrahim an-Nakha’i said that just as adopting taqwa is a means of acquiring sustenance, likewise leaving sins is a way of acquiring sustenance. And at the same time, if a person does not observe the fear of Allah, they will suffer from hunger and poverty.

Gratitude. Because Allah has promised: if you are grateful, I will increase for you your blessings.

Tawbah and istighfar. We learn that when you seek forgiveness from Allah, Allah will send down rain from the sky upon you in abundance, and He will provide you with wealth and give you in abundance.

Remembering Allah a lot — SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi — this is also a means of receiving more sustenance from Allah.

Hajj and ‘Umrah. We learn in a hadith that when a person follows Hajj with another Hajj, ‘Umrah with another ‘Umrah, then poverty and sins are removed from them just as impurities are removed from iron and gold and silver. So poverty is removed from a person when they go for Hajj and ‘Umrah.

Being good to your relatives — staying connected with your family, being good to them, spending on them — this also increases sustenance.

Spending on others. When you spend on those who are with you and around you, those you work with, your companions, your friends, your neighbours, your community — Allah says: you spend, and I will spend on you. And especially look after those who are in need; we learn in hadith that you are given sustenance and granted help because of the weak among you — when you take care of them, when you honour them, then Allah will also give you. Spending on students of knowledge also brings a person sustenance from Allah. We learn in hadith that there are some people who are given because they give others — and if they stop giving others, then Allah will stop giving them. So be a giver and Allah will give you.

Working first thing in the morning, because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam prayed for barakah for his ummah in their early mornings. So when you work at that time you will have the du’a of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and Allah will bless you in what He has given you.

Honesty — honesty in your buying and selling, honesty in your workplace, in whatever work you have. Be honest, and Allah will give you because of your honesty.

And some of the ulama say that there are four things that bring rizq: first, prayer in the night; secondly, istighfar at the time before Fajr; thirdly, giving sadaqah; and fourthly, remembering Allah at the beginning of the day and at the end of the day.

❖  ❖  ❖

What Prevents It

Sins. When we disobey Allah — Hasan al-Basri said: the clouds, by Allah, in the clouds is your sustenance, but you are deprived of it. You see the clouds above you but the rain does not fall — why? Because of your sins, because of your own wrong deeds. So remember that when we disobey Allah, whether in the form of constant backbiting, or constantly putting certain people down, or being consistently ungrateful to our families — whatever it may be, sins are of many kinds — because of these sins we are deprived of sustenance.

Ingratitude. Because of ingratitude what a person already has also gets ruined; a person is not able to enjoy it; a person loses the blessings which they already have.

Stinginess. When a person becomes stingy and selfish, and they don’t spend on themselves, on their family, in the way of Allah, on those around them — this is also a means of being deprived of rizq.

Killing children out of fear of poverty. At the time of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, and even today, this is common, where people will kill a child because they don’t want to have to raise another child, they don’t want to have to feed another mouth. This is something that also deprives people of sustenance. Remember that every child comes with their own rizq. So don’t think that because of having children you will have less, or because of having another child you will have less — you will have more, in fact, because each child brings their own sustenance. Allah is the provider of you and also of your children.

Cutting ties of kinship is also a means of deprivation of sustenance.

Begging people. We learn in a hadith that the slave does not open the door of begging except that Allah will open the door of poverty for him. When you spread your hand before the creation — give me, please give me, I beg you — then Allah will put you in poverty; but when you spread your hand before Allah, Allah gives you.

And we see this: that when a person begins to think that people provide, then you look at what they have, you look at the car they drive, the money they spend, the house they live in, the kind of things they buy, and you think: oh, they have a lot, they can give me something. And then you start expecting from them, and not just expecting — you start asking them again and again, in one way or another. When you begin to ask people, whether openly or directly or indirectly, then Allah will open the door of poverty for you; and then you will always think that it is people who provide, and so you will always be looking at people — please give me, please give me — and you will have low self-esteem, low confidence.

On the other hand, when you are in need and you ask Allah, you will have greater confidence, higher self-esteem; and then you will try, you will work, and whatever you earn, even when it is little, you will be happy, content with it, grateful for it. So do not make the mistake of becoming dependent on people’s charity. Earn with your hard work, and whatever you earn, Allah will bless it for you. In a hadith we learn that if a person were to go into a forest or the desert and collect firewood and come and sell it, that is better for him than begging people. If you cannot find good employment, something suitable for your education and background — it doesn’t matter: take a step down, take another step down if you have to, but put in your effort and seek sustenance with your effort and with your prayers. Do not spread your hand out before people and beg them.

Chapter One Hundred and Five

The Du’as for Sustenance

1. The du’a of ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam)
اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ، وَارْزُقْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ

O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven, to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the best of providers.

2. The du’a he taught to those who embraced Islam
اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَارْحَمْنِي وَاهْدِنِي وَعَافِنِي وَارْزُقْنِي

O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, give me good health, and provide for me. Whenever a person would embrace Islam, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would teach them how to pray salah, and then he would tell them to make this du’a. Or you can simply say Allahumma arzuqni — O Allah, provide for me.

3. After Fajr, every morning
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا

O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, pure provision, and deeds that are accepted.

4. Refuge from poverty and humiliation
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْفَقْرِ وَالْقِلَّةِ وَالذِّلَّةِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ أَنْ أَظْلِمَ أَوْ أُظْلَمَ

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from poverty, from shortage and from humiliation; and I seek refuge in You from doing wrong to someone, or from becoming the victim of someone else’s wrongdoing.

5. When hunger or thirst wakes you in the night
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ، رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ

There is no god worthy of worship but Allah, the One, the Prevailing; Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Almighty, the All-Forgiving. ‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) said that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this when he would wake up in the night and toss and turn out of hunger or thirst.

6. Suffice me with the lawful
اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ

O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and make me independent, by Your favour, of all others besides You.

Because sometimes a person is tempted to use unlawful means to acquire money or to increase their wealth. You find out that someone took an interest-based loan from the bank of three hundred thousand, mortgaged a house, sold it a year later with a huge profit — so they basically doubled their money with no money of their own. And you are tempted, especially when you see examples like this in your neighbourhood, in your workplace. Or in many places of work every person contributes a dollar or two every month to purchase a lottery ticket, so that when they win the lottery everyone will share in that money. Don’t fall into that mistake. Ask Allah: ya Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful for me, and protect me from what You have forbidden, and let me be dependent on You and You alone, no one else.

7. From the decline of His blessings
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ زَوَالِ نِعْمَتِكَ، وَتَحَوُّلِ عَافِيَتِكَ، وَفُجْأَةِ نِقْمَتِكَ، وَجَمِيعِ سَخَطِكَ

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the decline of Your blessing, the changing of the well-being You have given, the suddenness of Your punishment, and from all forms of Your wrath.

Sometimes you have certain blessings in your life and you are enjoying them, but you don’t know if you are going to have them forever, you don’t know if you are going to have them for long. Your car is functioning perfectly fine — it is possible that it breaks down tomorrow; it is possible that within a year or two it is no longer drivable. So: ya Allah, protect me from the decline of Your blessings.

8. After eating
اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَنَا فِيهِ وَأَطْعِمْنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ

O Allah, bless us in it and feed us better than it. There is no harm in seeking what is better; Allah is able to give you what is better than what He has given you.

9. None can restrict what You expand
اللَّهُمَّ لَا قَابِضَ لِمَا بَسَطْتَ، وَلَا بَاسِطَ لِمَا قَبَضْتَ، وَلَا مُقَرِّبَ لِمَا بَاعَدْتَ، وَلَا مُبَاعِدَ لِمَا قَرَّبْتَ، وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعْتَ، وَلَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، اللَّهُمَّ ابْسُطْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ بَرَكَاتِكَ وَرَحْمَتِكَ وَفَضْلِكَ وَرِزْقِكَ

O Allah, no one can restrict what You have expanded, and no one can expand what You have restricted; no one can bring near what You have put far, and no one can put far what You have brought near; no one can give what You have withheld, and no one can withhold what You have given. O Allah, expand for us of Your blessings and Your mercy and Your favour and Your sustenance.

Sometimes we think it is because of certain individuals that we have money or don’t have money. Sometimes there is another person at the workplace who gets the promotion that you were seeking, so you think that they are the problem. No — if Allah has written something for you then no one can keep it from you; no one can bring near what Allah puts far, and no one can put far what Allah brings near. Sometimes you go to the grocery store and you are standing in a very civilised way waiting for your turn, but before you get to the fruit stall the watermelon you had your eyes on is gone, somebody else took it — and now you are looking at their cart constantly: oh, they took what I wanted. No, that was not written for you, it was not decreed for you. So don’t look at the creation and don’t blame them; put your hope and your trust in Allah.

10. Permanent bliss, and security on the day of poverty
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ نَعِيمًا لَا يَنْفَدُ، وَقُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ لَا تَنْقَطِعُ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ الرِّضَا بَعْدَ الْقَضَاءِ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ بَرْدَ الْعَيْشِ بَعْدَ الْمَوْتِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَعْطَيْتَنَا وَشَرِّ مَا مَنَعْتَ عَنَّا

O Allah, I ask You for bliss that does not run out, and delight that does not come to an end; and I ask You for contentment after the decree; and I ask You for coolness of life after death. And I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You have given us and from the evil of what You have withheld from us.

You are asking Allah here for permanent joy, which is the joy of Paradise — because the enjoyment of this world eventually comes to an end, but the enjoyment of the Hereafter will never come to an end. And then: we seek refuge in You from the evil of what You have given us and the evil of what You have prevented from us. Sometimes there are certain blessings that we have been given but there is some evil attached to them. So we shouldn’t just be eager to have more sustenance; we should be eager that it should be good for us, and that Allah protects us from anything harmful or dangerous in it.

11. For the love that is the best provision
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ فِعْلَ الْخَيْرَاتِ وَتَرْكَ الْمُنْكَرَاتِ وَحُبَّ الْمَسَاكِينِ، وَأَنْ تَغْفِرَ لِي وَتَرْحَمَنِي، وَإِذَا أَرَدْتَ فِتْنَةً فِي قَوْمٍ فَتَوَفَّنِي غَيْرَ مَفْتُونٍ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ حُبَّكَ وَحُبَّ مَنْ يُحِبُّكَ وَحُبَّ عَمَلٍ يُقَرِّبُ إِلَى حُبِّكَ

O Allah, I ask You for the doing of good deeds and the leaving of evil deeds, and the love of the poor; and that You forgive me and have mercy on me. And when You have willed a trial among a people, then take me without my being tried. And I ask You for Your love, and the love of whoever loves You, and the love of the deed that brings one nearer to Your love.

Love is also a form of sustenance — the love of doing certain good deeds, the love of people; friendship is sustenance. And if we have this in our lives, where our heart is content and satisfied with the love of Allah, and the love of doing things Allah loves, and the love of people whom Allah loves, then this is the most satisfying thing in our lives. Money and good food bring some kind of satisfaction, but not ultimate satisfaction. That satisfaction comes from the love of Allah, the love of the right people, and the love of doing things that bring a person the love of Allah. So ask Allah for the most excellent sustenance: the sustenance of your heart, not just of your body.

12. When your pockets are empty
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ وَرَحْمَتِكَ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَمْلِكُهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ

O Allah, I ask You of Your favour and Your mercy, for none owns it except You.

When you see that your pockets are empty, when you don’t know how you are going to take care of your needs and your family, remember that Allah’s treasures are vast; He owns everything, and He has the ability to give you what you are in need of. So call upon Him with faith, with conviction — and have the intention to use the blessings that Allah gives you, the sustenance that He gives you, in ways that are pleasing to Him.

Warzuqna wa anta khayr ar-raziqin.
Ameen.
Chapter One Hundred and Six

Even the Prophets Felt Fear

Fear and anxiety is something that all people experience at some level. It doesn’t matter how experienced a person may be, what their age is, what their level of piety is, what their level of faith is. The fact that we are human means that we will experience some level of fear, some level of anxiety.

The prophets of Allah were not only the strongest and most courageous of men; they were also men who were very strong in their faith, in their belief in Allah. But because they were human, there were times when they experienced fear and also anxiety.

Musa (‘alayhis salam) felt afraid to go to Fir’awn, and then he felt afraid when the magicians performed their magic — and that fear is mentioned in the Qur’an. We learn in hadith that after the Battle of Uhud, when the Muslims had to go and face the army again, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and his companions felt fear in their hearts. And likewise Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) also felt fear in his heart.

So feeling fear and anxiety is completely part of being human, and it doesn’t make a person any less of a believer if they experience it. But we all know that it is not a pleasant feeling. When a person is feeling anxious and afraid, you want to do something to come out of that state.

And the thing is that the majority of the time the things causing us anxiety and fear are not in our control; and because they are not in our control, we are not able to change them. So if we are not able to remove the cause of the fear, how can we remove the fear? If we are not able to change the cause of our anxiety, how can we remove that anxiety? It is not always in our control. And it is not easy to be told “stop feeling like this, don’t feel like that,” because your feelings are also not always in your control.

So when we feel anxious, worried and afraid — whether these fears are real or imaginary, because sometimes you are feeling afraid and the people around you are not; you are feeling anxious and the people around you don’t think it’s that big of a deal, since every person responds in a different way — what should we do? Of course there are some thoughts that we need to change, and some thoughts that we need to bring into our minds and focus on. And at the same time, we also need to make du’a; we also need to call upon Allah.

And the type of anxiety being discussed here is occasional anxiety, which is a normal part of life — not an anxiety disorder, which of course needs its own kind of treatment. But even part of that treatment is that you make du’a to Allah.

❖  ❖  ❖

Fear Is Part of the Test

The Qur’an

“And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits — but give good tidings to the patient.”

Allah is promising us here that He will test us with fear. And why do people feel fear? Fear is because of violence, when you know that you are at risk of becoming a victim of violence. Fear is because of poverty, when you are afraid that you don’t have enough to feed yourself or your family. The cause of fear can be war; the cause can be abuse; it can be danger, or pain, or disease, illness, treatment, surgery, childbirth. There are so many causes of fear.

In this world there is a lot of fear. But Jannah is the home where there is no fear: no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.

Allah also says: and We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned. In both ways Allah tests us — through things that frighten us and also things that make us happy. Ibn ‘Abbas explains that this means: We will test you with hardship and ease, with health and disease, with wealth and poverty, with halal and haram, with obedience and disobedience, with guidance and misguidance.

So the things that cause fear and anxiety are something Allah has created in this life in order to test us. Test us in what way? That do we turn towards Allah or not? Do we seek His help or not? Do we put our trust in Him or not? Because in a state of fear and anxiety a person feels weak, and in that state of weakness is our test: do we think that we are self-sufficient, that we can do this on our own — or do we turn to someone to help us? And who is that someone we expect help from? Is it Allah, or is it someone other than Allah?

So this is a test of our faith, a test of our reliance on Allah, of our belief in tawhid, in the oneness of Allah. Do we begin to fear the cause more than we believe in the power of Allah? If it is an illness or a certain disease that we are afraid of, is our fear of that disease greater than our belief in the power of Allah?

And Allah tells us that He has created us weak — wa khuliqa al-insanu da’ifa — which means that we are not perfectly able to protect ourselves, to save ourselves, to even help ourselves. We need external help. So this is the test: do we seek that help from Allah or not? Because life is about ‘ubudiyyah, showing servitude to Allah. If we were able to take care of ourselves in every situation, then the majority of us would forget about Allah; we wouldn’t bother to show servitude to Him, we wouldn’t bother to seek His help.

So it is a blessing of Allah upon us that He has created us weak, not perfect; and secondly, that He has created us in such a way that there are things that frighten us, and situations in which we feel anxious and afraid, and we turn towards Allah, we strengthen our faith in Him, and we turn to Him for help.

Chapter One Hundred and Seven

Sufficient for Us Is Allah

The Qur’an — Surat Ali ‘Imran

“Those to whom the hypocrites said, ‘Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them’ — but it merely increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’ So they returned with favour from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them, and they pursued the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty. That is only shaytan who frightens you of his supporters. So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are indeed believers.”

Here we learn about an incident that occurred soon after the Battle of Uhud. Uhud was a very hard time for the believers, because their victory turned into sudden defeat, and there was a lot of loss and injury that the Muslims experienced. And soon after the battle, when the believers had barely recovered, somebody came and told them that Abu Sufyan and the mushrikun of Makkah were coming back to attack them — and this person tried very hard to frighten the Muslims.

But what happened? Allah says that instead of feeling afraid, this news only increased them in faith, and they said: hasbunallahu wa ni’mal wakil. Sufficient for us is Allah, and what an excellent trustee He is. Instead of succumbing to fear they increased in their faith and their courage, and they put their trust in Allah and said words that showed that trust.

And as they increased in their courage and their reliance on Allah, they went out of Madinah in order to pursue the enemy; and when the enemy learned that the Muslims were approaching, they left, they returned. Because now the enemy felt afraid: if these Muslims, who were supposed to be in a state of injury and weakness, are coming all the way to pursue us and fight us, then they must have a lot of help — so we are not in a position to fight them.

So the Muslims returned to Madinah with favour from Allah and bounty, and no harm touched them. The ulama say that ni’mah here refers to the fact that they returned home safe and sound without having fought any battle — Allah saved them; and fadl, favour, refers to the fact that they also earned so much reward from Allah. They didn’t actually fight another battle; they just went, pursued the enemy, the enemy left, and they returned home with great reward. And no evil touched them; they didn’t suffer anything at all. So they returned home having acquired benefits of the world and also eternal benefits in the Hereafter, and they also received Allah’s approval.

And then Allah says that it was only shaytan who was trying to frighten you of his supporters. And really, there are times when shaytan makes us more afraid. Sometimes the danger is real; other times it is imaginary; or sometimes the danger is not as big as we think it is, and we are way more afraid of it than we need to be. This is from shaytan. Shaytan wants to frighten us, because when we are in a state of fear we begin to panic, we begin to lose faith, we begin to lose courage, our faith in Allah decreases.

So Allah says: do not fear them, do not fear the friends of shaytan, do not fall to the whispers of shaytan — instead fear Me. And this teaches us something very important: that in a time of fear and anxiety, if we shift our focus to Allah — I need to do what pleases Allah, I need to put my faith in Allah, I need to fulfil my duty to Allah — then we are able to manage our feelings also.

❖  ❖  ❖

Hasb: Sufficiency

In this statement, first of all you put your trust in Allah — hasbunallah, Allah is enough for us. Secondly you praise and glorify Allah — wa ni’mal wakil, what an excellent trustee He is.

Hasb is sufficiency. So when you say hasbunallah, this means that Allah is enough for His slave, with His power and with His greatness — against everything that worries and frightens the slave.

For example, if there is some disease, or the treatment of a disease — surgery — that frightens you: that is very scary. You know that you will not be conscious at the time; you know that it will be painful; you know that there are risks associated with surgery; and especially with all of the paperwork you have to sign and all the questions you have to answer, you feel very afraid. So when you say hasbiyallah, what are you saying? You are saying that Allah is enough for me with His power and with His greatness, against anything and everything that worries me, that frightens me: that Allah is able to give me shifa through this, Allah is able to keep me safe through this, Allah is able to protect me from any potential danger through this. Allah has the power, He is able, He is great; nothing is too difficult for Him.

And when you say hasbunallah, this means that Allah is able to remove every danger that frightens you; He is able to repel every harm and any enemy that is trying to harm you.

Wakil: The One You Entrust Your Affair To

And then wa ni’mal wakil — you praise Allah, that He is an excellent Wakil. And Wakil is guardian, caretaker, protector; someone who is appointed to take care of your matters.

You find yourself in a situation where you don’t think you can manage on your own. If a person has to go to court, they don’t know the legal terms, they don’t understand how the law works, they don’t know how to defend themselves — so what will they do? They will get a lawyer. They will explain their situation to the lawyer and tell them: you figure out how I am supposed to deal with this problem. You are relying on the lawyer; you are entrusting your affair to them. Sometimes a person is not in a position to make proper decisions regarding their wealth or their property, so they appoint a trustee who will manage and decide things related to their property. Sometimes you are out of the country, so you appoint someone: you manage my property, you take care of it, you decide whatever needs to be done, I trust you — I am not able to manage this on my own.

This is wakil: someone to whom you entrust your affair. And al-Baghawi says that wakil is a guarantor — the one who guarantees and ensures the sustenance and benefits of his slaves. So Allah is al-Wakil: He is taking care of all of His creatures; He ensures that they have the sustenance they need and He is looking out for their benefits. He takes care of the entire creation, all of the worlds. He is the best protector, the best guardian; He guards the creatures by bestowing His favours on them, by planning for them, by guiding them, by decreeing in their favour.

So the one who puts his trust in Allah, saying hasbunallahu wa ni’mal wakil — Allah will not let him go to waste, Allah will not abandon him, Allah will not hand that slave over to anyone but Himself; Allah will Himself take care of that slave and his affairs.

You Were Not Built to Carry It Alone

When we receive news that is very upsetting — someone has left us, or someone has turned against us, or you sense danger in your workplace or in your community, or you feel that people are not there to support you, people are not doing what they should be doing, and sometimes you feel a sense of abandonment — you feel like you have to take care of or manage all of your problems on your own.

Say the statement. You don’t have to manage that mountain of a problem on your own, because you don’t have that capacity. You were not built for that — wa khuliqa al-insanu da’ifa. You were not built to take care of that huge problem on your own. You have Allah. So don’t put your faith in yourself; put your faith in Allah. Allah is enough for me, because with His power and His might He is able to take care of my little problem. For me it is massive; for Allah this problem is very, very tiny. He can just say kun and my problem will be solved.

At times we increase in our fear and anxiety because we falsely believe that we have to manage our problems on our own. This is completely false. You don’t have to manage everything on your own; you’re not expected to; you were not built to do that. You were built to rely on Allah: to accomplish your goals and repel any harm with the help of Allah.

In the Qur’an Allah says: and you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw. In battle, when you shot the enemy and you hit the target, it is not you who did that; it is Allah who did that. Your job is just to show up and shoot the shot; and it is Allah’s role to ensure that it reaches the target and that the goal is achieved. So your job is to show submission to Allah, to show up well when Allah puts you in any test, to put your faith, confidence and trust in Allah, and to ask Allah for help.

What Trials Are Really For

Remember that the tests Allah puts you in are not to see how strong you are, what you are made of. Allah already knows how strong you are; Allah made you a certain way, so He knows you better than you know yourself. The reason Allah puts us in trials and tests is to see how, and if, we turn to Him. That is the real goal, the real purpose of tests: do we turn to Allah or not, and how strongly do we hold on to Him, how strongly do we seek His help?

Because if there is a business, the loss of which frightens you — that business is not going to last forever anyway. If there is some illness that scares you — your body is not meant to live in this world forever anyway. If there is some danger, war, violence, abuse that frightens you — you were not meant to live in this world forever anyway. So our goal should not just be to survive in this life, or to ensure that our work survives. Our goal through these trials should be to draw closer and closer to Allah. Because business, health, security — all of these are things of the world, and yes, they are dear to us, but they are only a means through which Allah is testing us. The real home is the home of Paradise. This place is temporary, and everything in it is temporary.

Two Occasions for These Words

These words we are supposed to say mainly on two occasions. The first is when we receive a favour from Allah — any blessing. Because when we receive money, or some news, or a health report, anything with good news in it, we still have some fear and apprehension that maybe this is not enough, I was expecting more. In the Qur’an we learn: if only they had been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, “Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty” — this response would have been better. So when we receive something from Allah, whatever it may be, we should say hasbunallahu wa ni’mal wakil.

Secondly, we should say it in order to repel harm. Ibn ‘Abbas said that these words were said by Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) when he was thrown into the fire. And what happened? Allah was enough for him; Allah made that fire coolness and safety for him. His people had tried to harm him, but Ibrahim was unharmed, because Allah protected him; because Allah is enough for His slave, and His power and His planning is greater than the power and planning of the creation. And Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam also said this statement when the hypocrites said that the people have gathered to attack you, so be afraid — and Allah was enough for him.

So if your work is such that you have to deal with a lot of scary news — if every now and then you receive an email or a report or something that frightens you — make sure you write this du’a down and put it somewhere you can see it, so you can say it over and over again. Some people’s job is such that they are basically always putting out fires, or they work behind the scenes and have to manage the money, and that is not always easy. Some people don’t take their work too personally and are able to deal with scary news; other people take matters very personally and everything tends to frighten them, scare them, make them anxious. If you are like that, or if the nature of your work is such that you are always feeling anxious and afraid, then increase in saying hasbunallahu wa ni’mal wakil.

Chapter One Hundred and Eight

What Tawakkul Really Means

The Qur’an — Surat at-Tawbah

“But if they turn away, then say: Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.”

Allah is telling His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam that this is what you should say — fa qul, say this. Allah is teaching this du’a to His Messenger. So how blessed is this du’a.

And especially when is he told to say it? In tawallaw — if they turn away. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was sent as a messenger to invite people to the truth, to guidance, to the straight path, to save them. But if people still turn away, how should you deal with that? This is not your failure. If they turn away, this is their loss; and if they turn away, this is not a waste of your efforts. Then say: hasbiyallah. Allah is enough for me. He knows my efforts, He will reward me for my efforts. And if you abandon me, Allah is there to protect me; if you turn away and turn against me, Allah is there to save me, to protect me, to guard me.

So especially when you feel alone in your trials, when you feel abandoned by people — people who should have been there, people who should have been with you, and still they abandoned you — at such a time especially you should say: sufficient for me is Allah; there is no god worthy of worship but Him; on Him I put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.

Why do you say here that Allah is the Lord of the Great Throne? Because the ‘Arsh is the greatest creation of Allah. And if Allah is the creator of that creation, and He owns it — then what is smaller than the ‘Arsh? Allah has power over that also. If the biggest creation belongs to Allah, then what I fear, what is causing me fear and anxiety, also belongs to Allah, because it is certainly smaller and less than His throne. So Allah is able to help me in my fear, in the danger that I find myself in.

Abu ad-Darda (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that whoever says this seven times in the morning and in the evening, Allah will suffice him against all his worries. And if a companion of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is saying this, then this is true — because the companions did not make up the deen; they only transmitted what they learned from him. So we should also say this seven times in the morning and seven times in the evening — especially at times when life is so unpredictable, when everything is turned upside down, when nothing seems reliable, when the stability we had is perhaps not there anymore, whether because of loss of income, or loss of family members, or disease. Anything because of which we feel unstable and insecure, we need to increase in saying hasbiyallah, to remind ourselves: I have Allah; Allah is there to protect me, Allah is there to help me.

Say the Words Out Loud

And it is important that we say these words — because when you say positive words and you make yourself hear those positive words coming out of your mouth, then you are putting yourself in a positive cycle; you are inspiring positive thoughts in yourself. But when you stay silent, or when you say negative words, then you are letting your negative thoughts control you, and you are allowing shaytan to fill that void. So don’t allow shaytan to weaken you, to threaten you, to frighten you; repel that noise with the words of dhikr, with the words of reliance on Allah.

❖  ❖  ❖

Admitting Your Weakness

Tawakkul is to admit your weakness in regard to a matter: that I am not able to do this on my own, I am not able to take care of this on my own; I know that the means I have at my disposal are not enough — they are imperfect, they are incomplete — and I need external help. I need the help of the One who is able to do all things; the One who is perfect in His power, in His knowledge, in His planning; the One who does not make mistakes; the One who knows everything; the One who is able to protect me. And that is Allah.

That is tawakkul: that you admit your weakness along with your means. In spite of your means, or along with your means, you know that you are weak and your plan is weak, it is not perfect; and you put your trust in Allah, that Allah will ensure my safety, Allah will ensure that I am able to accomplish my goal, that He is able to bring me the benefit that I desire and able to repel the harm that I am trying to avoid.

And tawakkul is not contrary to adopting means. Part of tawakkul is that you adopt the means Allah has given you. Tawakkul is not just something you do when you cannot do anything on your own — you cannot find a way to pay off a loan, so you say “I put my trust in Allah.” You must have tawakkul even when you have the means, when you have a plan in place, whether you have a solid plan or a weak plan or no plan. No matter what your situation is, tawakkul is always relevant. And it is through tawakkul that we are able to achieve the benefits we desire and repel the harms we are trying to avoid. And tawakkul is that you have good, positive thoughts about Allah: that Allah is there, He will not abandon me, He will ensure my safety; and that you have belief in the promise of Allah, that He will protect, that He is enough.

One of the scholars said that putting your trust in Allah is an obligation, and it is from the major obligations that Allah has imposed on us. He said that it is mentioned more, and is more emphasised, than the command to make wudu or to take a bath of janabah — because how many times in the Qur’an has Allah commanded us to make wudu for salah, and how many times has He commanded us to put our trust in Him? Allah has commanded us to put our trust in Him more than He has commanded us to make wudu and take a bath.

And at the same time Allah has forbidden us from putting our trust in anyone other than Him. Tawakkul is essential; it is an obligation on us; it is part of our iman in Allah. Allah tells His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam to put his trust in Allah; Allah commands the believers to put their trust in Allah; it is part of being Muslim — put your trust in Allah if you are truly Muslims. And Allah has forbidden us from taking anyone other than Him as wakil, because everyone besides Allah is weak.

And we should put our trust in Allah in regard to every matter, big or small: when you have made your decision, then put your trust in Allah. Whether it is the decision to go out and do some errands, or to hire someone, or to apply for a job, or to take a job — whatever it is, a big thing or a small issue, put your trust in Allah: not in your plan, not in your car, not in your money, not in your time, not in your ability, not in your friends, not in your co-workers, not in your team, not on the internet, not on the computer, not in technology. All of these things are means; they are not the source of our help or of completing our tasks or goals.

Even Against the Greatest Fitnah

And no matter what issue it is — even for the fitnah of the Dajjal we are taught to put our trust in Allah. When the Dajjal appears he will say: I am your lord; he will declare that he is God. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught us that we should say: you are not our lord; our Lord is Allah; on Him we put our trust, and to Him we return, and we seek refuge with Allah against your evil.

Imagine: in the face of the fitnah of the Dajjal, which is the greatest trial that humanity has ever witnessed or will experience, we are taught to say ‘alayhi tawakkalna, on Allah we put our trust. So any other trial that we experience in our lives, anything else that frightens us or makes us anxious — remember that it is less than the fitnah of the Dajjal. If for the greatest fitnah we are taught to say “on Him we put our trust,” then for anything less than that we should certainly say it.

What Tawakkul Brings

When you put your trust in Allah — indeed Allah loves those who rely upon Him. Because when you put your trust in Allah, this is a way of drawing close to Allah, a way of seeking help from Allah, a way of purifying your tawhid. So you are taking steps to draw close to Allah, and Allah loves His slaves who draw close to Him.

When you put your trust in Allah, then He is sufficient for you; and sufficient is Allah as a Wakil, as the One who takes care of the affairs of His slaves. When you put your trust in Allah, you don’t need anyone else’s help; Allah grants you sufficiency, because you have Allah. When you have tawakkul in Allah you become more courageous, you become brave; Allah frees you from fear; Allah protects you against shaytan; any superstitious beliefs that you may have go away; and the fear of the creation also goes away. And for tawakkul there is huge reward in the Hereafter: we learn that Jannah is a reward for those who are patient and who put their trust in their Lord.

Chapter One Hundred and Nine

The Du’as for Fear and Anxiety

1. Sufficient for us is Allah
حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ

Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best disposer of affairs. The words of Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam) when he was thrown into the fire, and of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and the companions after Uhud.

2. Seven times in the morning and the evening
حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ، عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ

Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne. Abu ad-Darda (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said: whoever says this seven times in the morning and the evening, Allah will suffice him against all his worries.

3. When something frightened him
اللَّهُ اللَّهُ رَبِّي لَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا

Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him. In a hadith we learn that when something frightened or worried the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, he would say these words.

4. The perfect words of Allah
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ

I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created. We learn in a hadith that when a person stops somewhere while travelling and says this, nothing in that place will harm them until they leave.

Whether you stop somewhere to stay for some time or to rest overnight, or you stop at a hotel, or you are driving and stop at a store — say this at that time, and for the entire duration that you are in that place Allah will protect you. And sometimes it happens that you enter a hotel room and you think: maybe there are jinn here, maybe there is a snake under the bed, or bed bugs or spiders. Anything that frightens us, say this du’a.

And these days especially, when you enter a closed space — a restaurant, a store, a doctor’s office — and you are afraid: what if there is someone who has the virus, and what if it is lingering in the air, and what if I inhale it, what if I get infected, what if it is on the door handle and it gets on my hand, maybe it is on the chair, maybe it is in the food. You don’t always see the dangers. Sometimes you can see things that are dangerous to you, and other times you cannot. So you ask Allah: ya Allah, You protect me.

Because everything Allah has created is such that there is benefit in it, and there is also something that could potentially be evil for you. A knife is very beneficial — a sharp knife especially is very useful; in fact it is safer to use a sharp knife than a blunt knife, because a sharp knife will cut quickly and properly. But at the same time a sharp knife can also be very dangerous. So there is khayr and there is sharr. So anything that frightens you — whether it is chopping food in the kitchen, or driving, because it is possible that you end up in an accident — ask Allah to protect you from the evil: any evil, big or small, whether I know of it or I don’t, whether I can see it or I can’t.

5. From anger, from people, from the whispers of devils
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ غَضَبِهِ وَشَرِّ عِبَادِهِ وَمِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ

I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His anger, from the evil of His servants, from the evil suggestions of the devils, and from their presence.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam used to teach these words to the companions to say in a state of faza‘, in a state of fear and panic and worry. And ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (radiyallahu ‘anhu) would teach these words to his children — as soon as his children were able to understand, a three-year-old, a four-year-old, a five-year-old, he would teach them these words and tell them: say these words when you are feeling afraid. And sometimes children can get very afraid of bugs, of darkness, of certain sounds. So teach these words to your children.

Because sometimes the fear that we feel — whether of darkness or bugs, or the fear of abandonment, the fear that my husband doesn’t love me or that he will leave me, that this will happen, that will happen — a lot of the time we develop these fears because of the whispers of shaytan. So ask Allah to protect you from the whispers of shaytan also, and from the presence of shaytan. Sometimes jinn will literally bother people, will try to frighten them; at that time also seek refuge with Allah.

6. The du’a Jibril taught him — for fear in the night
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ الَّتِي لَا يُجَاوِزُهُنَّ بَرٌّ وَلَا فَاجِرٌ، مِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا، وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتَنِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ طَارِقٍ إِلَّا طَارِقًا يَطْرُقُ بِخَيْرٍ يَا رَحْمَٰنُ

I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which neither the upright nor the corrupt can overcome, from the evil of what descends from the sky and of what rises up to it, and from the evil trials of the night and the day, and from the evil of every night visitor — except the night visitor who comes with good, O Most Merciful.

Khalid ibn al-Walid (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that he used to get frightened in the night. Can you imagine? Khalid ibn al-Walid was a warrior, someone who fought in battle, very courageous, very brave. But still there were times when he would get afraid in the night; he would get nightmares, he would get scared in his sleep. So this is part of being human: you have certain strengths and you also have certain weaknesses, and you are not an evil person, you are not a loser, if you have these weaknesses.

He said: I used to get afraid in the night, so I came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and I told him that at times I get afraid in the night and I grab my sword — he would sense this fear that maybe there is someone coming, someone who is going to harm me, so he would grab his sword as if ready to fight something coming towards him. So the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told him: shall I not teach you words which ar-Ruh al-Amin taught me, meaning Jibril taught me? And these are those words.

So if you get nightmares, or your child gets nightmares, then make a point to learn this du’a — maybe write it down and put it next to your bed, so you can say it when you feel afraid, and your fear, insha’Allah, will go away.

And in these du’as you are seeking refuge in the perfect words of Allah. Allah’s words are very powerful: Allah says kun and it happens. Allah created Adam (‘alayhis salam), and He created ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam), with His word, with the word kun — which is why ‘Isa is called kalimatun minallah, a word from Allah, because he was created by the word of Allah. And Allah’s words include both the words of His decree and the words of His sharia, meaning the Qur’an.

And sometimes you are in bed about to fall asleep and all of a sudden you have this fear: did I close all the windows? Did I lock the front door? Is the back window closed? What if there is somebody outside? And now that we have put cameras everywhere and sensors everywhere, that worries us even more, because then we are always checking: is this locked or not, is there somebody outside or not? So: any incident that could occur in the night that could be potentially dangerous for me, ya Allah, You protect me from that.

7. You are my strength and my support
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ عَضُدِي وَنَصِيرِي، بِكَ أَحُولُ وَبِكَ أَصُولُ وَبِكَ أُقَاتِلُ

O Allah, You are my strength and You are my support; by You I go forth, by You I advance, and by You I fight. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say these words when he would go to battle.

‘Adud is the upper arm. You are my strength, You are my support; with Your help I go forth, with Your help I can reach, with Your help I can fight — not on my own; it is only with You, with Your help and support. And sometimes you are going to face something that literally feels like a battle, so say these words.

8. Conceal my faults, calm my fears — morning and evening
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي دِينِي وَدُنْيَايَ وَأَهْلِي وَمَالِي، اللَّهُمَّ اسْتُرْ عَوْرَاتِي وَآمِنْ رَوْعَاتِي، اللَّهُمَّ احْفَظْنِي مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيَّ وَمِنْ خَلْفِي وَعَنْ يَمِينِي وَعَنْ شِمَالِي وَمِنْ فَوْقِي، وَأَعُوذُ بِعَظَمَتِكَ أَنْ أُغْتَالَ مِنْ تَحْتِي

O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the next. O Allah, I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, conceal my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from what is in front of me and behind me, from my right and from my left and from above me; and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being struck down from beneath me.

This is a du’a the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say in the morning and in the evening, so we should also make a habit of saying it before the sun rises and before the sun sets.

Some people have an immense fear of the Hereafter, and that fear is paralysing: they don’t want to hear about matters of the Hereafter, they don’t want to think about it, because the moment they start thinking about it they are filled with fear. Sometimes you see this kind of response in children. And sometimes certain individuals are very afraid of Allah — there is more fear than hope. That is also not correct; there should be both fear and hope, and fear should not be paralysing. If it is like that, ask Allah to protect you.

And: conceal my faults — any of the wrong things that I have done, ya Allah, conceal them. And amin raw‘ati — any of the anguish, the worry, the anxiety that I feel in my heart, ya Allah, calm that, save me. And guard me from all directions — front, back, right, left, above, below — because this is where danger comes from.

At the Battle of al-Ahzab, Allah mentions how the hearts reached up to the throats; the Muslims were so afraid, the companions were so anxious, they were terrified. So they asked the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam to teach them something they could say, and he taught them: Allahumma astur ‘awratina wa amin raw‘atina — O Allah, conceal our weak points and calm our fears.

9. Protect me from going astray
اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْتُ وَبِكَ خَاصَمْتُ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِعِزَّتِكَ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ أَنْ تُضِلَّنِي، أَنْتَ الْحَيُّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَالْجِنُّ وَالْإِنْسُ يَمُوتُونَ

O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I believe, upon You I rely, to You I turn, and with Your help I contend. O Allah, I seek refuge in Your might — there is no deity but You — that You should let me go astray. You are the Ever-Living who does not die, while the jinn and mankind die.

Sometimes we have this fear: what if I go astray? What if I end up in Hell? What if the blessing of Islam is taken away from me? So you ask Allah to protect you from going astray.

10. Allah is greater than what I fear
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَعَزُّ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ جَمِيعًا، اللَّهُ أَعَزُّ مِمَّا أَخَافُ وَأَحْذَرُ، أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ، الْمُمْسِكِ السَّمَاوَاتِ السَّبْعِ أَنْ يَقَعْنَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ، مِنْ شَرِّ عَبْدِكَ فُلَانٍ وَجُنُودِهِ وَأَتْبَاعِهِ وَأَشْيَاعِهِ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ، اللَّهُمَّ كُنْ لِي جَارًا مِنْ شَرِّهِمْ، جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ وَعَزَّ جَارُكَ وَتَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ وَلَا إِلَٰهَ غَيْرُكَ

Allah is the greatest. Allah is mightier than all of His creation together. Allah is mightier than what I fear and what I am cautious of. I seek refuge in Allah, besides whom there is no deity, the One who holds the seven heavens from falling upon the earth except by His permission — from the evil of Your slave so-and-so, and his forces, his followers and his supporters, from among the jinn and mankind. O Allah, be my protector against their evil. Great is Your praise, mighty is Your protection, blessed is Your name, and there is no deity but You.

You can mention the name of the person you are terribly afraid of, whoever that person may be: ya Allah, protect me from this person’s evil — his evil and the evil of his forces. Because sometimes there are individuals who are trying to harm you, and they are not alone; they have gathered up armies to harm you. And sometimes there is a fear that so-and-so has done magic, or that they are using the power of magic against you — so ask Allah to protect you against that. Ibn ‘Abbas (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that when you go to an oppressive ruler and you are afraid that he will try to overcome you, to harm you, then you say this du’a three times.

11. Increase in tasbih
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ · سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ

Glory be to Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and there is no deity but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; glory be to Allah, the Most Great.

If you feel that in general you are an anxious person, or that you are increasing in your anxiety and you wonder what is happening to me — I was never so anxious before, why do I feel anxious all the time, why do I feel afraid? — if you see these changes in your life, that you were bold and courageous and things did not bother you, but now every email causes you to become anxious, then increase in these words. Because in a hadith we learn that if someone is afraid to spend their wealth, or is afraid of an enemy, or is afraid of struggling in the way of Allah, or the darkness of the night frightens him, then this person should increase in saying them. Increase in tasbih, and Allah will calm your heart, He will calm your fears, He will grant you courage. And when you glorify and praise Allah you are shifting your focus away from what frightens you to the power and perfection and greatness of Allah — so that you can know that Allah is enough for you against anything that frightens you.

Hasbunallahu wa ni’mal wakil.
Ameen.
Chapter One Hundred and Ten

Created Into Hardship

The Qur’an

“We have certainly created man into hardship.”

The way that Allah has created us, and the world that Allah has put us in, and the different stages that Allah makes us live through, and the different changes that Allah brings into our lives — they are such that we are constantly put into hardship.

And hardship is heavy on the nafs; it is very difficult for a person to endure. You barely get used to one thing and another significant change happens in your life, and so you are always struggling. At times this hardship comes in the form of not only physical hardship, but adjusting to loss, or adjusting to greater responsibilities, or having to earn an income and looking after your different needs. So when a person is constantly going through these difficult changes in life, it is only natural that a person will experience sadness and worry.

Because Allah tells us that Jannah is the home which is free of any hardship, any worry, any difficulty. Allah says about the people of Jannah that they will have no fear and they will not grieve — which means that in this world there are times when we feel afraid, and there are also times when we feel very sad.

Ibn ‘Abbas said about this that it refers to the difficulty the human being experiences in the womb of the mother, and then coming out of the womb, and then as the child nurses, and then as the child is weaned off the mother’s milk, and then as the teeth grow, and so on. With every stage of life there is another kind of difficulty, and with that difficulty there is also some kind of sadness. For a child to be weaned off the mother’s milk — yes, this is necessary for the child’s development and growth, the child has to start eating foods the body needs — but at the same time weaning is painful; it is painful for the heart, it is heartbreaking; the child does not understand why he or she cannot have the mother’s milk anymore. And then at the end of life there is death, and the pain and difficulty and hardships of death.

Qatadah said that kabad refers to the difficulties people experience in this world and also in the Hereafter — after death there are difficulties in the grave, in the gathering, and then on the Day of Judgement also. And it was said that the world has been created for trials and hardships, so the intelligent person should make himself patient. In this life there are always going to be some kind of difficulty, so a person who is intelligent, who wants not only to survive but to thrive, must learn to observe patience.

Hadith

The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever.

And no one is happy in prison. Yes, a person can come to terms with it — all right, I am here — but it doesn’t mean that they are happy and joyful and things are good. Just like that, the world is a prison for the believer, and the home of the Hereafter is the place where there is relief from all worries. We learn that the people of Paradise will say: all praise be to Allah, who has removed from us all sorrow.

Jannah Erases Sadness

Because Jannah is such that as soon as a person enters it they will forget about all of the worries and sadness and heartbreaks that they experienced in worldly life.

Hadith

A person from among the people of Hell who had lived a life of the greatest ease and plenty in the world will be brought and dipped once into the Fire, and then he will be asked: O son of Adam, did you ever see any good? Did you ever experience any blessing? And he will say: by Allah, no, my Lord. And a person from among the people of Paradise who had lived the most miserable life in the world will be brought and dipped once into Paradise, and then he will be asked: O son of Adam, did you ever see any hardship? Did you ever experience any distress? And he will say: by Allah, no, my Lord, I have never experienced any hardship, I have never faced any distress.

One second in Hell will make a person forget all of the ease that they enjoyed in the world; and one moment in Paradise will make a person forget every hardship they ever endured. This is so amazing. Jannah is the place where there is no sadness; in fact it is such that a person will forget all of their sadness and all the worries they ever experienced before. So our aim should be that through the difficulties and the ups and downs of this life we stay focused on the home of the Hereafter.

Chapter One Hundred and Eleven

He Called Out From the Darknesses

The Qur’an — Surat al-Anbiya

“And remember the man of the fish, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree upon him. And he called out within the darknesses: There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers. So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.”

Yunus (‘alayhis salam) was a prophet, and he was inviting his people to the worship of Allah alone for a very long time. But when they continued to show disobedience, it came to a point where he felt very frustrated and angry with them, and he left. He threatened them with Allah’s punishment and he left them, and he began travelling to go somewhere else.

However, a prophet is not allowed to leave his people without the permission of Allah — this is similar to how when you are working for someone you cannot just quit your work and leave. He became impatient with his people, he became angry with them, and he left in a state of extreme anger; he quit his work, and he didn’t think he was doing anything wrong.

So Allah says: he thought that We would not constrict his matters for him — because he didn’t think he was doing anything wrong; he thought Allah was on his side, because people were not listening, they were not believing, so they were inviting the punishment of Allah, and Yunus was doing the right thing by calling them. And now that he got angry and left, he thought Allah would still be on his side.

And then: he called out from the darknesses. He ended up boarding a ship, and there was a storm, and the people decided that one person would have to be thrown off the ship. How to decide who? They drew lots, and the name of Yunus came up. But they recognised him as a good man, a righteous man, so they said: let’s try again. They drew lots again, and again his name came up. They tried a third time — and as Allah says, he drew lots and was of those who were defeated. So they decided to throw him off the ship, and when he fell into the water a fish swallowed him; and this is the reason why he is called Dhun-Nun, nun being the fish.

So he was in the darkness of the belly of the fish, the darkness of the ocean, the darkness of the night. And from there he called upon Allah — because when he fell into the water and got trapped in the fish, he realised at that time that he had made a mistake. Up until that point he didn’t realise he was doing something wrong.

And so often this happens with us also: that we don’t even realise we have done anything wrong until we fall into some kind of difficulty, until something distresses us, something makes us very sad.

Layers of Darkness

And this darkness was not just tangible darkness — the darkness of the belly of the fish, of the water, of the night — but also the darkness that is intangible: the darkness of sadness, the darkness of loneliness, the darkness of guilt, the darkness of shame and embarrassment.

And so often this happens: that when you realise you have done something wrong, you feel like you are drowning in your guilt, and your sadness shrouds you, it covers you — your worry and your guilt and shame and feelings of embarrassment. What was I thinking? How could I have done something like this? Why did I do this? How could I have made this mistake? Is there any hope for me? Can I somehow make up for this?

In those darknesses he called out to Allah. And what did he say? There is no god but You. Ya Allah, You are One; there is absolutely no one worthy of worship but You. Subhanaka — You are perfect, glory be to You; You are free from any error, any mistake, any injustice. Inni kuntu min az-zalimin — it is I, it is me, who has been of those who do wrong. I am wrong here. This is my fault. This is my own wrongdoing.

And when he made this du’a, Allah says: so We responded to him and We saved him from his distress, from his sadness, from what was worrying him, from what was making him feel so sad. And then Allah says: and thus do We save the believers — meaning this is not exclusive to Yunus; any believer who feels immense sadness, whatever the reason may be.

The cause of immense sadness could be some worldly loss; it could be a mistake that a person has made; it could be finding oneself trapped in difficulty after difficulty, not knowing how to bring oneself out. Because think about Yunus: when he was trapped in the belly of the fish, how was he meant to come out of there? If a person is trapped in a room they will bang the doors and the walls, they will make noise, and if there is a window they will try to escape from there. But if a person is trapped in the belly of a fish — in the stomach there are digestive enzymes; you can only imagine that within moments the skin would begin to fall apart; and the smell, the darkness, the worry. How do you bring yourself out of that difficulty?

And sometimes a person finds themselves in situations like this, where they don’t know how to come out. It could be debt; it could be abandonment by people; it could be the oppression of people; it could be abuse by the people who are close to you. Sometimes you are trapped and you don’t know how to help yourself. But even in that situation, remember you have the ability to make du’a — and the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the weakest person is the one who is too weak to make du’a.

Even if you have no one to blame but yourself, like Yunus (‘alayhis salam) — he said inni kuntu min az-zalimin; it was his fault, he should not have left his people, he should not have been hasty. Sometimes you have no one else to blame except yourself; you know that it is entirely your fault that you are in the situation you are in, and you are feeling more and more sad because of that.

How Allah Rescued Him

But look at how Allah rescued him. The fish spat him out and he was at the shore, and he was saqim, unwell; and Allah caused a vine to grow over there, and the leaves not only provided him shade but that particular plant was also of benefit to him. So Allah brought him out of the belly of the fish, gave him physical healing, made him feel better. And then Yunus returned to his people and found that they had already believed and repented — because when he left them angrily, they realised they had done something wrong, and so they did collective tawbah, all of them together repenting to Allah and seeking His forgiveness, and so the punishment was averted from them.

Look at how Allah completely changed his situation: how he was so sad, trapped in a difficulty he had brought upon himself — and Allah rescued him and completely transformed his condition. And Allah says: and thus do We save the believers.

So if you find yourself in a situation where you are very upset and sad and regretful, where you feel alone and you find yourself in darkness, tangible and intangible, and you don’t know what steps to take — because in darkness you cannot even see your hands, you cannot even see your surroundings — sometimes you find yourself in such confusion, in such depths of sadness, that you don’t even know what to say, what to do, what steps to take, how to help yourself. And this is how depression is also: a person does not even find the ability to get out of bed, they don’t even find the energy, the strength, to crawl out of bed. This is how physically hard depression can be.

And so we learn from the example of Yunus that one of the most effective things to say is: there is no deity except You — declaring Allah’s absolute oneness; He has no partner, no one is like Him, no one is equal to Him, no one is similar to Him in any way whatsoever; He is One, He is unique, He is absolutely perfect, He is the only one worthy of worship. And then subhanaka — ya Rabb, You are perfect; declaring Allah’s perfection from any fault or error or injustice. And then inni kuntu min az-zalimin — admit your own wrongdoing, admit your own mistake.

Because when you are sad, when you are feeling down, and especially if you are physically unwell, at that time you begin to remember your shortcomings, your faults, your mistakes, your errors. So don’t let those thoughts take over you; repel them by seeking forgiveness from Allah. The first step towards rectification is admission: that yes, I am not perfect; yes, I am wrong; yes, I have made a mistake; yes, I should not have done this or that; I messed up. So admit your guilt before Allah, and believe in Allah’s mercy, His forgiveness, His perfection — and you will find light at the end of the tunnel, you will find a way out of your difficulty.

Hadith
