The supplication of Dhun-Nun when he called upon his Lord while in the belly of the whale: there is no deity except You, exalted are You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers. No Muslim ever supplicates with these words regarding any matter except that Allah answers him.

So this means that if a person is in sadness, in worry, in the depths of depression even — and they don’t know what to do, what to say, how to help themselves, and even if they are going through therapy and treatment and medication — along with all of that we must say this du’a.

And sometimes what is worrying you is a big deal to you, what is making you sad is a big deal for you, but for other people it is not that big of a deal; they are very dismissive. They say: oh, you are physically perfectly fine, you don’t have a broken bone, you don’t have any issue in your heart or your blood or any organ in your body — physically you’re fine, so just get over it. And it is not possible to just get over it; that is not how sadness and depression work. If there is something in the brain causing a person to feel like that, it is not as easy as “just get out of bed and you’ll be fine.” It is extremely hard.

And this incident is so validating, because Yunus was trapped in the darkness of the belly of the fish — and as mentioned, it was not just tangible darkness, it was intangible darkness; and it was not just one darkness, it was layers and layers of darkness. So how are you supposed to find a way out of that on your own? You cannot. You need help. You need the help of the one true God who is perfectly able to rescue you. So you need to connect to Him, you need to reach out to Him: ya Allah, You bring me out. And yes, you take the therapy, yes, you take the medication — but they are not the source of relief. The source of relief is Allah.

There Is No Fixed Number

Some people think that you have to say it a hundred thousand times, or some other number that they have specified, and then you will find relief. No, there is no specified number. We don’t even know how many times Yunus (‘alayhis salam) said this — who knows, maybe he said it only once or twice. The main thing is that you say it with your heart, with honesty, with presence of heart and mind.

Our problem is that we don’t exert effort when we are making du’a. We rush through du’a; we just want some words to say, and we just want to be able to say them a certain number of times, and then we want the results to come immediately, and we don’t bother to exert effort.

Du’a requires that you put in effort: that first of all you are fully present in mind and heart; and you weaken yourself before Allah, you show that weakness, that neediness, you cry, you humble yourself; you spend some time glorifying and praising Allah, because when you do that you recall and mention His perfection and you invite His mercy; and then you send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, because that is a form of gratitude to Allah and to His slave Muhammad salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam; and then you present your need before Allah, you seek forgiveness from Allah, you call upon Him by His beautiful names and attributes.

And notice: in this statement of Yunus, are we asking for anything? Is there any request in it? Ya Allah, bring me ease, bring me relief, take this problem away from me? No. You are declaring the absolute oneness of Allah, His perfection; you are declaring the fact that you are in need of Allah — because if He is perfect, if He is the only God, that means that I am His slave. So you are showing servitude before Allah, and you are admitting your fault, your error, your mistake. And through that you invite Allah’s mercy.

We think du’a is just saying “ya Allah, give me this.” Some people don’t even bother to say “ya Allah”; they will say “please give me this,” or not even the word please. This is our biggest problem: that we don’t exert effort in making du’a, we are hasty in making du’a, and we are very impatient with the results. We want to see the results right away, immediately, the way that we want — and if things don’t work out our way then we despair.

Yunus made this du’a with sincerity of heart, and look at how Allah answered him. So if we want to be rescued from our sadness and our worries, then we need to call upon Allah with similar dedication, with humility, with presence of heart.

Chapter One Hundred and Twelve

Sadness Is an Obstacle, Not a Destination

Sadness is a completely natural emotion, and we see that the prophets of Allah and the righteous experienced it a great deal. But we should also understand that sadness, even though it is natural, is still an obstacle on the path to Allah.

Ibn al-Qayyim says that you should know that sadness is an obstacle on the path to Allah, and it is not one of the levels of faith, nor one of the high stations or destinations of those who are on the path of Allah. It is actually an obstacle.

And this is the reason why not even once have we been commanded to be sad, to feel sad; and sadness has not been praised in the Qur’an or by the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. On the contrary, numerous times in the Qur’an we have been told la tahzan — do not be sad. We have been commanded to be patient, to have hope, to put our trust in Allah, to fear Allah — but we have never been commanded to feel sad.

Ibn al-Qayyim says that sadness is a trial, a musibah, and we ask Allah to remove it from us; because success is in the removal of sadness, as the people of Paradise will say: all praise be to Allah who has removed sadness from us. Which means that sadness is not a goal; it is not something we want to welcome into our lives or maintain in our lives. It comes, of course it comes, and it is not always in our control — but we have to try to get over it, we have to try to move on, we have to learn to manage it.

In the Qur’an Allah says regarding the believers at Uhud: so that you would not grieve. The reason He put them in trial after trial was so that they would stop grieving — little things would not cause them to be sad anymore; they would develop a greater capacity to bear hardship. Allah says: do not weaken and do not grieve. To the mother of Musa, Allah says: do not be afraid and do not grieve. And the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said to Abu Bakr: do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.

What Prolonged Sadness Does

Ibn al-Qayyim said that four things ruin the body: worry, sadness, hunger, and sleeplessness. If a person is always worrying, this will ruin his body. If a person is always sad, this will ruin his body. If a person is always hungry and doesn’t eat sufficiently, this will ruin his body. If a person does not sleep enough, this will ruin his body. And we have been taught that our body is an amanah, so we have to take care of it, look after it in a responsible way.

He also said that worry and sadness create weakness in the heart, and they take a person’s determination away — determination of the heart, strong will, courage; all of this is removed from the heart when a person is feeling sad. And he said that when a person is always worried and sad, this sadness becomes an obstacle, so that he is not able to work hard for things that are of benefit to him.

Think about it: if a person is feeling extremely sad and they are constantly in their home or in bed, they are not able to get water for themselves, they are not able to look after themselves, not able to help around at home, not able to go to work, not able to go to school — a person’s life is getting wasted. Or sometimes sadness prevents a person from seeking knowledge: a person does not even want to read, does not even want to listen to something of benefit, because it completely shrouds them like darkness; a person is surrounded by darkness, not able to see anything, not able to help themselves.

So yes, sadness is something normal, it happens — but we need to realise that it is something we have to learn to manage, and we have to learn to get over it. We don’t keep it in our lives like we would keep a pet, feeding it constantly, letting it define our lives, letting it define our identities. We have to learn to move past it.

Two Kinds of Sadness

Ibn al-Qayyim said that there are two types of sadness: one is the type of sadness which is in your favour, and the other is the type which is against you.

The sadness and worry which is in your favour is that which is in regard to the Hereafter. If a person commits a sin and then feels sad, feels bad about it, and is worried — this kind of sadness is good, it is healthy; because it will lead a person to seek forgiveness from Allah, it will lead a person to become better, to change their ways. And if a person does not feel sad on doing something wrong, then they will only get worse in their sins.

And the sadness which is against a person is when a person is sad and worried over the dunya, over worldly matters: oh, I am so sad I don’t have that much money; I am so sad I didn’t get such and such grades; I am so sad I didn’t get into such and such school or programme; I am so sad that my family is so big; I am so sad that my family is poor; I am so sad that my hair is of this texture, or that my skin is of this colour, or that my height is like this, or that my eyes are like this.

This kind of sadness works against a person. Why? Because first of all it is from shaytan, who likes to see us worried and mentally preoccupied and distracted and essentially unhappy — because when we are unhappy we cannot focus on the opportunities Allah has provided us. For example, you didn’t get the grades you were expecting: maybe this is a sign for you to change your programme, to change your career; maybe this is not working out, so you go and speak to a counsellor, you go talk to a professor, someone who can give you good advice; maybe this is an indication that you need to change the way you study. Not that you keep thinking: oh, this is terrible, God does not want me to succeed, I am just a failure, I am never going to be able to complete my degree, I will never get a good job, I will just be stuck in a cycle of poverty. One negative thought after another after another. This kind of worry and sadness, related to worldly matters, is extremely unhealthy, because it keeps a person away from doing things that they are capable of doing, and it leads a person on the path of ingratitude and away from Allah.

Allah has created us with the capacity to worry and the capacity to feel sad, and this is for a wisdom, for a benefit: that we feel sad and worried in regard to the matters of the Hereafter, not the matters of the world. This is similar to how Allah has given us wealth — what is that wealth for? So that you waste it, so that you show off with it, so that you commit abuse through it? No; Allah has given you wealth as an opportunity to earn the home of the Hereafter. So just like that, all of our emotions are a means: we can use them in a way that helps us in matters of the Hereafter, and we can also use them in a way that distracts us from it.

Ibn al-Qayyim mentions that when a person wakes up in the morning and enters the evening and his only concern is to connect with his Lord, to pursue the pleasure of Allah, to show servitude to Allah, then Allah takes care of all of his affairs and removes his worries; Allah empties the heart of this person for His love, and his tongue for His remembrance, and his limbs for His obedience. But when a person enters the morning and the evening in a state where his only concern is the world, then Allah attaches worldly concerns and worries to him — a person is constantly worried about worldly matters, constantly sad, constantly concerned about worldly things; and then a person does not experience the love of Allah; rather a person is preoccupied and distracted by the love of the creation; a person is not able to remember Allah on his tongue; instead his tongue is busy remembering people; a person is not able to use his limbs in obedience to Allah; instead his limbs are being used to serve the creation. What a difference.

The prophets of Allah: Allah says, indeed We chose them for an exclusive quality — remembrance of the home of the Hereafter. That was their concern. That is what worried them, what made them sad: are we going to make it there? Am I doing enough to get there?

‘Abdur-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, once food was brought to him while he was fasting — food to break his fast with, and it must have been very nice. And he said that Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr was better than me, and he was shrouded in one garment: if we covered his head his feet were exposed, and if we covered his feet his head was exposed. And then the dunya was expanded for us — so now I fear whether there is going to be any reward left for us in the Hereafter. And he began crying and crying until he was not able to eat.

Look at the concern of the sahabah. What made him sad was not “I don’t have any good food to eat”; what made him sad was “I am getting so much good food to eat — what is going to happen on the Day of Judgement?” This is how we need to think. Because whatever we focus on, that we will strive towards.

❖  ❖  ❖

How to Manage It

Purify your belief in tawhid. Constantly remind yourself that Allah alone is worthy of worship, that Allah alone is perfect in every way, free from any imperfection, any error, any fault.

Strengthen your belief in qadar. Yes, it is painful, yes, it makes us sad, but this was decreed. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam wept on many occasions; and when his son Ibrahim died he was crying, and he was asked: you also cry? He said yes — and he mentioned that the heart is sad and the eye weeps, but nothing that displeases Allah will come out of the tongue. We are pleased with the decree of Allah; and yes, we are sad, but we are not upset with Allah. We know that this was decreed, and that Allah decreed it with His wisdom and knowledge and mercy and justice.

Think positively about Allah. No matter what happens, no matter how sad you are, no matter how worried you are, think good about Allah. Instead of thinking that Allah wants me to fail, Allah doesn’t want me to succeed, Allah does not want me to live a happy life — these are all wrong thoughts. When you are feeling very down in your sadness and you don’t even have the energy to come out of bed or go to work, at that time also think good: I am going through this by the decree of Allah, and there is always good in what Allah decrees. Maybe completing this degree at this time is not good for me; maybe having this person in my life at this time is not good for me; maybe Allah is protecting me from something more dangerous; maybe Allah is protecting me from committing sin; maybe Allah is erasing my sins through this. Believe that Allah is on your side.

Focus on the reward. What are the benefits of experiencing difficulty? That Allah will remove your sins — this hardship will become an expiation, because even the prick of a thorn is something because of which the believer’s sins are removed. That Allah will raise your ranks. That Allah will perhaps protect you from something even greater.

Look at those who are suffering more. Maybe you are sad that you didn’t get to have dessert after iftar; maybe you are sad that you didn’t get to eat the best iftar for the third or fourth day in a row. But look at those who are suffering more than you, who are struggling more than you. Has Allah not kept you in a very good condition?

Recall the trials of the prophets. Think about the difficulty the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam endured, how he experienced loss and pain, how he managed his sadness. He lost Khadijah, the love of his life, whom he loved so dearly. He lost his uncle, and his uncle died as a non-Muslim — how heavy, how painful that was for him. And then his own people turned against him, and he had to leave his hometown, Makkah of all places, the Ka‘bah. And then in Madinah the hypocrites were constantly harming him, trying to attack him, so much so that they tried to hurt him by slandering his wife ‘A’ishah, the one whom he loved. Think about the difficulties he went through, and take hope: if he endured them, and Allah raised his ranks through them, then insha’Allah what is bothering me, what is heavy on me, Allah will help me through that as well. And if he was patient, I should also be patient; he had hope, I should also have hope.

And it’s okay to cry; it’s okay to feel sad. You are not sinful for feeling sad; you are not sinful for crying. But the thing with sadness is that prolonged sadness becomes an obstacle on the path; it hinders you from living to your full potential, from doing what is in your capacity.

Complain to Allah. Ya‘qub (‘alayhis salam) complained to Allah of his sadness, of his grief: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.

Busy yourself in the dhikr of Allah — unquestionably, it is in the remembrance of Allah that hearts find rest.

Focus on your obligations. If in one day you are not able to do a lot, but at least you are able to pray your five daily prayers on time, properly, with wudu — alhamdulillah, it was a good day. Because when a person is struggling with depression, even things like washing your face or brushing your hair are a big deal. So focus on your basic obligations, the five daily prayers; start with that. Just tell yourself: I have to get up and pray my Fajr. And yes, after Fajr you don’t have the energy, you lie down again — it doesn’t matter. Focus on completing your basic obligations, and then gradually increase in doing good deeds.

And I would advise the same to the family: if somebody in your household is going through such a phase, where extreme sadness or depression has overcome a person, then help them perform their obligatory prayers, and don’t let them miss any salah. Sometimes other things get missed, but salah — don’t miss that at all; because when a person prays salah they are in the protection of Allah, and you want that special protection.

Give sadaqah. Because when a person gives sadaqah this is something that cools the anger of Allah, something through which you invite Allah’s mercy, and something that brings relief. We learn in the Qur’an about those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah: they will have their reward, and there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.

Say positive words. Make a habit that when you check your results, when you receive some news, you say: I am pleased with Allah. Say words that show you are pleased with Allah’s decree. Of course you are sad, but don’t say things like “if only I had said such and such, if only I had done such and such” — because the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that “if only” opens the door to the work of shaytan, and you are inviting shaytan into your matter. It was written; and yes, I am sad, and Allah is the healer of hearts, and Allah is able to change my situation.

Check what you are eating. Eat comfort food, food that will be a source of comfort for you, and also food that is nutritious and easy to eat. We learn that it was the habit of ‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) that when someone passed away she would tell the women to cook talbinah — a kind of porridge — and she would give that to the family of the deceased, saying that it comforts the heart of the ill person and removes some of the sadness. And really, you will experience this: if you are feeling very low and you eat something nice, it uplifts your mood. And sometimes a person is feeling sad or constantly bitter because there is some kind of nutritional deficiency in the body; and part of the healing is not only medication but also taking supplements, because this helps with the deficiencies because of which there is an imbalance in the body. This doesn’t mean that you are always soothing yourself with chocolate or with food that is unhealthy for you — but it was the way of ‘A’ishah (radiyallahu ‘anha) to help people feel better by giving them food that was good for them.

Chapter One Hundred and Thirteen

The Du’as for Worry and Sadness

1. Busy the tongue with His remembrance
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ

Glory be to Allah, and all praise is for Allah, and there is no deity but Allah, and Allah is the greatest. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said regarding this that if there is anyone who is afraid of the darkness of the night, or too cowardly to face the enemy, or too worried to spend their wealth, then they should increase in saying these words.

Dhikr strengthens the heart; it brings courage to a person’s heart; it brings relief to a person’s heart. We learn in the Qur’an: and We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say — what the people say grieves you, makes you sad. And what was the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam told to do? So glorify your Lord with praise.

And sometimes when a person is feeling sad because of worldly matters — a person is really sad about how they are short, or the fact that their nose is too flat or too big — you say SubhanAllah. What does that mean? Allah is perfect; Allah does not make a mistake; He created me like this, this is His choice, He does not make a mistake. Alhamdulillah — thank You, Allah, for giving me life; thank You, Allah, for giving me intelligence, a mind, the ability to do so much. La ilaha illallah — I worship Him; and then you think about the different ways in which you can worship Allah in an excellent way. And Allahu Akbar — anything that worries me, anything that makes me sad, anything that frightens me: Allah is the greatest.

2. Send salawat on the Prophet
اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ

O Allah, send salah upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad. When you send salawat on him once, Allah sends ten blessings on you, ten mercies on you; ten sins are erased from you and ten ranks are raised.

And as we learn in the hadith, when a person devotes the whole duration of their du’a to sending salawat on him, then Allah will suffice them against all of their worldly concerns — meaning Allah will take care of all of their worldly matters, anything that worries them, that makes them sad. So increase in sending salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam.

And I would encourage you: make a list for yourself of the things you have to do when you feel down, and share these tips with people in your family, with your friends, especially someone who you know struggles with such feelings.

3. The du’a of Yunus (‘alayhis salam)
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ

There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed I have been of the wrongdoers. Allah says: so We responded to him and saved him from the distress — and thus do We save the believers.

4. At the time of distress
اللَّهُ اللَّهُ رَبِّي لَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا

Allah, Allah is my Lord; I do not associate anything with Him.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said to Asma bint ‘Umays: shall I not teach you words which you can say at the time of distress? And her life was not easy. She was first married to Ja‘far (radiyallahu ‘anhu) and she was with him in Abyssinia — and living as a minority is very difficult: you experience poverty, you experience discrimination, you experience isolation, loneliness; and all this time they were far from the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam. And then finally when they migrated to Madinah, in the seventh year after the hijrah, some companions would tell them: we are better than you, because we got to spend more time with the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam — and this bothered her a lot, and she complained to him about it. And soon after they migrated to Madinah, Ja‘far was martyred at the Battle of Mu’tah. So now she is a widow with little children. And then she married Abu Bakr (radiyallahu ‘anhu); and when they were going for the farewell pilgrimage she was full-term pregnant, and she gave birth on the way to Hajj. And then soon after the farewell pilgrimage the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam passed away; and Abu Bakr became the khalifah, and two years after that he also passed away.

This is not an easy thing for a woman — to experience loss after loss after loss. There is no stability. Typically a woman desires her own home, her husband, her children — so that if something changes, at least she has a place where she can feel secure. But there were constant changes, constant turbulence in her life. How did she manage? The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught her these words, and he would teach them to his family and say to them: when any worry or distress or sadness befalls you, say this.

And notice what we are doing in this du’a: we are taking the name of Allah twice, so that you find joy and comfort in taking the name of Allah. And as you say Allahu Allahu, you bring to mind His greatness, you strengthen your belief in His oneness, and you realise that the name Allah is very powerful, very blessed, and it encompasses within it all of the other names and attributes of Allah — because Allah means the God, the only one worthy of worship; and who can be the only one worthy of worship? The one who is ever-living, the one who is perfect in His ability, the one who is the creator, the fashioner. So all of the names and attributes of Allah are encompassed in meaning by the name Allah. And then: Allah is my Rabb, my Lord — He created me, He made me, He owns me, He guides me, He has given me everything I have; every blessing I have is from Him; I return to Him. So Allah is my Rabb; I am not alone; my Rabb is there, He takes care of me. And I do not associate anything with Him — I worship only Him, I expect help from Him alone.

5. O Ever-Living, O Sustainer
يَا حَيُّ يَا قَيُّومُ بِرَحْمَتِكَ أَسْتَغِيثُ

O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, by Your mercy I seek help. We learn in hadith that when a matter worried the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam, he would say this.

Here you are taking two names of Allah, and the ulama say that these are al-ism al-a‘zam, the greatest names of Allah; and we learn in hadith that if you call upon Allah by these names, Allah accepts the du’a. Al-Hayy means the Ever-Living, the one who is always there and always will be, because all of His attributes and qualities are perfect — His knowledge and His power do not fade away with time; His life, His existence, is perfect; and He is also the giver of life, the source of life. And al-Qayyum means the one who sustains everything, who is independent of all, while everything depends on Him. So you are calling upon Allah by these names in your time of worry and sadness: ya Allah, You are the giver of life — give life to my heart, revive my heart. You are al-Qayyum, the sustainer of all; nothing can survive without You — so ya Allah, You take my sadness away, You help me manage this difficult situation I am in.

6. Do not leave me to myself
اللَّهُمَّ رَحْمَتَكَ أَرْجُو فَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself for even the blink of an eye; and set right for me all of my affairs. There is no deity but You.

This is the du’a for one who is in extreme distress, overwhelmed by their worry and sadness. It is Your mercy that I desperately desire — so do not leave me to my own soul, because if You leave me to myself then I can end up in disobedience, in doing wrong things. So don’t leave me to myself; You take care of me, You protect me. And set right all of my matters — in my family, my house, my neighbours, my friends, my business, my studies, my inner self, my heart, my mind, my health, whatever it is. You fix it for me; I am not able to fix it on my own.

7. In times of difficulty
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ

There is none worthy of worship but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. There is none worthy of worship but Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne. There is none worthy of worship but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne. Ibn ‘Abbas (radiyallahu ‘anhu) said that the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would say this whenever some difficulty came.

In this dhikr we are declaring the oneness of Allah and His perfection — that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah — and we say it three times; and then we mention His perfect names: the Most Great, the Forbearing, the one who does not punish immediately. He is the Lord of the Great Throne — and if He is the Lord of the Great Throne, then everything else is less than the Throne, it is smaller than the Throne, so it is not difficult for Allah to take care of. So repeating the statement la ilaha illallah lightens the burden of sadness in your heart; this is the cure.

8. Refuge from grief, weakness and laziness
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, from weakness and from laziness, from miserliness and from cowardice, from being overcome by debt and from being overpowered by men.

Sometimes when you are feeling so down you don’t know if it is sadness or weakness or laziness; you are feeling sad, and because of that sadness you don’t have the capacity to do anything, you don’t have the mental bandwidth to do much work — and people think you are being lazy. You may have experienced this, or maybe you think of others who are going through sadness that they are being lazy. So whether it is laziness, or sadness, or weakness, or grief — whatever it is, I seek refuge with You from all of this. Because all of these are obstacles on the path to Allah; they keep a person away from excelling in good deeds, from going forward in good works; they preoccupy a person and distract them from fulfilling the purpose of their life.

9. O Lord of the people, remove the trouble
اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، أَذْهِبِ الْبَاسَ، اشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي، لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا

O Allah, Lord of the people, remove the trouble; heal, for You are the Healer; there is no healing but Your healing — a healing that leaves behind no illness.

Sometimes you see your own child and they are feeling extremely sad and not able to overcome their sadness, and you wonder: okay, it’s just a broken toy, why isn’t my child able to get over it? Sometimes we laugh at our children; sometimes we start yelling at them; sometimes we become very harsh. And that is not the solution. The solution is that you acknowledge the feelings of sadness; don’t pretend like they don’t exist, acknowledge them. Part of managing such negative feelings is first of all to label the feeling, to pinpoint it, identify it, acknowledge it, put your finger on it: this is the issue. If you pretend that it is not there, that is not going to solve anything. So with your child also — whether your child is five or ten or fifteen or thirty — talk to them: this is what you are feeling, this is how you are feeling; let them process and understand what is going on; identify it, and then make du’a together.

Because sometimes a person has been taking medication for so long, medication with so many side effects, but people are desperate. It is not fun to take medication to manage depression or anxiety or any disorder; not only is it expensive, there are so many side effects that people who have to take it don’t want to take it. So call upon Allah: in Your hand is the cure; no one can remove this distress except You. Ask Allah to heal you, to make that medication work for you, to protect you from its side effects.

10. Make the Qur’an the spring of my heart
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي عَبْدُكَ، وَابْنُ عَبْدِكَ، وَابْنُ أَمَتِكَ، نَاصِيَتِي بِيَدِكَ، مَاضٍ فِيَّ حُكْمُكَ، عَدْلٌ فِيَّ قَضَاؤُكَ، أَسْأَلُكَ بِكُلِّ اسْمٍ هُوَ لَكَ سَمَّيْتَ بِهِ نَفْسَكَ، أَوْ أَنْزَلْتَهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ، أَوْ عَلَّمْتَهُ أَحَدًا مِنْ خَلْقِكَ، أَوِ اسْتَأْثَرْتَ بِهِ فِي عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ عِنْدَكَ، أَنْ تَجْعَلَ الْقُرْآنَ رَبِيعَ قَلْبِي، وَنُورَ صَدْرِي، وَجِلَاءَ حُزْنِي، وَذَهَابَ هَمِّي

O Allah, I am Your slave, the son of Your male slave, the son of Your female slave. My forehead is in Your hand; Your judgement upon me is assured, and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that You have named Yourself with, or revealed in Your book, or taught to any one of Your creation, or kept with Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen — that You make the Qur’an the spring of my heart, and the light of my chest, and the banisher of my sadness, and the reliever of my distress.

After the winter, when spring comes, what happens? You see so many colours, you see brightness, you see light, you hear sounds, you smell different smells. Spring is life after the dead of winter. So you are asking Allah: ya Allah, make the Qur’an the spring of my heart — just as my heart feels dead and lifeless and cold and colourless, You bring life to it through the Qur’an.

And in this is guidance: that what brings life to the heart is the Qur’an. This is the reason why we say that when a person is feeling sad, when a person is feeling down, they need to recite Qur’an. And unfortunately a lot of people mock this. But the Qur’an is shifa; the Qur’an has to be part of our plan to feel better; this is part of our prescription. So listening to the Qur’an, reciting the Qur’an, reflecting on the Qur’an, learning the Qur’an, memorising the Qur’an — this is not contrary to therapy; it is not contrary to taking medication. It is alongside all of those things. So take the medication, go for therapy, whatever it is — but don’t neglect the Qur’an, because Allah has revealed the Qur’an for our healing also.

Think about it: the people before us, at the time of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam — do you think they never experienced any trauma? Do you think they never experienced any death or loss or pain? What they suffered was way more than us. Can you imagine a woman giving birth while travelling, under a tree? It is so common that women experience trauma from childbirth even when they give birth in the safety of a hospital or in their own home. If a person experiences poverty for some time, that can cause trauma. So the people at the time of the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam experienced hardship that was way more than the hardship we endure, and of course they experienced all of these feelings. What means did they have to help themselves feel better? They did not have access to modern medication; they did not have access to therapy. They had access to the Qur’an, and they used it.

So part of our healing plan, part of the prescription, is to use the Qur’an: listen to it, recite it — and that will help you feel better, because this is the word of Allah; this is not the word of man. When Allah says kun, things come to life. Every ayah is the speech of Allah — do you think it doesn’t have power? This is a miracle. When Musa (‘alayhis salam) threw the staff it turned into a snake; when ‘Isa (‘alayhis salam) made something out of clay it came to life. These were the miracles given to the prophets before. The miracle given to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is the Qur’an. I am not saying that medication and therapy are useless — they are an excellent means that Allah has given us; but greater than that means is the Qur’an. So don’t belittle it in order to raise the status of what people have come up with. Use the Qur’an.

And really, the more time you spend with the Qur’an, your concerns and your worries will reduce in proportion to the time you spend with it. Get busy listening to the Qur’an; start memorising the Qur’an; and you will have something in your life that will make you happy. Because when something is making you constantly sad in life, yes, those factors are there — but you also need something in your life that will bring you joy, that will bring you a sense of accomplishment, that will make you feel that you are worthy, that you did something. And when you recite the Qur’an, when you memorise it, ayah after ayah, surah after surah, you are gaining a treasure that is better than all the things that people gather. We learn in hadith that when a person makes this du’a, Allah will convert his worry and sadness into ease.

11. In any distress or sadness
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْكَرِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ

There is no god worthy of worship but Allah, the Noble, the Forbearing. Glorified is He, and blessed is Allah, Lord of the Great Throne; and all praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam taught these words to say whenever a person would be in some kind of difficulty or distress or sadness.

12. The du’a on rising from a gathering
اللَّهُمَّ اقْسِمْ لَنَا مِنْ خَشْيَتِكَ مَا يَحُولُ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ مَعَاصِيكَ، وَمِنْ طَاعَتِكَ مَا تُبَلِّغُنَا بِهِ جَنَّتَكَ، وَمِنَ الْيَقِينِ مَا تُهَوِّنُ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا مَصَائِبَ الدُّنْيَا، وَمَتِّعْنَا بِأَسْمَاعِنَا وَأَبْصَارِنَا وَقُوَّتِنَا مَا أَحْيَيْتَنَا، وَاجْعَلْهُ الْوَارِثَ مِنَّا، وَاجْعَلْ ثَأْرَنَا عَلَى مَنْ ظَلَمَنَا، وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى مَنْ عَادَانَا، وَلَا تَجْعَلْ مُصِيبَتَنَا فِي دِينِنَا، وَلَا تَجْعَلِ الدُّنْيَا أَكْبَرَ هَمِّنَا وَلَا مَبْلَغَ عِلْمِنَا، وَلَا تُسَلِّطْ عَلَيْنَا مَنْ لَا يَرْحَمُنَا

O Allah, apportion for us such fear of You as shall come between us and acts of disobedience to You; and such obedience to You as shall cause us to obtain Your Paradise; and such certainty as shall make the afflictions of this world easy for us. And let us enjoy our hearing, our sight and our strength for as long as You keep us alive, and make it inherit from us; and let our vengeance be upon those who have wronged us, and aid us against those who show enmity towards us. And do not make our affliction in our religion, and do not make this world our greatest concern nor the limit of our knowledge, and do not give power over us to those who will not have mercy on us.

Typically, when you are sitting in a gathering and talking, our conversations revolve around what is happening in the political scene, or in your community, or the latest news from war in one country or war crimes in another part of the world. And these things are very heavy on the heart. So when you get up, make this du’a; ask Allah to protect you. And especially: grant us such certainty that the difficulties of the world become manageable for us; and allow us to benefit from our hearing and our vision and our abilities for as long as we live — because a person can be alive and breathing, but day after day is slipping away because they are experiencing such sadness that they are not able to do anything.

Alhamdulillahi alladhi adhhaba ‘anna al-hazan.
All praise be to Allah, who removed from us all sorrow.
Chapter One Hundred and Fourteen

Guide Us to the Straight Path

The first and most important du’a that we already make every day of our lives is ihdinas-siratal mustaqim — our Lord, guide us to the straight path. We make it in Surat al-Fatihah, which is a surah that is basically a prayer; and we make it in every salah, in every rak‘ah. This shows us how important the prayer for guidance is.

What Hidayah Actually Is

Hidayah is to direct someone to the right path; it is to ensure that they remain on the right path; and then you make sure that they also reach the destination.

When you put your destination into a maps application, it not only shows you the way — when you ask it to guide you on the way, then if you ever take a wrong turn or miss an exit, it will ensure that you get back on the right path; and then it will make sure that you reach your destination; and if you keep going off the path, it will keep guiding you back onto it. This is the concept of guidance: that you not only show someone what the right path is, but you ensure that they remain on it, and then you make them reach the correct destination also.

So when we ask Allah “guide us to the straight path,” we are asking Allah to direct us to the right path, not the wrong path; and we are also asking Allah to enable us to remain on the right path, to protect us from veering off; and we are asking Allah to grant us the ability to remain on it, to grant us firmness, stability, steadfastness on it, so that we reach the right destination, which is Allah’s approval.

In this ayah we are taught to ask Allah for the guidance of knowledge — guidance towards the truth; and the guidance of tawfiq — the ability to follow the truth, to adopt it, to live it; and then the guidance of tathbit — stability and firmness, for all our life.

And remember that as human beings our success is in reaching Jannah, because Allah says that the person who is saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has attained success. And this is ultimate success. Ultimate success is not in this life, not in this world, because no matter what level you reach in this life, your question is “what next?” In Jannah there is no “what next,” because it is ultimate success.

And Jannah is attained through Islam, because Allah tells us that whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. So when we say ihdinas-siratal mustaqim, we are asking Allah to give us the ability to leave every other way and hold on to Islam, to strengthen us in our Islam.

Ibn as-Sa‘di says that in this verse we are asking Allah for the truth: ya Allah, enable us to recognise the truth, and lead us towards it, and make us adhere to it. So we are asking Allah for the blessing of Islam, for the ability to adhere to it, and to guide us to all of the teachings of Islam, all of its different aspects.

For example, part of Islam is that a person prays salah regularly, five times a day — so when we ask ihdina, part of this du’a is: ya Allah, give me the ability to pray; teach me how to pray properly, in a way that is pleasing to You; give me the ability to pray in an excellent way. Likewise zakat is part of Islam: so you are asking Allah for the ability to calculate your zakat correctly, on time, and then give it in the best way, in the right place. So every single aspect of Islam, everything that is pleasing to Allah, every deed or word, big or small, any action, internal or external, manifest or private — all of that is included in this du’a. It is a very comprehensive and very beneficial du’a that every single person is in need of.

Why It Is in Every Rak‘ah

And our five daily prayers are based on it. In salah, what are we doing? We begin with thana, the praise of Allah; we recite Surat al-Fatihah, which is du’a; and then after that we recite some Qur’an; we go into ruku‘, we praise and glorify Allah; we stand up again, we glorify and praise Allah; we go into sajdah, again we glorify and praise Allah; and the rest of the salah is mainly glorifying and praising Allah. So the beginning of salah, the end of salah, the middle of salah is all praise and glorification of Allah — and we are basically asking for one thing, and that is guidance.

And if a person does not recite al-Fatihah, their salah is not valid; if a person misses Surat al-Fatihah in a rak‘ah, that rak‘ah is not valid, a person has to repeat the entire rak‘ah. So salah is based on this du’a. Five times a day we are asking Allah for hidayah, because we are always in need of it. A person can never have enough of hidayah.

If a person prays to have children and Allah grants them two, three, four, five children, then this is not a du’a they make anymore, because they are satisfied with the children Allah has given them. A person prays for wealth, and Allah gives them a lot of rizq, a lot of sustenance, so they are happy with what Allah has given. But when it comes to guidance, a person can never say: I am content and satisfied with the amount of guidance Allah has given me, so I don’t need to ask for more. No matter how much guidance you have, the fact is that you are always in need of more and better guidance — which is why you say it in one rak‘ah, and then in the next rak‘ah you make the same request again.

❖  ❖  ❖

Four Levels of Guidance

The first level is general guidance, or intuition, which Allah has put in every creature. Allah says: glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who destined and then guided. He gave every creature its unique form, and then He also guided it. A bird knows how to eat, where to find its food, what to avoid. A baby knows how to suck, how to drink milk. Each creature is guided in a way that Allah has taught it: how to breathe, how to live, how to eat.

The second level is the guidance of knowledge, where through the prophets and messengers Allah has taught people how to do things in a better way, in a way that is pleasing to Him; and when people learn those ways and follow them, they are brought out of darkness into light. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is addressed in the Qur’an: and indeed you guide to a straight path. He taught people what the straight path is, how to do things that please Allah.

The third level is tawfiq: the ability to adopt guidance, to accept the truth, not only to recognise the truth but to accept it, to internalise it. This is guidance that only Allah is able to give, because He is the one who opens the hearts of people, and He is the one who allows everything to come together so that a person can adopt guidance, internalise it, and act upon it.

Allah says to His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam: indeed you do not guide whom you love — meaning you cannot make people accept guidance, no matter how much you love them. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam loved his uncle Abu Talib, but he was not able to make him accept Islam. He could only tell him, only inform him, only show him the way. Abu Talib would have accepted that guidance if he had had that willingness, that yearning, that desire — and then Allah would also have given him tawfiq. But he did not have it, so Allah did not give him tawfiq. We learn: but Allah guides whom He wills.

The fourth level is guidance on the Day of Judgement, where a person is directed towards Paradise or towards Hellfire. We learn that as the people of Paradise enter it they will say: all praise is to Allah, who guided us to this — who showed us the way to Paradise. And on the Day of Judgement those who had taqwa will be driven to Paradise in groups, and there will be others who will be led towards Hellfire.

What It Takes to Reach a Destination

Think about it: if you want to reach a destination, there are a few things you need. If you are going to drive there, first and foremost you need to know how to drive — you need knowledge, you need a licence. Then having knowledge of driving and a licence alone is not enough; you also need a vehicle, a means of transportation, something that you can drive. So knowledge alone is not enough; you also need tawfiq, the ability from Allah, the means, the opportunity, the ability to obey Him and worship Him and do things in the best way. And a vehicle alone is not enough; you also need fuel. And then you need the directions, the map. And then on the road you need patience and determination and focus — because what happens with some people is that as they are driving they get distracted: oh, there’s a mall over here, oh, there’s a beach over here — and then they forget where they were going, and they get distracted by things on the way. And sometimes you are driving towards your destination but the roads are closed, so you need the roads to be open as well. And more than that, you also need experience and courage — how to drive on a certain road, through certain traffic, to get to a certain destination.

The final stage of guidance is that a person is put on the path to Paradise; and the one who was guided to the straight path in the world will be put on the right path to Paradise, the home of reward. And a person’s feet will be firm on that path in proportion to the firmness of his feet on the straight path in the world.

On the Day of Judgement we all have to cross the Sirat, the path, which is suspended over Hellfire, and that is the only way to Paradise. How can a person cross that path, which is sharper than a sword and thinner than a hair? How can a person have stability and firmness on it? It is only possible if a person was stable and firm on the right path in the world, on sirat al-mustaqim in the world. The way you are journeying on the straight path right now in this life is the way that you will cross that path on the Day of Judgement. So you need experience to cross that path — and how do you get that experience? In this world: how swift are you in obedience to Allah; how consistent are you in obedience to Allah; how much attention do you put into doing things the way that Allah is pleased with.

Guidance Before Everything Else

And remember that guidance is more important than anything else in your life — more important even than the food you eat. In fact the ulama say that there is no comparison between guidance and even your most basic necessities such as food. Why? Because the one who is given guidance becomes of the muttaqin; and the person who has taqwa, who is conscious of Allah, Allah will show him the way out of every trouble and give him sustenance from where he cannot even expect. If you have guidance, Allah will also provide you sustenance. Taqwa, iman, guidance is the key to worldly success also.

This doesn’t mean that we pray and fast and give sadaqah so that we can live a wealthy, easy, disease-free life in the world — that is not the goal; that is a side benefit. The real goal is the pleasure of Allah. And when you please Allah, when Allah is on your side, then all of your needs will be taken care of, and you will not have to chase after the little things in life. When a person is left to himself to take care of himself, his life becomes incredibly hard, very difficult; and when Allah takes care of the matters of His slave, the slave’s life becomes worry-free and easy.

In Every Matter

And we are in need of guidance in every single matter of our lives, because every moment we are doing something, choosing to do something, making a decision to do or not do something.

Sometimes we are talking and we have a tendency to move our hands a lot, and that is fine — but what is a better way of talking? When the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam would address people and give khutbah, how would he move his hands? We learn that he would just use the pointer finger; he wouldn’t be waving his arms back and forth, raising his arms up and down constantly. So imagine: now if a person is talking and they are expressive and they use their pointer finger, then they are rewarded for using their pointer finger in the way the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam did. Now even their hand gestures are a means of earning Allah’s pleasure. Isn’t this beautiful?

There are so many things that we do in one day, so many actions we do without even thinking, and not every action is necessarily a religious action; but if we do our worldly actions also in a way that is pleasing to Allah, in the way the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam demonstrated, then we are earning hasanat even for the mundane. So we are in need of guidance and improvement in every matter of our lives.

Think about it: when it comes to perfecting something and beautifying something, you pay attention to a lot of detail. A full face of makeup — is it just a little bit of lipstick and some eyeliner? No, there is even a way of “no-makeup makeup”; there is a certain type of layering that you do on your face in different ways using different products, because you are paying attention to detail. And if we can put in so much effort on a regular basis, and so much money, just to look a certain way, just to get the right shade, just to get the right effect — why can we not strive to earn the approval of Allah, which will be everlasting? How long do you keep your makeup on for? Not very long; in fact if you make wudu regularly you cannot keep it on for very long anyway. So why can we not exert effort and learn ways of improving our actions and our worship in order to earn the eternal approval of Allah? And we cannot do that without guidance from Allah.

So we need guidance related to everything: whether it is external and visible, or internal and hidden; a very private matter of our lives, or something deep in our heart.

We need guidance towards tawbah, repentance, for mistakes that we have made, for things we have done in ignorance. And we may be doing things in a way that is not perfect and complete, where there is room for improvement. If we are reciting Qur’an, we may be reciting correctly in the sense that we are not making any major mistakes; but if you recite to a teacher, they will stop you at every letter, every word, and direct you to improve your recitation. You may be praying salah thinking that you are praying perfectly fine, but when you ask someone of knowledge to check how you are praying, they might correct you: you should be sitting in this way, your toes should be facing that way, when you are making ruku‘ your back needs to be more straight, what you are reciting can be improved. So there is always a need of improving and perfecting the actions we are already doing.

Sometimes we have the willingness to do something but we don’t have the ability. So when we ask Allah for guidance, we are asking Allah for the ability to do good also. And sometimes we have the ability but not the willingness — we may have the money sitting with us, but we don’t have the willingness, the knowledge, the intention to spend it in the right place. We ask Allah for guidance, and Allah sends someone our way who shows us: you can give this much money over here for such and such cause. And it may be a little amount of money, but you give it, and Allah increases you in guidance.

And sometimes you are doing good in the present, but there is no guarantee that you will continue to do these good deeds in the future. Doesn’t it happen that a person is doing something good at a certain time, but then five years later, ten years later, things change, and they are no longer doing what they used to do? They stop, they discontinue — because doing that particular good deed became very hard for them, their nafs prevented them, or the fear of people, or whatever prevented them, so they no longer had the ability to continue. So when we ask Allah for guidance, we are asking for guidance in the future also.

So when you say ihdinas-siratal mustaqim, keep all of these matters in your mind: ya Allah, guide me to repent from sins and errors I have made out of ignorance; give me the ability to remain consistent; give me the ability to be guided in the future also; increase me in my taqwa, and perfect my guidance in all my matters.

Chapter One Hundred and Fifteen

O Turner of the Hearts

Allah tells His Messenger salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam: so remain on a right course as you have been commanded. Meaning: right now you are on the right path — remain on the right path; have istiqamah, have stability.

And Allah tells him in the Qur’an: and if We had not given you stability, you would have almost inclined to them a little bit — you would have inclined to accepting the request of the mushrikun a little; and you did not, because We gave you stability.

If the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam was in need of stability on right guidance, then what about us? We are in greater need of istiqamah. We can never think: oh, I have guidance, I am a Muslim, I pray five times a day, I wear the hijab, I’m fine; I want to know other du’as — the du’as of guidance I already have. No. We are always in need of guidance, in extreme need of guidance, no matter what our level is. Even if we have just done Hajj and ten ‘Umrahs, and we have a habit of reciting Surat al-Baqarah every day, and we complete the Qur’an every seven days, and we send salawat on the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam a hundred thousand times a day — no matter what our level, no matter what good deeds we do, we are still in need of guidance. Because if he needed tathbit, if he needed istiqamah, then we need it even more.

The Heart Is Always Turning

Hadith

Umm Salamah was asked what du’a the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam made most frequently, and she replied that he would say: “O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.” She said: I asked him, why do you make this du’a so much? He said: O Umm Salamah, there is no person except that his heart is between two of the fingers of Allah; and Allah makes steadfast whom He wills, and causes to deviate whom He wills.

She was implying: you are the Prophet of Allah, you are already firm on the religion of Allah — why do you keep asking Allah to keep your heart firm on His religion? And the answer is that there is no guarantee that your heart will remain as it is, because the nature of the heart is that it changes, it turns, it shifts. This is the nature of the heart.

Ibn al-Qayyim said that when the slave comes to know that Allah is the Turner of the hearts, and that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart, and that every day He is bringing about a new matter, and that He does what He wills and commands what He wills, and guides whom He wills to the straight path and sends astray whom He wills, and honours whom He wills and abases whom He wills — when a person comes to know this, then such a person does not become free of fear. He is afraid lest his heart be turned away, lest Allah prevent him from guidance, or turn his heart after having guided him.

And this is the reason why Allah praises those slaves who say: our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower. It was said: if there were no fear of the hearts becoming deviated, they would not make this du’a. There is a chance that the heart can be deviated after having been guided — this is why they pray to Allah.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the heart is called qalb because of its constant turning about. And he said that the example of the heart is like that of a feather hanging off a tree: the wind turns it about from one direction to another. Because it is so light and it is hanging from the tree, it doesn’t have to be a fast wind or a tornado — a light breeze is enough to change the direction of that feather. One moment it is facing one way, another moment it has turned around, it is spinning, and now it is facing another way.

This is the state of the heart: that the different circumstances of life, and the different desires and temptations of the nafs, and the whispers of shaytan, and the things we see around us, constantly turn the state of our heart. One second we are focused on Allah, and the very next moment we are tempted to do something else, to do something that is not pleasing to Allah.

In another hadith we learn that the heart of the son of Adam turns about faster than a boiling pot. If you have noticed how a pot of water boils when you want it to boil before you put in pasta or rice — it is bubbling, and in the bubbling water there is a lot of intensity, a lot of speed, and you see how the bubbles are constantly rising to the surface, and the water is constantly turning about: it comes to the surface out of pressure and then it goes back down, and then from the pressure again it rises to the surface. This is how the heart is: constantly changing, constantly turning; there is a constant flow of different emotions, different feelings, different thoughts, different ideas, different conditions going through our heart.

Even the Prophets Prayed for It

And the prophets of Allah were people of faith, people of yaqin — yet they prayed for themselves. Look at Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam): he broke the idols with his own hands, yet he said: my Lord, keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. Can you imagine? Ibrahim broke idols with his own hands; he left his family, he left his father, because of these idols; he didn’t want to have anything to do with them. And he is the one making du’a: ya Allah, You protect me. There is no guarantee in the future; I don’t have any control over myself in the future; I don’t know what will become of me — so You protect me from ever worshipping idols, me and my children. This is why we make du’a: do not leave me to my nafs for even the blink of an eye.

And look at the du’a Yusuf (‘alayhis salam) made: cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous. When did he make this du’a? After he had endured what he endured in the house of al-‘Aziz and in the prison, and then he was brought out of there and given power; his family is reunited; all these years he has been making the right choices; his tests were very difficult but he was making right choices — and still he makes du’a: O my Lord, allow me to die as a Muslim. Up until this point I have been in submission to You, but I don’t know what is going to happen in the future.

We don’t know what is going to happen in the future, what test might come that could turn us away from right guidance. And it is necessary that we keep working, striving, to strengthen and renew our faith. This is why we are obligated to pray five times a day — we are obligated to worship Allah not once a day, not once a month, not once a week, but five times a day, every single day, no matter what day it is. It could be the day you are getting married; it could be the day you are taking a really serious, difficult exam — still you have to pray five times a day.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that iman becomes worn out inside of you just as your clothes become old. Over time clothes become old: sometimes there is a tear, there is a rip, and you have to mend them; you have to wash them, iron them, fix them. Just like that, your iman inside of you also becomes worn, so you need to renew it. He said: pray to Allah to renew the faith in your heart.

And we have to be firm until we die. Allah says: and worship your Lord until there comes to you certainty — meaning until you die. And: do not die except while you are Muslim, in a state of submission to Allah.

How You Will Cross

And the speed and manner in which we proceed on the straight path in this world is the same speed and manner in which we will go on the Sirat on the Day of Judgement. In a hadith we learn that some people will cross the path in the blink of an eye; others will cross it like lightning; some as fast as moving clouds — sometimes you see the clouds in the sky, how quickly they move; other people will cross it like shooting stars; some like a fast-blowing wind; some like running horses; some like people running; and some will have to crawl on all fours, on their hands and feet. And the ulama say this is because: are you recompensed except for what you used to do? Your condition on the Day of Judgement will be exactly how your spiritual state was in the world.

❖  ❖  ❖

How to Have Steadfastness

Know that it is Allah who gives it. It is Allah who gives stability to those who believe through the firm word, in worldly life and also in the Hereafter. It is not your strength, your grit, your knowledge, your family, your circumstances, your inner strength or your self-discipline that enables you to be firm on the straight path. This is purely from Allah. So ask Allah to increase you in guidance, to keep you firm on guidance.

Adhere to iman and taqwa. Allah says: O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and He will make for you a light by which you will walk, and He will forgive you.

Hold on to the Qur’an, because the Qur’an is the rope of Allah, and it has been revealed so that Allah gives firmness and stability to those who believe. When you hold on to the Qur’an — you recite it, you reflect on it, you keep learning it, you keep studying it — then Allah will also keep you firm and steadfast on the right path. So find a way of holding on to the Qur’an; your life is unique, so you have to see what is possible for you.

Keep learning. Never think that the Islamic studies you studied at school, or in Sunday school, or a course you studied once upon a time, or a class you took on a weekend, or a lecture you heard five weeks ago, is sufficient. These things definitely help, but it is necessary that we keep learning. Even if you go for Jumu‘ah, select a place where there are quality khutbahs, where you actually learn something; and when you sit in the khutbah, pay attention, listen attentively, try to remember what you heard; if something was difficult to comprehend, go and ask the imam, ask questions, seek clarification. Because knowledge is nur and ignorance is darkness, and we learn that Allah is the friend of those who believe and brings them out of darkness into light. When you increase in knowledge you have greater confidence, better clarity, strength in your actions, and the motivation to continue.

Learn about the lives of the righteous, especially the prophets of Allah. In the Qur’an Allah mentions the stories of His prophets so that We may make firm your heart with it. These stories are an inspiration for us. The story of Ibrahim (‘alayhis salam), how he was thrown into the fire and yet did not leave his faith; and when Jibril came to help him he said: Allah is enough for me, I don’t need your help. The story of Musa (‘alayhis salam) standing before the water with Fir’awn coming from behind, and as the people around him were giving up hope, he said: indeed, with me is my Lord, He will guide me. The magicians who believed in Musa, when Fir’awn threatened to kill them, and they said: indeed, to our Lord we will return. So learn these stories, reflect on them, review them, so that when you are becoming weak you find strength, stability and firmness.

Strive in the way of Allah. Sometimes it is not easy to make time, sit down, open the Qur’an and recite; you really have to struggle against your nafs. Sometimes it is not easy to recite the Qur’an properly; you have to slow down, pay attention to every letter. Sometimes wearing the hijab is incredibly hard. But just because something is difficult, it doesn’t mean that we quit. Remember: and those who strive for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways.

Keep busy doing good things. Ask yourself, no matter what you are doing: is this something that is good, is this worth my time and effort, how can I improve it, how can I do it in a way that is pleasing to Allah? Maybe I can correct my intention; maybe I can correct my manner; maybe as I am engaged in this work I can continue to remember Allah. Allah says that if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and a firmer position for them in faith; and then We would have given them from Ourselves a great reward, and We would have guided them to a straight path.

Be mindful of Allah and guard what He has obligated. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said: guard Allah and He will guard you — meaning guard what Allah has imposed on you, what Allah has obligated on you, and then Allah will guard you: your body, your mind, your family, your property, and most importantly your deen.

Do good, however little it may be. When Allah gives you the ability and the willingness to do something good, don’t belittle it; do it anyway, because one good deed leads to another. It was reported that when you see someone doing something good, realise that there is a string of good deeds behind that particular good deed. A person doesn’t randomly do a major good deed; before any good deed there were a number of other good deeds. If a person is reciting a juz of Qur’an a day, how does that happen? Not randomly — it is because the person was in the habit of reciting Qur’an even before; yes, it may have been a little on a daily basis, but it was something because of which they were able to recite more.

Do not belittle sins. And when you see someone doing something bad, realise that there are many sisters of that evil; this is not a unique occurrence; there were many other sins the person did before, which led to this sin. Ibn al-Qayyim said that sins are like wounds — and how many wounds there are that lead a person to death and destruction. A person gets injured, and then that injury becomes a wound, and that wound gets infected, and then there is high fever and complications, and a person can literally die. He said: the one who wishes to be steadfast, it does not befit him that he belittles sins, or that he finds joy in committing sins, or that he makes a pile of minor sins — because sins are destructive. Allah says: so We destroyed them for their sins.

Keep good company. The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam is told in the Qur’an: and keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face. Because when you remain in their company, you increase in faith, you increase in hope.

Ibn al-Qayyim said about his teacher that there would be times when they would be filled with fear — and fear leads to negative thoughts, sometimes even negative thoughts about Allah — and they would go to their teacher, and at times they would just see him and he would begin talking, and that would remove all of their fear and negative thoughts, and would in fact convert their condition into that of strength and conviction and satisfaction.

Sometimes when you are alone in your head you only have your own thoughts to hear, your own negative thoughts, and then you get trapped in them. So when you keep righteous company and you hear them say good things, positive words — even if they are not directly advising you, they are just talking about their day or their thoughts or their plan of action — what does that do? It fills you with hope, it inspires you, it encourages you. One of the companions would say to another: come, sit with us, let us believe for an hour — meaning come, let us sit together and talk about something good so that we revive and strengthen our faith.

And the benefit of keeping good company is that every believer is the mirror of his brother. A good person will help you see your good qualities and also the areas where you need improvement. Because sometimes we have a lot of self-doubt; we really undermine our potential; we discredit ourselves constantly; we don’t believe that we have any good quality; sometimes we are trapped in a cycle of negativity. So a righteous friend gives you encouragement and assures you that you are capable, that you are able to do good things. When you look at yourself in a mirror you don’t just see faults; you also see good things. Likewise a good friend will direct you to recognising your potential and your good qualities, for which you can praise and thank Allah; and they will also help you identify your errors and mistakes so that you can improve.

Watch your tongue. Be careful about what you say when you are angry, when you are hurt, when you are overloaded with work, when you are struggling. Do not say wrong, negative things about your parents, about your loved ones, about your children, about your employer, about your co-workers, about your helpers, about your Lord. Because when a person begins to say negative things, you never know — that might be a time of acceptance of supplications, and Allah makes that negative thing your reality.

The Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that a person’s faith cannot be upright until his heart is upright, and his heart cannot be upright until his tongue is upright. So keep tight control on your tongue; learn to remain silent in situations where you do not need to talk, where you do not need to offer your golden advice — to remain silent and not bother people, not offend them, not injure their feelings, not make life difficult for them. Learn to keep silent when you need to be silent, and keep control on your tongue, so that you know what to say, when to say it, how much to say, and in which manner. And ask Allah: saddid lisani — O my Lord, make my tongue straight.

Keep holding yourself accountable. Don’t think that you did something to discipline yourself when you were young, or five years ago, and that is sufficient; this is an ongoing journey. One of the salaf said: I have spent forty years fighting against my nafs. Forty years. Hasan al-Basri said that the believer continues to watch over himself and continues to hold himself accountable for the sake of Allah; and on the Day of Judgement the account of such people will be easier, because they already held themselves accountable; and those who do not hold themselves accountable, who don’t discipline themselves, their account will be harder.

If you strive to discipline yourself, you will check how much you are talking, how much you are eating, in which way you are looking at people, what words you are selecting. And when you are careful you protect yourself from a lot of mistakes and errors; but when you are careless and you let yourself loose, you end up injuring this person and that person again and again, and you end up accumulating so many wrong things. Allah says: he has certainly succeeded who purifies himself.

What Blocks the Path

Following desires. Allah says: and do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from the way of Allah. Which desire? Wrong desire — for example the desire to eat something while you are fasting; don’t follow that. Likewise the desire to give someone an earful when you are upset with them; don’t follow that desire. The desire to look at something that is not appropriate to look at; don’t follow that desire.

Forgetting the verses of Allah — a person detaches himself from the book of Allah. There was once a time when they were connected with it, and now they leave it. We learn in the Qur’an that the person who turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful — shaytan is appointed to him as a companion, and that person becomes of those who are misguided.

Being impressed with yourself — oh, I have done this and this and this, I have accomplished such and such, I am a good person, I am a righteous person. This is a huge mistake; it prevents a person from striving to become better, from improving themselves, because they are satisfied with their present condition; and so they will not bother to improve, and they will actually fall backwards.

The colourful things of this world are also a huge obstacle on the right path. And bad company is a huge obstacle on the right path.

What Steadfastness Brings

When a person is steadfast on the right path, Allah gives them abundant blessings; He protects them from fear, from grief, from regret, from sadness; He gives them the company and friendship of the angels, and the angels inspire good, positive thoughts in them; and especially at the time of death the angels welcome such a person and give them good news.

And when a person is steadfast and spends their life in obedience to Allah, the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam said that the white hairs of the believer are a light. So if you develop grey hair in Islam, white hair in Islam, we learn in hadith that for every white hair a person receives a good deed and his rank is raised.

Hadith

A man came to the Prophet salla Allahu 'alayhi wa sallam and said: I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah; and I pray the five daily prayers, and I fast in the month of Ramadan and pray in it, and I give zakat — then where will I be on the Day of Judgement? He said: whoever dies in this way will be among the truthful and among the martyrs.

Chapter One Hundred and Sixteen

The Du’as for Firmness on Guidance

1. In every rak‘ah of every salah
اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ

Guide us to the straight path. Guide us to repentance; guide us to improvement; guide us in every aspect, every matter of our lives; teach us more things, better things; give us the willingness to obey You, and give us the ability to obey You.

2. Do not let our hearts deviate
رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ

Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy; indeed You are the Bestower.

Here we are asking Allah for special mercy — min ladunka rahmah, from Yourself mercy — because the mercy of Allah is the greatest and the best, and it includes every good thing of this life and the next. It includes iman; it includes different acts of obedience; it includes ease in earning our livelihood; it includes safety and health, well-being physical and mental; it includes sufficiency in this life; it includes ease in life, and ease at the time of death, and ease in the grave, and ease on the Day of Judgement — and ultimately Jannah is Allah’s mercy. And remember that it is because of Allah’s mercy that a person is guided to faith, that a person has taqwa, that a person has the special friendship of Allah. So what gift are we asking for in this du’a? The gift of guidance, the gift of steadfastness on guidance, and great mercy from Allah.

3. The du’a of Yusuf (‘alayhis salam)
فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ

Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.

He is first acknowledging that every good thing in his life was because of Allah, because Allah is the one who created everything. And: You are my friend in this life and in the next life — because everyone in our lives is temporary: spouse, children, good friends, parents, whoever they are, they are temporarily with us. Who is always with us? Allah. So: cause me to die while I am in submission to You, and in the Hereafter join me with the righteous, keep me in their company, which is of course in Jannah.

4. Pour upon us patience
رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ

Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims.

This is the du’a the magicians of Fir’awn made after they believed in Musa (‘alayhis salam) and Fir’awn threatened to kill them all. They understood that Fir’awn was a tyrant who was going to torture them, who was going to make their life very difficult and painful — so they asked Allah: ya Allah, pour patience on us, so that we are able to remain steadfast in the face of all of these difficulties. And sometimes it happens that you find yourself surrounded by trials, and you try to stabilise yourself, and then another test comes, another trial, another difficulty. So ask Allah: ya Allah, pour down patience on me, give me steadfastness, and cause me to die as a Muslim — that when I leave this world I am in a state of submission to You.

5. Live us and die us as Muslims
